.. _preambles-guide:

Guide to Preambles in ETC
=========================

.. rubric:: Prepared by Clark Kimberling (August 2026)

This Guide catalogs the inter-center group preambles across all 37 Parts of the *Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers* (ETC), providing a searchable index of thematic center families, geometric transformations, contributors, and definitions.

.. _guide-preamble-0022:

* :ref:`X_1601 <X_1601>`–:ref:`X_1634 <X_1634>` — **TCC Perspectors**

  Suppose P is a point. As noted in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 201, the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>` is perspective to the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`. (The tangential triangle is also perspector to the circum-:term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, with the same perspector as for the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`.) In August 2003, Jean-Pierre Ehrmann gave barycentrics for the perspector, called the TCC-perspector of P. For further properties of TCC perpsectors, published some 14 years after their introduction here, see I. Minevich and P. Morton, *International Journal of Geometry* 2017, `"Synthetic foundations of cevian geometry, IV" <https://ijgeometry.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/61-85.pdf>`__

* :ref:`X_1908 <X_1908>`–:ref:`X_1982 <X_1982>` — **Centers from bicentric pairs**

  Suppose P and U are a bicentric pair. Many operations on :g:`P <P>` and U result in :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`. Among these are trilinear and barycentric product, bicentric sum, bicentric difference, :term:`crosssum <crosssum>`, and :term:`crossdifference <crossdifference>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0028:

* :ref:`X_1992 <X_1992>`–:ref:`X_2006 <X_2006>` — **Orthocorrespondents**

  Suppose that P is a point in the plane of triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The perpendiculars through :g:`P <P>` to the lines :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`CP <[ C P ]>` meet the lines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively, in collinear points. Let :g:`L <L>` denote their line. The :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of :g:`L <L>` is the *orthocorrespondent of :g:`P* <P*>`. This definition was introduced by :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`.

Then PK(X) is the point of intersection of the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of :g:`X <X>` and the trilinear polar of :math:`X ^{-1}`, and NK(P) is the pole of the line :math:`XX^{-1}` with respect to the conic that passes through points :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`X <X>`, and :math:`X ^{-1}`. Also, PK(X) is the :term:`crossdifference <crossdifference>`, and NK(X) the :term:`crosssum <crosssum>`, of :g:`X <X>` and :math:`X ^{-1}`.

The term ":term:`complementary conjugate <complementary-conjugate>`" already in use at the time of this writing (November 11, 2004) is a synonym for "medial :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`", as is ":term:`anticomplementary conjugate <anticomplementary-conjugate>`" for "anticomplementary isogonal conjugate"; accordingly, the earlier terms will be used in the sequel. .. _guide-preamble-0045:

* :ref:`X_2979 <X_2979>`–:ref:`X_2998 <X_2998>` — **Dual triangles: DC points and CD points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`. Suppose :g:`DEF << D E F >>` is a triangle in the plane of triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`D' <D'>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the point of intersection of line :g:`EF <[ E F ]>` and the line at infinity. Define :g:`E' <E'>` and :g:`F' <F'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>` is here named the *dual* of :g:`DEF << D E F >>`. The vertices of :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>` lie on the circumcircle, and :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>` is similar to :g:`DEF << D E F >>`. The duality is between the sidelines :g:`EF <[ E F ]>`, :g:`FD <[ F D ]>`, :g:`DE <[ D E ]>` and the points :g:`D' <D'>`, :g:`E' <E'>`, :g:`F' <F'>`, respectively. For example, if :g:`E <E>` and :g:`F <F>` remain fixed and D varies, then :g:`D' <D'>` remains fixed, while :g:`E'F' <[ E' F' ]>` varies. Actually :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>` is the dual of any triangle homothetic to :g:`DEF << D E F >>`. Indeed, :g:`DEF << D E F >>` need not be a triangle but can be the union of three concurrent lines. Suppose U is a point having :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` :g:`DEF << D E F >>` and :term:`dual triangle <dual-triangle>` :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>`. Then there exists a point DC(U) whose circum-:term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` (:cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 201) is :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>`. To construct DC(U) from :g:`U <U>`, let :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`AD' <[ A D' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the {B,C}-harmonic conjugate of :g:`A' <A'>`. Define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur in DC(U). Also, DC(U) = U-:term:`isoconjugate <isoconjugate>` of the :term:`crosssum <crosssum>` of :g:`U <U>` and :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`.

Part 3
------

.. _guide-preamble-0047:

* :ref:`X_3027 <X_3027>`–:ref:`X_3028 <X_3028>` — **Antipodal Pairs on Circles**

  In response to Stevanovic's findings (:ref:`X_3000 <X_3000>` to :ref:`X_3006 <X_3006>`), :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` noted (:cite:`Hyacinthos <hyacinthos>`, 12/9/2004) a method for mapping a pair of antipodal points on one circle to an antipodal pair on another circle. The method depends on centers of similitude: Suppose :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and :g:`O_{2} <O_2>` are circles, that P is on :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and that :g:`P' <P'>` is the antipode of :g:`P <P>` on :g:`O_{1} <O_1>`. Let :g:`U <U>` be the internal center of similitude (insimilicenter) of :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and :g:`O_{2} <O_2>`, and V the exsimilicenter. Define :g:`Q <Q>` = :g:`PU <[ P U ]>` ∩\ :g:`P' <P'>` V and :g:`Q' <Q'>` = PV ∩\ :g:`P' <P'>` U. Then on :g:`O_{2} <O_2>`, point :g:`Q' <Q'>` is the antipode of Q. Moreover, the lines :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>` and :g:`QQ' <[ Q Q' ]>` are parallel.

.. _guide-preamble-0048:

* :ref:`X_3112 <X_3112>`–:ref:`X_3118 <X_3118>`

  represent points introduced by Quang Tuan Bui in :cite:`Hyacinthos <hyacinthos>`, August 5, 2006. Suppose X is a point not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let

  | gX = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of X
  | tX = :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of X
  | tgX = isotomic conjugate of gX
  | gtX = isogonal conjugate of tX
  | Gt = intersection of lines X(tX) and (gX)(gtX)
  | Tg = intersection of lines X(gX) and (tX)(tgX)

  Then the points :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, gX, tX, Tg, Gt are on a conic. As a circumconic, it is the image under the isogonal conjugate mapping of line X(gtX). It is also the image under the isotomic conjugate mapping of line X(tgX).

.. _guide-preamble-0049:

* :ref:`X_3119 <X_3119>`–:ref:`X_3126 <X_3126>` — **Danneels Perspectors**

  | Suppose :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`X <X>`. Let :g:`L_{AB} <L_AB>` be the line through :g:`B <B>` parallel to :g:`A_{1}B_{1} <[ A_1 B_1 ]>`, and let :g:`L_{AC} <L_AC>` be the line through :g:`C <C>` parallel to :g:`A_{1}C_{1} <[ A_1 C_1 ]>`.
  | Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`L_{AB} <L_AB>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{AC} <L_AC>`, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Let

  :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` = :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`AA_{2} <[ A A_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` = :g:`AA_{2} <[ A A_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`.

  Eric Danneels proves in "A Simple Perspectivity," *:cite:`Forum Geometricorum <forum-geometricorum>`* 6 (2006) 199-203, that the triangles :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics), then the Danneels perspector P(X) is given by

  P(X) = x(y - z)\ :sup:`2` : y(z - x)\ :sup:`2` : z(x - y)\ :sup:`2`.

.. _guide-preamble-0050:

* :ref:`X_3272 <X_3272>`–:ref:`X_3283 <X_3283>` — **are associated with six equilateral triangles**

  related to the (1st) Morley triangle; trilinears for vertices of these triangles are given just below. Received from Milorad R. Stevanovic, November 24, 2007 and December 25, 2007.

.. _guide-preamble-0051:

* :ref:`X_3310 <X_3310>` — **Barycentric Products of Perpendicular Directions**

  Suppose P and U are points on the line at infinity, given in barycentric coordinates by :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`. We call P and U *perpendicular directions* if for every point X not in the line at infinity, the lines XP and XU are perpendicular. (It is well known that if P and U are an antipodal pair on the circumcircle, then their :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` are perpendicular directions.)

.. _guide-preamble-0052:

* :ref:`X_3318 <X_3318>`–:ref:`X_3328 <X_3328>` — **Incircle transforms**

  Suppose that :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears) is a point other than the symmedian point, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. The *incircle transform of :g:`U* <U*>` is the point T(U) = a (a - b + c) (a + b - c) (c v - b w)^2 : : , which lies on the incircle. Geometrically, T(U) is the Brisse transform of the psi transform of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and U. (Brisse transform is described just before :ref:`X_1254 <X_1254>`, and psi transform, also called the "Psi mapping" elsewhere in ETC, and :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 80, is defined in the preamble just before :ref:`X_98 <X_98>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0053:

* :ref:`X_3415 <X_3415>`–:ref:`X_3446 <X_3446>` — **Vertex conjugates**

  Suppose that :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (trilinears) are points not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :math:`f(a,b,c) = a/[a^{2}vwyz - ux(bw + cv)(bz + cy)]`. The U-:term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of :g:`X <X>` is the point :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)`. For a geometric interpretation, let :g:`T <T>` be the vertex triangle of the circumcevian triangles, :g:`A_{U}B_{U}C_{U} << A_U B_U C_U >>` and :g:`A_{X}B_{X}C_{X} << A_X B_X C_X >>`, of :g:`U <U>` and X; viz., the sidelines of :g:`T <T>` are :g:`A_{U}A_{X} <[ A_U A_X ]>`, :g:`B_{U}B_{X} <[ B_U B_X ]>`, :g:`C_{U}C_{X} <[ C_U C_X ]>`. Then T is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is the :g:`U <U>`-vertex conjugate of :g:`X <X>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0054:

* :ref:`X_3602 <X_3602>`–:ref:`X_3609 <X_3609>` — **Points associated with Morley cubics K29, K30, K31**

.. _guide-preamble-0055:

* :ref:`X_3616 <X_3616>`–:ref:`X_3637 <X_3637>` — **Homothetic centers**

  Suppose that X is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, that M is the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, and that t is a real number. The t-dilation of M from :g:`X <X>`, denoted by H(X; M, t), is a triangle center. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (trilinears), then

  H(X; M, t) = bc[(1 + t)ax + (1 - t)by + (1 - t)cz] : ca[(1 - t)ax + (1 + t)by + (1 - t)cz] : ab[(1 - t)ax + (1 - t)by + (1 + t)cz],

  with inverse given by

  :math:`H^{-1}(X; M, t)` = bc[(1 - t)(by + cz) - 2ax] : ca[(1 - t)(cz + ax) - 2by : ab[(1 - t)(ax + by) - 2cz].

  :person:`César E. Lozada <cesar-lozada>` contributed several such triangle centers (March 21, 2011).

.. _guide-preamble-0056:

* :ref:`X_3647 <X_3647>`–:ref:`X_3652 <X_3652>` — **Kirikami-Schiffler Points**

  Suppose that X is a point and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line through :g:`A' <A'>` parallel to the Euler line of triangle :g:`BCX << B C X >>`, let :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` be the line through :g:`B' <B'>` parallel to the Euler line of :g:`CXA << C X A >>`, and let :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` be the line through :g:`C' <C'>` parallel to the Euler line of :g:`AXB << A X B >>`.

  It is well known that if :g:`X <X>`\ =\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, the incenter, then the three aforementioned Euler lines concur in the Schiffler point, :ref:`X_21 <X_21>`. If their parallels, the lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur, the point of concurrence is the Kirikami-Schiffler point of the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, denoted by KS(:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`). Seiichi Kirikami (February 1, 2011) found that those lines concur if :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and also concur if :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`. :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` found additional cases and properties..

.. _guide-preamble-0057:

* :ref:`X_3663 <X_3663>`–:ref:`X_3861 <X_3861>` — **Central Triangles and More Combos**

  Many :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` can be defined (as just above) by the form Xcom(nT), where T denotes a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`. In order to present such centers, it is helpful to introduce the notation T(f(a,b,c), g(b,c,a)) for central triangles. (This lengthly preamble was completed December 23, 2011.)

.. _guide-preamble-0058:

* :ref:`X_3739 <X_3739>`–:ref:`X_3757 <X_3757>` — **More Combos. Continuing the discussion of points Xcom(T)**

  suppose that T is an arbitrary triangle, and let nT denote the normalization of T. Let NT denote the set of these triangles, as matrices, and let \* denote matrix multiplication. Then NT is closed under \*. Also, NT is closed under matrix inversion. Consequently, (NT, \*) is a group, comparable to the group of stochastic matrices. Suppose that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are triangles. In many cases, the product :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is well-defined (e.g., :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, page 175). However, n(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) may not be n(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`)\*n(:g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) if :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are not normalized. Therefore, it is important, when dealing with products, to include the "n" if it is intended.

.. _guide-preamble-0059:

* :ref:`X_3758 <X_3758>`–:ref:`X_3861 <X_3861>` — **Central Triangles and More Combos**

  (See just above, Centers :ref:`X_3663 <X_3663>`-:ref:`X_3861 <X_3861>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0060:

* :ref:`X_3862 <X_3862>`–**X_4162** — **Inverse Triangles and More Combos**

  The :term:`Euler triangle <euler-triangle>` and the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th Euler triangles are discussed in the preamble to :ref:`X_3758 <X_3758>`, along with eight other :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>` using the notation T(f(a,b,c), g(b,c,a)). Recall that the inverse of a normalized central triangle :g:`T <T>`, denoted by Inverse(nT) or Inverse(n(T)), is also a normalized central triangle. Barycentrics for the inverse of each of the 13 triangles and properties of these triangles were given (:person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 2011).

.. _guide-preamble-0065:

* **X_5000**–**X_5001** — **Walsmith Points**

  Early in 2012, Russell Walsmith introduced this point and conjectured that it lies on the Euler line. :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` found barycentrics for the point and its inverse-in-the-circumcircle, X_5001, and proved that the two points lie on the Euler line.

.. _preambles-part-4:

Part 4
------

.. _guide-preamble-0066:

* **X_5376**–**X_5389** — **Points on the Hutson-Moses hyperbola**

  The Hutson-Moses hyperbola, introduced at X_5375, is given by the following barycentric equation:

  a(a - b)(a - c)yz + b(b - c)(b - a)zx + c(c - a)(c - b)xy = 0.

  This hyperbola has perspector :ref:`X_100 <X_100>`, center X_5375, meets the circumcircle in :ref:`X_898 <X_898>` and the Steiner circumellipse in :ref:`X_666 <X_666>`, and is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the line :ref:`X_244 <X_244>`\ \ :ref:`X_665 <X_665>`. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics) is a point on the circumcircle, then the point :math:`H(X) = x/(a(b - c))`: y/(b(c - a)) : z/(c(a - b)) is on the Hutson-Moses hyperbola.

.. _guide-preamble-0067:

* **X_6000**–**X_6031** — **Isogonal Conjugates With Respect To Various Triangles**

.. _guide-preamble-0068:

* **X_6056**–**X_6069** — **Lozada Perspectors**

  Suppose that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>`. Let :g:`L <L>` be the line through :g:`A' <A'>` tangent to the incircle, and let :g:`A* <A*>` be the touchpoint; define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. Then :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for all P. (:person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 7, 2014, :cite:`Anopolis #1466 <adgeom>`)

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinears), then the perspector is :g:`P* <P*>` = a(b + c - a)\ :math:`p^{2}` : b(a + c - b)\ :math:`q^{2}` : c(a + b - c)\ :math:`r^{2}`.

.. _guide-preamble-0069:

* **X_6070**–**X_6083** — **Points Associated with the Steiner Deltoid**

  Suppose that :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is a triangle. Its Steiner deltoid, SD, is the envelope of the Simson lines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (September 14, 2014) defined a mapping from (O) to SD; the mapping is here denoted by M and named the **Moses-Steiner image**.

.. _guide-preamble-0070:

* **X_6103**–**X_6111** — **the Dao-Moses-Telv Circle and Associated Points**

  The Dao-Moses-Telv circle is defined as the circle passing through these six points:

  | :g:`F_{1} <F_1>` = :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, the 1st Fermat point
  | :g:`F_{2} <F_2>` = :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`, the 2nd Fermat point
  | :g:`F_{3} <F_3>` = inverse of :g:`F_{1} <F_1>` in the circumcircle
  | :g:`F_{4} <F_4>` = inverse of :g:`F_{2} <F_2>` in the circumcircle
  | :g:`F_{5} <F_5>` = inverse of :g:`F_{1} <F_1>` in the nine-point circle
  | :g:`F_{6} <F_6>` = inverse of :g:`F_{2} <F_2>` in the nine-point circle

  :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>` noted that these points are concyclic, Telv Cohl gave a proof, and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` discovered properties described in this preamble. The center of the Dao-Moses-Telv circle is :ref:`X_1637 <X_1637>`. (Francisco Javier García Capitán, November 3, 2014)

  The Dao-Moses-Telv circle is orthogonal to the circumcircle, the nine-point circle, and all the other circles in their coaxal family. The circle passes through X_5000 and X_5001, these being the Walsmith point and its inverse in the circumcircle. (Peter Moses, November 6, 2014)

.. _guide-preamble-0071:

* **X_6112**–**X_6128** — **Moses Radical Circle and Associated Points**

  Summarizing notes from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (November 7, 2014), the circle here named the Moses radical circle, MRC, is defined as the radical circle of the circumcircle, nine-point circle, and Brocard circle. The center of MRC is :ref:`X_647 <X_647>`, and, like the Dao-Moses-Telv circle (see X_6103, MRC passes through X_5000 and X_5001.

.. _guide-preamble-0072:

* **X_6129**–**X_6136** — **Centers of Circles Orthogonal to the Coaxal System of the Circumcircle and Nine-Point Circle**

  Continuing :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`'s discussion in the preamble to X_6112-X)6128), suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point other than the circumcenter. Let U(P) be the circle that passes through :g:`P <P>` and its circumcircle-inverse and is orthogonal to the coaxal system of the circumcircle and nine-point circle. Then X_5000 and X_5001 lie on :g:`U <U>`

.. _guide-preamble-0073:

* **X_6137**–**X_6140** — **Centers of Circles Orthogonal to the Coaxal System of the Circumcircle and Brocard Circle**

  Continuing :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`'s discussion in the preambles to X_6112 and X_6129, suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point other than the circumcenter. Let V(P) be the circle that passes through :g:`P <P>` and its circumcircle-inverse and is orthogonal to the Schoute coaxal system; that is, the coaxal system of the circumcircle and Brocard circle. Then :ref:`X_15 <X_15>` and :ref:`X_16 <X_16>` lie on V, and the center of V is the point M(V) =\ :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)` given by . . .

.. _guide-preamble-0074:

* **X_6337**–**X_6661** — **and X_6600-XX(6661), Symbolic Substitution**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, August 8, 2026. The notation "SS(a → :math:`S_{A})`" denotes barycentric :term:`symbolic substitution <symbolic-substitution>`, similar to trilinear symbolic substitution defined at :ref:`X_3221 <X_3221>`. **Symbolic substitution carries lines to lines, conics to conics, and cubics to cubics.** For example, since :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`, :ref:`X_57 <X_57>`, :ref:`X_1073 <X_1073>`, :ref:`X_1249 <X_1249>` lie on the Thomson cubic, their images under SS(a →\ :math:`S_{A})` lie on the cubic given by

  :math:`x(S^{2}_{C}`\ :math:`y^{2}` - :math:`S^{2}_{B}`\ :math:`z^{2})` + :math:`y(S^{2}_{A}`\ :math:`z^{2}` - :math:`S^{2}_{C}`\ :math:`x^{2})` + :math:`z(S^{2}_{A}`\ :math:`x^{2}` - :math:`S^{2}_{A}`\ :math:`y^{2})` = 0.

  The subject of symbolic substitution was introduced in C. Kimberling, "Symbolic substitutions in the transfigured plane of a triangle," *Aequationes Mathematicae* 73 (2007) 156-171.

.. _guide-preamble-0075:

* **X_6395**–**X_6502** — **Centers associated with Lucas triangles and Lucas circles**
