.. _guide-preamble-0076:

* **X_6570**–**X_6577** — **Circumeigencenters (CET)**

  The :term:`eigencenter <eigencenter>` of a triangle is defined in the Glossary and in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 192. In case the triangle is the circumcevian triangle of a point :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears), the eigencenter is given by [formula]. This point is here named the **circum-eigentransform** of :g:`U <U>`, denoted by **CET(U)**. The point CET(U) lies on the circumcircle. Pairs (i,j) such that CET(X_i) = X_j include the following [list].:

.. _guide-preamble-0077:

* **X_6666**–**X_6723** — **Centroids of Quadrilaterals**

  Suppose that X is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The centroid, G,′ of {:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`X <X>`} is the :term:`complement <complement>` of the complement of :g:`X <X>`, hence also the midpoint of :g:`X <X>` and the complement of :g:`X <X>`, as well as the Kosnita(X,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) point. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics), then :g:`G' <G'>` = 2x + y + z : x +\ :math:`2y : z : x` + y + 2z. :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, February 24, 2015, noted that properties described at X_6600 and X_6601 hold generally, as follows. Let :g:`G″ <G″>` be the complement of :g:`X <X>`, and let :g:`K_aK_bK_c << K_a K_b K_c >>` be the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`G″ <G″>`. The reflection of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>` in :g:`G' <G'>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of the centroid of {:g:`K_a <K_a>`,\ :g:`K_b <K_b>`,\ :g:`K_c <K_c>`,\ :g:`G″ <G″>`}. This perspector is also the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the TCC-perspector of the isogonal conjugate of :g:`G″ <G″>`. (The TCC-perspector of a point is defined in the preamble to :ref:`X_1601 <X_1601>`.)

.. _guide-preamble-0078:

* **X_6724**–**X_6796** — **Homologous images**

  , contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, March 15, 2015. The term "homologous" means "having the same relation or relative position to". Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` be two triangles, and P a point in the plane of triangle :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`. The point :g:`P' <P'>` in the plane of triangle :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is a :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`-to-:g:`T_{2} <T_2>` homologous image of P if :g:`P' <P'>` has the same relation or relative position to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` as P has to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`. If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are similar triangles, this meaning is unambiguous, and we call :g:`P' <P'>` the :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`-to-:g:`T_{2} <T_2>` :term:`similarity image <similarity-image>` of P. If, however, :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are not similar, the term "homologous images" can apply to several kinds of mappings. We present three such mappings here.>

  **Trilinear image:**

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point with trilinears :math:`x : y : z` wrt :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`. Then the :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`-to-:g:`T_{2} <T_2>` :term:`trilinear image <trilinear-image>` of :g:`P <P>` is the point :g:`P' <P'>` with trilinears :math:`x : y : z` wrt :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. This is a non-affine collineation, preserving collinearities, but not ratios of distances between collinear points. Parallel lines do not remain parallel under this mapping, so that points on the line at infinity map to finite points. Circumconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to circumconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and inconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to inconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

  **Barycentric image:**

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point with barycentrics :math:`x : y : z` wrt :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`. Then the :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`-to-:g:`T_{2} <T_2>` :term:`barycentric image <barycentric-image>` of :g:`P <P>` is the point :g:`P' <P'>` with barycentrics :math:`x : y : z` wrt :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. This is an affine collineation, preserving collinearities as well as ratios of distances between collinear points. Parallel lines remain parallel under this mapping, so that the line at infinity maps to itself. Conics map to conics of the same type (ellipses, including circles, map to ellipses, parabolas to parabolas, hyperbolas to hyperbolas). Circumconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to circumconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and inconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to inconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

  **Functional image:**

  Let the sidelengths of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` be denoted :math:`a_{1}`, :math:`b_{1}`, :math:`c_{1}` and the sidelengths of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` be denoted :math:`a_{2}`, :math:`b_{2}`, :math:`c_{2}`. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point with coordinates :math:`f(a_{1},b_{1},c_{1}) : g(b_{1},c_{1},a_{1}) : h(c_{1},a_{1},b_{1})` with respect to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, where f, g, h either have the same degree of homogeneity, or else one is the zero function and the other two have the same degree of homogeneity. (If P is a center of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, then f = g = h.) Then the :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`-to-:g:`T_{2} <T_2>`-:term:`functional image <functional-image>` of :g:`P <P>` is the point :g:`P' <P'>` with coordinates :math:`f(a_{2},b_{2},c_{2}) : g(b_{2},c_{2},a_{2}) : h(c_{2},a_{2},b_{2})` with respect to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Coordinates here can be trilinears or barycentrics, as long as the same system is used for :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. :g:`P' <P'>` serves the same 'function' wrt :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` (e.g., centroid, circumcenter, 1st Brocard point, :g:`A <A>`-vertex of :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`, etc.) as P serves wrt :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`. For example, the orthic-to-excentral functional image of :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` = :ref:`X_40 <X_40>`, since :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` and :ref:`X_40 <X_40>` are the respective circumcenters of the orthic and :term:`excentral triangles <excentral-triangle>`. This is a non-affine collineation, preserving collinearities, but not ratios of distances between collinear points (except where these distance ratios define the point, such as midpoints, reflections, etc.). Parallel lines remain parallel under this mapping, so that the line at infinity maps to itself. Circles map to circles. Other conics map to conics, but not necessarily of the same type (e.g., the MacBeath circumconic of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` may be an ellipse, but maps to the MacBeath circumconic of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, which may be a hyperbola.) Circumconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to circumconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and inconics of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` map to inconics of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

.. _preambles-part-5:

Part 5
------

.. _guide-preamble-0079:

* **X_7001**–**X_7373** — **Centers associated with extra-triangles**

  contributed by Richard Hilton, March 19, 2015. Suppose that f(a,b,c) is a polynomial and that a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` X has barycentric coordinates :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)`. Then the A-extraversion of :g:`X <X>` is obtained by replacing a by -a in all three of its barycentric coordinates. Likewise, the B-extraversion is obtained by the substitution b → -b, and the C-extraversion by c → -c. The three extraversions are the vertices of a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` which we shall call the **extra-triangle** of X. In the notation introduced in the preamble to :ref:`X_3758 <X_3758>`, the extra-triangle of :g:`X <X>` is T(f(-a,b,c), f(b,c,-a)). For centers that have no such polynomial representation, the three extraversions are defined "by construction" [details omitted here]. The focus in this section is on centers for which the extra-triangle is perspective with :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0080:

* **X_7584**–**X_7588** — **Endo-homothetic centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 22-27, 2015. Suppose that :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` are a pair of homothetic triangles. There is a well-known point, X, called the homothetic center of :g:`U <U>` and V. For example, the homothetic center of the 1st circumperp and 2nd :term:`extouch triangles <extouch-triangle>` is :g:`X <X>` = X_7580. Now, we can "view" X from :g:`ABC << A B C >>` as X_7580, or we can "view" X from :g:`U <U>`, in which case X is :ref:`X_1993 <X_1993>`-of-U, and by homothety, X is also :ref:`X_1993 <X_1993>`-of-V. In general, if :g:`X <X>` = :g:`X' <X'>`-of-U (or equivalently, :g:`X <X>` = :g:`X' <X'>`-of-V), then the point :g:`X' <X'>` (as a function of the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`) is introduced here as the endo-homothetic center of :g:`U <U>` and V.

.. _guide-preamble-0081:

* **X_7597**–**X_7602** — **Touchpoints of pairs of circles**

  Tran Quang Hung found that the incircle of the :term:`hexyl triangle <hexyl-triangle>` is tangent to the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The point of tangency, or touchpoint, is X_7597. Let S be the set of incircles, circumcircles, and nine-point circles of 60 :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>` listed in MathWorld. :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` checked pairs of circles in S for tangency and found several new points, X_7598-X_7602. He notes (May 10, 2015) that these six points together with points already in ETC account for *all* touchpoints of pairs of circles in S.

.. _guide-preamble-0082:

* **X_7693**–**X_7709** — **Similar triangles and centers of similitude**

  contributed by :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` and :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, June 8, 2017. If two similar figures lie in the plane but do not have parallel sides (i.e., they are similar but not homothetic), there exists a center of similitude, also called a self-homologous point, which occupies the same homologous position with respect to the two figures (Johnson 1929, p. 16). See `Similitude Center at MathWorld. <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/SimilitudeCenter.html.>`__ Algebraically, the center of similitude of two similar triangles :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` is the invariant :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` under the affine transformation that maps U into V. If :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` are homothetic then their center of similitude coincides with their homothetic center.

.. _guide-preamble-0083:

* **X_7713** — **Hatzipolakis-Lozada Homothetic Centers**

  :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>` posed the following construction and related questions (June 10, 2015). Let :g:`H_aH_bH_c << H_a H_b H_c >>` be the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and H = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`. Let :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` be the orthogonal projection of :g:`H_a <H_a>` on line :g:`HH_b <[ H H_b ]>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` be the orthogonal projection of :g:`H_a <H_a>` on line :g:`HH_c <[ H H_c ]>`, and define :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` and :g:`C_{B} <C_B>` cyclically. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point (in the usual sense of a function defined on a subset of the set of points in the plane of an abstract triangle with variable side-lengths a,b,c). Let :g:`P_{A} <P_A>` = P-of-:g:`H_aA_BA_C << H_a A_B A_C >>`, :g:`P_{B} <P_B>` = P-of-:g:`H_bB_CB_A << H_b B_C B_A >>`, :g:`P_{C} <P_C>` = P-of-:g:`H_cC_AC_B << H_c C_A C_B >>`. Let :g:`P_{A} <P_A>`\ :sub:`B` be the reflection of :g:`P_{A} <P_A>` in line :g:`HH_b <[ H H_b ]>`, and define :g:`P_{B} <P_B>`\ :sub:`C` and :g:`P_{C} <P_C>`\ :sub:`A` cyclically. Let :g:`P_{A} <P_A>`\ :sub:`C` be the reflection of :g:`P_{A} <P_A>` in line :g:`HH_c <[ H H_c ]>`, and define :g:`P_{B} <P_B>`\ :sub:`C` and :g:`P_{C} <P_C>`\ :sub:`A` cyclically. Let :g:`M_{A} <M_A>` be the midpoint of :g:`P_{A} <P_A>`\ :sub:`B` and :g:`P_{A} <P_A>`\ :sub:`C`, and define :g:`M_{B} <M_B>` and :g:`M_{C} <M_C>` cyclically. Then :g:`M_{A}M_{B}M_{C} << M_A M_B M_C >>` is homothetic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the Euler line of :g:`M_{A}M_{B}M_{C} << M_A M_B M_C >>` is parallel to the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` (June 10, 2015) found that if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinears), then the homothetic center of :g:`M_{A}M_{B}M_{C} << M_A M_B M_C >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the point given by

  HL(P) = [(:math:`a^{2}` + :math:`b^{2}` + :math:`c^{2})`\ p + 2abq + 2acr]/((:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})` : : = (:math:`S_{\omega }`\ p + abq + acr)/:math:`S_{A}` : :

  If P is on the infinity line, then HL(P) = P, and if P lies on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then Euler-line-of-:g:`M_{A}M_{B}M_{C} << M_A M_B M_C >>` = Euler-line-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0084:

* **X_7720**–**X_7733** — **Centers related to the orthocentroidal triangle**

  :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` (June 18, 2015) finds perspectors, orthologic centers, and parallelogic centers associated with the orthocentroidal triangle. This triangle is defined at X_5476 as follows. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the intersection, other than :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, of the :g:`A <A>`-altitude and the orthocentroidal circle, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The orthocentroidal triangle, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, is inversely similar to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with center :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` of similitude.

.. _guide-preamble-0085:

* **X_7745**–**X_7754** — **Points on the Euler line**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 6, 2015.

.. _guide-preamble-0086:

* **X_7755**–**X_7999** — **Centers associated with mixtilinear triangles**

  :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` (July 6, 2015) introduced the 2nd-to-6th mixtilinear triangles and contributes associated :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0087:

* **X_8002**–**X_8021** — **Centers associated with the Stammler triangle**

  :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` (July 22, 2015) introduced centers associated with the Stammler triangle. :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, an equilateral triangle whose vertices are the centers of the Stammler circles; see `MathWorld: Stammler Circles <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/StammlerCircles.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0088:

* **X_8012**–**X_8042** — **Danneels points**

  Danneels points are introduced at :ref:`X_3078 <X_3078>`. The definition is restated here for a point :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics): D(U) = :math:`u^{2}(v + w)` : :math:`v^{2}(w + u)` : :math:`w^{2}(u + v)`. It is proved at :ref:`X_3078 <X_3078>` that if U is on the Euler line of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then D(U) is also on the Euler line.

.. _guide-preamble-0089:

* **X_8075**–**X_8104** — **Points associated with tangential-midarc triangles**

  This section was contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 18, 2015. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle with incenter I. Let :g:`D' <D'>` and :g:`D″ <D″>` be the points in which the line :g:`AI <[ A I ]>` meets the incircle, where :g:`D' <D'>` is the closer of the two points to A. Define :g:`E' <E'>` and :g:`F' <F'>` cyclically, and defined :g:`E″ <E″>` and :g:`F″ <F″>` cyclically. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the triangle whose sidelines are the tangents to the incircle at :g:`D' <D'>`, :g:`E' <E'>`, :g:`F' <F'>`. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` has been called the tangential-midarc triangle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (e.g., `MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/TangentialMid-ArcTriangle.html>`__), but here it is the *1st tangential-midarc triangle of :g:`ABC* << A B C* >>`. Let :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be the triangle whose sidelines are the tangents to the incircle at :g:`D″ <D″>`, :g:`E″ <E″>`, :g:`F″ <F″>`. Triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here introduced as the *2nd tangential-midarc triangle of :g:`ABC* << A B C* >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0090:

* **X_8117**–**X_8140** — **Endo-homothetic centers**

  This section was contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 7, 2015.

.. _guide-preamble-0091:

* **X_8141**–**X_8159** — **Centers of central circles**

  This section was contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 22, 2015. There are more than sixty central circles included at `MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/topics/TriangleCircles.html>`__. Triangles centers X_8141-X_8155 are centers of such circles that are not among the points X_i for i < 8141.

.. _guide-preamble-0092:

* **X_8162**–**X_8171** — **Similicenters of pairs of circles**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 5, 2015.

.. _guide-preamble-0093:

* **X_8176**–**X_8182** — **Centers associated with Van Lamoen circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 10, 2015. Let :g:`M_aM_bM_c << M_a M_b M_c >>` be the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let G = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, the centroid of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (and of :g:`M_aM_bM_c << M_a M_b M_c >>`). It is well known that the circumcenters of triangles :g:`GBM_c << G B M_c >>`, :g:`GCM_a << G C M_a >>`, :g:`GAM_b << G A M_b >>`, :g:`GCM_b << G C M_b >>`, :g:`GAM_c << G A M_c >>`, :g:`GBM_a << G B M_a >>` lie on a circle, called the van Lamoen circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. See `van Lamoen Circle at MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/vanLamoenCircle.html>`__. More generally, let :g:`U <U>` be any triangle perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector P such that the six circumcenters all lie on a circle. That circle is introduced here as the U-van Lamoen circle.

.. _guide-preamble-0094:

* **X_8185**–**X_8253** — **Centers associated with homothetic pairs of triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 13, 2015.

.. _guide-preamble-0095:

* **X_8254**–**X_8263** — **Midpoints associated with pedal and antipedal triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 17, 2015. In :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, pp. 187-188, it is noted that if :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is a triangle and P is a point not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` is homothetic to the :term:`antipedal triangle <antipedal-triangle>` of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`, :g:`P' <P'>`, of :g:`P <P>`, and also that the product of the areas of the two triangles is the square of the area of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Moreover, the vertices of the pedal triangles of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` are concyclic, and the center of the circle is the midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>`. The following table shows examples of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`P' <P'>`, and their midpoint.

.. _guide-preamble-0096:

* **X_8268**–**X_8272** — **Centers of apedal conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 19, 2015. Suppose that :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is a triangle and P is a point not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`P' <P'>` denote the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P. The vertices of the :term:`antipedal triangles <antipedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` lie on a conic, here denoted by apedal(P). The following table shows examples of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`P' <P'>`, and the center of apedal(:g:`P' <P'>`). Conjecture: For every :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P, the conic apedal(P) is a hyperbola.

.. _guide-preamble-0097:

* **X_8273**–**X_8350** — **Perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, Oct. 21, 2015. Perspectors are given for pairs of triangles Many of these triangles were introduced in connection with specific :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` in ETC.

.. _guide-preamble-0098:

* **X_8372**–**X_8424** — **Perspectors of pairs of triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 2, 2015. :term:`Central triangles <central-triangle>` :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are **perspective** if the lines :g:`A'A″ <[ A' A″ ]>`, :g:`B'B″ <[ B' B″ ]>`, :g:`C'C″ <[ C' C″ ]>` concur. The point of concurrence is their **perspector** (or center of perspective). If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are not only perspective, but homothetic, their perspector is their **homothetic center**.

.. _guide-preamble-0099:

* **X_8431**–**X_8533** — **Ceva conjugates**

  , contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 4, 2015. These points on the Neuberg cubic, K001 in :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`'s Cubics in the Triangle Plane. Each of these centers is the perspector of two triangles from a list of 25 triangles found in `Table 19.1 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Tables/table19.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0100:

* **X_8537**–**X_8550** — **Centers associated with Ehrmann circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 9, 2015. In `Hyacinthos #6098 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=6098>`__), December 2, 2002, Jean-Pierre Ehrmann defines a circle as follows. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and not on the lines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` the the point of intersection of the circle {{P,B,C}} and the line :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Define :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` symmetrically, and define :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, :g:`B_{A} <B_A>`, :g:`C_{A} <C_A>`, :g:`C_{B} <C_B>` cyclically. These six points of intersection are on a circle if and only if :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. This circle is here named the **Ehrmann circle**. The circles {{:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,B,C}}, {{:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,C,A}}, {{:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,A,B,}} are the **A-Ehrmann circle, B-Ehrmann circle, C-Ehrmann circle**, respectively.

.. _guide-preamble-0101:

* **X_8551**–**X_8579** — **Coefficient Points of Circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 15, 2015. Every circle has a trilinear equation of the following form:

  (Lα + Mβ + Nγ)⋅(aα + bβ + cγ) + K⋅(aβγ + bγα + cαβ) = 0 (1)

  and conversely, if K ≠ 0 then the equation (1) represents a circle.

  A circle Λ is a **central circle** if :math:`L : M : N` is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` and K is a homogeneous symmetric function of (a,b,c); see :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, pp 219-226 and `CircleFunction at MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/CircleFunction.html>`__). In such a case,\ :math:`L : M : N` is called the **coefficient point** of the circle Λ. (The coefficients L, M, N, K are homogeneous in a,b,c, so that :math:`L : M : N` is unambiguously defined. In other words, there is no loss in assuming that K = 1 in equation (1).)

.. _guide-preamble-0102:

* **X_8580**–**X_8583** — **Perspectors associated with the Atik triangle**

  , contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 22, 2015. Suppose that V is a point outside a circle (U,u). Let (V,v) be the circle with center V that is orthogonal to (U,u), so that :math:`v^{2}` = \|\ :g:`UV <[ U V ]>`\ \|\ :sup:`2` - :math:`u^{2}` = power of V with respect to (U,u). Let :g:`U_{V,A} <U_V,A>` be the circle (V,w) obtained from (U,r) = :g:`A <A>`-excircle and V = incenter, and let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the radical axis of :g:`U_{V,A} <U_V,A>` and the :g:`A <A>`-excircle. Define :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` and :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` cyclically. Let :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{C} <L_C>`, :g:`B' <B'>` = :g:`L_{C} <L_C>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`C' <C'>` = :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the Atik triangle (Atik being the name of a star). The Atik triangle is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :ref:`X_3062 <X_3062>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0103:

* **X_8601**–**X_8614** — **Points associated with orthocevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 22, 2015. Let (O,R) be the circumcircle, and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`X <X>`. Let (:g:`O_{A} <O_A>`,\ :math:`r_{A})` be the circle through :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` and orthogonal to (O,R). That is, (:g:`O_{A} <O_A>`,\ :math:`r_{A})` is the circle that passes through the points :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` and also their inverses in (O,R). Define (:g:`O_{B} <O_B>`,\ :math:`r_{B})` and (:g:`O_{C} <O_C>`,\ :math:`r_{C})` cyclically. The triangle T(X) = :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` is here named the **orthocevian triangle of X**.

.. _guide-preamble-0104:

* **X_8616**–**X_8665** — **Gibert circumtangential conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 26, 2015, based on notes from :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, November 2, 2015, in connection with the cubic `K024 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k024.html>`__. The Gibert circumtangential conjugate of a point :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics) is defined as the point

  a^2 (a^2 b^2 c^2 u v - b^2 c^4 u v + a^4 c^2 v^2 - a^2 c^4 v^2 + a^2 b^2 c^2 u w - b^4 c^2 u w - 3 a^2 b^2 c^2 v w + a^4 b^2 w^2 - a^2 b^4 w^2) : :

  A related point is the circumtangential-:term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`, defined by

  a^2 (a^2 c^2 u v - c^4 u v + a^2 c^2 v^2 - c^4 v^2 + a^2 b^2 u w - b^4 u w + a^4 v w - a^2 b^2 v w - a^2 c^2 v w - 2 b^2 c^2 v w + a^2 b^2 w^2 - b^4 w^2) : :

  If U is on the circumcircle, then its Gibert circumtangential conjugate, denoted by :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`\ (U), is on the Lemoine axis, :ref:`X_187 <X_187>`\ \ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`, and the circumtangential-isogonal conjugate, denoted by :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`\ (U), is on the line at infinity, :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`\ \ :ref:`X_511 <X_511>`. Thus, if U is on :ref:`X_187 <X_187>`\ \ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`, then :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`\ (U) is on the circumcircle, and if U is on :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`\ \ :ref:`X_511 <X_511>`, then :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`\ (U) is on the circumcircle. For a selection of circumtangential-isogonal conjugates, see X_8666-X_8714.

.. _guide-preamble-0105:

* **X_8666**–**X_8714** — **Circumtangential-isogonal conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 26, 2015, based on notes from :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, November 2, 2015, in connection with the cubic `K024 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k024.html>`__. The circumtangential-:term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`, denoted by :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`\ (U), is defined by

  a^2 (a^2 c^2 u v - c^4 u v + a^2 c^2 v^2 - c^4 v^2 + a^2 b^2 u w - b^4 u w + a^4 v w - a^2 b^2 v w - a^2 c^2 v w - 2 b^2 c^2 v w + a^2 b^2 w^2 - b^4 w^2) : :

  If U is on the circumcircle, then :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`\ (U), is on the line at infinity, :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`\ \ :ref:`X_511 <X_511>`, so that if U is on :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`\ \ :ref:`X_511 <X_511>`, then :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`\ (U) is on the circumcircle. Related conjugates are :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`\ (U) defined in the preamble to X_8616 and the circumnormal-isogonal conjugate :g:`M_{3} <M_3>`\ (U) defined in the preamble to X_8715.

.. _guide-preamble-0106:

* **X_8715**–**X_8725** — **Circumnormal-isogonal conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 28, 2015, based on notes from :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, November 28, 2015, as a sequel to the preceding section on circumtangential-:term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0107:

* **X_8726**–**X_8734** — **Perspectors involving the Ascella triangle**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 3, 2015. Let :g:`A' <A'>` = incircle-inverse of :g:`A <A>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` be the circle {{B,C,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`}}, and define :g:`O_{B} <O_B>` and :g:`O_{C} <O_C>` cyclically. The circles :g:`O_{A} <O_A>`, :g:`O_{B} <O_B>`, :g:`O_{C} <O_C>` are orthogonal to the incircle. Let :g:`V_{A} <V_A>` be the center of :g:`O_{A} <O_A>`, and define :g:`V_{B} <V_B>` and :g:`V_{C} <V_C>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`V_{A}V_{B}V_{C} << V_A V_B V_C >>` is here named the Ascella triangle. The Ascella triangle is also the mid-triangle of the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` and the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0108:

* **X_8735**–**X_8756** — **Points associated with orthoanticevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, and :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, November 9, 2015. Let (O,R) be the circumcircle, and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`X <X>`. Let (:g:`O_{A} <O_A>`,\ :math:`r_{A})` be the circle through :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` and orthogonal to (O,R). That is, (:g:`O_{A} <O_A>`,\ :math:`r_{A})` is the circle that passes through the points :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` and also their inverses in (O,R). Define (:g:`O_{B} <O_B>`,\ :math:`r_{B})` and (:g:`O_{C} <O_C>`,\ :math:`r_{C})` cyclically. The triangle T(X) = :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` is here named the **orthoanticevian triangle of X**. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) and T(P) is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then the perspector is barycentric product of :g:`P <P>` and the orthocenter;

.. _guide-preamble-0109:

* **X_8782**–**X_8855** — **Centers associated with Ehramann circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 11, 2015. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and let :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` =\ :math:`p_{1} : q_{1} : r_{1}`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` =\ :math:`p_{2} : q_{2} : r_{2}`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>` =\ :math:`p_{3} : q_{3} : r_{3}` (barycentrics) be three non-collinear points, none on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The locus of a point M such that the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of M and the triangle :g:`T <T>` = :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` are perspective, with perspector denoted by Z(M), is given by

  :math:`F(x,y,z) =`\ δ\ :sub:`11`\ (:math:`r_{1}`\ y-:math:`q_{1}`\ z)\ :math:`x^{2}`\ +δ\ :sub:`22`\ (:math:`p_{2}`\ z-:math:`r_{2}`\ x)\ :math:`y^{2}`\ + δ\ :sub:`33`\ (:math:`q_{3}`\ x-:math:`p_{3}`\ y)\ :math:`z^{2}`\ +(:math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`q_{3}`\ :math:`r_{1}`-:math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`q_{1}`\ :math:`r_{2})`\ xyz = 0 (1)

  where δ\ :sub:`ij` is the (i, j)-minor of the vertex matrix of the triangle :g:`T <T>`.

  If T and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective, then :math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`q_{3}`\ :math:`r_{1}` - :math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`q_{1}`\ :math:`r_{2}` = 0 and, if the equation (1) is non-degenerate, it represents a pivotal cubic with pole Ω(T) and pivot P(T) given by:

  | Ω(T) = δ\ :sub:`22`\ δ\ :sub:`33`\ :math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`p_{3}` : δ\ :sub:`33`\ δ\ :sub:`11`\ :math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`q_{1}` : δ\ :sub:`11`\ δ\ :sub:`22`\ :math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`r_{1}`
  | P(T) = δ\ :sub:`22`\ δ\ :sub:`33`\ :math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`r_{2}` : δ\ :sub:`33`\ δ\ :sub:`11`\ :math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`r_{1}` : δ\ :sub:`11`\ δ\ :sub:`22`\ :math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`r_{1}`

  This section deals with the poles and pivots of these cubics and the perspectors Z(M) for most of the centers M lying on them.

.. _guide-preamble-0110:

* **X_8856**–**X_8950** — **Loci associated with selected triangles (2)**

  , contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 11, 2015. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and let :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` =\ :math:`p_{1} : q_{1} : r_{1}`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` =\ :math:`p_{2} : q_{2} : r_{2}`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>` =\ :math:`p_{3} : q_{3} : r_{3}` (barycentrics) be three non-collinear points, none on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The locus of a point M such that the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of M and the triangle :g:`T <T>` = :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` are perspective, with perspector denoted by Z(M), is given by

  :math:`F(x,y,z) = (r_{3}`\ δ\ :sub:`32`\ :math:`y^{2}`-δ\ :sub:`23`\ :math:`q_{2}`\ :math:`z^{2})`\ x+(δ\ :sub:`31`\ :math:`r_{3}`\ :math:`x^{2}`-δ\ :sub:`13`\ :math:`p_{1}`\ :math:`z^{2})`\ y+(δ\ :sub:`21`\ :math:`q_{2}`\ :math:`x^{2}`-δ\ :sub:`12`\ :math:`p_{1}`\ :math:`y^{2})`\ z+(:math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`q_{3}`\ :math:`r_{1}`-:math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`q_{1}`\ :math:`r_{2})`\ xyz = 0 (1)

  where δ\ :sub:`ij` is the (i, j)-minor of the vertex matrix of the triangle :g:`T <T>`.

  If T and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective, then :math:`p_{2}`\ :math:`q_{3}`\ :math:`r_{1}` - :math:`p_{3}`\ :math:`q_{1}`\ :math:`r_{2}` = 0 and, if the equation (1) is non-degenerate, it represents a pivotal cubic with pole Ω(T) and pivot P(T) given by:

  | Ω(T) = :math:`p_{1}`\ δ\ :sub:`12`\ δ\ :sub:`13` : :math:`q_{2}`\ δ\ :sub:`21`\ δ\ :sub:`13` : :math:`r_{3}`\ δ\ :sub:`31`\ δ\ :sub:`12`
  | P(T) = δ\ :sub:`13`\ δ\ :sub:`32` : -δ\ :sub:`13`\ δ\ :sub:`31` : δ\ :sub:`31`\ δ\ :sub:`12`

  This section deals with the poles and pivots of these cubics and the perspectors Z(M) for most of the centers M lying on them.

.. _guide-preamble-0111:

* **X_8953**–**X_8998** — **Centers associated with quadsquare triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 21, 2015. "In every quadrilateral may be inscribed at least one square having a vertex on each of the four sides. If there is more than one such square in a given quadrilateral, there is an infinite number". Reference: Hebbert, C. M., *Annals of Mathematics*, Second Series, Vol. 16, No. 1/4 (1914 - 1915), pp. 38-42.

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane Π of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and let ϒ\ :sub:`A` = :g:`A_{C} <A_C>`\ :g:`A'_{B}A'_{C}A_{B} << A'_B A'_C A_B >>` be a square inscribed in the quadrilateral ABPC, with :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` on line :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`A'_{B} <A'_B>` on :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`A'_{C} <A'_C>` on :g:`PC <[ P C ]>`, and :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` on :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`. It is easy to prove, using homogeneous coordinates, that ϒ\ :sub:`A` is unique if P does not lie on the conic κ\ :sub:`A` given by the trilinear equation

  :math:`Sa^{2}`\ :math:`u^{2}` + :math:`bc(a^{2}` + S)vw + :math:`ca(b^{2}` + S)wu + :math:`ab(c^{2}` + S)uv = 0

  Note that :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` lie on κ\ :sub:`A`. Define κ\ :sub:`B` and κ\ :sub:`C` cyclically. If

  P ∈ Π - κ\ :sub:`A`\ ∪κ\ :sub:`B`\ ∪κ\ :sub:`C` (1),

  then there exist unique squares ϒ\ :sub:`A`, ϒ\ :sub:`B`, ϒ\ :sub:`C` inscribed in the quadrilaterals ABPC, BCPA, CAPB, respectively. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears) satisfies (1), then the vertices of ϒ\ :sub:`A` are as shown here:

  | :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` = (au + bv + cw)uS + (abv + :math:`S_{C}`\ u)\ :math:`cw : 0 : bvwS` + (bcv + :math:`S_{A}`\ w)au
  | :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` = (au + bv + cw)uS + (acw + :math:`S_{B}`\ u)bv : cvwS + (bcw + :math:`S_{A}`\ v)au : 0
  | :g:`A'_{B} <A'_B>` = u(auS + :math:`bS_{B}`\ v) : (S + :math:`S_{A})`\ auv + abcuw + (S + :math:`S_{C})`\ cvw : w(auS + :math:`bS_{B}`\ v)
  | :g:`A'_{C} <A'_C>` =\ :math:`u(auS + cS_{C}w) : v(auS + cS_{C}w) : abcuv` + (S + :math:`S_{A})`\ auw + (S + :math:`S_{B})`\ bvw

  If P lies on the side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then ϒ\ :sub:`A` is the **A-inner-inscribed square** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, as defined at `Mathworld: Inner Inscribed Squares Triangle <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/InnerInscribedSquaresTriangle.html>`__. The square ϒ\ :sub:`A` is here named here the **A-quadsquare triangle** of P. The sidelength of ϒ\ :sub:`A` is given by

  :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` = S\*Sqrt(abc(2\ :math:`uvw(aS_{A}`\ u+S(bv + cw)) + bc(v^2 w^2 + u^2 w^2 + u^2 v^2)a))/\|(au + cw)(au + bv)S + (avw + buw + cuv)abc\|

  Let :g:`O_{A} <O_A>`, :g:`O_{B} <O_B>`, :g:`O_{C} <O_C>` be the centers of the squares ϒ\ :sub:`A`, ϒ\ :sub:`B`, ϒ\ :sub:`C`, respectively. The triangle :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` is here named the **P-quadsquares triangle**. The vertex :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` are given by

  :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` = a(bcvw + 2Su^2) + (S + :math:`S_{B})`\ buv + (S + :math:`S_{C})`\ cuw : abcuw + (S + :math:`S_{A})`\ auv + (S + :math:`S_{C})`\ cvw : abcuv + (S + :math:`S_{A})`\ auw + (S + :math:`S_{B})`\ bvw,

  and cyclically for :g:`O_{B} <O_B>` and :g:`O_{C} <O_C>`.

  The P-quadsquares triangle is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for all P satisyfing (1). The perspector is given by

  Z(P) = u((S + :math:`S_{B})`\ bv + (S+\ :math:`S_{C})`\ cw) + abcvw : :

  The transformation P → Z(P) maps lines onto conics. For P on the Euler line, the locus of Z(P) is the conic through :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_485 <X_485>` and the vertices of the three inner-inscribed-squares triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0112:

* **X_8999**–**X_9111** — **Crossdifferences involving X_6**

  contributed by Peter J. C. Moses, December 28-31, 2015. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics) are points. It is well known that the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line :g:`PU <[ P U ]>`, given by barycentrics 1/(rv - qw) : 1/(pw - ru) : 1/(qu - sv) , lies on the circumconic with perspector P and on the circumconic with perspector U (e.g., the trilinear pole of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ U is the point 1/(v - w) : 1/(w - u) : 1/(u - v), on the Steiner circumellpse. If P lies on the circumcircle, then P is the trilinear pole of the line :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ Q, where :g:`Q <Q>` = :term:`crossdifference <crossdifference>` of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`; e.g., :ref:`X_99 <X_99>` = trilinear pole of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_524 <X_524>`, where :ref:`X_524 <X_524>` = crossdifference of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_512 <X_512>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0113:

* **X_9114**–**X_9117** — **Orthologic centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 5, 2016. Let :g:`L_{i} <L_i>` and :g:`G_{c} <G_c>` be the triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`, respectively, defined at X_9112, i.e., :g:`L_{i} <L_i>` is the equilateral triangle with **least** area inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`G_{c} <G_c>` is the equilateral triangle with **greatest** area circumscribed to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`G_{i} <G_i>` and :g:`L_{c} <L_c>` be the triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`, respectively, defined at X_9113, i.e., :g:`G_{i} <G_i>` is the equilateral triangle with **greatest** area inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`L_{c} <L_c>` is the equilateral triangle with **least** area circumscribed to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0114:

* **X_9118**–**X_9122** — **Loud centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 8, 2016. In 1891, Frank Herbert Loud published the following theorem:

  Let :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`, :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`, :math:`R_{1}`, :math:`R_{2}`, :math:`R_{3}` be nine distinct points on a cubic Ψ such that:

  | (1) :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>` are collinear on a line, :g:`L_{P} <L_P>`;
  | (2) :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :math:`R_{1}` are collinear on a line, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`;
  | (3) :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :math:`R_{2}` are collinear on a line, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`;
  | (4) :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`, :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`, :math:`R_{3}` are collinear on a line, :g:`L_{3} <L_3>`.

  Define :math:`S_{1}`, :math:`S_{2}`, :math:`S_{3}` and :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` as follows:

  | (i) :math:`S_{1}` = :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ :math:`R_{3}`\ ∩\ :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ :math:`R_{1}` and :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ :math:`R_{3}`\ ∩Ψ - {:g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :math:`R_{3}`}
  | (ii) :math:`S_{2}` = :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`\ :math:`R_{1}`\ ∩\ :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ :math:`R_{2}` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`\ :math:`R_{1}`\ ∩Ψ - {:g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`, :math:`R_{1}`}
  | (iii) :math:`S_{3}` = :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ :math:`R_{2}`\ ∩\ :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`\ :math:`R_{3}` and :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` = :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ :math:`R_{2}`\ ∩Ψ - {:g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :math:`R_{2}`}

  Then (a) the points :math:`S_{1}`, :math:`S_{2}` and :math:`S_{3}` are collinear (on a line :g:`L_{S} <L_S>` ); (b) the points :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` are collinear (on a line :g:`L_{T} <L_T>` ); and (c) the lines :g:`L_{P} <L_P>`, :g:`L_{S} <L_S>` and :g:`L_{T} <L_T>` concur.

  Reference: Loud F.H. "A theorem in plane cubics", *Annals of Mathematics*, Vol. 6, No. 1 (Jun., 1891), pp. 5-6

.. _guide-preamble-0115:

* **X_9123**–**X_9214** — **Parry triangles and associated centers**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, January 15, 2016. Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` be the intersection, other than :ref:`X_111 <X_111>`, of the Parry circle and the line A\ :ref:`X_111 <X_111>`, and define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` are cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`, here named the **1st Parry triangle**, is similar to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and orthogonal to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with similitude center :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the intersection, other than :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`, of the Parry circle and line A\ :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, here named the **2nd Parry triangle**, is similar to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and orthogonal to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with similitude center :ref:`X_111 <X_111>`. On the Parry circle, :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` are antipodes. The Euler line of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the Euler line of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, and the Brocard axis of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the Brocard axis of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`. The Brocard axis of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`, and also of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, is the Lemoine axis of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Let :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` be the intersection, other than :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, of the Parry circle and the :g:`A <A>`-median, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`, here named the **3rd Parry triangle**, is similar to the 4th Brocard triangle, with similitude center the intersection, other than :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, of the Parry circle and the orthocentroidal circle. Also, :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is the reflection of the circumsymmedial triangle of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` in the common Brocard axis of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` (which is also the Brocard axis of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`). The triangles :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` are perspective at :ref:`X_647 <X_647>`. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the reflection of the circumsymmedial triangle in the Brocard axis. Then :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is similar to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, with similitude center :ref:`X_111 <X_111>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0116:

* **X_9217**–**X_9461** — **Centers related to bicentric pairs**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>` - January 17, 2016 and January 19, 2016

.. _guide-preamble-0117:

* **X_9517**–**X_9582** — **Midpoints on the infinity line**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 11, 2016. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics) are distinct points on the line :g:`L <L>` at infinity; that is, p + q + r = 0 and u + v + w = 0. As in the definition of :term:`orthopoint <orthopoint>` (copied below from Glossary), P may be regarded as a "direction" in the plane of the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and all the (parallel) lines in this direction meet in :g:`P <P>`, and likewise for U. Let L(P) be any line that meets L in :g:`P <P>`, and let L(U) be any line that meets L in U. Let :g:`W_{1} <W_1>` and :g:`W_{2} <W_2>` be the angle bisectors of the angles between L(P) and L(U) at L(P)∩L(U). The midpoints of :g:`P <P>` and U are here defined as :g:`W_{1} <W_1>`\ ∩L and :g:`W_{2} <W_2>`\ ∩L. Since L(P) and L(U) are perpendicular lines, the two midpoints are a pair of orthopoints, defined in the Glossary of ETC.

.. _guide-preamble-0118:

* **X_9534**–**X_9715** — **Centers of similitude**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 27, 2016. The appearance of (Φ\ :sub:`2`, i, j) in the following lists means that the insimilcenter and the exsimilcenter of the circles Φ\ :sub:`1` and Φ\ :sub:`2` are X_i and X_j, respectively. (Followed by lists.)

.. _guide-preamble-0119:

* **X_9718**–**X_9721** — **Centers related to Dou circle**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 10, 2016. The Dou circle is defined in MathWorld as the circle cutting the sidelines of the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` so that angle(:g:`A'AA″ << A' A A″ >>`) = angle(:g:`B'BB″ << B' B B″ >>`) = angle(:g:`C'CC″ << C' C C″ >>`) = 90Âº. The center of the Dou circle is :ref:`X_155 <X_155>`.

  Let :math:`f(a,b,c) = (a^{2})[S_{A} (2 R^{2}-S_{A})` and :math:`g(a,b,c) = bc(S^{2}+S_{B} S_{C}-2 (S_{B}+S_{C}) R^{2})`. A trilinear equation for the Dou circle is then

  f(a,b,c)x^2 + f(b,c,a)y^2 + f(c,a,b)z^2 + g(a,b,c)yz + g(b,c,a)zx + g(c,a,b)xy = 0,

  and the radius-squared is (4\*R^6-S^2\*(5\*R^2-SW))/(4\*R^2-SW)^2.

  Let S = {circumcircle, nine-points-circle, orthocentroidal circle, orthoptic circle of the Steiner inellipse, polar circle (for obtuse :g:`ABC << A B C >>`), tangential circle, Taylor circle}, and suppose that :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` are in S. The radical circle of {U, V, Dou circle} is here named the Dow radical circle of :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>`, denoted by Dou(U,V). The center of Dou(U,V) is :ref:`X_2501 <X_2501>`, and the radius-squared of Dou(U,V) is the power of :ref:`X_2501 <X_2501>` with repect to :g:`U <U>` and V. Moreover, Dou(U,V) is orthogonal to the Dou circle and every circle in S. The Stevanovic circle is orthogonal to the Apollonius circle, Bevan circle, excircles-radical circle, as well as every circle in S except the Taylor circle. The radical axis of the Stevanovic and each Dou-radical circle is the Euler line, and their :term:`radical trace <radical-trace>` is :ref:`X_468 <X_468>`. If :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is acute then Dou(U,V) passes through X_5000 and X_5001.

.. _guide-preamble-0120:

* **X_9742**–**X_9775** — **Artzt triangle**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 25, 2016. The A-Artzt parabola of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the parabola tangent at :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` to the sidelines :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`, respectively. See William Gallatly, *The Modern Geometry of the Triangle,* 2nd ed. (London: Hodgson, 1913), p. 42.

  The A-Artzt parabola has trilinear equation :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`x^{2}` - 4bcyvz = 0. Its axis is the line :math:`a(b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})`\ x + :math:`b(a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` - :math:`3c^{2})`\ y - (:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`3b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})`\ cz = 0, and its directrix is the line (:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})`\ ax + :math:`2bc^{2}`\ y + :math:`2b^{2}`\ cz = 0.

  The B- and C-Artzt parabolas are defined cyclically. The foci of the three parabolas are the vertices of the :term:`2nd Brocard triangle <2nd-brocard-triangle>`.

  The :term:`trilinear poles <trilinear-pole>` of the directrices of the Artzt parabolas lie on the cubics K675 and K676.

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` bounded by the directrices of the Artzt parabolas is here named the **Artzt triangle**.

.. _guide-preamble-0121:

* **X_9776**–**X_9812** — **Conway triangle**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 2, 2016. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a a triangle with opposite sidelengths a,b,c, respectively. Let :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` be the point :g:`P <P>` on line :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` such that \|\ :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`\ \| = b and B lies between A and P. Define :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` and :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` cyclically. Likewise, let :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` be the point :g:`Q <Q>` on line :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` such that \|\ :g:`CP <[ C P ]>`\ \| = c and C lies between A and P. Define :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` and :g:`C_{B} <C_B>` cyclically. It is known that these six points lie on the Conway circle, with center :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` and radius-squared :math:`r^{2}` + :math:`s^{2}`, where r = inradius and s = semiperimeter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Let :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`B_{A}B_{C} <[ B_A B_C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C_{A}C_{B} <[ C_A C_B ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the **2nd Conway triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be the (1st) Conway triangle, introduced at X_7411, and let :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` be the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`; :g:`A' <A'>` = reflection of :g:`A″ <A″>` in :g:`A* <A*>`, and likewise for :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>`, as noted by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 2, 2016.

  | area(:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`) = 8Rs
  | \|\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`\ \| = sqrt(8\*\ :g:`S*R <[ S* R ]>`\ \*a/((s-b)\*(s-c)))
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = - (a + b + c) : a + b - c : a - b + c (barycentric coordinates)

  The vertices :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` lie on these cubics: K007 (Lucas cubic), K028, K461, K651.

  Another construction of :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` and :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` follows. Let :math:`p_{a}` be the parabola tangent to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` at the A-:term:`cevian <cevian>`-trace-of-:ref:`X_75 <X_75>` and also tangent to the sidelines :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`. :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` and :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` are the touchpoints of :math:`p_{a}` with :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`.

  :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`; it is also perspective with perspector :ref:`X_8 <X_8>` to these triangle: anticomplementary, Fuhrmann and outer-Garcia.

  :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :term:`Fuhrmann triangles <fuhrmann-triangle>` are inversely similar, with X_9782 as center of inverse similitude.

.. _guide-preamble-0122:

* **X_9813**–**X_9837** — **Submedial triangle and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 15, 2016. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, and suppose that :g:`C' <C'>` is a point on side :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and that :g:`B' <B'>` is a point on side :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`. Let r(:g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`) be the rectangle whose vertices are :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, and the orthogonal projections of :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` onto side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Let :math:`R_{A}` be the rectangle r(:g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`) of maximal area, which is obtained by taking :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` to be the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` be the center :math:`R_{A}`, and define :g:`O_{B} <O_B>` and :g:`O_{C} <O_C>` cyclically. The :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` is here named the **submedial triangle**; c.f. the Calabi triangle (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calabi_triangle).

  The :g:`A <A>`-vertex of :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` is given by

  :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` = 2\*a\*b\*c : (3\*a^2+b^2-c^2)\*c : (3\*a^2-b^2+c^2)\*b (trilinears)

  The vertices of the submedial triangle lie on the cubic K281, and

  | X_6688 = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-of-:g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>`
  | :ref:`X_3628 <X_3628>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>`
  | X_5462 = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-of-:g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>`

  The circumcircle of :g:`O_{A}O_{B}O_{C} << O_A O_B O_C >>` passes through these points: X_6667, X_6721, X_6722, X_6723, and the :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` is the radical center of the circumcircles of the rectangles :math:`R_{A}`, :math:`R_{B}`, :math:`R_{C}`.

.. _guide-preamble-0123:

* **X_9833**–**X_10000** — **Orthologic centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>` - April 28, 2016.

.. _preambles-part-6:

Part 6
------

.. _guide-preamble-0124:

* **X_10001**–**X_10014** — **Parallels-Conics and related points**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 2, 2016. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the line through a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) parallel to line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Let :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` = :g:`A' <A'>`\ ∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` = :g:`A' <A'>`\ ∩\ :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`. Define :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` and :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` cyclically, and define :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` and :g:`C_{B} <C_B>` cyclically. The six points :g:`A_{B} <A_B>`, :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, :g:`C_{A} <C_A>`, :g:`A_{B} <A_B>`, :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` lie on a conic, here called the parallels-conic of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by Cpar(P). The point :g:`P <P>` is here called the base-point of Cpar(P). The center of Cpar(P) is the point W(P) given by

  W(P) = p\*(:math:`p^{2}` - pq - pr - 2qr) : q\*(:math:`q^{2}` - qr - qp - 2rp) : r\*(:math:`r^{2}` - rp - rq - 2pq)

  The perspector of Cpar(P) is the point

  :g:`W* <W*>`\ (P) = p(2qr + 2pq + pr)(2qr + 2pr + pq) : q(2rp + 2qr + qp)(2rp + 2qp + qr) : r(2pq + 2rp + rq)(2pq + 2rq + rp)

  Cpar(P) is an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola according as P lies inside, on, or outside the Steiner inellipse.

  Let :g:`P' <P'>` be the reflection of :g:`P <P>` in W(P). Then :g:`P' <P'>` is the base-point of another conic, Cpar(:g:`P' <P'>`), also having center W(P). For example, if :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, then :g:`P' <P'>` = :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`.

  :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>` observes that W(P) is the midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`. (July 20, 2016)

  If P lies on the orthic axis, then Cpar(P) is a rectangular hyperbola, and the locus of W(P) as P traces the orthic axis a circular cubic.

.. _guide-preamble-0125:

* **X_10025**–**X_10030** — **H-transforms and K-transforms**

  , contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 13, 2016. Suppose that R =\ :math:`r : s : t` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics) are points not on a sideline of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let

  | :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line of the points :math:`0 : t : r` and :math:`- v : w : u`
  | :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` be the line of the points :math:`s : 0 : r` and :math:`v : - w : u`
  | :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` be the line of the points :math:`s : t : 0` and :math:`v : w : - u`
  | :g:`L'_{A} <L'_A>` be the line of the points :math:`0 : r : s` and :math:`- w : u : v`
  | :g:`L'_{B} <L'_B>` be the line of the points :math:`t : 0 : s` and :math:`w : - u : v`
  | :g:`L'_{C} <L'_C>` be the line of the points :math:`t : r : 0` and :math:`w : u : - v`

  The lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur in a point, P, and the lines :g:`L'_{A} <L'_A>`, :g:`L'_{B} <L'_B>`, :g:`L'_{C} <L'_C>` concur in a point, :g:`P' <P'>`. If R and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then P and :g:`P' <P'>` are a pair of :term:`bicentric points <bicentric-points>` and :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>` is a central line f\*x + g\*y + h\*z = 0, so that the point H(R,U) =\ :math:`f : g : h` is a triangle center, here introduced as the H-transform of R and U, given by first barycentric

  f = v\*w\*(u/r + v/s - w/t)(u/r - v/s + w/t) - u^2 (v/s + w/t - u/r)^2 .

  Next, let

  | :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line of the points :math:`0 : t : r` and :math:`- w : u : v`
  | :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` be the line of the points :math:`s : 0 : r` and :math:`w : - u : v`
  | :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` be the line of the points :math:`s : t : 0` and :math:`w : u : - v`
  | :g:`L'_{A} <L'_A>` be the line of the points :math:`0 : r : s` and :math:`- v : w : u`
  | :g:`L'_{B} <L'_B>` be the line of the points :math:`t : 0 : s` and :math:`v : - w : u`
  | :g:`L'_{C} <L'_C>` be the line of the points :math:`t : r : 0` and :math:`v : w : - u`

  The lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur in a point, P, and the lines :g:`L'_{A} <L'_A>`, :g:`L'_{B} <L'_B>`, :g:`L'_{C} <L'_C>` concur in a point, :g:`P' <P'>`. If R and U are triangle centers, then P and :g:`P' <P'>` are a pair of bicentric points and :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>` is a central line f\*x + g\*y + h\*z = 0, so that the point K(R,U) =\ :math:`f : g : h` is a triangle center, here introduced as the K-transform of R and U, given by first barycentric

  f = v\*w\*(u/t + w/s - v/r)(u/s + v/t - w/r) - u^2 (v/r + w/s - u/t)(v/t + w/r - u/s)

  Let G = centroid = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. Then :math:`H(G,P) = K(G`,P) and :math:`H(P,G) = K(P`,G) for all P. For fixed X, the locus of a point P satisfying :math:`H(P,X) = G is the circumconic with center X`. In particular, for :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_125 <X_125>`, the locus is the Jerabek hyperbola; for :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_115 <X_115>`, the Kiepert hyperbola; and for :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`, the Feuerbach hyperbola.

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r`, then :math:`H(P,P) = qr - p^{2}`: rp - :math:`q^{2}` : pq - :math:`r^{2}`, which is the Steiner-circumellipse-inverse of :g:`P <P>`.

  If P is on the circumcircle, then K(P,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) = :ref:`X_384 <X_384>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0126:

* **X_10037**–**X_10094** — **Inner- and outer- Yff triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 4, 2016. The Yff circles are the two triplets of congruent circles in which each circle is tangent to two sides of a reference triangle (see `Mathworld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/YffCircles.html>`__). The circles in each triplet have radius :math:`r_{1}`\ =r\*R/(R+r) and :math:`r_{2}`\ =r\*R/(R-r), respectively. The centers :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` for the :g:`A <A>`-circles of the first and second triplets have respective trilinear coordinates:

  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`\ = -(a^4-2\*(b^2+b\*c+c^2)\*a^2+(b^2-c^2)^2)/(2\*a^2\*b\*c) : 1 : 1
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`\ = +(a^4-2\*(b^2-b\*c+c^2)\*a^2+(b^2-c^2)^2)/(2\*a^2\*b\*c) : 1 : 1

  and cyclically :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` and :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` for the B- and C- circles.

  The triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` are known as the inner- and outer- Yff triangles, respectively.

.. _guide-preamble-0127:

* **X_10097**–**X_10103** — **Points associated with Dao circles**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, August 4, 2016, based findings of :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`. Suppose that P is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, but not on a sideline (:g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`). Let :g:`P' <P'>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P. Let (O) be the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let C(P) be the conic through :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`,\ :g:`P' <P'>`. Let :g:`D <D>` be the point in (O)∩C(P) other than :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`; let :g:`E <E>` be a point on (O), other than :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`D <D>`, and let :g:`E' <E'>` the point in :g:`DE <[ D E ]>`\ ∩C(P), other than D. The points :g:`P <P>`,\ :g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`E <E>`,\ :g:`E' <E'>` lie on a circle, here named the **Dao circle of P, denoted by D(P)**. The point :g:`E' <E'>` is here named the **1st (P,E)-Dao point.** (Based on "A generalization of the Sawayama-ThÃ©bault theorem", Dao Thanh Oai, July 21, 2016; `ADGEOM 3383 <http://www.adgeom.epizy.com/message.php?msg=3383>`__)

  Write :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics). Then C(P) is given by

  :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`p^{2}`\ x(y - z) + :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`q^{2}`\ y(z - x) + :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`r^{2}`\ z(x - y) = 0.

  The perspector of C(P) is

  :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`p(b^{2}`\ :math:`r^{2}` - :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`q^{2})` : :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`q(c^{2}`\ :math:`p^{2}` - :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`r^{2})` : :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`r(a^{2}`\ :math:`q^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`p^{2})`.

  The circle D(P) meets (O) in another point, the **2nd (P,E)-Dao point**, and D(P) meets C(P) in another point, the **3rd (P,E)-Dao point**. These points are represented by F and :g:`F' <F'>`, respectively, in the following examples.

  | Example 1. C(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) is the Jerabek conic. Taking :g:`E <E>` = :ref:`X_111 <X_111>` gives :g:`E' <E'>` = X_10097, :g:`F <F>` = X_5505, :g:`F' <F'>` = X_10098.
  | Example 2. Continuing with C(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`), take :g:`E <E>` = :ref:`X_98 <X_98>`. Then :g:`E' <E'>` = :ref:`X_879 <X_879>`, :g:`F <F>` = :ref:`X_67 <X_67>`, :g:`F' <F'>` = :ref:`X_935 <X_935>`.
  | Example 3. Continuing with C(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`), take :g:`E <E>` = :ref:`X_105 <X_105>`. Then :g:`E' <E'>` = X_10099, :g:`F <F>` = X_10100, :g:`F' <F'>` = X_10101; i.e. the 1st, 2nd, 3rd (:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_105 <X_105>`)-Dao points are :g:`E' <E'>`, :g:`F <F>`, :g:`F' <F'>`.
  | Example 4. 1st, 2nd, 3rd (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_112 <X_112>`)-Dao points are :ref:`X_25 <X_25>`, X_10101, X_10102.

.. _guide-preamble-0128:

* **X_10129**–**X_10136** — **ATFF points of pairs of triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, August 21, 2016, following the example at X_5643 contributed by :person:`Angel Montesdeoca <angel-montesdeoca>`. Suppose that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are distinct triangles in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The finite fixed point of the affine transformation that carries :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` onto :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named accordingly and is denoted by ATFF(:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`).

.. _guide-preamble-0129:

* **X_10137**–**X_10148** — **Hex2T circles**

  | contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 26, 2016. Suppose that :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are (central) triangles in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :g:`T' <T'>`-of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`
  | :g:`A_{a}A_{b}A_{c} << A_a A_b A_c >>` = :g:`T″ <T″>`-of-:g:`AB'C' << A B' C' >>`
  | :g:`B_{b}B_{c}B_{a} << B_b B_c B_a >>` = :g:`T″ <T″>`-of-:g:`A'BC' << A' B C' >>`
  | :g:`C_{c}C_{a}C_{b} << C_c C_a C_b >>` = :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`A'B'C << A' B' C >>`
  | Hex2T(:g:`T' <T'>`,\ :g:`T″ <T″>`) = hexagon with vertices :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`.

  For many choices of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`, the vertices of Hex2T(:g:`T' <T'>`,\ :g:`T″ <T″>`) lie on a conic and for a few of them the conic is a circle.

.. _guide-preamble-0130:

* **X_10153**–**X_10200** — **Centroidal conics and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 28, 2016. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be the reference triangle and :g:`U <U>`, :g:`V <V>`, :g:`W <W>` three points, at least two of them distinct, and let

  | :g:`G_{a} <G_a>` = centroid of AVW, and define :g:`G_{b} <G_b>` and :g:`G_{c} <G_c>` cyclically
  | :g:`G_{u} <G_u>` = centroid of :g:`UBC << U B C >>`, and define :g:`G_{v} <G_v>` and :g:`G_{w} <G_w>` cyclically.

  Then the six centroids lie on a (possibly degenerate) conic, and the triangles :g:`G_{a}G_{b}G_{c} << G_a G_b G_c >>` and :g:`G_{u}G_{v}G_{w} << G_u G_v G_w >>` are congruent and homothetic, and their homothetic center is the center of the conic.

  | The conic is here named the **UVW-centroidal conic** and also the **centroidal conic of UVW**. The triangles :g:`G_{a}G_{b}G_{c} << G_a G_b G_c >>` and :g:`G_{u}G_{v}G_{w} << G_u G_v G_w >>` are the **1st and 2nd UVW-centroidal triangles** and also the
  | 1st and 2nd centroidal triangles of :g:`UVW << U V W >>`.

  The center O(:g:`UVW << U V W >>`) of the centroidal-conic-of-:g:`UVW << U V W >>` is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` if :g:`U <U>`, :g:`V <V>`, :g:`W <W>` are either triangle centers or vertices of a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`. Such center is the centroid of the six centroids above specified.

.. _guide-preamble-0131:

* **X_10237**–**X_10259** — **Eulerologic centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 2, 2016. Let :g:`T' <T'>`\ = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be triangles. If the Euler lines of :g:`A'B″C″ << A' B″ C″ >>`, :g:`B'C″A″ << B' C″ A″ >>`, :g:`C'A″B″ << C' A″ B″ >>` concur, then the triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are **(T′, T″)-eulerologic** and the point of concurrence is here named the **(T′, T″)-eulerologic center**. (Definitions given by :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>` in `Anopolis 3841 <http://anopolis.epizy.com/message.php?msg=3841>`__).

  Note that the existence of the (:g:`T' <T'>`,\ :g:`T″ <T″>`)-eulerologic center does not imply the existence of a (:g:`T″ <T″>`,\ :g:`T' <T'>`)-eulerologic center.

  | Clearly, if two triangles have the same circumcircle then they are mutually eulerologic. Examples:
  | (1) The following triangles are inscribed in the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, so that each pair are mutually eulerologic: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, circummedial, circumorthic, 1st circumperp, 2nd circumperp, circumsymmedial, 3rd mixtilinear, 4th mixtilinear. The eulerologic center of each pair is :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`.
  | (2) The following triangles are inscribed in the nine-point circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, so that each pair are mutually eulerologic: Euler, 2nd Euler, 3rd Euler, 4th Euler, 5th Euler, Feuerbach, medial, orthic. The eulerologic center of each pair is :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0132:

* **X_10276**–**X_10281** — **Feuerbach quadrangle and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 17, 2016. Let :g:`F_{A} <F_A>`, :g:`F_{B} <F_B>`, :g:`F_{C} <F_C>` be the A-, B-, C- Feuerbach points of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, respectively (i.e., the touchpoints of the nine-points-circle and the excircles). Let :g:`F_{D} <F_D>`\ =\ :ref:`X_11 <X_11>` be the Feuerbach point of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The cyclic quadrangle :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>`\ ={:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`,\ :g:`F_{B} <F_B>`,\ :g:`F_{C} <F_C>`,\ :g:`F_{D} <F_D>`} is here named the **Feuerbach quadrangle of ABC**. The centroid of :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>` is X_10276. Properties:

  (1) A **maltitude** ("midpoint altitude") is a perpendicular drawn to a side of a quadrilateral from the midpoint of the opposite side. In a cyclic quadrilateral the four maltitudes concur at the `anticenter <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/Anticenter.html>`__. The anticenter of :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>` is X_10277.

  (2) In a cyclic quadrangle the centroids of the component triangles are the vertices of another cyclic quadrangle. For :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>` this last quadrangle has centroid coinciding with the centroid of :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>`.

  | (3) The diagonal triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` of :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>` has vertices with barycentric coordinates:
  | :g:`A* <A*>` = {:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`,\ :g:`F_{B} <F_B>`}∩{:g:`F_{C} <F_C>`,\ :g:`F_{D} <F_D>`} = -(SB-SC) : SA-SC : SA-SB
  | :g:`B* <B*>` = {:g:`F_{B} <F_B>`,\ :g:`F_{C} <F_C>`}∩{:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`,\ :g:`F_{D} <F_D>`} = SB-SC : -(SC-SA) : SB-SA
  | :g:`C* <C*>` = {:g:`F_{C} <F_C>`,\ :g:`F_{A} <F_A>`}∩{:g:`F_{B} <F_B>`,\ :g:`F_{D} <F_D>`} = SC-SB : SC-SA : -(SA-SB)
  | :g:`A* <A*>`, :g:`B* <B*>`, :g:`C* <C*>` lie all on the cubics K237, K238, K239, K672.
  | :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` has: area=area(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`)/2, centroid = X_10278 , circumcenter = X_10279, orthocenter = :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` and nine-point-center=X_10280

  | In terms of Chris van Tienhoven's `Encyclopedia of Quadri-Figures (EQF) <http://www.chrisvantienhoven.nl/index.php/mathematics/encyclopedia>`__, some centers of :g:`QA_{F} <[ Q A_F ]>` are:
  | :g:`QA <[ Q A ]>`-:g:`P_{1} <P_1>` = Quadrangle centroid = X_10276
  | :g:`QA <[ Q A ]>`-:g:`P_{2} <P_2>` = Euler-Poncelot point = X_10277 = common point of the nine-point-circles of the component triangles
  | :g:`QA <[ Q A ]>`-:g:`P_{3} <P_3>` = Gergonne-Steiner Point = :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` = common point of the midray-circles
  | The midray circles of the quadrangle {:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`,\ :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`,\ :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`,\ :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`} are the circumcircles of the triangles :g:`M_{ij}M_{ik}M_{il} << M_ij M_ik M_il >>`, for all combinations of (i,j,k,l) in {1,2,3,4}, where :g:`M_{ij} <M_ij>` = midpoint of {:g:`P_{i} <P_i>`,\ :g:`P_{j} <P_j>`}.

.. _guide-preamble-0133:

* **X_10290**–**X_10608** — **Points associated with mid-triangles and cross-triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, October 22, 2016. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>` (or a pair of bicentric triangles) in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  | Let :g:`A' <A'>` = midpoint of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` and :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the **mid-triangle** of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, denoted by MT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`).
  | Let :g:`A″ <A″>` = :g:`B_{1}C_{2} <[ B_1 C_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C_{1}B_{2} <[ C_1 B_2 ]>`, and :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named the **cross-triangle** of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, denoted by XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`).

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are homothetic, then both MT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) and XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) are homothetic to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are directly similar, then MT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is also directly similar to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, with the same center of similitude.

  If any pair in {:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`)} are perspective, then every pair in the set are perspective.

  If the vertices of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` lie on a conic, then XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is degenerate (consisting of 3 collinear points). If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are also perspective, XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) lies on the polar of the perspector wrt the conic. If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are the :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>`, resp., then XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is degenerate and collinear with :g:`P <P>` and Q.

  If the vertices of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` lie on the respective sidelines of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` (e.g., :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` lies on :g:`B_{1}C_{1} <[ B_1 C_1 ]>`)), then XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) = :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`.

  | For many choices of triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{3} <T_3>`,
  | (perspector of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and XT(:g:`T_{2} <T_2>`,\ :g:`T_{3} <T_3>`)) = (perspector of :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{3} <T_3>`)) = (perspector of :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` and XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`)).

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is the cevian triangle of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`Q <Q>`, then XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is collinear with these 3 points: P, P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`Q <Q>`, :g:`Q <Q>`-:term:`cross conjugate <cross-conjugate>` of P. Also, XT(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is perspective to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` at :g:`Q <Q>`.

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`, then XT(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`,\ :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`) is perspective to the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P* <P*>`, where :g:`P* <P*>` is the circumcircle-inverse of P. The perspector lies on the circumcircle.

  The cross-triangle of the :term:`cevian <cevian>` and anticevian triangles of :g:`P <P>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :g:`P <P>`.

  The cross-triangle of the cevian and circumcevian triangles of :g:`P <P>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at gcgP, where g = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` and c = :term:`complement <complement>`.

  The (degenerate) cross-triangle of the circumcevian triangles of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at Λ(gP, gQ). Also, the centroid of the (degenerate) cross-triangle of the anticevian triangles of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` is the tripolar centroid of the :term:`cevapoint <cevapoint>` of :g:`P <P>` and Q.

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, then the perspector of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and XT(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`,\ :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`) is the barycentric product :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`\ \*\ :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`\ \*\ :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0134:

* **X_10631**–**X_10682** — **Tri-equilateral triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 5, 2016. As with the Kenmotu squares, we inscribe in a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` **three congruent equilateral triangles** :g:`PA_{b}A_{c} << P A_b A_c >>`, :g:`PB_{c}B_{a} << P B_c B_a >>` and :g:`PC_{a}C_{b} << P C_a C_b >>`, with :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` on :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` on :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. There are two points P making possible this construction: :g:`P <P>` = :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`\ =\ :ref:`X_15 <X_15>` and :g:`P <P>` = :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`\ =\ :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`. The equilateral triangles obtained in each case are here named the **A-, B-, C- inner/outer equilateral triangles**, respectively.

  In each case, the points :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` are obviously concyclic. Their circles Γ\ :sub:`i` and Γ\ :sub:`o`, here named **the inner and outer tri-equilateral circles**, are denoted and determined as follows:

  | Γ\ :sub:`i`: center = :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, radius = 2\*R/\|\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ +cot(ω)\|
  | Γ\ :sub:`o`: center = :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`, radius = 2\*R/\|\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`-cot(ω)\|,

  where R and ω are the circumradius and the Brocard angle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, respectively.

* **X_10695**–**X_10705** — **Reflections of circumcircle-points in the incenter**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 10, 2016. Suppose that P is a point on the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = reflection of :g:`P <P>` in the incenter, I, of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.
  | :math:`P^{c}` = :term:`complement <complement>` of P
  | :math:`P^{a}` = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of P
  | :g:`P″ <P″>` = reflection of :ref:`X_8 <X_8>` in :math:`P^{c}`.

  Then

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = PI∩\ :math:`P^{c}`\ :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`
  | :g:`P' <P'>` = reflection of :ref:`X_8 <X_8>` in :math:`P^{c}`
  | :g:`P' <P'>` = midpoint of :ref:`X_145 <X_145>` and :math:`P^{a}`, where :ref:`X_145 <X_145>` = anticomplement of anticomplement of :g:`I <I>`.

* **X_10706**–**X_10720** — **Reflections of circumcircle-points in the centroid**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 8, 2016. Suppose that P is a point on the circumcrcle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = reflection of :g:`P <P>` in the centroid, G, of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`
  | :math:`P^{c}` = :term:`complement <complement>` of P
  | :math:`P^{a}` = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of :g:`P <P>`.

  Then

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = midpoint of G and :math:`P^{a}`
  | :g:`P' <P'>` = reflection of G in :math:`P^{c}`
  | :g:`P' <P'>` = {:math:`P^{c}`, :math:`P^{a}`}-harmonic conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.

* **X_10721**–**X_10727** — **Reflections of circumcircle-points in the orthocenter**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 9, 2016. Suppose that P is a point on the circumcrcle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 10, 2016. Suppose that P is a point on the circumcrcle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = reflection of :g:`O <O>` in :math:`P^{c}`.
