* **X_11147**–**X_11188** — **Points associated with the anti-Artzt triangle**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, December 8, 2016. The **anti-Artzt triangle**, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, is here introduced as the triangle of which :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the Artzt triangle. :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is also the anti-McCay triangle of the :term:`1st Brocard triangle <1st-brocard-triangle>`. :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :ref:`X_598 <X_598>` and homothetic to the Artzt triangle at :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is similar to the circumsymmedial triangle with similitude center :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`, and inversely similar to the 4th Brocard triangle with center of inverse similitude X_11187, to the 4th anti-Brocard triangle with center of inverse similitude :ref:`X_1995 <X_1995>`, and to the McCay and anti-McCay triangles with center of inverse similitude :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

  Barycentrics for the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of the anti-Artzt triangle are given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`b^{2}` + :math:`c^{2}` - :math:`5a^{2}` : :math:`4a^{2}` + :math:`4b^{2}` - :math:`2c^{2}` : :math:`4c^{2}` + :math:`4a^{2}` - :math:`2b^{2}`
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = SA - 2\*SC - 2\*SB : SA + SB + 4\*SC : SC + SA + 4\*SB

.. _guide-preamble-0144:

* **X_11189**–**X_11268** — **Centroids and circumcenters associated with central triangles**

  Suppose that G = centroid, and that T is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`. :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` has observed that the center of the centroidal conic of T (defined in the preamble to X_10153 is the midpoint of the segment from G(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) to G(T). Equivalently, G(T) is the reflection of G in the center of the conic.

.. _guide-preamble-0145:

* **X_11363**–**X_11536** — **Anti-triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 24, 2016. Several anti-triangles have been previously defined in ETC, including anti-Brocard triangles, anti-McCay and anti-Artzt. Associated with anti-triangles are composite triangles. For example, there are pairs of much-studied triangles whose composite is simply the reference triangle; e.g., the (2nd circumperp triangle of circumorthic triangle) = :g:`ABC << A B C >>`; and conversely, (circumorthic triangle of 2nd circumperp) = :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Further examples of such pairs include these:

  | 2nd circumperp, circumorthic
  | 2nd Euler, hexyl
  | excentral, orthic
  | Johnson, Johnson
  | intouch, tangential

.. _guide-preamble-0146:

* **X_11615**–**X_11633** — **Circles through X_111 and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 8, 2017. Sava Grozdev and Deko Dekov found, by using a computer program, 23 circles (21 of them distinct, 18 of them unnamed until now) all passing through the Parry center :ref:`X_111 <X_111>` (See `this reference <http://www.journal-1.eu/2016-1/Grozdev-Dekov-Parry-Point-pp.11-14.pdf>`__). These circles were verified algebraically and, in the following table, they are described together with their centers. (Followed by a table.)

.. _guide-preamble-0147:

* **X_11634**–**X_11644** — **Clifford(4) centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 9, 2017. Clifford's theorems, named after the English geometer William Kingdon Clifford, are a sequence of theorems relating to intersections of circles in general position.

  1st theorem: Given four circles :math:`d_{i}`, i=1..4, passing through a common point M, let :g:`P_{ij} <P_ij>` be the second intersection of :math:`d_{i}` and :math:`d_{j}`. Define the circles d':sub:`l`\ ={:g:`P_{ij} <P_ij>`, :g:`P_{jk} <P_jk>`, :g:`P_{ki} <P_ki>`} for l=1..4. Then these last four circles have a common point :g:`Q <Q>`, here denoted as the Clifford(4) center of circles :math:`d_{i}`.

  2nd theorem: Given five circles passing through a common point M, every subset of four of these circles determines a Clifford(4) center :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>` (by the first theorem). Then these five points :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>` lie on a circle S whose center will be denoted as the **Clifford(5) center** of the given circles.

  3rd theorem: Given six circles passing through a common point M, every subset of five circles determines a circle :math:`S_{i}` (by the 2nd theorem). Then these six circles have a common point, denoted here as the **Clifford(6) center** of the given circles.

  The sequence of theorems can be continued indefinitely. (References: `Mathworld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/CliffordsCircleTheorem.html>`__ and `Wikipedia <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clifford>`__).

.. _guide-preamble-0148:

* **X_11677**–**X_12691** — **Inner-Conway triangle and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 13, 2017. As a variant of the construction of the Conway circle at MathWorld `Conway circle <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/ConwayCircle.html>`__, define :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` inwards; i.e., :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` is on the ray :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`, and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` on the :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, with \|\ :g:`AA_{b} <[ A A_b ]>`\ \| = \|\ :g:`AA_{c} <[ A A_c ]>`\ \| = \|\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ \| = a.

  Construct :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` bounded by the lines :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`, :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>` is here named the **inner-Conway triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with :g:`A <A>`-vertex given by trilinears :g:`A' <A'>` = bc : (c - b)c : (b - c)b. (:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is also the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` of the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>`.)

.. _guide-preamble-0149:

* **X_11752**–**X_11791** — **Centers associated with the Przybyłowski-Bollin configuration**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 22, 2017. In connection with the Przybyłowski-Bollin configuration described at X_11753, there are four remarkable triangles. Two of them stem from :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, and the other two from :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`. For :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, the two triangles are denoted by AiBiCi, associated with the incenter, and :g:`A_{a}B_{b}C_{c} << A_a B_b C_c >>`, associated with the :g:`A <A>`-excenter. In order to write barycentrics for the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of each triangle, let

  :g:`U <U>` = Sqrt[2(a^2+b^2+c^2+2 :math:`\sqrt{3}` S)] = 2 Sqrt[SW+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}` S]. Then

  Ai = a^2 (:math:`\sqrt{3}` (-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) + 2 S) : b (:math:`\sqrt{3}` b (a^2 - b^2 + c^2) + 2 S (b + U)) : c (:math:`\sqrt{3}` c (a^2 + b^2 - c^2) + 2 S (c + U))

  :g:`A_{a} <A_a>` = a^2 (:math:`\sqrt{3}` (-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) + 2 S) : b (:math:`\sqrt{3}` b (a^2 - b^2 + c^2) + 2 S (b - U)) : c (:math:`\sqrt{3}` c (a^2 + b^2 - c^2) + 2 S (c - U))

  The triangles AiBiCi and :g:`A_{a}B_{b}C_{c} << A_a B_b C_c >>` are perspective, with perspector :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`.

  Let :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` = midpoint of Ai and :g:`A_{a} <A_a>`, and define :g:`O_{b} <O_b>` and :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` cyclically. The points Ai, :g:`A_{a} <A_a>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>` lie on a circle with center :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, and the triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` is perspective to the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` with X_11752 as perspector.

.. _guide-preamble-0151:

* **X_12064**–**X_12079** — **X-parabola and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 27, 2017. Let :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` be the side triangle of the medial and :term:`orthic triangles <orthic-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`. Then :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` lie on a parabola here named the **X-parabola of ABC**. Some properties of this parabola are:

  It has barycentric equation: (b^2-c^2)^2\*y\*z+(c^2-a^2)^2\*z\*x+(a^2-b^2)^2\*x\*y=0 It passes through the vertices of the :term:`antipedal triangle <antipedal-triangle>` of :ref:`X_477 <X_477>` and centers :ref:`X_476 <X_476>`, :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`, :ref:`X_685 <X_685>`, :ref:`X_850 <X_850>`, :ref:`X_892 <X_892>`, :ref:`X_2395 <X_2395>`, :ref:`X_2501 <X_2501>`, X_4024, X_4036, X_4581, X_4608, X_5466, X_8599, X_10412 and X_12079. Its directrix and the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are parallel, therefore its axis and the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perpendicular. Its 4th intersection with the circumcircles of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is :ref:`X_476 <X_476>` The focus and vertex are X_12064 and X_12065, respectively. Its axis is the line {523, 5972}, :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of X_12066. Its directrix is the line {30, 10279}, trilinear polar of X_12067. The perspector is :ref:`X_115 <X_115>` and the center is :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`. The dual conic of the X-parabola has center :ref:`X_620 <X_620>`, perspector X_4590 and passes through the vertices of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of X_4590 and centers :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`, :ref:`X_439 <X_439>`, :ref:`X_593 <X_593>`, :ref:`X_1509 <X_1509>`, :ref:`X_2482 <X_2482>`, :ref:`X_3926 <X_3926>`, X_4027, X_7058, X_7794, X_11128, X_11129.

  Let :math:`t_{a}`, :math:`t_{b}`, :math:`t_{c}` be the tangents to the X-parabola at :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, respectively; the triangle :g:`A_{t}B_{t}C_{t} << A_t B_t C_t >>` bounded by these tangents is here named the **X-parabola-tangential triangle of ABC**.

.. _guide-preamble-0156:

* **X_12835**–**X_12841** — **Centers associated with the ellipse IE59**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 29, 2017. Let IE59 denote the inellipse with perspector :ref:`X_59 <X_59>`. The center of IE59 is X_13006, and IE59 passes through X_i for these i:

  55, 56, 181, 202, 203, 215, 1124, 1335, 1362, 1397, 1672, 1673, 1682, 2007, 2008, 3235, 3236, 3237, 3238, 6056, 7005, 7006, 7066, 10799, 12835, 12836, 12837, 12838, 12839, 12840, 12841

  This ellipse IE59 is the locus of the centers of similtude (insimilicenter and exsimilicenter) of the incircle with Tucker circles. Also, IE59 intersects the incircle in :ref:`X_1362 <X_1362>` and three other points, so that the corresponding four Tucker circles are tangent to the incircle. The Tucker circle through :ref:`X_1362 <X_1362>` has the following parameter:

  arccos[(:math:`t^{2}` - :math:`s^{2})`/(:math:`t^{2}` + :math:`s^{2})`], where t = r + 4R.

  The centers of the other three Tucker circles are the extraversions of :ref:`X_970 <X_970>`, and they lie on the Brocard axis. Not only are these circle internally tangent to the incircle, but they are also externally tangent to the two corresponding excircles. In this section, the names for centers X_12835 to X_12841, the notation "Tucker (X,p)-circle" represents the Tucker circle with center X and parameter p.

  Let :math:`f(a,b,c,x,y,z) = b^{4}c^{4}(a - b - c)^{2}(b - c)^{4}x^{2} - 2a^{4}b^{2}c^{2}(a - b)^{2} (a - b + c)(c - a)^{2}(a + b - c)yz`. The ellipse IE59 is given by the barycentric equation f(a,b,c,x,y,z) + f(b,c,a,y,z,x) + :math:`f(c,a,b,z,x,y) = 0`.

  Possibly the earliest mention of IE59 occurs in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, page 238, in a list of inscribed ellipses; in that list, this ellipse is denoted by W(:g:`X_{11} <X_11>`).

.. _guide-preamble-0163:

* **X_13637**–**X_13721** — **Tri-squares triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, July 1, 2017, with notes by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 7, 2017. Inscribe three squares into a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` such that each square has two vertices on two distinct sides of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the other vertices of the three squares coincide at the vertices of another triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`. Let the squares be σ\ :sub:`a`\ =\ :g:`B' <B'>`:g:`C'A_{c}A_{b} << C' A_c A_b >>`, σ\ :sub:`b`\ =\ :g:`C' <C'>`:g:`A'B_{a}B_{c} << A' B_a B_c >>` and σ\ :sub:`c`\ =\ :g:`A' <A'>`:g:`B'C_{b}C_{a} << B' C_b C_a >>` with :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` on :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` on :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and centers :g:`A_{o} <A_o>`, :g:`B_{o} <B_o>`, :g:`C_{o} <C_o>`, respectively. This construction has four solutions. For each case, the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` will be named here the **tri-squares triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the triangle :g:`A_{o}B_{o}C_{o} << A_o B_o C_o >>` will be referred here as **tri-squares-central triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0166:

* **X_14030**–**X_14047** — **Moses-Euler Points**

  On July 21, 2017, :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` noted a relatively simple form for a point P(k) on the Euler line: P(k) = :math:`b^{4}` - :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`c^{2}` + :math:`c^{4}` + k\*(:math:`a^{4}` + :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`c^{2})` : : (barycentrics)

  The point is here named the **Moses-Euler Point (k = f)**, where f is a function of (a,b,c), homogeneous of degree 0. The point is given by the :term:`combo <combo>` P(k) = 3(k + 1)(:math:`a^{4}` + :math:`b^{4}` + :math:`c^{4})`\ \*\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` + 4(k - 1)\ :math:`S^{2}`\ \*\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0167:

* **X_14163**–**X_14164** — **Moses-Yff images**

  based on notes from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 30, 2017. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) lies on the circumcircle, then the following point, introduced here as the Moses-Yff image of :g:`P <P>`, lies on the Yff hyperbola:

  Y(P) = b^2 c^2 (a^4+a^2 b^2-2 b^4-2 a^2 c^2+4 b^2 c^2-2 c^4) (a^4-2 a^2 b^2-2 b^4+a^2 c^2+4 b^2 c^2-2 c^4) p-a^2 (2 a^4-a^2 b^2-b^4-a^2 c^2+2 b^2 c^2-c^4) (c^2 (-a^2 b^2+(a^2+b^2-c^2)^2) q+b^2 (-a^2 c^2+(a^2-b^2+c^2)^2) r) : : .

  For example, the Moses-Yff image of :ref:`X_110 <X_110>` is :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and that of :ref:`X_74 <X_74>` is :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0168:

* **X_14169**–**X_14188** — **Le Viet An equilateral triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 30, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and :g:`BCA' << B C A' >>`, :g:`CAB' << C A B' >>`, :g:`ABC' << A B C' >>` equilateral triangles erected out/in - wardly of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` be the circumcenters of :g:`CC'B << C C' B >>` and :g:`BB'C << B B' C >>`, respectively, and build :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` cyclically. Denote the circumcenters of :g:`B_{c}C_{b}A << B_c C_b A >>`, :g:`C_{a}A_{c}B << C_a A_c B >>`, :g:`A_{b}B_{a}C << A_b B_a C >>` as :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, :g:`O_{b} <O_b>`, :g:`O_{c} <O_c>`, respectively. Then, in each case, the triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` is equilateral. (See: `Hyacinthos 26551 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=26551>`__).

  | For :g:`BCA' << B C A' >>`, :g:`CAB' << C A B' >>`, :g:`ABC' << A B C' >>` built outwards :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` will be referred here as the **outer-Le Viet An triangle**.
  | This triangle has sidelength :g:`O_{b}O_{c} <[ O_b O_c ]>` = 4\*S^2\*\ :g:`R* <R*>`\ \|(SW+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S)/((sqrt (3)\*SA+S)\*(:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*SB+S)\*(sqrt (3)\*SC+S))\|.
  | :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` has coordinates: :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` = (SW+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S)\*a : (SB-SC)\*b : (SC-SB)\*c (trilinears)

  | For :g:`BCA' << B C A' >>`, :g:`CAB' << C A B' >>`, :g:`ABC' << A B C' >>` built inwards :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` will be referred here as the **inner-Le Viet An triangle**.
  | This triangle has sidelength :g:`O_{b}O_{c} <[ O_b O_c ]>` = 4\*S^2\*\ :g:`R* <R*>`\ \|(SW-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S)/((sqrt (3)\*SA-S)\*(:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*SB-S)\*(sqrt (3)\*SC-S))\|
  | :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` has coordinates: :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` = (SW-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S)\*a : (SB-SC)\*b : (SC-SB)\*c (trilinears)

  Both triangles are perspective to the anti-orthocentroidal triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0169:

* **X_14206**–**X_14213** — **Nguyen Images**

  :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, August 11, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, let :g:`L <L>` be the line through B orthogonal to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, let :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` be any point on :g:`L <L>`, and let :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` be the point such that :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`B_{C}C <[ B_C C ]>` is a rectangle. Likewise, let :math:`CC_{B}`\ :g:`C_{A}A <[ C_A A ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` and let :math:`AA_{C}`\ :g:`A_{B}B <[ A_B B ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the midpoint of :g:`B_{A}C_{A} <[ B_A C_A ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line through :g:`A' <A'>` perpendicular to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` and :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` cyclically. Nguyen Ngoc Giang found that the lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur.

.. _guide-preamble-0170:

* **X_14226**–**X_14245** — **Nguyen-Euler centers**

  :contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 4, 2017. This section is based on Nguyen Ngoc Giang's paper mentioned in the preamble just before X_14206. The paper appears in the `International Journal of Computer Discovered Mathematics <http://www.journal-1.eu/index.htm>`__, vol 2(2017), pp 135-140.

  Let :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`C_{A}C <[ C_A C ]>`, :math:`CC_{B}`\ :g:`A_{B}A <[ A_B A ]>`, :math:`AA_{C}`\ :g:`B_{C}B <[ B_C B ]>` be three rectangles built on the sides of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, such that \|\ :g:`BB_{A} <[ B B_A ]>`\ \|/a = \|\ :g:`CC_{B} <[ C C_B ]>`\ \|/b = \|\ :g:`AA_{C} <[ A A_C ]>`\ \|/c = λ = constant. Assume that λ %gt; 0 means that rectangles are built outwards from :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and λ < 0 means that rectangles are built inwards from :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Nguyen proved that if :g:`N_{A} <N_A>`, :g:`N_{B} <N_B>`, :g:`N_{C} <N_C>` are :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` (i.e., the nine-point-center) of triangles :g:`AB_{A}C_{A} << A B_A C_A >>`, :g:`BC_{B}A_{B} << B C_B A_B >>` and :g:`CA_{C}B_{C} << C A_C B_C >>`, respectively, then triangles :g:`N_{A}N_{B}N_{C} << N_A N_B N_C >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are orthologic.

  | In addition, it can be proved that if the three nine-point-centers (the N's) are replaced by any other point :g:`P <P>` on the Euler line such that (:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ P)\|/(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`) = (:g:`OP <[ O P ]>`)/(OH) = t, a constant invariant of (a,b,c), then the triangles :g:`P_{A}P_{B}P_{C} << P_A P_B P_C >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` remain orthologic. In this case, the orthologic center :g:`P_{A}P_{B}P_{C} << P_A P_B P_C >>` to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is:
  | :g:`X' <X'>` = (2\*a^6 - (b^2+c^2)\*(a^4+(b^2-c^2)^2))\*(3\*t-1)\*λ - 2\*\ :g:`S* <S*>`\ (a^2+b^2-c^2)\*(a^2-b^2+c^2) : : (barycentrics)
  | and the orthologic center :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to :g:`P_{A}P_{B}P_{C} << P_A P_B P_C >>`:
  | :g:`X″ <X″>` = 1/(((2\*a^4 + 2\*(b^2+c^2)\*a^2 + 4\*b^2\*c^2 - 4\*(b^2+c^2)^2)\*t + (a^2+b^2+c^2)\*(-a^2+b^2+c^2))\*λ + 2\*\ :g:`S* <S*>`\ (-a^2+b^2+c^2)) : : (barycentrics)

  The point :g:`X' <X'>` is here named the **Nguyen-Euler(λ) point of P**, and the point :g:`X″ <X″>`, the **Nguyen-Euler(λ) adjoint point of P**.

.. _guide-preamble-0171:

* **X_14272**–**X_14353** — **Triaxial points**

  : contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 6, 2017. "Let :g:`F_{1} <F_1>`, :g:`F_{2} <F_2>`, :g:`F_{3} <F_3>` be three figures in perspective two and two in the same plane, show that if they have a common centre of perspective, their three axes of perspective are concurrent." (Quoted from Lachlan, R.: *An Elementary Treatise on Modern Pure Geometry*, McMillan & Co., 1893, pp. 123). For three triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` satisfying the those conditions, the point of concurrence of the three axes is here named the **triaxial point of the triangles**.

.. _guide-preamble-0172:

* **X_14459**–**X_14478** — **Koutras-Hatzipolakis-Moses points**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 14, 2017. Following problem 1165a in Stathis Koutras's posting to `Romantics of Geometry <https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=1625848124155410&set=gm.1439118379535197&type=3&theater>`__, :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>` posed the following in `Hyacinthos 26601 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=26601>`__, September 12, 2017:

  | Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let
  | :g:`L_{AC} <L_AC>` = line through :g:`A <A>` parallel to line :g:`CP <[ C P ]>`, and define :g:`L_{BA} <L_BA>` and :g:`L_{CB} <L_CB>` cyclically
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{AC} <L_AC>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically
  | :g:`M_{A} <M_A>` = midpoint of :g:`A <A>` and :g:`A' <A'>`, and define :g:`M_{B} <M_B>` and :g:`M_{C} <M_C>` cyclically.
  | :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`AM_{C} <[ A M_C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically.
  | The points :g:`A* <A*>`, :g:`B* <B*>`, :g:`C* <C*>` are collinear (Koutras).

  | :g:`L_{AB} <L_AB>` = line through :g:`A <A>` parallel to line :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, and define :g:`L_{BC} <L_BC>` and :g:`L_{CA} <L_CA>` cyclically
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{AB} <L_AB>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically
  | :g:`N_{A} <N_A>` = midpoint of :g:`A <A>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`, and define :g:`N_{B} <N_B>` and :g:`N_{C} <N_C>` cyclically.
  | :g:`A* <A*>`\ \* = :g:`AN_{B} <[ A N_B ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B″C″ <[ B″ C″ ]>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>`\ \* and :g:`C* <C*>`\ \* cyclically.
  | The points :g:`A* <A*>`\ \*, :g:`B* <B*>`\ \*, :g:`C* <C*>`\ \* are collinear. (Hatzipolakis).

  What can be said about the point of intersection of the lines :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` and :g:`A* <A*>`\ \*\ :g:`B* <B*>`\ \*\ :g:`C* <C*>`\ \*? (Hatzipolakis)

  Peter Moses responds as follows. Write :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics). The point of intersection, here denoted by KHM(P), lies on the line P\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and is given by

  KHM(P) = :math:`p^{3}` - :math:`q^{3}` - :math:`r^{3}` + :math:`3p^{2}(q + r)` - 2qr(q + r) - pqr : :

  and by the following :term:`combo <combo>`:

  KHM(P) = 3 (:math:`p^{3}` + :math:`q^{3}` + :math:`r^{3}` + 2 (q r (q + r)+ r p (r + p) + p q (p + q) + 3 p q r))\*\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` - (p + q + r) (2 (:math:`p^{2}` + :math:`q^{2}` + :math:`r^{2})` + 5 (q r + r p + p q))\*P

.. _guide-preamble-0173:

* **X_14483**–**X_14488** — **Nguyen-Moses images**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 19, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, let :g:`L <L>` be the line through B orthogonal to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, let :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` be any point on :g:`L <L>`, and let :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` be the point such that :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`B_{C}C <[ B_C C ]>` is a rectangle. Likewise, let :math:`CC_{B}`\ :g:`C_{A}A <[ C_A A ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` and let :math:`AA_{C}`\ :g:`A_{B}B <[ A_B B ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line through :g:`A <A>` perpendicular to :g:`B_{C}C_{B} <[ B_C C_B ]>`, and define :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` and :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` cyclically. Starting with Nguyen Ngoc Giang's rectangles (as in the preamble just before X_14206), Peter Moses found that the lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur.

  Let :g:`U <U>` be the ratio of the height of the rectangle :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`B_{C}C <[ B_C C ]>` to the base; that is, :g:`U <U>` = \|\ :g:`BA_{B} <[ B A_B ]>`\ \|/a. Define :g:`V <V>` and :g:`W <W>` cyclically. The point :g:`X' <X'>` of concurrence is given by

  :g:`X' <X'>` = 1 / (-a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 2 S U) : : (barycentrics)

  If X is a point in the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then it has actual trilinear distances (possibly nonpositive) that are the heights of rectangles as in the above construction. Therefore, starting with :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics), we have :g:`U <U>` = kx/:math:`a^{2}`, where k = S/(x + y + z), and V = ky/:math:`b^{2}` and W = kz/:math:`c^{2}`. Consequently,

  :g:`X' <X'>` = a^2 / (a^2 (-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) + 2 S^2 x (x + y + z)) : :

  The point :g:`X' <X'>` is here named the **Nguyen-Moses image** of :g:`X <X>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0174:

* **X_14526**–**X_14527** — **Schiffler triange, Schiffler circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 23, 2017). Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the 1st Schiffler triangle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A_{a'} <A_a'>`, :g:`B_{b'} <B_b'>`, :g:`C_{c'} <C_c'>` be the orthogonal projections of :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>` on :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, :g:`C'A' <[ C' A' ]>`, :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`, respectively, and :g:`A'_{a} <A'_a>`, :g:`B'_{b} <B'_b>`, :g:`C'_{c} <C'_c>` the orthogonal projections of :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. These six points lie on a circle here named the **1st Schiffler circle**, with center X_14526 and squared radius ((9\*R+2\*r)\*R^2\*r^2+(R+2\*r)\*S^2)\*R/((R+2\*r)^2\*(3\*R+2\*r)^2). This circle passes through :ref:`X_11 <X_11>` and :ref:`X_1365 <X_1365>` and is the circumcircle of the :term:`pedal triangles <pedal-triangle>` of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` pair :ref:`X_35 <X_35>` and :ref:`X_79 <X_79>`.

  Next, if "1st Schiffler triangle" is replaced by "2nd Schiffler triangle", the resulting six points lie on a circle, here named the **2nd Schiffler circle**, with center :ref:`X_1737 <X_1737>` and squared radius R\*r^2/(R-2\*r). This circle passes through :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`, X_5532, X_13141, X_14027 and is the circumcircle of the pedal triangles of the isogonal conjugate pair :ref:`X_36 <X_36>` and :ref:`X_80 <X_80>`.

  Continuing, let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the 1st Schiffler triangle and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the 2nd Schiffler triangle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` be the orthogonal projections of :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` on :g:`B″C″ <[ B″ C″ ]>`, :g:`C″A″ <[ C″ A″ ]>`, :g:`A″B″ <[ A″ B″ ]>`, respectively, and :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` the orthogonal projections of :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` on :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, :g:`C'A' <[ C' A' ]>` and :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`. These six points :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` , :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` lie on a circle here named the **3rd Schiffler circle**, with center X_14527. This circle also passes through :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`.

  For definitions of Schiffler triangles, see See César Lozada, **Hyacinthos 26620** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html#S``)

.. _guide-preamble-0175:

* **X_14538**–**X_14541** — **Nguyen orthoimages**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 25, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, let :g:`L <L>` be the line through B orthogonal to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, let :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` be any point on :g:`L <L>`, and let :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` be the point such that :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`B_{C}C <[ B_C C ]>` is a rectangle. Likewise, let :math:`CC_{B}`\ :g:`C_{A}A <[ C_A A ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` and let :math:`AA_{C}`\ :g:`A_{B}B <[ A_B B ]>` be a rectangle with base :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`A_{B}C_{B} <[ A_B C_B ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{C}B_{C} <[ A_C B_C ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line through :g:`A' <A'>` orthogonal to line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` and :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` cyclically. Nguyen Ngoc Giang found that the lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur. See the preamble just before A(14206).

  Let :g:`U <U>` be the ratio of the height of the rectangle :math:`BB_{A}`\ :g:`B_{C}C <[ B_C C ]>` to the base; that is, :g:`U <U>` = \|\ :g:`BA_{B} <[ B A_B ]>`\ \|/a. Define :g:`V <V>` and :g:`W <W>` cyclically. Peter Moses found (September 23, 2017) that the point :g:`X' <X'>` of concurrence of the lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` is given by

  :g:`X' <X'>` = :math:`2a^{2}(a^{2} - b^{2} - c^{2})`\ :g:`UV <[ U V ]>` + :math:`2a^{2}(a^{2} - b^{2} - c^{2})`\ UW + (:math:`a^{2}` + :math:`b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})`\ (:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` + :math:`c^{2})`\ :g:`VW <[ V W ]>` : :

  If X is a point in the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then it has actual trilinear distances (possibly nonpositive) that are the heights of rectangles as in the above construction. Therefore, starting with :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics), we have :g:`U <U>` = kx/:math:`a^{2}`, where k = S/(x + y + z), and V = ky/:math:`b^{2}` and W = kz/:math:`c^{2}`. Consequently,

  :g:`X' <X'>` = :math:`2a^{2}`\ :math:`c^{2}(a^{2} - b^{2} - c^{2})`\ xy + :math:`2a^{2}`\ :math:`b^{2}(a^{2} - b^{2} - c^{2})`\ xz + :math:`a^{2}(a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2})`\ (:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` + :math:`c^{2})`\ yz : :

  :g:`X' <X'>` = :math:`a^{2}`\ (:math:`S_{B}`\ :math:`S_{C}`\ yz - :math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`S_{A}`\ xz - :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`S_{A}`\ xy : :

  | :g:`X' <X'>` = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-:term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of X
  | :g:`X' <X'>` = reflection-in-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>` of the isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the **X-Nguyen triangle**, and the point :g:`X' <X'>` is named the **Nguyen orthoimage** of :g:`X <X>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0176:

* **X_14649**–**X_14706** — **Singular Foci of Cubics**

  Let O(P) denote the orthopivotal cubic of a point :g:`P <P>`, as defined at `Orthopivotal cubics <http://bernard-gibert.fr/gloss/orthopivotalcubi.html>`__. Five points on this cubic are :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, and :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`. The singular focus of O(P), denoted by Psi(P) defines an involutory mapping P → Psi(P), and Psi(P) is called the Psi-transform of P. The centers X_14649-X_14706 involve these orthopivotal cubics for these points: X_14651, X_14656, X_14660, X_14704, X_14705, X_14706. The others involve circular cubics. See **Singular Focus of Circular Cubics in Bernard Gibert's CTC** (``SingularFocusOfCubics.html``).

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 10, 2017. The following table shows the ETC indexes of centers of conics circumscribing two or more :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>`. For definitions of triangles see the **Index of triangles referenced in ETC** (``www.faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

.. _guide-preamble-0178:

* **X_14782**–**X_14806** — **Involution and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 10, 2017. "When several pairs of points :g:`A <A>`, :g:`A' <A'>`; B, :g:`B' <B'>` ; C, :g:`C' <C'>` ; . . . lying on a straight line are such that their distances from a fixed point :g:`O <O>` are connected by the relations

  :g:`OA <[ O A ]>` .\ :g:`OA' <[ O A' ]>` = :g:`OB <[ O B ]>`.\ :g:`OB' <[ O B' ]>` = :g:`OC <[ O C ]>`.\ :g:`OC' <[ O C' ]>` = . . . ,

  the points are called a **range in involution**." (Lachlan, R.: *An Elementary Treatise on Modern Pure Geometry.* MacMillan & Co., 1893, chapter 5, pp. 37-41).

  A range in involution is denoted by {A, :g:`A' <A'>`}, {B, :g:`B' <B'>`}, {C, :g:`C' <C'>`}. The point :g:`O <O>`, collinear with the given points, is called the **center of involution** and each pair of corresponding points, as A and :g:`A' <A'>`, are said to be a **conjugate-couple**.

  To construct O, let {A, :g:`A' <A'>`}, {B, :g:`B' <B'>`} be two pairs of points on a straight line. Through :g:`A <A>` and :g:`B <B>` draw any two lines :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`BP <[ B P ]>` intersecting in :g:`P <P>` and through :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>` draw :g:`A'Q <[ A' Q ]>`, :g:`B'Q <[ B' Q ]>` parallel to :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` respectively, meeting in :g:`Q <Q>`. :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` meets :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` in :g:`O <O>`. (Proof in the above reference). From this construction, it is clear that two pairs of points are sufficient for determining the range unambigously and its notation can be shortened to {A, :g:`A' <A'>`}, {B, :g:`B' <B'>`}.
