.. _guide-preamble-0180:

* **X_14870**–**X_14889** — **Simpedal points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 19, 2017. "To determine a point P whose :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` with regard to a given triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` shall be similar to a given triangle :g:`A*B*C << A* B* C >>`\ \*". *(Johnson, Roger A.: Advanced Eucliden Geometry, Dover, New York, 1960, problem 205, pp. 142.)*

  Assume :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` are not inversely similar. For finding P, take any two points :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` on :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` and :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively, and build :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` directly similar to :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`. Then, through :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`\ =\ :g:`AA_{1} <[ A A_1 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, draw parallels to :g:`A_{1}B_{1} <[ A_1 B_1 ]>` and :g:`A_{1}C_{1} <[ A_1 C_1 ]>`, cutting :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` and :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` at :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`, respectively. The required P is the Miquel point of :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. (Proof in the cited reference).

  The point :g:`P <P>` and the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` will be named here the **simpedal point of A\*B\*C\* in ABC** and the **simpedal triangle of A\*B\*C\* in ABC**, respectively.

  Let :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`U_{A} <U_A>` : :g:`V_{A} <V_A>` : :g:`W_{A} <W_A>` (trilinears) and similarly :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>`. Let M be the trilinear matrix of :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` and :math:`m_{ij}` the (i, j)-minor of M. Denote δ\ :sub:`ij` = (-1)\ :sup:`i+j` :math:`m_{ij}`. Then,

  :g:`P <P>` = a (b δ\ :sub:`33` δ\ :sub:`21` (a^2 - b^2) + c δ\ :sub:`22` δ\ :sub:`31` (a^2 - c^2) + b c (b δ\ :sub:`32` δ\ :sub:`21` + c δ\ :sub:`23` δ\ :sub:`31`) - (δ\ :sub:`21` δ\ :sub:`31` + δ\ :sub:`22` δ\ :sub:`32` + δ\ :sub:`23` δ\ :sub:`33`) a b c + a δ\ :sub:`22` δ\ :sub:`33` (b^2 + c^2 - a^2))/(a :g:`U_{A} <U_A>` + b :g:`V_{A} <V_A>` + c :g:`W_{A} <W_A>`) : :

.. _guide-preamble-0181:

* **X_14941**–**X_14952** — **Brocard-Lemoine points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 24-27, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P any point in its plane (not on its sidelines) and :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` the traces of :g:`P <P>` on :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` be the points where :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` is cut by the parallel to :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` through :g:`B' <B'>` and the parallel to :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` through :g:`C' <C'>`, respectively. Build :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. Then lines :g:`AA_{b} <[ A A_b ]>`, :g:`BB_{c} <[ B B_c ]>`, :g:`CC_{a} <[ C C_a ]>` concur at a point :g:`W_{1} <W_1>` and lines :g:`AA_{c} <[ A A_c ]>`, :g:`BB_{a} <[ B B_a ]>`, :g:`CC_{b} <[ C C_b ]>` concur at a point :g:`W_{2} <W_2>`.

  | For :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears), :g:`W_{1} <W_1>` and :g:`W_{2} <W_2>` have trilinears as shown:
  | :g:`W_{1} <W_1>` =\ :math:`c/v : a/w : b/u`
  | :g:`W_{2} <W_2>` =\ :math:`b/w : c/u : a/v`

  Note that for :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :g:`W_{1} <W_1>` and :g:`W_{2} <W_2>` are the Brocard points of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  The previous construction is due to Lemoine as an attempt to generalize the Brocard geometry (Roger A. Johnson, *Advanced Eucliden Geometry*, Dover, New York, 1960, §499-500, pp. 299). Johnson writes, *these points have many properties resembling those of the Brocard points*.

  This preamble includes notes from :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0182:

* **X_14953**–**X_14966** — **Bicentrically induced harmonic conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 25, 2017. Using barycentric coordinates, suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` are a bicentric pair of points. Let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = line p\*x + q\*y + r\*z = 0
  | :g:`U' <U'>` = line u\*x + v\*y + w\*z = 0
  | :g:`L <L>` = a line
  | :g:`P* <P*>` = L∩\ :g:`P' <P'>`
  | :g:`U* <U*>` = L∩\ :g:`U' <U'>`
  | :g:`X <X>` = a point on L
  | :g:`X' <X'>` = (:g:`P* <P*>`,\ :g:`U* <U*>`)-harmonic conjugate of :g:`X <X>`, to be expressed as **L(P,U)-harmonic conjugate of X**

  If L is a central line and X is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, then :g:`X' <X'>` is a triangle center. For example, if X is on the Euler line, then :g:`X' <X'>` is on the Euler line, for every choice of bicentric pair (P,U), and the point :g:`X' <X'>` in this case is written as **Euler(P,U)-harmonic conjugate of X**. If X is on the Brocard axis, then :g:`X' <X'>` is written as **Brocard(P,U)-harmonic conjugate of X**.

.. _guide-preamble-0183:

* **X_15015**–**X_15142** — **Centers related to altimedial triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, October 27, 2017. The term **altimedial triangle** was introduced in `Hyacinthos 253 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=253>`__, by :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>`, January 30, 2000. A recap follows:

  | Let :g:`M_{A} <M_A>`, :g:`M_{B} <M_B>`, :g:`M_{C} <M_C>` be the midpoints of sides :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, resp.
  | Let :g:`H_{A} <H_A>`, :g:`H_{B} <H_B>`, :g:`H_{C} <H_C>` be the feet of the altitudes from :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, resp.

  The triangles :g:`H_{A}M_{C}M_{B} << H_A M_C M_B >>`, :g:`M_{C}H_{B}M_{A} << M_C H_B M_A >>`, :g:`M_{B}M_{A}H_{C} << M_B M_A H_C >>` are the A-, B- and C-altimedial triangles. Each is inversely congruent to the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` and inversely similar to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (with center of inverse similitude the respective vertex of the orthocentroidal triangle).

  The A-altimedial triangle has barycentric vertex matrix:

  | 0 : tan B : tan C
  | :math:`1 : 1 : 0`
  | :math:`1 : 0 : 1`

  The A-, B- and C-**anti-altimedial triangles**, :g:`A_{A}B_{A}C_{A} << A_A B_A C_A >>`, :g:`A_{B}B_{B}C_{B} << A_B B_B C_B >>`, :g:`A_{C}B_{C}C_{C} << A_C B_C C_C >>` are here introduced as the triangles of which :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the A-, B- and C-altimedial triangle, resp. To construct the A-anti-altimedial triangle, take :g:`A_{A} <A_A>` as the reflection of :g:`A <A>` in line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Then :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` is the reflection of :g:`A_{A} <A_A>` in :g:`B <B>`, and :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` is the reflection of :g:`A_{A} <A_A>` in C. The B- and C-anti-altimedial triangles are constructed cyclically. The anti-altimedial triangles are each inversely congruent to the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>` and homothetic to the respective altimedial triangle, with center of homothety the respective vertex of the orthocentroidal triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0184:

* **X_15254**–**X_15299** — **Perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 14, 2017. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be two perspective triangles such that neither is inscribed in the other. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A'C' <[ A' C' ]>`, and likewise for :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`. As :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` are perspective, the pairs of lines {:g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`}, {:g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`C'A' <[ C' A' ]>`} and {:g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`} concur at three collinear points, and the lines :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`, :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>` join opposite vertices of an hexagon. By Pascal's theorem, the six points lie on a conic, here named the **perspeconic** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0185:

* **X_15345**–**X_15349** — **Dao images**

  based on notes from :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, November 20, 2017. Let :g:`P <P>` be an arbitrary point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` be the centere of the circumcircle of :g:`BPC << B P C >>`. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line through :g:`O_{A} <O_A>` parallel to line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, and define :g:`L_{B} <L_B>` and :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` cyclically. The lines :g:`L_{A} <L_A>`, :g:`L_{B} <L_B>`, :g:`L_{C} <L_C>` concur in a point :g:`Q <Q>` = Q(P), here named the **Dao image of P**. (Dao Thanh Oai, November 20, 2017).

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), then

  :g:`Q <Q>` = p (c^2 q^2 + (-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) q r + b^2 r^2) (2 a^2 q r + p (-(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) p + (a^2 - b^2 + c^2) q + (a^2 + b^2 - c^2) r)) : :

  If P is on the circumconic Γ = {:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, P}, then Q is on the :term:`complement <complement>` of Γ. (:person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 23, 2017)

  The Dao image of :g:`P <P>` is the complement of the Kirikami-Euler image of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, December 2, 2017)

  The Dao image of :g:`P <P>` is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of the 2nd Vu point of :g:`P <P>`. (Randy Hutson, November 17, 2019)

.. _guide-preamble-0186:

* **X_15411**–**X_15423** — **Gibert-Simson Transforms**

  This section continues the section on Gibert-Simson transforms, :ref:`X_2394 <X_2394>`-:ref:`X_2419 <X_2419>`, with preamble just before :ref:`X_2394 <X_2394>`. See also :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`'s

.. _guide-preamble-0187:

* **X_15428**–**X_15445** — **Always-perspective triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 2, 2017. Centers :ref:`X_1601 <X_1601>`-:ref:`X_1634 <X_1634>` refer to perspectors of the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>` and the circumcevian triangle of an arbitrary point :g:`P <P>`. This section deals with the perspectivities between a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` and a triangle depending on P. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears) be a point not on the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and let the **reflections-of-P triangle** be the triangle whose vertices are the reflections of :g:`P <P>` in the lines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. The following pairs of triangle are perspective for all P: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3-reflections and antipedal-of-P:

  The perspector Q(P) of these triangles is given by trilinears

  Q(P) = b\*c\*(SA\*u^2\*(SB^2\*v^2+SC^2\*w^2)+a\*u\*v\*w\*(w\*b+v\*c)\*(S^2-2\*SB\*SC)-SB\*SC\*a^2\*v^2\*w^2)+(S^4-2\*SB\*SC\*(S^2+SA^2))\*u^2\*v\*w : : /

  Q(P) is the reflection in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the reflection in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` of the isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.

  If P is at infinity, Q(P) is the isogonal conjugate of the antipode of the isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.

  If P lies on the circumcircle and :g:`P' <P'>` = circumcircle-antipode of :g:`P <P>`, then Q(SR(:ref:`X_98 <X_98>`, P)) = SR(:ref:`X_98 <X_98>`, :g:`P' <P'>`), where SR(U,V) is the Simson-Rigby point of :g:`U <U>` and V. (See the preamble just before :ref:`X2677 <X_2777>` )

.. _guide-preamble-0188:

* **X_15535**–**X_15555** — **Lester-Moses Points**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 18, 2017. The Lester circle is the circle that passes through the points :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`, :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, andf :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`. See `MathWorld: Lester Circle <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/LesterCircle.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0189:

* **X_15607**–**X_15639** — **Centers related to some problems in chapter 7 of TCCT**

  : contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 22, 2017. This section refers to the general solutions to some selected problems in chapter 7 of :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, pp. 211-216.

  Problem 1:

  Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` be the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` be the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of any point P inside Δ\ :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Prove that the side-triangle of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is perspective to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and that the center of perspective lies on the nine-points-circle.

  | If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (trilinears) and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is the pedal triangle of :g:`P <P>`, then the perspector Q(P) is:
  | Q(P) = b\*c\*((b^2-c^2)\*u+a\*(b\*v-c\*w))\*(c\*(-c^2+a^2+b^2)\*v-b\*(-b^2+c^2+a^2)\*w) : : (trilinears)

  The perspector Q(P) is the same point on the nine-points-circle for every point on the line :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ P and it will be denoted here as the (7-1)-:cite:`TCCT <tcct>` image of the line :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ P .

.. _guide-preamble-0190:

* **X_15648**–**X_15669** — **Cross-perspeconics centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 28, 2017. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be two perspective triangles, neither inscribed in the other. Let

  1) :math:`a_{b}` = :g:`A_{1}B_{2} <[ A_1 B_2 ]>`, :math:`a_{c}` = :g:`A_{1}C_{2} <[ A_1 C_2 ]>`, :math:`b_{c}`\ = :g:`B_{1}C_{2} <[ B_1 C_2 ]>`, :math:`b_{a}` = :g:`B_{1}A_{2} <[ B_1 A_2 ]>`, :math:`c_{a}` = :g:`C_{1}A_{2} <[ C_1 A_2 ]>`, :math:`c_{b}` = :g:`C_{1}B_{2} <[ C_1 B_2 ]>`

  2) :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = :math:`a_{b}`\ ∩\ :math:`b_{c}`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = :math:`a_{c}`\ ∩\ :math:`c_{b}`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` = :math:`b_{c}`\ ∩\ :math:`c_{a}`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` = :math:`b_{a}`\ ∩\ :math:`a_{c}`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` = :math:`c_{a}`\ ∩\ :math:`a_{b}`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` = :math:`c_{b}`\ ∩\ :math:`b_{a}`

  Then the six points :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` lie on a conic, here named the cross-perspeconic of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0191:

* **X_15670**–**X_15723** — **Points on the Euler line, by combos**

  Certain points on the Euler line are easily represented as :term:`combos <combo>`, as defined in the Introduction, in Part 1. If :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` are points on the Euler line, then the points h P + k Q, where h and k are constants, comprise the **thinline** of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>`, denoted by TL(P,Q). Points X_15670-X_15680 are on TL(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_21 <X_21>`), and points X_15681-X_15723, X_15759, X_15764, X_15765 are on TL(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`).

  The Euler line contains infinitely many thinlines, all of which contain the point :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>` at infinity. Otherwise, distinct thinlines meet in at most one point.

  In general, if :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` are points, then many combos h P + k Q are composites of the midpoint and reflection operations. Let m = midpoint and r = reflection. Then

  | P + :g:`Q <Q>` = m(P,Q)
  | P - 2 :g:`Q <Q>` = r(P,Q)
  | 3 P + :g:`Q <Q>` = m(P,m(P,Q))
  | 3 P - :g:`Q <Q>` = m(r(Q,P)),P)
  | 3 P - 2 :g:`Q <Q>` = r(r(P,Q)),P)
  | 3 P - 4 :g:`Q <Q>` = r(P,r(P,Q))
  | 4 P - 5 :g:`Q <Q>` = r(r(Q,P),r(P,Q))
  | 5 P + 3 :g:`Q <Q>` = m(m(m(P,Q),r(Q,P)),Q)

  An open question is whether h\*P+k\*Q is such a composite for all choices h, k or integers (not both 0). Note that TL(P,Q) also contains points such as P + :math:`2^{1/2}`\ \*Q which is not such a composite.

.. _guide-preamble-0192:

* **X_15766** — **Euler lines and Brocard axis concurrences**

  :contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 02, 2018. Let r be the Euler line of Δ\ :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P a variable point. Let :math:`r_{a}`, :math:`r_{b}`, :math:`r_{c}` be the Euler lines of the **triangulation** of :g:`P <P>`, here defined as ordered triple (Δ\ :g:`PBC << P B C >>`, Δ\ :g:`PCA << P C A >>` and Δ\ :g:`PAB << P A B >>`) of triangles. Then, if P is on the Neuberg cubic, the four lines r, :math:`r_{a}`, :math:`r_{b}`, :math:`r_{c}` concur. Under the same conditions, the Brocard axes of Δ\ :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, Δ\ :g:`PBC << P B C >>`, Δ\ :g:`PCA << P C A >>` and Δ\ :g:`PAB << P A B >>` concur.

.. _guide-preamble-0193:

* **X_15808**–**X_15886** — **Tangential perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 8, 2018. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are two perspective triangles, neither inscribed in the other, then the six lines :g:`A'B″ <[ A' B″ ]>`, :g:`A'C″ <[ A' C″ ]>`, :g:`B'C″ <[ B' C″ ]>`, :g:`B'A″ <[ B' A″ ]>`, :g:`C'A″ <[ C' A″ ]>` and :g:`C'B″ <[ C' B″ ]>` are tangent to a unique conic, here named **the tangential perspeconic of A'B'C' and A"B"C"**.

  | Suppose the first triangle is the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the second is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics). Then :g:`XA' <[ X A' ]>`/:g:`XA <[ X A ]>` = λ\ :sub:`a`, :g:`XB' <[ X B' ]>`/:g:`XB <[ X B ]>` = λ\ :sub:`b` and :g:`XC' <[ X C' ]>`/:g:`XC <[ X C ]>` = λ\ :sub:`c`, where λ\ :sub:`a` = λ(a,b,c), λ\ :sub:`b` = λ(b,c,a), λ\ :sub:`c` = λ(c,a,b) and λ(a,b,c) is a degree-0 homogeneous function of a,b,c. In this case, the center Q of the tangential perspeconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is:
  | :g:`Q <Q>` = λ\ :sub:`a` (λ\ :sub:`b` λ\ :sub:`c` - 1) (y + z) + (λ\ :sub:`b` + λ\ :sub:`c` - 2) x : : (barycentrics)

.. _guide-preamble-0194:

* **X_15915**–**X_15928** — **Gamma-triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 20, 2018. The gamma triangle Γ(T) of a triangle :g:`T <T>` is defined as the triangle having vertices the :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of the :term:`orthopoints <orthopoint>` of the sidelines of :g:`T <T>`. (:cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, 6-46, pp. 178-179). From this definition, it is clear that every member of a set of homothetic triangles has the same gamma-triangle. It is proved in the given reference that if T is not a degenerated triangle then T and Γ(T) are similar. Their center of similitude will be named here as the **gamma-center of similitude of T**.

.. _guide-preamble-0195:

* **X_15995**–**X_15999** — **Points associated with the Garcia reflection triangle**

  This preamble is based on notes from several contributors named in the preamble. The Garcia :term:`reflection triangle <reflection-triangle>` is introduced here as follows. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the excenter of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the midpoint of segment :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. Let :g:`A* <A*>` be the reflection of :g:`A' <A'>` in :g:`A″ <A″>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. Emmanuel Jose Garcia conjectured that the triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`, here named the **Garcia reflection triangle,** is perspective to the outer-Garcia triangle. :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` proved (January 28, 2018) that the conjecture is true. He found barycentric coordinates:

  | :g:`A* <A*>` = a : c - a : b - a
  | :g:`B* <B*>` = c :math:`- b : b : a` - b
  | :g:`C* <C*>` = b - c : a - c : c

.. _preambles-part-9:

Part 9
------

.. _guide-preamble-0196:

* **X_16112**–**X_16162** — **2nd Fuhrmann triangle and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 13, 2018. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` be the midpoint of the arc :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` of its circumcircle not containing A. Define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is called the **Fuhrmann triangle of ABC**. (See :term:`Fuhrmann triangle <fuhrmann-triangle>` from `MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/FuhrmannTriangle.html>`__). The Furhrman triangle is the reflection of the 2nd circumperp triangle in the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the midpoint of the arc :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` containing A, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically.. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named the **2nd Fuhrmann triangle of ABC**. This triangle is the reflection of the 1st circumperp triangle in the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Its :g:`A <A>`-vertex has barycentric coordinates:

  :g:`A″ <A″>` = -a^2 : b\*c+a^2-c^2 : b\*c+a^2-b^2

  :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` has area :g:`S* <S*>`\ (2\*r+3\*R)/(4\*r), where r, R and S are the inradius, circumradius and double-area of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, respectively.

  The 2nd Fuhrmann triangle is perspective to triangles in the following list with perspector :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`: anti-Hutson intouch, anti-incircle-circles, 6th anti-mixtilinear, Ara, Ascella, 1st Brocard, 1st circumperp, 2nd circumperp, 1st Ehrmann, 2nd Euler, Fuhrmann, Johnson, inner-Johnson, outer-Johnson, Kosnita, McCay, medial, inner-Napoleon, outer-Napoleon, 1st Neuberg, 2nd Neuberg, tangential, Trinh, inner-Vecten, outer-Vecten. Also, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is perspective to the inner- and outer-Johnson triangles with perspectors X_16112 and X_12635, respectively.

.. _guide-preamble-0197:

* **X_16189**–**X_16220** — **Eulerologic centers 2**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 19, 2018. Eulerologic triangles and centers are defined in the preamble just before X10237.

.. _guide-preamble-0198:

* **X_16286**–**X_16302** — **Collineation images on the Euler line**

  A regular collineation m is defined by its action on four points, :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`, :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`, no three of which are collinear. Given four such points, let :g:`P_{k} <P_k>` = m(:g:`P_{k-4} <P_k-4>`) for k = 5,6,7,8. The eight points :g:`P_{k} <P_k>` determine m; conversely, given eight such points, a collineation m is uniquely determined. For every point :g:`X <X>`, the point m(X) is here called the (:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`, :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`; :g:`P_{5} <P_5>`, :g:`P_{6} <P_6>`, :g:`P_{7} <P_7>`, :g:`P_{8} <P_8>`) collineation image of :g:`X <X>`. (Regular collineations are discussed in :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, `Collineations, Conjugacies and Cubics <http://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2002volume2/FG200204.pdf>`__).

  Collineations map lines to lines. Thus, for example the collineation m indicated by (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`; :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`) maps the Nagel line, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, onto the Euler line, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. Examples of :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` m(X) found in this way are X_16286-X_16302. For more collineation images on the Euler line, see X_16342-X_16355, X_16367-X_16384, and X_16393-X_16458. See also the preamble just before X_16544.

.. _guide-preamble-0199:

* **X_16544**–**X_16614** — **Collineation images**

  This section follows the discussion of collineations just before X_16286. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` other than :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`) is a regular collineation, as is its inverse, given by (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`). The collineation images at X_16544-X_16576 result from :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>`, :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`. We write the image of X as m(X); let :math:`m^{-1}` denote the inverse collineation. Then centers X_16544-X_16576 are examples of m(X), and X_16577-X_16614 are examples of :math:`m^{-1}(X)`. Other examples are given by the following list . . .

.. _guide-preamble-0200:

* **X_16678**–**X_16759** — **Collineation images**

  This section follows the discussion of collineations just before X_16286, and especially just before X_16544. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` other than :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`) is a regular collineation, as is its inverse, given by (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`).

.. _guide-preamble-0201:

* **X_17043**–**X_17077** — **Collineation images**

  If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` other than :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`) is a regular collineation, as is its inverse, given by (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`). The collineation images at X_17043-X_17097 result from :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`. We write the image of X as m(X); let :math:`m^{-1}` denote the inverse collineation. Then centers X_17043-X_17073 are examples of m(X), and X_17074-X_17097 are examples of :math:`m^{-1}(X)`.

.. _guide-preamble-0202:

* **X_17134**–**X_17219** — **Collineation images**

  If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` other than :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`) is a regular collineation, as is its inverse, given by (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`). The collineation images at X_17134-X_17219 result from :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`. We write the image of X as m(X); let :math:`m^{-1}` denote the inverse collineation. Then centers X_17134-X_17166 are examples of m(X), and X_17167-X_17219 are examples of :math:`m^{-1}(X)`.

.. _guide-preamble-0203:

* **X_17227**–**X_17400** — **Moses points**

  Consider the set :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` having first barycentric of the form

  k(1)\*a^2 + k(2)\*(ab + ac) + k(3)(b^2 + c^2) + k(4)\*bc,

  where k(i) is in {-2,-1,0,1,2} for i = 1,2,3,4. There are 273 such centers, of which 99 are listed above. The remaining 174 appear below as X_17227 to X_17400, with names of the form MOSES (k(1),k(2),k(3),k(4)) POINT. Barycentrics contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 8, 2018.

  We refer to ordered tuples such as (k(1),k(2),k(3),k(4)) as the **Moses code** for a point :g:`X <X>`. If X has a first barycentric that is a polynomial in a,b,c, then the Moses notation can be generalized in a straightforward manner, as in X_17669-X_17698. The notation can also be extended to cover certain nonpolynomials; e.g. :ref:`X_615 <X_615>` can be coded as the Moses (1,0,0,0;-2S) point.

  Specifically, for :term:`polynomial centers <polynomial-center>` of degree 3, the Moses code is the 6-tuple (k(1),...,k(6)) of coefficients in

  k(1)\*a^3 + k(2)\*a^2\*(b + c) + k(3)\*a\*(b^2 + c^2) + k(4)\*a\*b\*c + k(5)\*(b^3 + c^3) + k(6)\*(b^2\*c + b\*c^2); see, for example, X_17591.

  For degree 5, the Moses code is the 12-tuple (k(1),...,k(12)) representing

  k(1)\*a^5 + k(2)\*a^4\*(b + c) + k(3)\*a^3\*(b^2 + c^2) + k(4)\*a^2\*b\*c + k(5)\*a^2\*(b^3 + c^3) + k(6)\*a^2\*(b^2\*c + b\*c^2) + k(7)\*a\*(b^4 + c^4) + k(8)\*a\*(b^3 c + b\*c^3) + a(9)\*a\*b^2\*c^2 + a(10)\*(b^5 + c^5) + a(11)(b^4 c + b\*c^4) + a(12)\*(b^3 c^2 + b^2 c^3); see for example, X_17787.

.. _guide-preamble-0204:

* **X_17410**–**X_17436** — **Homo-perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 10, 2018. *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be two not homothetic triangles. Let :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be any other triangle perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and homothetic to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`. Then the perspectors of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` lie on a fixed circumconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, March 17, 2018)*. (A proof of this theorem is given in **Homo-Perspeconics** (``Homo-Perspeconics.pdf``).)

  This circumconic is here named the **homo-perspeconic of A′B′C′ to ABC**. It is obvious that if two triangles are homothetic then their homo-perspeconics to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are the same.

  The following lists show triangles grouped by their homo-perspeconics to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`:

  | The homo-perspeconic of the following triangles to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the circumcircle: 1st Parry, 2nd Parry
  | The homo-perspeconic of the following triangles to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the Feuerbach hyperbola: Ascella, Atik, 1st circumperp, 2nd circumperp, inner-Conway, Conway, 2nd Conway, 3rd Conway, 3rd Euler, 4th Euler, excenters-midpoints, excenters-reflections, excentral, extouch, 2nd extouch, Fuhrmann, 2nd Fuhrmann, inner-Garcia, Garcia-reflection, hexyl, Honsberger, Hutson extouch, inner-Hutson, Hutson intouch, outer-Hutson, incircle-circles, intouch, inverse-in-incircle, 6th mixtilinear, 2nd Pamfilos-Zhou, 1st Schiffler, 2nd Schiffler, 1st Sharygin, tangential-midarc, 2nd tangential-midarc, Yff central
  | The homo-perspeconic of the following triangles to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the Kiepert hyperbola: anti-Artzt, 1st anti-Brocard, 6th anti-Brocard, anti-McCay, Artzt, 1st Brocard, 6th Brocard, inner-Fermat, outer-Fermat, 3rd Fermat-Dao, 4th Fermat-Dao, 7th Fermat-Dao, 8th Fermat-Dao, 11th Fermat-Dao, 12th Fermat-Dao, 15th Fermat-Dao, 16th Fermat-Dao, 1st isodynamic-Dao, 2nd isodynamic-Dao, 1st Lemoine-Dao, 2nd Lemoine-Dao, McCay, inner-Napoleon, outer-Napoleon, 1st Neuberg, 2nd Neuberg, 1st tri-squares-central, 2nd tri-squares-central, 1st tri-squares, 2nd tri-squares, 3rd tri-squares, 4th tri-squares, inner-Vecten, outer-Vecten
  | The homo-perspeconic of the following triangles to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the Jerabek hyperbola: anti-Ascella, 1st anti-circumperp, anti-Conway, 2nd anti-Conway, 3rd anti-Euler, 4th anti-Euler, anti-excenters-reflections, anti-Hutson intouch, anti-incircle-circles, anti-inverse-in-incircle, 6th anti-mixtilinear, anti-orthocentroidal, Aries, circumorthic, 1st Ehrmann, 2nd Ehrmann, 2nd Euler, extangents, 3rd Hatzipolakis, 1st Hyacinth, 2nd Hyacinth, intangents, 1st Kenmotu diagonals, 2nd Kenmotu diagonals, Kosnita, midheight, orthic, orthocentroidal, reflection, submedial, tangential, inner tri-equilateral, outer tri-equilateral, Trinh
  | The homo-perspeconic of the following triangles to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the Morley conic: (see X16271) 1st Morley, 2nd Morley, 3rd Morley, Roussel, Stammler

.. _guide-preamble-0205:

* **X_17438**–**X_17499** — **Collineation images**

  If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` other than :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P and U are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`) is a regular collineation, as is its inverse, given by (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`). The collineation images at X_17438-X_17499 result from :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`incentral triangle <incentral-triangle>`, :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`. We write the image of X as m(X); let :math:`m^{-1}` denote the inverse collineation. Then centers X_17438-X_17478 are examples of m(X), and X_17479-X_17499 are examples of :math:`m^{-1}(X)`.

.. _guide-preamble-0206:

* **X_17603**–**X_17668** — **Ursa-minor and Ursa-major triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 14, 2018. *Lemma: The internal tangents of two exterior circles touch them in four concyclic points. Also, the external tangents of two circles, none totally interior to the other, touch the circles in four concyclic points.*

  In a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the common internal tangents of the incircle and the :g:`A <A>`-excircle touch them in four concyclic points. Let {:math:`o_{a}`} be the circle through these touchpoints and denote as a′ the radical axis of {:math:`o_{a}`} and the incircle. Build b′ and c′ cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` bounded by a′, b′ and c′ will be named here the **Ursa-minor triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Continuing with the previous construction, let a″ be the radical axis of {:math:`o_{a}`} and the :g:`A <A>`-excircle and build b″ and c″ cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` bounded by a″, b″ and c″ will be named here the **Ursa-major triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  | A-vertices of both triangles have trilinear coordinates:
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = (b+c)\*a-(b-c)^2 : -(a-b+c)\*(a-c) : -(a+b-c)\*(a-b)
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = (b+c)\*(a^2+b^2+c^2)-2\*(b^2+c^2)\*a : -((a-b)^2+(2\*a-c)\*c)\*(a-c) : -((a-c)^2+(2\*a-b)\*b)\*(a-b)

.. _guide-preamble-0207:

* **X_17669**–**X_17698** — **Moses points on the Euler line**

  based on notes from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 14, 2018. Consider a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` X having first barycentric of the form

  k(1) a^4 + k(2) a^3 (b + c) + k(3) a^2 (b^2 + c^2) + k(4) a^2 b c + k(5) a (b^3 + c^3) + k(6) a(b^2 c + b c^2) + k(7) (b^4 + c^4) + k(8) (b^3 c + b c^3) + k(9) b^2 c^2,

  where k(i) is in {-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3} for k = 1, . . . , 9. Such a point :g:`X <X>` is here named the **MOSES (k(1), k(2), k(3), k(4), k(5), k(6), k(7), k(8), k(9)) POINT.** Extending the coding system introduced in the preamble just before X_17227, we refer to the 9-tuple (k(1),k(2),...,k(9)) as the **Moses code** for :g:`X <X>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0208:

* **X_17807**–**X_17850** — **Excosine triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 20, 2018. *If the tangents at :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` to the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` intersect at :g:`A' <A'>`, then the circle with center :g:`A' <A'>` passing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` is called A-excosine circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This circle cuts :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` again at two points which are the extremities of a diameter of it.*. (Reference: `Weisstein, Eric W. "Excosine Circle." From MathWorld <http://mathworld.wolfram.com/ExcosineCircle.html>`__)

.. _preambles-part-10:

Part 10
-------

.. _guide-preamble-0209:

* **X_18214**–**X_18261** — **Zaniah triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 01, 2018. In a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`A_{m}B_{m}C_{m} << A_m B_m C_m >>` be the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, I the incenter and :g:`A' <A'>` the touchpoint of the incircle with the side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Then the lines :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`IA_{m} <[ I A_m ]>` and :g:`B_{m}C_{m} <[ B_m C_m ]>` are concurrent at a point :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`. Denote :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is here named the **1st Zaniah triangle of ABC**.

  Continuing with the previous construction, let :g:`J_{a} <J_a>` be the :g:`A <A>`-excenter and :g:`A″ <A″>` the touchpoint of the :g:`A <A>`-excircle with the side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Then the lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`J_{a}A_{m} <[ J_a A_m ]>` and :g:`B_{m}C_{m} <[ B_m C_m ]>` are concurrent at a point :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`. Denote :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` is here named the **2nd Zaniah triangle of ABC.**

.. _guide-preamble-0210:

* **X_18300**–**X_18587** — **Triangles and centers related to the Ehrmann pivots**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 2, 2018. Let :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the triangle obtained by rotating :g:`ABC << A B C >>` about the 1st Ehrmann pivot, P(5), by an angle of 2π/3, so that :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` circumscribes :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Triangle :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` is here named the **1st Ehrmann circumscribing triangle**. Let :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be the triangle obtained by rotating :g:`ABC << A B C >>` about the 2nd Ehrmann pivot, U(5), by an angle of -2π/3, so that :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` circumscribes :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Triangle :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` is here named the **2nd Ehrmann circumscribing triangle**. :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` and :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` are inscribed in the Johnson circle (centered at :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`).

  Let :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>`\ =\ :g:`A'_{1}B'_{1}C'_{1} << A'_1 B'_1 C'_1 >>` be the triangle obtained by rotating :g:`ABC << A B C >>` about the 1st Ehrmann pivot, P(5), by an angle of -2π/3, so that :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>` is inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Triangle :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>` is here named the **1st Ehrmann inscribed triangle**. Let :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>`\ =\ :g:`A'_{2}B'_{2}C'_{2} << A'_2 B'_2 C'_2 >>` be the triangle obtained by rotating :g:`ABC << A B C >>` about the 2nd Ehrmann pivot, U(5), by an angle of 2π/3, so that :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>` is inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Triangle :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>` is here named the **2nd Ehrmann inscribed triangle**. :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>` and :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>` are inscribed in a common conic, here named the **Ehrmann conic**. The center of the Ehrmann conic is X_14993.

  The orthocenter of :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` is the circumcenter of :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>`, and is here introduced (and at **Bicentric Pairs** (``BicentricPairs.html``)) as **P(173)**. P(173) is therefore the intersection of the Euler lines of :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` and :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>`. The orthocenter of :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` is the circumcenter of :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>`, and is here introduced as **U(173)**. U(173) is therefore the intersection of the Euler lines of :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` and :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>`. PU(173) lie on the Hatzipolakis axis (line PU(5) or :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`\ \ :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`). The midpoint of PU(173) is :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`. P(173), :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` are the vertices of an equilateral triangle with center P(5). U(173), :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` are the vertices of an equilateral triangle with center U(5).

  The vertex-triangle of :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>` and :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>` is here named the **Ehrmann vertex-triangle**. The Ehrmann vertex-triangle is the :term:`Kosnita triangle <kosnita-triangle>` of the Johnson triangle (or equivalently, the reflection of the Kosnita triangle in :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`), and the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>` of the Ehrmann mid-triangle (defined below). The vertex-triangle of :g:`T_{I1} <T_I1>` and :g:`T_{I2} <T_I2>` is :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Let :g:`V_{A}V_{B}V_{C} << V_A V_B V_C >>` be the Ehrmann vertex-triangle. Then :g:`V_{A} <V_A>` is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`A'_{1} <A'_1>` wrt :g:`T_{C1} <T_C1>`, and the isogonal conjugate of :g:`A'_{2} <A'_2>` wrt :g:`T_{C2} <T_C2>`, and cyclically for :g:`V_{B} <V_B>` and :g:`V_{C} <V_C>`.

  | The :g:`A <A>`-vertex of the Ehrmann vertex-triangle has barycentric coordinates:
  | :g:`V_{A} <V_A>` = a^6 - a^4(b^2 + c^2) - a^2(b^4 + c^4) + (b^2 - c^2)^2(b^2 + c^2) : -(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)[(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2 - b^2c^2] : -(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)[(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2 - b^2c^2]

  The Ehrmann vertex-triangle is orthologic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with orthology center :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`.

  The Ehrmann vertex-triangle is Eulerologic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at X_7577.

  The Ehrmann vertex-triangle is perspective to the reflections-of-P triangle for all P.

.. _guide-preamble-0211:

* **X_18588**–**X_18752** — **Collineations inverse-images**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 4, 2018. Suppose that m is a collination. If :g:`P <P>` = m(Q), then P is the m collineation-image of :g:`Q <Q>`, as in the preambles just before X_16286 and X_16504, and Q is here named the **m inverse colllineation-image of P**. Explicitly, if :g:`P <P>` = (:g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`U <U>`; :g:`A″ <A″>`,\ :g:`B″ <B″>`,\ :g:`C″V <[ C″ V ]>`) collineation image of :g:`Q <Q>`, then :g:`Q <Q>` = (:g:`A″ <A″>`,\ :g:`B″ <B″>`,\ :g:`C″ <C″>`,V; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,c",U) collination inverse-image of :g:`P <P>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0212:

* **X_18810**–**X_18831** — **Perspectors of Inconics**

  | Based on notes from :person:`Thanh Oai Dao <dao-thanh-oai>`, May 17, 2018. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = reflection of :g:`P <P>` in :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically;
  | :g:`Q <Q>` = circumcenter of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`;
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = :g:`QA' <[ Q A' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically.
  | The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let D(P) denote the perspector. The points :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` are the foci of the inconic tangent to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` at :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`, respectively.

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), then D(P) = q r/(:math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`r^{2}`\ + :math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`q^{2}` + (:math:`b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2}` - :math:`a^{2})` q r) : : , and

  | D(P) = :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of (midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`)
  | D(P) = :term:`cevapoint <cevapoint>` of :g:`P <P>` and the orthocorrespondent of P
  | D(P) = :term:`cross conjugate <cross-conjugate>` of (midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`) and G
  | If P is on the infinity line, then D(P) = isotomic conjugate of P
  | If P on the circumcircle or infinity line, then D(P) lies on the Steiner circumellipse.
  | (:person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 21, 2018)

.. _guide-preamble-0213:

* **X_18840**–**X_18855** — **Dao-bipedal-perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 26, 2018. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P, Q two :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` points and :g:`P_{a}P_{b}P_{c} << P_a P_b P_c >>`, :g:`Q_{a}Q_{b}Q_{c} << Q_a Q_b Q_c >>` their respective :term:`pedal triangles <pedal-triangle>`. Let t be a real number, :g:`P'_{a} <P'_a>` the point on :g:`PP_{a} <[ P P_a ]>` such that :g:`PP'_{a} <[ P P'_a ]>`/:g:`PP_{a} <[ P P_a ]>`\ =t and :g:`Q'_{a} <Q'_a>` the point on :g:`QQ_{a} <[ Q Q_a ]>` such that :g:`QQ'_{a} <[ Q Q'_a ]>`/:g:`QQ_{a} <[ Q Q_a ]>`\ =t; define :g:`P'_{b} <P'_b>`, :g:`P'_{c} <P'_c>`, :g:`Q'_{b} <Q'_b>`, :g:`Q'_{c} <Q'_c>` cyclically. Denote :g:`A' <A'>`\ =\ :g:`PQ'_{a} <[ P Q'_a ]>` ∩ :g:`QP'_{a} <[ Q P'_a ]>` and similarly :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>`. Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective and, for given P, Q, the locus of the perspectors is a rectangular hyperbola. (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, May 22, 2018)

.. _guide-preamble-0214:

* **X_18859**–**X_18864** — **Circumperp conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 28, 2018. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P a point. The perpendicular bisectors of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` intersect the circumcircle at (:g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`), (:g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`), (:g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`) ,respectively. Then the circumcircles of :g:`PA_{1}A_{2} << P A_1 A_2 >>`, :g:`PB_{1}B_{2} << P B_1 B_2 >>`, :g:`PC_{1}C_{2} << P C_1 C_2 >>` are coaxial. (:person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>`, May 26, 2018, `Anopolis 7568 <https://groups.yahoo.com/neo/groups/Anopolis/conversations/messages/7568>`__)

  Let :g:`Q <Q>` be the point of intersection (other than P) of the three indicated circles. Then:

  :g:`Q <Q>` = reflection-in-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>` of (the circumcircle-inverse-of-P) :g:`Q <Q>` = circumcircle-inverse-of-(reflection-of-P in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`)

  | For P other than :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, the mapping P → Q is a conjugacy. The point :g:`Q <Q>` is here named the **Q=circumperp conjugate of P** (as :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` are the vertices of the circumperp triangles). For :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :math:`u:v:w` (trilinears), coordinates of Q(P) are:
  | Q(P) = (-a\*(-b\*c\*SC\*SB\*u^2+2\*w\*v\*SA^3)-SA\*a\*b\*c\*(b^2\*v^2+c^2\*w^2)+b\*((SA+SB)\*S^2-2\*SA\*SB^2)\*w\*u+c\*((SA+SC)\*S^2-2\*SA\*SC^2)\*u\*v)\*a : :

  Some properties: +

  Q(P) lies on the line :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ P If P lies on the circumcircle, then Q(P) = reflection of :g:`P <P>` in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, i.e, Q(P) is the antipode of :g:`P <P>` in the circumcircle. If P lies on the line at infinity, then Q(P) = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`

.. _guide-preamble-0215:

* **X_18909** — **Anti-triangles**

  | contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, June 4, 2018. Let :g:`T <T>`\ =\ :g:`A_{t}B_{t}C_{t} << A_t B_t C_t >>` be a triangle perspective and orthologic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Suppose :g:`P_{t} <P_t>` is the perspector (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`T <T>`) and :g:`O_{t} <O_t>` is the orthologic center :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to :g:`T <T>`, both expressed with respect to T. The anti-triangle-of-T is :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and, if T is taken as the reference triangle, then its anti-triangle :g:`T' <T'>`\ =\ :g:`A'_{t}B'_{t}C'_{t} << A'_t B'_t C'_t >>` is given by:
  | :g:`A'_{t} <A'_t>` = :g:`P_{t}A <[ P_t A ]>` ∩ (perpendicular to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` through :g:`O_{t} <O_t>`)
  | and cyclically for :g:`B'_{t} <B'_t>` and :g:`C'_{t} <C'_t>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0216:

* **X_19347**–**X_19511** — **Hutson triangles and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, June 10, 2018. The following triangles are referenced in ETC by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`: AAOA and AOA (in the preamble of X_15015 and 2nd anti-extouch, anti-tangential-midarc and Lucas(±1) antipodal tangents (at the preamble of X_18300). For definitions of these triangles, see **index of triangles referenced in ETC** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``). Centers X_19347-X_19511 are perspectors, homothetic centers, orthologic centers and parallelogic centers of these triangles and other triangles. For a complete list, see **X(19347)-Hutson-triangles.pdf** (``X(19347)-Hutson-triangles.pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0217:

* **X_19901**–**X_19926** — **Polar co-centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, June 26, 2018. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be two triangles not inscribed in the same circle and such that the perpendicular bisectors of :g:`A_{1}A_{2} <[ A_1 A_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{1}B_{2} <[ B_1 B_2 ]>` and :g:`C_{1}C_{2} <[ C_1 C_2 ]>` concur at a point :g:`O <O>`. The point O provides a common center for handling :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` in polar coordinates. In such cases, triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are called **polar co-centric** and the point :g:`O <O>` is here named the **polar co-center** of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0218:

* **X_21153**–**X_21168** — **Gibert-Moses Centroids**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 20, 2018. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not on one of the sidelines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let pK(K, P) denote the pivotal isocubic with pole K and pivot P (see `Bernard Gibert's Notations <http://bernard-gibert.fr/notations.html>`__. The cubic pK(K,P) intersects the circumcircle in :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>` and three other points, :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`. The centroid of {:g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`} is the point, here named the P-Gibert-Moses centroid, given by the :term:`combo <combo>` G(P) = 2\*\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` + P and

  :math:`G(P) = (b^{2} + c^{2} - a^{2)}(3a^{4} + b^{4} + c^{4} - 4 a^{2} b^{2} - 4 a^{2} c^{2} - 2 b^{2} c^{2})p - 2 a^{2} (q + r)`: :

.. _guide-preamble-0220:

* **X_21509**–**X_21543** — **Brocard-Euler points of type 1**

  Suppose that X is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and that X has barycentrics

  :math:`a^{2}(h a^{2} + k b^{2} + k c^{2})` : :math:`b^{2}(h b^{2} + k c^{2} + k a^{2})` : :math:`c^{2}(h c^{2} + k a^{2} + k b^{2})`,

  where h and k are symmetric functions of (a,b,c) having the same degree of homogeneity. Then X is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` that lies on the Brocard axis, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, and the point

  (:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`;\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) COLLINEATION IMAGE OF X

  lies on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This point is here named the **(h,k) Brocard-Euler point of type 1.** (For type 2, see the preamble just before X_21544.)

.. _guide-preamble-0221:

* **X_21544**–**X_21577** — **Brocard-Euler points of type 2**

  Suppose that X is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and that X has barycentrics

  :math:`a(h \cos A + k \sin A) : b(h \cos B + k \sin B) : c(h \cos C + k \sin C)`

  where h and k are symmetric functions of (a,b,c) having the same degree of homogeneity. Then X is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` that lies on the Brocard axis, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, and the point

  (:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`;\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) COLLINEATION IMAGE OF X

  lies on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This point is here named the **(h,k) Brocard-Euler point of type 2.** (For type 1, see the preamble just before X_21509.)

.. _guide-preamble-0222:

* **X_21616**–**X_21663** — **Wasat and anti-Wasat triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, August 27, 2018. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` its :term:`incentral triangle <incentral-triangle>` and (I) its incircle. Denote (:g:`O_{a} <O_a>`) the circle with diameter :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>` and :math:`r_{a}` the radical axis of (:g:`O_{a} <O_a>`) and (I) and cyclically (:g:`O_{b} <O_b>`), (:g:`O_{c} <O_c>`) and :math:`r_{b}`, :math:`r_{c}`. Let :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` be the triangle bounded by :math:`r_{a}`, :math:`r_{b}`, :math:`r_{c}`. Then: 1) :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` share the same nine-point-center; 2) the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` of :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`; and 3) the medial triangle of :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is the 3rd :term:`Euler triangle <euler-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. (See :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>`, `Hyacinthos #28081 <http://www.hyacinthos.epizy.com/message.php?msg=28081>`__). The triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is here named the **Wasat triangle of ABC**. For Wasat triangle:

  The Wasat triangle is also the extraversion triangle of :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`, the :term:`complement <complement>` of the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>`, the reflection of the 2nd circumperp triangle in :ref:`X_1125 <X_1125>`, and the mid-triangle of the Ursa-minor and Ursa-major triangles. Also, the anti-Wasat triangle is also the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>` of the orthic triangle, and the reflection of the circumorthic triangle in :ref:`X_389 <X_389>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, August 29, 2018)

  :g:`A* <A*>` = b+c : c-a : b-a (barycentrics) \|\ :g:`B*C* <[ B* C* ]>`\ \| = 2\*R\*cos(A/2) Area(:g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`) = (:g:`R* <R*>`/r)\*Area(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`)/2

.. _guide-preamble-0223:

* **X_22466**–**X_23047** — **Miscellaneous centers**

.. _guide-preamble-0224:

* **X_23097**–**X_23110** — **K244 Moses images**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, November 30, 2018. If a point :g:`P <P>` on the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` has barycentrics :math:`p : q : r`, then then point a^2 q r (c^2 q + b^2 r) : : lies on the cubic K244. The following fourteen examples of K244 Moses images were contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 13, 2018. See also the preamble just before X_23342. The Moses K244 image of :g:`P <P>` is the trilinear cube of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0225:

* **X_22291**–**X_23333** — **Anti-Ursa-minor triangle and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 17, 2018. The **anti-Ursa-minor triangle** of an acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` whose Ursa-minor triangle is :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` can be constructed as the anti-Hutson-:term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` of the :term:`Euler triangle <euler-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` has the following properties:

  :g:`A' <A'>` = b^2+c^2 : c^2-a^2 : b^2-a^2 (barycentrics) \|\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`\ \| = (a/4)\*\|sec(B)\*sec(C)\| area(:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`) = \|sec(A)\*sec(B)\*sec(C)\|\*area(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`)/8

.. _guide-preamble-0226:

* **X_23342**–**X_23351** — **K229 Moses images**

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point of the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`Q <Q>` be the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ P. Let :g:`X <X>` be the Q-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, so that also, :g:`X <X>` = :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of :g:`P <P>` and Q. Then X lies on the cubic K229. See also the preamble just before X_23097.

.. _guide-preamble-0227:

* **X_23352**–**X_23355** — **K635 Moses images**

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point of the circumconic with perspector :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`; that is, the circumconic with barycentric equation a y z + b z x + c x y = 0. Points on this conic include X_i for i = 88, 100, 162, 190, 651, 653, 655, 658, 660, 662, 673, 771, 799, 823, 897, 1156, 1492, 1821, 2349, 2580, 2581, 3257, 4598, 4599, 4604, 4606, 4607, 8052, 20332, as well as vertices of the Honsberger triangle (see X_7670 and the inner Conway triangle (see X_11677. Let :g:`Q <Q>` be the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ P, and let :g:`X <X>` be the Q-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, so that also, :g:`X <X>` = :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of :g:`P <P>` and Q. Then X lies on the cubic K635. See also the preambles just before X_23097 and X_23342.

.. _guide-preamble-0228:

* **X_23582**–**X_23594** — **Points associated with barycentric squares of lines (inscribed ellipses)**

  Several weeks before the appearance of this preamble on September 29, 2018, :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, and independently, :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, developed the notion of (pointwise) squares and cubes of points on lines, and they computed examples found below. Centers X_23582-X_23594 were contributed by Kimberling and Moses, and X_23962-X_24041 by Hutson. The latter are in two groups: X_23962-X_23992 (barycentrc squares) and X_23993-X_24041 (trilinear) See the preambles just before X_23962 and X_23993.

  Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`L <L>` be the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of :g:`P <P>`, so that L meets the sidelines in :math:`0 : q : -r`, :math:`-p : 0 : r`,\ :math:`p : -q : 0`. The barycentric squares of these points are the points :g:`A' <A'>` = 0 : q^2 : r^2, :g:`B' <B'>` = p^\ :math:`2 : 0 : r`\ ^2, :g:`C' <C'>` = p^2 : q^2 : 0. The perspector of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the barycentric square P^2 = p^2 : q^2 : r^2, so that P^2 is the perspector of the inellipse that is the locus of squares of points on L. The center of the ellipse is the point p^2 (q^2 + r^2) : q^2 (r^2 + p^2) : r^2 (p^2 + q^2), which is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of P^2, as well as the :term:`complement <complement>` of the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of P^2. The ellipse is here named the **barycentric square of L.**

.. _guide-preamble-0229:

* **X_23606**–**X_23616** — **Points associated with pointwise barycentric cubes of lines**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 23, 2018. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`L <L>` be the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of :g:`P <P>`, and let :g:`X <X>` be a point on L. The locus of a point X^3 (barycentric cube) is a cubic curve, here named the **pointwise barycentric cubic** of L. Let :math:`f(p,q,r,x,y,z) = q^{9}r^{9}x^{3} + 3p^{9}q^{3}r^{3}yz(q^{3}z+r^{3}y)`. An equation for the cubic follows:

  f(p,q,r,x,y,z) + f(q,r,p,y,z,x) + f(r,p,q,z,x,y) - 21 (p q r)\ :sup:`3`\ x y z = 0.

  An equivalent equation is (p^3 x + q^3 y + r^3 z)^3 - 27 p^3 q^3 r^3 x y z = 0.

  If :g:`L <L>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` (the Euler line), then :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_648 <X_648>`, and the cubic passes through the points X_i for i = 2, 3081, 6524, 23606, 23607, 23608, 23609.

  If L is the line at infinity, then :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and the cubic is K656, which passes through X_i for i = 2, 3081, 6545, 8017, 8028, 8029, 8030, 8031, 8032, 23610, 23611, 23612, 23613, 23614, 23615, 23616.

.. _guide-preamble-0230:

* **X_23870**–**X_23888** — **Points on the infinity line**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 27, 2018. Suppose that a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is given by :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics). The **infinite difference point of P** is introduced here as the point given by D(P) = q - r : r - p : p - q.

.. _guide-preamble-0231:

* **X_23962**–**X_23992** — **Points associated with barycentric squares of lines (inscribed ellipses)**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, September 29, 2018 Continuing from the preamble before X_23582, let :g:`L <L>` be a line in the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of L. Let :g:`E <E>` be the inellipse that is the (pointwise) barycentric square of L. The :term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of the foci of :g:`E <E>` is the point a^2 p^2 : b^2 q^2 : c^2 r^2. Let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` be points on L so that U^2 and X^2 lie on E. The trilinear pole of the tangent to :g:`E <E>` at U^2 is the barycentric product :g:`P*U <[ P* U ]>` = p\*u : q\*v : r\*w, which lies on the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of the Brianchon point (perspector) of E. The intersection of the tangents to :g:`E <E>` at U^2 and X^2 is the barycentric product :g:`U*X <[ U* X ]>` = u\*x : v\*y : w\*z.

.. _guide-preamble-0232:

* **X_23993**–**X_24041** — **Points associated with trilinear squares of lines (inscribed ellipses)**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, September 29, 2018. The following discussion is analogous to the preambles just before X_23582 and X_23962. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinears) is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`L <L>` be the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of :g:`P <P>`, so that L meets the sidelines in :math:`0 : q : -r`, :math:`-p : 0 : r`,\ :math:`p : -q : 0`. The trilinear squares of these points are the points :g:`A' <A'>` = 0 : q^2 : r^2, :g:`B' <B'>` = p^\ :math:`2 : 0 : r`\ ^2, :g:`C' <C'>` = p^2 : q^2 : 0. The perspector of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the trilinear square P^2, so that P^2 = p^2 : q^2 : r^2 is the perspector of the inellipse that is the locus of squares of points on L. The center of the ellipse is the point p^2(q^2 + r^2) : q^2(r^2 + p^2) : r^2(p^2 + q^2), which is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of P^2, as well as the :term:`complement <complement>` of the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of P^2. The ellipse is here named the **trilinear square of L**.

  Let :g:`E <E>` be the inellipse that is the trilinear square of L. The :term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of the foci of :g:`E <E>` is the point a^2 p^2 : b^2 q^2 : c^2 r^2. Let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` be points on L so that U^2 and X^2 lie on E. The :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the tangent to :g:`E <E>` at U^2 is the trilinear product :g:`P*U <[ P* U ]>` = p\*u : q\*v : r\*w, which lies on the trilinear polar of the Brianchon point (perspector) of E. The intersection of the tangents to :g:`E <E>` at U^2 and X^2 is the trilinear product :g:`U*X <[ U* X ]>` = u\*x : v\*y : w\*z.

.. _preambles-part-13:

Part 13
-------

.. _guide-preamble-0233:

* **X_24307**–**X_24309** — **Perspectors involving obverse triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 3, 2018. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The **obverse triangle of P** is here introduced as the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, where :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`p : r : q`, :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`r : q : p`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`q : p : r`. If P is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, then the obverse triangle of :g:`P <P>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0234:

* **X_24310**–**X_24312** — **Perspectors involving N-obverse triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 3, 2018.

  Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The **N-obverse triangle of P** is here introduced as the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, where :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`- p : r : q`, :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`r : - q : p`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`q : p : - r`. If P is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, then the obverse triangle of :g:`P <P>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0235:

* **X_24477**–**X_24481** — **Centers associated with the obverse and N-obverse triangles of X_1**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, October 5, 2018. Obverse and N-obverse triangles are introduced in preambles just before X_24307 and X_24310.

.. _guide-preamble-0236:

* **X_24482**–**X_24518** — **Collineation mappings involving trilinear obverse triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 5, 2018. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Trilinears for :g:`P <P>` are :math:`p/a : q/b : r/c`. The **trilinear obverse triangle of P** is here introduced as the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, where :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`p/a : r/c : q/b`, :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`r/c : q/b : p/a`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`q/b : p/a : r/c` (trilinears). The same triangle is given by barycentrics :g:`A' <A'>` = b c p : b^2 r : c^2 q, :g:`B' <B'>` = a^2 r : c a q : p c^2 p, :g:`C' <C'>` = a^2 q : b^2 p : a b r. For example, the trilinear obverse triangle of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` has first barycentric b c : b^2 : c^2.

.. _guide-preamble-0237:

* **X_24519**–**X_24536** — **Collineation mappings involving trilinear N-obverse triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 5, 2018., contributed by Clark Kimberling, October 5, 2018.Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Trilinears for :g:`P <P>` are :math:`p/a : q/b : r/c`. The **trilinear N-obverse triangle of P** is here introduced as the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, where :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`- p/a : r/c : q/b`, :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`r/c : - q/b : p/a`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`q/b : p/a : - r/c` (trilinears). The same triangle is given by barycentrics :g:`A' <A'>` = - b c p : b^2 r : c^2 q, :g:`B' <B'>` = a^2 r : - c a q : p c^2 p, :g:`C' <C'>` = a^2 q : b^2 p : - a b r. For example, the trilinear obverse triangle of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` has first barycentric - b c : b^2 : c^2.

.. _guide-preamble-0238:

* **X_24537**–**X_24571** — **Collineation mappings involving Gemini triangle 1**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 6, 2018.

  Following is a list of :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>`, by barycentric coordinates of :g:`A <A>`-vertex. The full names are Gemini triangle 1, Gemini triangle 2, Gemini triangle 3, etc. (*Gemini* is a constellation of stars - and the Latin noun for *twin*.) These triangles are cited in the sequel.

  | Gemini 1 a : b + c : b + c
  | Gemini 2 - a : b + c : b + c

  | Gemini 3 a : a + b : a + c
  | Gemini 4 - a : a + b : a + c

  | Gemini 5 a : a - b : a - c
  | Gemini 6 a : b - a : c - a

  | Gemini 7 a : a - c : a - b
  | Gemini 8 a : c - a : b - a (Garcia :term:`reflection triangle <reflection-triangle>`)

  | Gemini 9 a : b + c - a : b + c - a
  | Gemini 10 - a : b + c - a : b + c - a

  | Gemini 11 a : a + b + c : a + b + c
  | Gemini 12 - a : a + b + c : a + b + c

  | Gemini 13 b +\ :math:`c : a : a`
  | Gemini 14 b +\ :math:`c : 2a : 2a`

  | Gemini 15 b +\ :math:`c : b : c` (Gergonne line extraversion triangle; see X_10180. See note below.)
  | Gemini 16 b +\ :math:`c : c : b` (See note below.)

  | Gemini 17 b + c : b - c : c - b (See note below.)
  | Gemini 18 b + c : c - b : b - c (See note below.)

  | Gemini 19 b + c : a + b : a + c (See note below.)
  | Gemini 20 2b +\ :math:`2c : a : a` (See note below.)

  | Gemini 21 a + b +\ :math:`c : a : a`
  | Gemini 22 a + b +\ :math:`c : - a : - a`

  | Gemini 23 a + b + c : b + c : b + c
  | Gemini 24 a + b + c : - b - c : - b - c

  | Gemini 25 a + b + c : a + b : a + c
  | Gemini 26 a + b + c : a + c : a + b

  | Gemini 27 a - b :math:`- c : a : a`
  | Gemini 28 a - b - c : b + c : b + c (See note below.)

  | Gemini 29 a : b - c : c - b (See note below.)
  | Gemini 30 a : c - b : b - c (Inner Conway triangle; see note below.)

  | Gemini 31 b c : a^2 : a^2
  | Gemini 32 - b c : a^2 : a^2

  | Gemini 33 a^2 : b c : b c
  | Gemini 34 - a^2 : b c : b c

  | Gemini 35 cos :math:`A : 1 : 1`
  | Gemini 36 - cos :math:`A : 1 : 1`

  | Gemini 37 sec :math:`A : 1 : 1`
  | Gemini 38 - sec :math:`A : 1 : 1`

  | Gemini 39 -a + b + c : a + b + c : a + b + c
  | Gemini 40 a + b + c : - a + b + c : - a + b + c

  | Notes: (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, beginning November 9, 2018)
  | (Gemini triangle 15) = :term:`complement <complement>` of :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :ref:`X_75 <X_75>`
  | (Gemini triangle 16) = complement of :term:`incentral triangle <incentral-triangle>`
  | (Gemini triangle 17) = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of cevian triangle of :ref:`X_75 <X_75>`
  | (Gemini triangle 17) = anticomplement of anticomplement of Gemini triangle 15
  | (Gemini triangle 18) = anticomplement of incentral triangle
  | (Gemini triangle 19) = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of obverse triangle of :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`
  | (Gemini triangle 19) = obverse triangle of :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`
  | (Gemini triangle 20) = complement of Gemini triangle 28
  | (Gemini triangle 23) = complement of Gemini triangle 39
  | (Gemini triangle 28) = anticomplement of Gemini triangle 20
  | (Gemini triangle 29) = anticomplement of :term:`extouch triangle <extouch-triangle>`
  | (Gemini triangle 29) = anticomplement of anticomplement of 1st Zaniah triangle
  | (Gemini triangle 30) = anticomplement of :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`
  | (Gemini triangle 30) = anticomplement of anticomplement of 2nd Zaniah triangle
  | (Gemini triangle 33) = :term:`unary cofactor triangle <unary-cofactor-triangle>` of 2nd Sharygin triangle
  | (Gemini triangle 34) = unary cofactor triangle of 1st Sharygin triangle
  | (Gemini triangle 39) = anticomplement of Gemini triangle 23

  For more Gemini triangles, see the preambles just before X_26153 and X_27378.

  If T is a central triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` with :g:`A' <A'>` of the form :math:`f(a,b,c) : g(a,b,c) : g(a,b,c)`, then the (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) collineation image of the Euler line is the Euler line. Examples include Gemini triangles 1,2,9,10,11,12,13,14,21,22,23,24,27,28, and 31-40.

  Let m(X) denote the (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) collineation image of :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, where :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = Gemini triangle 1, as in centers X_24537-X_24571. Then

  m(X) = a (a + b - c)(a - b + c) x + (b + c - a) (a + b - c) (a + c) y + (b + c - a) (a - b + c) (a + b) z : : ,

  and m(X) is on the Euler line if and only if X is on the Euler line.

* **X_24973**–**X_24980** — **4th intersections of inconics and the circumcircles of their polar triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, October 11, 2018. Let :g:`E <E>` be an inconic (other than the incircle) with Brianchon point (perspector) P. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the polar triangle of :g:`E <E>`, which is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. Let :g:`O* <O*>` be the circumcircle of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` (i.e., the :term:`cevian <cevian>` circle of :g:`P <P>`). E and :g:`O* <O*>` intersect in 4 points: :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` and a 4th intersection which is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`. The appearance of (E,i,\ :g:`O* <O*>`,j) in the following list means that inconic E with perspector X_i intersects circle :g:`O* <O*>` (other than at :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`) at X_j:

  | (Brocard inellipse, 6, symmedial circle, **24973**)
  | (incentral inellipse, 1, incentral circle, 23063)
  | (Kiepert parabola, 99, 2nd Steiner circle, **24974**)
  | (Lemoine inellipse, 598, 3rd Lemoine circle, 20383)
  | (MacBeath inconic, 264, MacBeath circle, **24977**)
  | (Mandart inellipse, 8, Mandart circle, 11)
  | (orthic inconic, 4, nine-point circle, 125)
  | (Steiner inellipse, 2, nine-point circle, 115)
  | (Yff parabola, 190, cevian circle of :ref:`X_190 <X_190>`, **24979**)

.. _guide-preamble-0254:

* **X_25045**–**X_25050** — **Points associated with a family of ellipses**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 10, 2018. Let :g:`E <E>` be the circumellipse with center :ref:`X_141 <X_141>`, given by

  a^2 (b^2 + c^2) y z + b^2 (c^2 + a^2) x z + c^2 (a^2 + b^2) x y = 0.

  This ellipse is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of the de Longchamps line, and it passes through X_i for i = 67, 110, 660, 670, 694, 1634, 4553, 4576, 8050, 20021.

  For arbitrary fixed nonzero constant k, let E(k) be the ellipse obtained from E by dilation from :ref:`X_141 <X_141>` with ratio k; then E(k) is given by

  (b^2 + c^2) ((a^2 + b^2) (a^2 + c^2) k^2 - b^2 c^2) x^2 + 2 (a^2 b^2 c^2 + (b^2 + c^2) (c^2 + a^2) (a^2 + b^2) k^2) y z + (cyclic) = 0.

  The major axis of every E(k) passes through X_i for i = 6, 1344, 2574, 8105, 9173, 13414, and the minor axis, through X_i for i = 6, 1345, 2575, 8106, 9174, 13415, 14899. The two axes are parallel to the Simson lines of :ref:`X_1113 <X_1113>` and :ref:`X_1114 <X_1114>`.

  These ellipses are associated with a problem in navigation posed by William Lionheart (see the link at :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`), in connection with the fact that if a point P moves on E(k), the sum of squared distances from :g:`P <P>` to the sidelines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` stays constant. The value of the constant is

  (a^2 b^2 c^2 + (b^2 + c^2) (c^2 + a^2) (a^2 + b^2) k^2) / (4 (a^2 + b^2 + c^2) R^2).

  Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` is a point on the circumcircle. Then the point

  LM(P,k) = (b^2 + c^2) k ((2 a^2 + b^2 + c^2) p + (-a^2 - c^2) q + (-a^2 - b^2) r) - a^2 ((b^2 + c^2) p + (c^2 + a^2) q + (a^2 + b^2) r) : :

  is on the ellipse E(k). The point LM(P,k) is here named the **Lionheart-Moses k-image** of P. Centers X_25045-X_25050 are examples of such images, for k = 1, as are :ref:`X_3448 <X_3448>`, X_11061, X_25332, and X_25333; see also X_25314-X_25336.

Extending the preambles just before X_24537 and X_26153, let m(X) denote the (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) collineation image of :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, where :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = Gemini triangle 48, as in centers X_26653-X_26699. Then

  m(X) = a^2 (b + c - a) x + (a - b + c) (a - c)^2 y + (a + b - c) (a - b)^2 z : : ,

.. _guide-preamble-0295:

* **X_26700**–**X_26717** — **Circumcircle-X-antipodes**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (definitions and presentation) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (formulas and centers), November 2, 2018. Let C(P) be the circumconic with perspector :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), and let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`F <F>` =\ :math:`f : g : h` be distinct points, with :g:`U <U>` on C(P). Let :g:`U* <U*>` be the point, other than U, that lies on C(P) and on the line :g:`FU <[ F U ]>`. Then

  :g:`U* <U*>` = u^2 q r (h v p + f w q + f v r) (g w p + f w q + f v r) : :

  If :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, then C(P) is the circumcircle; in this case, the point :g:`U* <U*>` is here named the **circumcircle-F-antipode of U**, given by

  :g:`U* <U*>` = b^2 c^2 u^2 (a^2 h v + b^2 f w + c^2 f v)(a^2 g w + b^2 f w + c^2 f v) : :

  Note that the circumcircle-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-antipode of :g:`U <U>` is the ordinary antipode of :g:`U <U>`.

  This preabmle continues with lists of examples, bypified by these:

  Circumcircle-:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`-antipodes: {74, 26700}, {99, 741}, {100, 106}, {101, 105}, {102, 108}, {103, 934}, {104, 109}, {107, 26701}{110, 759}, {111, 8691}, {112, 26702}, ...

  Circumcircle-:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-antipodes: {74, 1302}, {98, 110}, {99, 111}, {100, 105}, {101, 675}, {102, 9056}, {103, 9057}, {104, 9058}, {106, 9059}, {107, 1297}, {108, 26703}, {109, 1311}, {112, 2373}, {476, 842}, {477, 9060}, ...

  Circumcircle-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-antipodes: {74, 110}, {98, 99}, {100, 104}, {101, 103}, {102, 109}, {105, 1292}, {106, 1293}, {107, 1294}, {108, 1295}, {111, 1296}, {112, 1297}, {476, 477}, ...

  Circumcircle-:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-antipodes: {74, 107}, {98, 112}, {99, 3563}, {100, 915}, {101, 917}, {102, 26704}, {103, 26705}, {104, 108}, {105, 26706}, {110, 1300}, {477, 1304}, ...

.. _guide-preamble-0299:

* **X_26864**–**X_26958** — **Endo-homothetic centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 3, 2018. This section comprises the endo-homothetic centers of the family of triangles homothetic with the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` of a reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This family is composed by the following 31 triangles: Ascella, Atik, 1st circumperp, 2nd circumperp, inner-Conway, Conway, 2nd Conway, 3rd Conway, 3rd Euler, 4th Euler, excenters-reflections, excentral, 2nd extouch, hexyl, Honsberger, inner-Hutson, Hutson intouch, outer-Hutson, incircle-circles, intouch, inverse-in-incircle, 6th mixtilinear, 2nd Pamfilos-Zhou, 1st Sharygin, tangential-midarc, 2nd tangential-midarc, Ursa major, Ursa minor, Wasat, Yff central, 2nd Zaniah. For definitions and coordinates of these triangles, see the **index of triangles referenced in ETC** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

* **X_27424**–**X_27470** — **Collineation mappings involving Gemini triangle 62**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, November 8, 2018. Extending the preambles just before X_24537, X_26153, and X_27378, let m(X) denote the (:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`; :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) collineation image of :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, where :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = Gemini triangle 62, as in centers X_27424-X_27470. Then

  m(X) = (bc+ac-ab)(ab-ac+bc)(b^2+bc+c^2)x + (c^2+ab)(ab-ac+bc)ab-ac-bc)y + (b^2+ac)(ac-ab-bc)(ac-ab-bc)z : : ,

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, December 9, 2018. Definition: Point Castor(h,j,k,p,q,a,b,c) =\ :math:`f(h,j,k,p,q,a,b,c) : f(h,j,k,p,q,b,c,a) : f(h,j,k,p,q,c,a,b)` (barycentrics), where

  :math:`f(h,j,k,p,q,a,b,c) = h (a^{3} + b^{3} + c^{3}) + j (a^{2} b + b^{2} c + c^{2} a + a^{2} c + b^{2} a + c^{2} b) + k (a b c) + a (p (a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}) + q (b c + c a + a b))`,

  where h, j, k, p, q are real numbers, not all zero. These points lie on the line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

Then
