.. _guide-preamble-0497:

* **X_37869**–**X_37880** — **Antigonal images**

  based on notes contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, April 9, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than P, in which the line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` meets the circle (:g:`PBC << P B C >>`), and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically; the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is called the circlecevian triangle of :g:`P <P>` with respect to triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` by :person:`Floor van Lamoen <floor-van-lamoen>` (:cite:`Hyacinthos #10039 <hyacinthos>`); see the preambles just before X_34520 and X_34892.

  Assume that P is not :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, and let :g:`A″ <A″>` = reflection of :g:`A' <A'>` in line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`,\ :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur in a point IA(P), and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is the circlecevian triangle of IA(P) with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The point IA(P) is the :term:`antigonal image <antigonal-image>` of :g:`P <P>`; for a definition see the Glossary of ETC, where it is noted that.

  IA(P) = p / ( a^2 (p + q) (p + r) - b^2 p (p + q) - c^2 p (p + r) ) : :

  Note that IA(IA(P)) = P, and that IA(P) lies on the rectangular hyperbola passing through these five points: :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`P <P>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`.

  Examples:

  | IA(:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`) = :ref:`X_80 <X_80>`
  | IA(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) =\ :ref:`X_671 <X_671>`
  | IA(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) = :ref:`X_265 <X_265>`
  | IA(:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`) (undefined)
  | IA(:ref:`X_5 <X_5>`) = :ref:`X_1263 <X_1263>`
  | [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0498:

* **X_37896**–**X_37980** — **Parallels-tangential-conics and related centers**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 15, 2020. Parallels-conics are defined in the preamble just before X_10001:

  Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the line through a point :g:`P <P>` parallel to line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Let :g:`A_{B} <A_B>` = :g:`A' <A'>`\ ∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`A_{C} <A_C>` = :g:`A' <A'>`\ ∩\ :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`. Define :g:`B_{C} <B_C>` and :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` cyclically, and define :g:`B_{A} <B_A>` and :g:`C_{B} <C_B>` cyclically. The six points :g:`A_{B} <A_B>`, :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, :g:`C_{A} <C_A>`, :g:`A_{B} <A_B>`, :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, :g:`C_{A} <C_A>` lie on a conic, here named the parallels-conic of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by Cpar(P).

  Also, the lines :g:`AB_{A} <[ A B_A ]>`, :g:`AC_{A} <[ A C_A ]>`, :g:`BC_{B} <[ B C_B ]>`, :g:`BA_{B} <[ B A_B ]>`, :g:`CA_{C} <[ C A_C ]>`, :g:`CB_{C} <[ C B_C ]>` are tangent to another conic, here named the **parallels-tangential-conic of P** and denoted by *TCpar(P)*. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics), then TCpar(P) has center O(P) and perspector W(P) given by

  O(P) = 2\*x^3 + x\*y\*(5\*x + 3\*y + 2\*z) + x\*z\*(5\*x + 2\*y + 3\*z) + 2\*y\*z\*(x + y + z) : :

  W(P) = (x + y)\*(x + z)\*(y\*(x + y + z) + 2\*x\*z)\*(z\*(x + y + z) + 2\*x\*y) : :

.. _guide-preamble-0499:

* **X_37994**–**X_37997** — **Circumcircle-inverses of points on the Euler line**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 18-19, 2020. If X is a point on the Euler line, then the circumcircle-inverse of :g:`X <X>` is on the Euler line. In addition to the 4877 :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` on the Euler line that are listed in the Central Lines page (accessible via Tables at the top of this page), this section introduces 85 more.

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_i and X_j are a pair of circumcircle-inverses on the Euler line: {2,23), (3,30), (4,186), (5,2070), (20,2071), (21,1325), (22,858), (24,403), (25,468), (26,2072), (27,2073), (28,2074), (29,2075), (140,5899), (199,33329), (235,37917), (237,1316), (297,36176), (376,7464), (378,10295), (381,7575), (382,15646), (384,37896), (401,37918), (404,37919), (427,21284), (428,37920), [and others].

Part 20
-------

.. _guide-preamble-0500:

* **X_38001**–**X_38002** — **Stationary points of Hutson right hyperbolas**

  conributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, based on notes from :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 26, 2020. The following note is copied from X_37904. "Let :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` be circumcircle antipodes. Let :g:`Q <Q>` be the midpoint of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and P. Let :g:`Q' <Q'>` be the midpoint of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and :g:`P' <P'>`. The rectangular hyperbola passing through :g:`P <P>`, :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`Q <Q>`, :g:`Q' <Q'>` has center X_37904 for all P. (Randy Hutson, April 24, 2020)".

  There are two stationary points on the family of Hutson rectangular hyperbolas, and on the Euler line, as can be seen by dragging P around the circumcircle in this GeoGebra diagram: **Hutson Right Hyperbolas** (``HutsonRightHyperbolas.ggb``). (Peter Moses, April 26, 2020)

  | Let HRH(P) denote the Hutson right hyperbola of :g:`P <P>`.
  | HRH(:ref:`X_74 <X_74>` passes through X_i for these i: 74, 110, 2574, 2575, 2930, 5642, 5646, 38001, 38002.
  | HRH(:ref:`X_98 <X_98>`) passes through X_i for these i: 98, 99, 2482, 6055, 38001, 38002.
  | HRH(:ref:`X_111 <X_111>`) passes through X_i for these i: 111, 1296, 9172, 33900, 38001, 38002.

  For :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) on the circumcircle, let

  :math:`h(a,b,c,p,q,r,x,y,z) = (a^{2} - 5 b^{2} - 5 c^{2}) \cdot (2 a^{2} b^{2} c^{2} p (-q + r) - c^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}) \cdot (a^{2} + c^{2}) q^{2} - 2 b^{2} (b^{2} - c^{2}) c^{2} q r + b^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2}) \cdot (a^{2} - b^{2} + c^{2}) r^{2}) x^{2} - (a^{4} - b^{4} + 10 b^{2} c^{2} - c^{4}) \cdot ((b^{4} - c^{4}) p^{2} + 2 a^{2} p (b^{2} q - c^{2} r) + a^{2} (a^{2} + c^{2}) q^{2} - a^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2}) r^{2}) y z`

  An equation for HRH(P) is

  h(a,b,c,p,q,r,x,y,z) + H(b,c,a,q,r,p,y,z,x) + :math:`H(c,a,b,r,p,q,z,x,y) = 0`.

  The family of Hutson right hyperbolas can be generalized by replacing :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` in the definition of HRH(P) by :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`. Let

  :math:`H(a,b,c,u,v,w,p,q,r,x,y,z) = (c^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2}) \cdot (a^{2} + c^{2}) q^{2} + 2 a^{2} b^{2} c^{2} p (q - r) + 2 b^{2} c^{2} (b^{2} - c^{2}) q r - b^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2}) \cdot (a^{2} - b^{2} + c^{2}) r^{2}) \cdot (c^{2} u v + 2 c^{2} v^{2} + b^{2} u w - (a^{2} - 2 b^{2} - 2 c^{2}) v w + 2 b^{2} w^{2}) x^{2} - ((b^{4} - c^{4}) p^{2} + a^{2} (a^{2} + c^{2}) q^{2} - a^{2} (a^{2} + b^{2}) r^{2} + 2 a^{2} p (b^{2} q - c^{2} r)) \cdot (4 b^{2} c^{2} u^{2} + c^{2} (a^{2} + 3 b^{2} - c^{2}) u v + b^{2} (a^{2} - b^{2} + 3 c^{2}) u w + a^{2} (a^{2} - b^{2} - c^{2}) v w) y z`

  Then the general right hyperbola is given by

  H(a,b,c,u,v,w,p,q,r,x,y,z) + h(b,c,a,v,w,u,q,r,p,y,z,x) + :math:`h(c,a,b,w,u,v,r,p,q,z,x,y) = 0`,

  with the following point, independent of :g:`P <P>`, as center:

  4\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*u^3 + c^2\*(4\*a^4 + 3\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - 5\*a^2\*c^2 - 2\*b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*u^2\*v + a^2\*c^2\*(3\*a^2 + b^2 - 3\*c^2)\*u\*v^2 + b^2\*(4\*a^4 - 5\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 + 3\*a^2\*c^2 - 2\*b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*u^2\*w + 2\*a^2\*(2\*a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - c^4)\*u\*v\*w + 3\*a^4\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*v^2\*w + a^2\*b^2\*(3\*a^2 - 3\*b^2 + c^2)\*u\*w^2 + 3\*a^4\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*v\*w^2 : : ,

  and two stationary points on the line U\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. The midpoint of the two points is the center of the hyperbola. As an example, for :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, the center is :ref:`X_468 <X_468>` and the stationary points are X_5000 and X_5001, and if :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_74 <X_74>`, then the hyperbola is the Walsmith rectangular hyperbola. (Peter Moses, April 26, 2020)

  The general hyperbola is denoted by (U,P)-MHRH and here named the **(U,P)-Moses-Hutson right hyperbola**. For further examples, see X_38010-X_38014.

.. _guide-preamble-0501:

* **X_38005**–**X_38009** — **Vu pedal translations**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, April 25, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, but not on the circumcircle, and not the incenter or any of the three excenters. Let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`
  | V = vector :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>`
  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = V(:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`)

  Then :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector, here named the **Vu pedal translation of P**, is the point

  V(P) = (a^4 q r + (b^2 - c^2) p (c^2 q + b^2 r) + a^2 (c^2 q (p - r) + b^2 r (3 p + 3 q + 2 r)))\*(a^4 q r - (b^2 - c^2) p (c^2 q + b^2 r) + a^2 (b^2 (p - q) r + c^2 q (3 p + 2 q + 3 r))) : :

  See **Vu Pedal Translation** (``VuPedalTranslation.pdf``).

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:
  | (2,38005), (3,4), (4,4846), (5,38006), (6,18842), (7,38007), (8,38008), (9,38009)

  See the preamble just before X_38305 for Vu antipedal translation.

.. _guide-preamble-0502:

* **X_38017**–**X_38020** — **Foci of circumparabolas**

  :based on notes from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, April 28-29, 2020. Suppose that one focus of a circumparabola is :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` on the line at infinity. Then the other focus lies on the `circumparabolas foci quintic, Q077 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/curves/q077.html>`__ and is given by

  p\*((-a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*p^2\*q\*r - a^2\*q^2\*r^2 + b^2\*r^2\*p^2 + c^2\*p^2\*q^2): :

  The circumparabola, given by

  p(q + r) y z + q( r + p ) z x + r( p + q) = 0

  is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the line tangent to the circumcircle at the isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that X_i is on the line at infinity and X_j is the corresponding focus of a circumparabola: (30,38246), (512,38017), (513,38018), (514,38019), (523,12064), (524,38020), (525,38233). (Peter Moses, April 29, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0504:

* **X_38247**–**X_38304** — **Vu-Lozada QA-points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 1, 2020. The following theorem is enunciated in the preamble just before X_36598:

  *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P a point, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` and ℭ a conic through :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`. If :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` are the points, others than :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, at which ℭ cuts :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively, then :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur.*

  It is also written in that preamble that if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` and ℭ has perspector :g:`X' <X'>` =\ :math:`x' : y' : z'` with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (barycentrics), then the triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` have perspector Q(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = x (x' y z + x (z' y - 3 y' z)) (x' y z + x (y' z - 3 z' y)) : :

  Vu Thanh Tung observed that if the previous construction is applied to a quadrangle :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`\ :g:`P_{2}P_{3}P_{4} << P_2 P_3 P_4 >>` and every :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>` is calculated as above in the triangle :g:`P_{j}P_{k}P_{ℓ} << P_j P_k P_ℓ >>`, then the four lines :g:`P_{n}Q_{n} <[ P_n Q_n ]>` are also concurrent (`Quadri-and-Poly-Geometry #243 <https://groups.io/g/Quadri-and-Poly-Geometry/message/249>`__). César Lozada found that this point of concurrence T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) has barycentrics coordinates:

  T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = x' (x' y z + x (y' z - 3 z' y)) (x' y z + x (z' y - 3 y' z)) : : . The point T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) is nere named the **Vu-Lozada QA-point of (P, X')**. Notes:

  If :g:`P <P>` = :g:`X' <X'>` or P lies on the :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-circumconic with perspector :g:`X' <X'>` then T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = P. If :g:`X' <X'>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` then T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = IsotomicConjugate(:term:`Anticomplement <anticomplement>`\ (Anticomplement(IsotomicConjugate(P)))). If :g:`X' <X'>` = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` then T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = PolarConjugate(Anticomplement(Anticomplement(PolarConjugate(P)))). If :g:`X' <X'>` = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` then T(P, :g:`X' <X'>`) = IsogonalConjugate(Anticomplement(Anticomplement(IsogonalConjugate(P)))).

  | The appearance of (i, j, n) in the following list means that the Vu-Lozada :g:`QA <[ Q A ]>`-point of (X_i, X_j) is X_n:
  | (1, 2, 38247), (1, 3, 38248), (1, 4, 38249), (1, 6, 3445), (1, 7, 38250), (1, 8, 38251), (1, 31, 38252), (2, 1, 8056), (2, 3, 1073), (2, 4, 38253), (2, 6, 8770), (2, 7, 38254), (2, 8, 38255), (2, 111, 38280), (3, 1, 36600) [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0505:

* **X_38305**–**X_38309** — **Vu antipedal translations**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 1, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, but not on the circumcircle. Let

  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`antipedal triangle <antipedal-triangle>` of P
  | V = 2 \* vector :g:`OP' <[ O P' ]>`

  V(P) = 1 / ( c^4 q (2 p - r) + b^4 (2 p - q) r - 3 a^4 q r - 2 a^2 (c^2 q (p - 2 r) + b^2 (p - 2 q) r) + 2 b^2 c^2 (q r + p (q + r)) ) : :

  See **Vu Antipedal Translation** (``VuAntipedalTranslation.pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0506:

* **X_38310**–**X_38313** — **Points Associated with generalized Paasche conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 4, 2020. As stated at X_37861, if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics) are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` having the same degree of homogeneity in a,b,c, then the (p,u)-generalized Paasche conic, GPC(p,u), is the conic that passes through these six :math:`points: 0 : r` : w,\ :math:`0 : v : q`,\ :math:`u : 0 : p`,\ :math:`r : 0 : w`,\ :math:`q : v : 0`,\ :math:`u : p : 0` and is given by the equation p v w x^2 + q w u y^2 + r u v z^2 - (q r u + u v w) y z - (r p v + u v w) z x - (p q w + u v w) x y = 0.

  The perspector of GPC(p,u) is the barycentric quotient P/:g:`U <U>` = p v w : q w u : r u v, and the center of GPC(p,u) is 2 p^2 v^2 w^2 - u v w (2 p q r + 2 q r u + 2 p r v + 2 p q w + r u v + q u w) : :

  Note, for example, that GPC(p,2u) is not the same conic as GPC(p,u); i.e., the definition of generalized Paasche conic depends on the representations of centers P and U. Nevertheless, we write GPC(P,U) instead of GPC(p,u) in cases where p and u are the first barycentrics as shown in ETC; in particular, this is the case when p and u are polynomials in a,b,c with relatively prime coefficients that agree in parity. Examples of this kind include the following:

  Degree 2 of homogeneity:

  | GPC(:ref:`X_9 <X_9>`,\ :ref:`X_192 <X_192>`) passes through X_10030.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_75 <X_75>`,\ :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`) passes through :ref:`X_3307 <X_3307>` and :ref:`X_3308 <X_3308>`, and has center :ref:`X_650 <X_650>`.
  | GPC(141),\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) passes through :ref:`X_1662 <X_1662>` and :ref:`X_1663 <X_1663>`, a hyperbola with center :ref:`X_182 <X_182>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_192 <X_192>`,\ :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`) passes through :ref:`X_3685 <X_3685>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_239 <X_239>`,\ :ref:`X_320 <X_320>`) passes through :ref:`X_320 <X_320>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_320 <X_320>`,\ :ref:`X_239 <X_239>`) passes through :ref:`X_239 <X_239>` and its antipode, X_38311.

  Degree 3 of homogeneity:

  | GPC(:ref:`X_11 <X_11>`,\ :ref:`X_55 <X_55>`) passes through :ref:`X_101 <X_101>` and :ref:`X_3939 <X_3939>`, and has center X_15260.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_11 <X_11>`,\ :ref:`X_100 <X_100>`) passes through :ref:`X_765 <X_765>`, X_4564, and has center X_38310.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_38 <X_38>`, :ref:`X_31 <X_31>`) = GPC(:ref:`X_141 <X_141>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`).
  | GPC(:ref:`X_42 <X_42>`,\ :ref:`X_171 <X_171>`) passes through X_4128.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_55 <X_55>`,\ :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`)) passes through :ref:`X_514 <X_514>` and :ref:`X_522 <X_522>`, a hyperbola with center X_15280
  | GPC(:ref:`X_55 <X_55>`,\ :ref:`X_43 <X_43>`) passes through X_10030.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_55 <X_55>`,\ :ref:`X_312 <X_312>`) passes through :ref:`X_1921 <X_1921>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_100 <X_100>`,\ :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`)) passes through :ref:`X_514 <X_514>` and :ref:`X_522 <X_522>`, a hyperbola with center :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`
  | GPC(:ref:`X_100 <X_100>`,\ :ref:`X_244 <X_244>`) passes through :ref:`X_514 <X_514>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_171 <X_171>`,\ :ref:`X_42 <X_42>`) passes through :ref:`X_2643 <X_2643>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_244 <X_244>`,\ :ref:`X_100 <X_100>`) passes through :ref:`X_1016 <X_1016>`.
  | GPC(:ref:`X_321 <X_321>`,\ :ref:`X_210 <X_210>`) = GPC(:ref:`X_75 <X_75>`,\ :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`).
  | GPC(:ref:`X_354 <X_354>`,\ :ref:`X_210 <X_210>`) passes through :ref:`X_3932 <X_3932>`.

  GPC(p,u} passes through :math:`u : v : w` if q r + r p + p q + v w + w u + u v = p u + q v + r w.

  GPC(p,u} passes through :math:`p : q : r` if q^2 r^2 u + p^2 r^2 v + p^2 q^2 w + (q r + r p + p q) u v w = p^3 v w + q^3 w u + r^3 u v.

  As noted at X_37861, :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>` observed that the Paasche inner conic (i.e., the Paasche ellipse), passes through the points indicated by the notation GCP(1,sin A). To generalize, the locus of the center of GCP(t, sinA) as t goes through the real numbers is the quartic curve given by

  a\*b\*(b - c)^2\*c\*x^4 + 2\*(a - b)\*b\*(a - 2\*c)\*(b - c)\*c\*x^3\*y + a\*b\*c\*(a^2 - 4\*a\*b + b^2 + 2\*a\*c + 2\*b\*c - 2\*c^2)\*x^2\*y^2 - 2\*a\*(a - b)\*(b - 2\*c)\*(a - c)\*c\*x\*y^3 + a\*b\*(a - c)^2\*c\*y^4 - 2\*(a - 2\*b)\*b\*(a - c)\*(b - c)\*c\*x^3\*z - 2\*a\*b\*c\*(a^2 - a\*b + b^2 - a\*c - b\*c + c^2)\*x^2\*y\*z - 2\*a\*b\*c\*(a^2 - a\*b + b^2 - a\*c - b\*c + c^2)\*x\*y^2\*z + 2\*a\*(2\*a - b)\*(a - c)\*(b - c)\*c\*y^3\*z + a\*b\*c\*(a^2 + 2\*a\*b - 2\*b^2 - 4\*a\*c + 2\*b\*c + c^2)\*x^2\*z^2 - 2\*a\*b\*c\*(a^2 - a\*b + b^2 - a\*c - b\*c + c^2)\*x\*y\*z^2 - a\*b\*c\*(2\*a^2 - 2\*a\*b - b^2 - 2\*a\*c + 4\*b\*c - c^2)\*y^2\*z^2 + 2\*a\*(a - b)\*b\*(a - c)\*(2\*b - c)\*x\*z^3 - 2\*a\*(a - b)\*b\*(2\*a - c)\*(b - c)\*y\*z^3 + a\*(a - b)^2\*b\*c\*z^4 = 0.

  This curve passes through the points X_i for i = 2, 9, 3218, 8183, 37861, 37862, 38312, 38313.

  The following table identifies the conics GPC(t, sin A) for several choices of t:

  t GPC(t, sin A) center 0 Steiner circumellipse :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` 1 Paasche elllipse X_37861 -1 Paasche outer conic X_37862 infinity circumellipse centered at :ref:`X_9 <X_9>` :ref:`X_9 <X_9>` -2/(3R) hyperbola :ref:`X_3218 <X_3218>` -W^(1/2) (see below) (pending) X_38312 W^(1/2) (see below) (pending) X_38313

  In the table, W = 3S/(4Rs) = 3(-a+b+c)(a-b+c)(a+b-c)/(4 a b c).

.. _guide-preamble-0507:

* **X_38317**–**X_38319** — **Centers of Vu pedal-centroidal circles**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 4, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let

  | G = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` = centroid of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`
  | :g:`A_{0}B_{0}C_{0} << A_0 B_0 C_0 >>` = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`
  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of P
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = centroid of :g:`A_{1}B_{0}C_{0} << A_1 B_0 C_0 >>`
  | :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` = centroid of :g:`B_{1}A_{0}C_{0} << B_1 A_0 C_0 >>`
  | :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` = centroid of :g:`C_{1}A_{0}B_{0} << C_1 A_0 B_0 >>`

  The points :g:`G <G>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` lie on a circle, here named the **Vu pedal-centroidal circle of P**. The center of this circle is the point

  V(P) = a^4 (2 p + q + r) + (b^2 - c^2)^2 (3 p + 2 (q + r)) - a^2 (b^2 + c^2) (5 p + 3 (q + r)) : :

  See **PedalCentroidCircle** (``PedalCentroidCircle.pdf``)

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,11230), (2,15699), (3,2), (4,5), (5,547), (6,38317), (7,38171), (8,38042), (9,38318), (10,10172), (11,38319), (20,549), (74,34128), (98,34127), (140, 3628), (376, 11539), (381, 5055), (382, 381)

  If :g:`P* <P*>` is the circumcircle-inverse of :g:`P <P>`, then the Vu pedal-centroidal circles of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P* <P*>` are tangent at :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 5, 2020)

  If P lies on the Euler line, then V(P) also lies on the Euler line. If P lies on the line at infinity, then V(P) = P. (Randy Hutson, May 5, 2020)

  V maps the circumcircle onto the circle of the points V(:ref:`X_104 <X_104>`) = X_34126, V(:ref:`X_98 <X_98>`) = X_34127, and V(:ref:`X_74 <X_74>`) = X_32128; the center of this circle is :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. (Randy Hutson, May 5, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0508:

* **X_38331**–**X_38334** — **Vu circumcevian-orthocenter perspectors**

  | based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 9, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), and let
  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = circumcevian triangle of P
  | :g:`H_{bc} <H_bc>` = orthocenter of :g:`PB_{1}C << P B_1 C >>`, and define :g:`H_{ca} <H_ca>` and :g:`H_{ab} <H_ab>` cyclically
  | :g:`H_{cb} <H_cb>` = orthocenter of :g:`PC_{1}B << P C_1 B >>`, and define :g:`H_{ac} <H_ac>` and :g:`H_{ba} <H_ba>` cyclically
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`H_{ca}H_{ac} <[ H_ca H_ac ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`H_{ab}H_{ba} <[ H_ab H_ba ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically.
  | Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is given by

  V(P) = (2 b^2 c^2 p^2 + a^2 c^2 p q + b^2 c^2 p q - c^4 p q + a^2 b^2 p r - b^4 p r + b^2 c^2 p r + a^4 q r - a^2 b^2 q r - a^2 c^2 q r) \* (-a^2 b^2 c^2 p q + b^4 c^2 p q - a^2 c^4 p q - 2 b^2 c^4 p q + c^6 p q - a^4 c^2 q^2 + a^2 b^2 c^2 q^2 - a^2 c^4 q^2 + a^4 b^2 p r - 2 a^2 b^4 p r + b^6 p r - 2 b^4 c^2 p r + b^2 c^4 p r + a^6 q r - 2 a^4 b^2 q r + a^2 b^4 q r - a^4 c^2 q r - a^2 b^2 c^2 q r) \* (a^4 c^2 p q + b^4 c^2 p q - 2 a^2 c^4 p q - 2 b^2 c^4 p q + c^6 p q - a^2 b^4 p r + b^6 p r - a^2 b^2 c^2 p r - 2 b^4 c^2 p r + b^2 c^4 p r + a^6 q r - a^4 b^2 q r - 2 a^4 c^2 q r - a^2 b^2 c^2 q r + a^2 c^4 q r - a^4 b^2 r^2 - a^2 b^4 r^2 + a^2 b^2 c^2 r^2) : :

  See **Vu Circumcevian-Orthocenter Perspector** (``VuCircumcevianOrthocenterPerspector.pdf``).

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j: (1,79), (2,38331), (3,3), (4,14111), (5,38332), (6,22100) (7,38333), (8,38334)

.. _guide-preamble-0509:

* **X_38336**–**X_38343** — **2nd Vu circumcevian-orthocenter perspectors and trilinear poles**

  | based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 10, 2020. As in the preamble just before X_38331, let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), and let
  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = circumcevian triangle of P
  | :g:`H_{bc} <H_bc>` = orthocenter of :g:`PB_{1}C << P B_1 C >>`, and define :g:`H_{ca} <H_ca>` and :g:`H_{ab} <H_ab>` cyclically
  | :g:`H_{cb} <H_cb>` = orthocenter of :g:`PC_{1}B << P C_1 B >>`, and define :g:`H_{ac} <H_ac>` and :g:`H_{ba} <H_ba>` cyclically
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`H_{ca}H_{ac} <[ H_ca H_ac ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`H_{ab}H_{ba} <[ H_ab H_ba ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically.
  | Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`, and the perspector, here named the 2nd Vu circumcevian-orthocenter perspector of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ 2(P). The points :g:`P <P>`, V(P), :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (P) are collinear in a line d(P), here named the Vu circumcevian-orthocenter perspectrix. Barycentrics for V(P) are given in the preamble just before X_38331, and barycentrics for :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (P) and T(P) are given **here** (``VuBarycentricsPreambleX(38336).txt``). See **Second Vu Circumcevian-Orthocenter Perspector** (``SecondVuCircumcevianOrthocenterPerspector.pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0510:

* **X_38344**–**X_38429** — **Equicenters: X_38344-X_38429**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 10, 2020. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be triangles inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The affine transformation sending :g:`A' <A'>` to :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B' <B'>` to :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C' <C'>` to :g:`C″ <C″>` has a fixed point E named the **equicenter** of triangles :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`. (Reference: `The Triangle Web by Quim Castellsaguer <http://www.xtec.es/~qcastell/ttw/ttweng/definicions/d_equicentre_p.html>`__).

  The fixed point :g:`E <E>` is unique, and if :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are homothetic, then E is their homothetic center.

  The equicenter of the affine transformation sending (:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`) to (:g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`) coincides with the equicenter of the inverse affine transformation sending (:g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`) to (:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`). Therefore, the equicenter of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` may be referred simply as the **equicenter of triangles T' and T"**, regardless of the order in which the triangles are listed.

  The equicenter of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` is also the :term:`similarity image <similarity-image>` of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`..

  Some particular results:

  If *normalized barycentric* coordinates of :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` are :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`x_{a} : y_{a} : z_{a}` and :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`x_{b} : y_{b} : z_{b}` : :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`x_{c} : y_{c} : z_{c}`, then the equicenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is given by

  Ed(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`) = :math:`x_{b}` :math:`x_{c}` + :math:`x_{b}` :math:`y_{c}` + :math:`x_{c}` :math:`z_{b}` : :

  Suppose that :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics). If :g:`T_{X} <T_X>` = :term:`cevian <cevian>`-of-X and :g:`T_{U} <T_U>` = cevian-of-U, then E(:g:`T_{X} <T_X>`, :g:`T_{U} <T_U>`) = x u (y w - z v) ((y - z) u - (x + z) v + (x + y) w) : :

  For a list of equicenters related to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` see **here** (``./X38344List.txt``). Also, definitions of triangles mentioned can be found in the **index of triangles** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

  Open problem: give a geometric construction of the equicenter of two arbitrary triangles.

  Indeed, on October 29, 2005, François Rideau provided and proved a method, based strictly on intersections of lines, for constructing the fixed point of an affine transformation (see **Francois Rideau - Les points fixes d'une application affine.pdf** (``Francois%20Rideau%20-%20Les%20points%20fixes%20d%27une%20application%20affine.pdf``) (in French)). This is his construction:

  *Given two non-homothetic triangles :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` and the affine transformation* ƒ({ :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` }) → { :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` }, *we complete the parallelograms A'B':g:`C'D' <[ C' D' ]>` and A"B":g:`C″D″ <[ C″ D″ ]>`; i.e., :g:`D' <D'>` is the reflection of :g:`B' <B'>` in the midpoint of segment :g:`A'C' <[ A' C' ]>` and :g:`D″ <D″>` is the reflection of :g:`B″ <B″>` in the midpoint of segment :g:`A″C″ <[ A″ C″ ]>`. Let* :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>` ∩ :g:`A″B″ <[ A″ B″ ]>`, :g:`B* <B*>` = :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` ∩ :g:`B″C″ <[ B″ C″ ]>`, :g:`C* <C*>` = :g:`C'D' <[ C' D' ]>` ∩ :g:`C″D″ <[ C″ D″ ]>`, :g:`D* <D*>` = :g:`D'A' <[ D' A' ]>` ∩ :g:`D″A″ <[ D″ A″ ]>`. *Then the fixed point M of the affine transformation ƒ is* M = :g:`A*C* <[ A* C* ]>` ∩ :g:`B*D* <[ B* D* ]>`.

  Additionally, Rideau provided a very simple method for finding ƒ(X) of a given point :g:`X <X>`: let :g:`U <U>` = :g:`A*B* <[ A* B* ]>` ∩ parallelLine(X, :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`) and V = :g:`B*D* <[ B* D* ]>` ∩ parallelLine(X, :g:`A'D' <[ A' D' ]>`). Then ƒ(X) = parallelLine(U, :g:`A″B″ <[ A″ B″ ]>`) ∩ parallelLine(V, :g:`A″D″ <[ A″ D″ ]>`).

  Many thanks to Francisco Javier García Capitán for his notes with simplifications of Rideua conclusions and to :person:`Angel Montesdeoca <angel-montesdeoca>` for sending me these notes. (César Lozada, January 26, 2021.)

  If :g:`T_{X} <T_X>`\ =pedal-of-X and :g:`T_{U} <T_U>`\ =pedal-of-U, then E(:g:`T_{X} <T_X>`,\ :g:`T_{U} <T_U>`) is the orthopole of line XU. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 19, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0511:

* **X_38433**–**X_38449** — **Points associated with Vu (k)-conics**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 13-14, 2020 and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 13, 2020. Suppose that 0 < k < π/2. Let :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>` be the points on line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` such that \|\ :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`\ \| = \|\ :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`\ \| and angle :g:`A'AA″ << A' A A″ >>` has measure 2k. Likewise, let :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`B″ <B″>` on :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` and :g:`C' <C'>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` on :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` be the points such that the triangles :g:`B'BB″ << B' B B″ >>` and :g:`C'CC″ << C' C C″ >>` are similar to :g:`A'AA″ << A' A A″ >>`. Then the points :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` lie on a conic, here named the **Vu (k)-conic**. Peter Moses found that these conics all have center :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and that the perspector, V(k), of the Vu (k)-conic is given by

  V(k) = 1/((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*Cos[k]^2 - 4\*(a^4 - b^4 - c^4)\*S^2\*Sin[k]^2) : : (barycentrics)

  Moses also found that he ratio of minor axis to major axis is :math:`\sqrt{(J-1) (J+3) / ((J-3) (J+1))}`, where J = \|OH\|/R, as at :ref:`X_1113 <X_1113>`.

  Accordingly, the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>`, T(k), and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`, U(k), are given by

  T(k) = (a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*Cos[k]^2 - 4\*(a^4 - b^4 - c^4)\*S^2\*Sin[k]^2 : :

  U(k) = a^2 ((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*Cos[k]^2 - 4\*(a^4 - b^4 - c^4)\*S^2\*Sin[k]^2) : :

  | V(k) lies on the Jerabek rectangular hyperbola {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`}}.
  | T(k) lies on the line :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`\ \ :ref:`X_264 <X_264>`.
  | U(k) lies on the Euler line.

  X_6145 = perspector of the Vu (π/4) conic, and X_18434 = perspector of the Vu (π/6) conic.

  For every real number x, the perspector of the Vu (acrctan(x))-conic is

  1/((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2) - 4\*(a^4 - b^4 - c^4)\*S^2\*x^2) : : , with isogonal conjugate

  a^2\*((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2) - 4\*(a^4 - b^4 - c^4)\*S^2\*x^2) : :

  on the Euler line. (Peter Moses, May 15, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0512:

* **X_38451**–**X_38456** — **Points associated with Vu P-cirumcircle points**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 16, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, but not :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` and not on the circumcircle. Let

  | :g:`P' <P'>` = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P
  | :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` = line tangent to the circle APP' at :g:`A <A>`, and define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` cyclically.

  The lines :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`, :g:`T_{b} <T_b>`, :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` concur in a point V(P) on the circumcircle:

  V(P) = V(:g:`P' <P'>`) = a^2 / (c^2 p^2 q + b^2 p^2 r - a^2 q^2 r - a^2 q r^2) : :

  The point V(P) is here named the **Vu P-circumcircle point**.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j: (2,111), (3,74), (4,74), (5,14979), (6,111), (9,2291), (7,38451), (8,38452), (10,38453)

  See **Vu Circumcircle Point** (``Vu%20Circumcircle%20Point.pdf``).

  V(P) is the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line through :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and the PK-transform of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 19, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0513:

* **X_38457**–**X_38465** — **Points associated with Vu (P,U)-circles points**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 18-19, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be distinct points in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not both on the circumcircle. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than A, that lies on both circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (APU), and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The four lines :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>`, :g:`PU <[ P U ]>` concur in a point, V(P,U), here named the **Vu {P,U}-circles point** point, given by

  V(P,U) = V(U,P) = a^2 (- p y w (p + r + q) + q r u (u + v + w)) + b^2 p u (r (u + v) - (p + q) w) + c^2 p u (-(p + r) v + q (u + w)) : :

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that V(X_i,X_j) = V(X_j,X_i) = X_k: (1,2,7292), (1,3,36), (1,6,16784), (1,4,1870 ), (1,5,38458), (1,6,16784), (1,7,38459), (1,8,38460), (2,3,23), (2,4,468), (2,5,37760), (2,6 11580), (2 7,37761), (2,8,37762), (3,4,186), (3,5,2070), (3,6,187), (3,7,32624), (3,8,17100), (4,5,37943), (4,6,8744), (4,75,38457), (13,14,1989), (15,16,6), (61,62,35006), (371,372,1692)

  See **Vu PU Circles Point** (``VuPUCirclesPoint.pdf``).

  Let :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (P,U) denote the point introduced in the preamble just before X_37756, given by

  :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ ( (P, U) = q r (a^2 (q r u (u+v+w) - p v w (p+q+r)) - b^2 p u (w (p+q) - r (u+v)) - c^2 p u (v (p+r) - q (u+w))) : :

  | Then
  | V(P,U) = barycentric product :g:`P* <P*>` :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (P,U)
  | V(P,U) = barycentric product :g:`U* <U*>` :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (U,P)
  | :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (P,U) = barycentric product :g:`U* <U*>`\ :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (U,P)
  | V(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,U) = V(U,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) = :g:`V_{2} <V_2>`\ (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,U)
  | V(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,U) = V(U,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) = circumcircle-inverse of :g:`U <U>`

  The Vu {P,U}-circles point is related to the Vu circlecevian point as follows: Let :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`U' <U'>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` and U, resp. Then the Vu {P,U}-circles point is the isogonal conjugate of the Vu circlecevian point V(:g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`U' <U'>`). (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 20, 2020)

  :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` =\ :math:`0 : 2R : c`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` =\ :math:`0 : b : 2R`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` =\ :math:`a : 0 : 2R`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` =\ :math:`2R : 0 : c`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` =\ :math:`2R : b : 0`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` =\ :math:`a : 2R : 0` (These points lie on the Paasche ellipse; see X_37861 and :ref:`X_3788 <X_3788>`

  | :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = 0 : 4R + c : c and :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` =\ :math:`0 : b : 4R` + b
  | :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>` =\ :math:`a : 0 : 4R` + a and :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>` = 4R +\ :math:`c : 0 : c`
  | :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>` = 4R+\ :math:`b : b : 0` and :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>` = a : 4R+a : 0

  Geometrically, :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = midpoint of :g:`B <B>` and :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` = midpoint of :g:`C <C>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, etc.. Using the notation in the preamble just before X_38310, these midpoints are given by taking (p,q,r) = (4R + a, 4R + b, 4R + c) and (u,v,w) = (a,b,c).

.. _guide-preamble-0516:

* **X_38497**–**X_38529** — **Dilations of points on the circumcircle to other circles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 23, 2020. Suppose that P and U are distinct points in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let Γ(P,U)) denote the circle with center P and pass-through point :g:`U <U>`. Suppose that V is a point distinct from :g:`U <U>`, and let D(P,U,V) denote the dilation from :g:`P <P>` that maps Γ(P,U)) onto Γ(P,V)). Centers X_38497-X_38519 are dilations from the circumcircle to Γ(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`), and centers X_38520-X_38529 are dilations from the circumcircle to Γ(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_76 <X_76>`)

  The appearance of {{:math:`i_{1}`, :math:`i_{2}`, . . . :math:`i_{k}`}} in the following list means that the k points all lie on the circle Γ(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :math:`X(i_{1})`): {{1,40,13534,22939}}, {{2,376,11006,14916}}, [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0517:

* **X_38536**–**X_38550** — **Vu (P,U)-circles perspectors**

  based on notes contributed by Thanh Tung, May 23, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be points in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` such that P, U, :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, where :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`U_{1} <U_1>` are the respective :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` and U, are distinct finite points. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than A, in which the circles (APU) and (AP1U1) intersect, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` are perspective, and their perspector is given by

  V(P,U) = V(U,P) = V(:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`,\ :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`) = V(:g:`U_{1} <U_1>`,\ :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`) = (c^2 p q u^2 + b^2 p r u^2 + a^2 q r u^2 - c^2 p^2 u v + b^2 p r u v - c^2 p r u v + a^2 q r u v - b^2 p^2 u w - b^2 p q u w + c^2 p q u w + a^2 q r u w - a^2 p^2 v w - a^2 p q v w - a^2 p r v w)\*(-a^2 c^2 p q u v + c^4 p q u v - a^2 c^2 q^2 u v + b^2 c^2 p r u v - a^2 c^2 p q v^2 - a^2 c^2 q^2 v^2 - a^2 c^2 q r v^2 + b^2 c^2 p q u w + b^4 p r u w + a^2 b^2 q r u w - a^2 c^2 q^2 v w + a^2 b^2 p r v w + a^4 q r v w - a^2 c^2 q r v w)\*(c^4 p q u v + b^2 c^2 p r u v + a^2 c^2 q r u v + b^2 c^2 p q u w - a^2 b^2 p r u w + b^4 p r u w - a^2 b^2 r^2 u w + a^2 c^2 p q v w + a^4 q r v w - a^2 b^2 q r v w - a^2 b^2 r^2 v w - a^2 b^2 p r w^2 - a^2 b^2 q r w^2 - a^2 b^2 r^2 w^2) : :

  The point V(P,U)) is here named the **Vu (P,U)-circles perspector**.

  See **Vu Circles Perspector** (``Vu%20Circles%20Perspector.pdf``)

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i,X_j) = X_k:

  (2,3,14246) and (2,4,14246), (4,6,14246) and (3,6,14246), (2,5,38536), (2,7,38537), (2,8,38538), (3,5,38539), (3,7,38540), (3,8,38541), (4,5,38542), (4,7,38543), (4,8,38544), (5,6,38545), (5,7,38546), (5,8,38547), (6,7,38548), (6,8,38549), (7,8,38550)

.. _guide-preamble-0518:

* **X_38723**–**X_38870** — **Circum-Euler-points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 28, 2020. The centroids of the four triangles determined by four concyclic points are concyclic. . (Reference: Halsted, George Bruce, Elementary Synthetic Geometry, 1892, problem 24, pp. 84.) Indeed, the above result is true for other points distinct from the centroids, although the exact locus is still unknown.

  Part of this locus is as follows: let :g:`Q <Q>` be a point on the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P a point on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` such that \|\ :g:`OP <[ O P ]>`\ \|/\|OH\| = λ, λ being a real number not depending on :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Denote :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` = P-of-:g:`QBC << Q B C >>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>` = P-of-:g:`QCA << Q C A >>` and :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` = P-of-:g:`QAB << Q A B >>`. Then the points :g:`P <P>`, :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` are concyclic on a circle with radius r' = \|λ\| R and whose center :g:`O' <O'>`\ (Q, P) is here named the **Q-circum-Euler-point of P**. In this case, :g:`O' <O'>`\ (Q, P) = λ (Q + :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`) + (1 - 2 λ) :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, and it lies on the line {:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, midpoint(:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, Q) }. Moreover, when P is fixed and Q varies, the locus of :g:`O' <O'>`\ (Q, P) is another circle with the same radius r' and center P.

  There are other P such that P, :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` are concyclic. A numerical calculus shows that a partial list of such points contains :g:`P <P>`\ =X_n for n ∈ {1, 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, 26, 36, 40, 80, 125, 155, 165, 186, 265, 368, 369, 370, 399, 1144, 1147, 1385, 1482, 1511, 1658, 2070, 2071, 2072, 2077, 3167, 3232, 3576, 3579, 5159, 5373, 5394, 5473, 5474, 5537, 5609, 5611, 5615, 5626, 5899, 5961, 5962, 5963, 5964, 6104, 6105, 6699, 6771, 6774, 7387, 7464, 7575, 7689, 7982, 7987, 7991, 8008, 8009, 8148, 8697, 9909} (n<10000). When :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, P, :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` are vertices of a rectangle.

  Curiously, when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_15 <X_15>` and Q varies, the locus of :g:`O' <O'>`\ (Q,P) are the sides of a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` having :g:`A <A>`-vertex with barycentric coordinates :g:`A' <A'>` = (:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S+SA)\*(SB+SC): S^2-SA\*SC : S^2-SA\*SB. This triangle is perspective to the following triangles with perspector :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`: (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 2nd anti-extouch, 2nd Hyacinth, Lucas antipodal(±1), Lucas central(±1), X3-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` reflections). It is also perspective to the following triangles with the given perspectors: (circumsymmedial, 11485), (outer-Le Viet An, 3129), (symmedial, 61), (tangential, 22236). A similar locus does not occur for :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`.

  The following table contains the Q-circum-Euler-point of :g:`P <P>` for selected :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` [table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0519:

* **X_38809**–**X_38824** — **Vu cevian tangential perspectors**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, May 31, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P
  | :math:`t_{a}` = line tangent to the circle (:g:`AB'C' << A B' C' >>`) at :g:`A <A>`, and define :math:`t_{b}` and :math:`t_{c}` cyclically
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`t_{b}`\ ∩\ :math:`t_{c}`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically.

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of the point

  V(P) = a^2/(p q + p r) : b^2/(q r + q p) : c^2/(r p + r q),

  which is the perspector of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`.

  See **Vu Cevian Tangential Perspector** (``VuCevianTangentialPerspector.pdf``).

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,81), (2,6), (3,275), (4,2), (5,288), (6,83), (7,1), (8,57), (9,1170), (10,1171), (11,38809), (31, 38810), (32, 38811), (75,58), (76,251), (560,38812), (561, 38813)

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is also perspective to :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` , the perspector, denoted by :g:`V' <V'>`\ (P), being the P-Ceva-conjugate of V(P):

  :g:`V' <V'>`\ (P) = a^2/(p(q+r)) \* (b^2/(q^2(r+p)) + c^2/(r^2(p+q)) - a^2/(p^2(q+r))) : :

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that :g:`V' <V'>`\ (X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,38814), (2,3), (3,38815), (4,193), (5,38816), (6,38817), (7,57), (8,34488), (9,38818), (10,38819), (31,38820), (32,38821)

  V(P) is the :term:`cevapoint <cevapoint>` of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :g:`P' <P'>`, where :g:`P' <P'>` is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 31, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0520:

* **X_38825**–**X_38843** — **Vu cevian-circles perspectors and related cyclocevian conjugates**

  based on notes from Vu Thanh Tung, June 1-3, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, but not on any of the medians (i.e., the lines AG, BG, CG), and let

  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = the point, other than A, in which the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (:g:`AB_{1}C_{1} << A B_1 C_1 >>`) intersect, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically

  The triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` are perspective, and the perspector is the point

  V(P) = a^2\*(p + q)\*(p + r) : b^2\*(q + r)\*(q + p) : c^2\*(r + p)\*(r + q).

  Also, V(P) = :term:`complement <complement>` of the :term:`anticomplementary conjugate <anticomplementary-conjugate>` of P (:person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, June 4, 2020)

  Also, V(P) is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the complement of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, June 9, 2020)

  :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of V(P), given by

  :g:`A' <A'>` = -a^2\*(p + q)\*(p + r) : b^2\*(q + r)\*(q + p) : c^2\*(r + p)\*(r + q).

  See **Vu Cevian-Circles Perspector** (``VuCevianCirclesPerspector.pdf``).

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the **Vu cevian-circles triangle of P**.

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,58), (3,54), (4,4), (5,1173), (6,251), (7,57), (8,1), (9,1174), (10,1126), (11,18771), (21,38825), (22, 38828), (23, 38831), (32,38826), (75,81), (76,83), (560,38827), (1501,38829), (1502,38830), (1928,38843)

  Let :g:`V' <V'>`\ (P) = :term:`cyclocevian conjugate <cyclocevian-conjugate>` of V(P) wrt :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, which is also the perspector of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, given by

  :g:`V' <V'>`\ (P) = a^2\*(p + q)\*(p + r)\*(p\*q + p\*r - q\*r) : :

  :g:`V' <V'>`\ (P) is the barycentric product V(P)\*[P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`] = V(P)\*[anticompliment of :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of P]. (Randy Hutson, June 9, 2020)

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that :g:`V' <V'>`\ (X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,38832), (3, 26887), (4, 6353), (5,38833), (6,38834), (7,1420), (8,165), (9,38835), (10,38836), (31,38837), (32,38838), (75,21), (76,1799), (560,38839), (561,38840), (1501, 38841), (1502, 38842)

  The triangle :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` is here named the **Vu perspectivities triangle of P**; see the preamble just before X_38848. Barycentrics for :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` are given by

  :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = a^2\*(p + q)\*(p + r) : b^2\*(q - r)\*(p + q): c^2\*(r - q)\*(p + r) : :

.. _guide-preamble-0521:

* **X_38848**–**X_38887** — **Vu tangential transforms**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, June 7, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The Vu perspectivies triangle of :g:`P <P>`, here denoted by T(P), is introduced in the preamble just before X_38825. The :g:`A <A>`-vertex is given by

  a^2\*(p + q)\*(p + r) : b^2\*(q - r)\*(p + q) : c^2\*(r - q)\*(p + r) : :

  T(P) is perspective to the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>` for every P on the de Longchamps axis (a^2 x + b^2 y + c^2 z = 0).

  T(P) is perspective to the anticomplementary triangle for every P on the following conic:

  a^2(b^2 - c^2)x^2 + b^2(c^2 - a^2)y^2 + c^2(a^2 - b^2)z^2 = 0, this being the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of the conic {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`}}, which passes through X_i for these i: 2, 69, 75, 1272, 1369, 1370, 6527, 14360, 17135, 17149, 18133, 18750, 19583, 20245, 20351, 20934, 22339, 22340, 25332, 30698, 32747.

  T(P) is perspective to the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` for every P on the anticomplement of the excentral triangle.

  T(P) is perspective to the excentral triangle for every P on the following conic: anticomplement of the conic {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`}}, which passes through X_i for these i: 2, 8, 329, 556, 1655, 2895, 8055, 17794, 18297, 20344, 21219, 30578, 30695.

  T(P) is perspective to the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>` for every P. The perspector, here named the **Vu tangential transform of P**, denoted by VT(P), is given by

  VT(P) = a^2\*(p^2 + p\*q + p\*r - q\*r) : b^2\*(q^2 + q\*r + q\*p - r\*p) : c^2\*(r^2 + r\*p + r\*q - p\*q).

  Then VT(P)) = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the perspector of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the reflection of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` in the centroid of ABCP (or the :term:`complement <complement>` of the complement of :g:`P <P>`). It is also the perspector :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ (:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,P), as defined in the preamble just before X_33760. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, June 9, 2020)

  If P lies on the circumcircle, then VT(P) = isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>` wrt its cevian triangle. If P lies on the line at infinity, then VT(P) = isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`. (Randy Hutson, June 9, 2020)

  The Vu tangential transform of the Euler line is a conic centered at X_15647 and passing through X_i for these i: 6, 24, 74, 1498, 1614, 38848, 38850, 38851, 38852, 38867, 38879, 38885. (Randy Hutson, June 9, 2020)

  From Peter Moses (June 10, 2020): Suppose that P lies on a line u x + v y + w z = 0. Then VT(P) lies on the following conic:

  4\*b^4\*c^4\*u^2\*(v - w)^2\*x^2 - a^4\*b^2\*c^2\*(u^4 - 2\*u^2\*v^2 + v^4 - 4\*u^2\*v\*w + 8\*u\*v^2\*w - 4\*v^3\*w - 2\*u^2\*w^2 + 8\*u\*v\*w^2 - 2\*v^2\*w^2 - 4\*v\*w^3 + w^4)\*y\*z + (cyclic) = 0.

  | Examples:
  | conic VT(Euler line) passes through X_i for these i: 6, 24, 74, 1498, 1614, 1620, 35217, 35218, 35219
  | conic VT(:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) passes through X_i for these i: 104, 595, 1614
  | conic VT(Brocard axis) passes through X_i for these i: 98, 1614, 1627, 33773
  | conic VT(Soddy line) passes through X_i for these i: 103, 595, 1498, 1617, 1619, 1622
  | conic VT(Nagel line) passes through X_i for these i: 3, 6, 106, 595, 1616, 23374, 33771, 33804, 35223
  | conic VT(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) passes through X_i for these i: 6, 22, 111, 1611, 1627, 33774, 35212, 35216

.. _guide-preamble-0522:

* **X_38900**–**X_38929** — **Vu PCC perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, June 22, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, not on any of the lines :g:`AO <[ A O ]>`, :g:`BO <[ B O ]>`, :g:`CO <[ C O ]>`, where :g:`O <O>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = circumcenter. Let

  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of P
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = the point, other than A, where the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (:g:`AB_{1}C_{1} << A B_1 C_1 >>`) meet, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically
  | :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` = circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`.

  Then :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` is perspective to :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, and the perspector is the point V(P), here named the **Vu 1st PCC perspector**, given by

  V(P) = a^2 (2 b^2 c^2 p^2 + a^2 c^2 p q + b^2 c^2 p q - c^4 p q + a^2 b^2 p r - b^4 p r + b^2 c^2 p r + a^4 q r - a^2 b^2 q r - a^2 c^2 q r) : :

  Also, :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` is perspective to :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`, and the perspector is the point T(P), here named the **Vu 2nd PCC perspector**, given by [coordinates omitted herej].

  See **Vu Pedal Circles Circumcevian Perspector** (``Vu%20Pedal%20Circles%20Circumcevian%20Perspector.pdf``).

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,56),(2,1995), (4,24), (5,13621), (6,1384), (7,38900), (8,38901), (9,38902), (10,38903), (31,38904), (32,38905), (75,38906), (76,38907), (83,38908), (141,38909), (560,38910), (561,38911), (1501,38912), (1502,38913), (1928,38914), (2321,38915), (2887,38916), (3676,38917)

  | The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that T(X_i) = X_j:
  | (1,1394), (2,38918), (4,4), (5,38919), (6,38920), (8,38922), (9,38923), (10,38924), (31,38925), (32,38926), (75,38927) (76,38928), (83,38929)

  V(P) is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the pedal antipodal perspector of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, June 17, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0523:

* **X_38957**–**X_39102** — **Crosssums of circumcircle-P-antipodes and line intercepts**

  contributed by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, June 17, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`P' <P'>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P. Then the locus of the :term:`crosssum <crosssum>` of circumcircle-P-antipodes is the bicevian conic of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and :g:`P' <P'>`, with center 2 a^2/p + b^2/q + c^2/r : :. For example, the locus of the crosssum of circumcircle antipodes is the nine-point circle, which is the bicevian conic of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, and the locus of the crosssum of circumcircle-:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`-antipodes is the Steiner inellipse, which is the limit of the bicevian conic of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and Q as Q approaches :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

  Let :g:`L <L>` be a line. The crosssum of the (real or nonreal) circumcircle-intercepts of :g:`L <L>` is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of the :term:`crossdifference <crossdifference>` of every pair of points on :g:`L <L>`, and is the center of the circumconic that is the isogonal conjugate of L. If L passes through :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, then the crosssum is also the orthopole of :g:`L <L>`, and lies on the :term:`cevian <cevian>` circle of the isogonal conjugate of every point on :g:`L <L>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0524:

* **X_39103**–**X_39108** — **Points on the self-dual permutation ellipse**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, June 20, 2020. Suppose that Γ is a conic. The dual of Γ is the conic consisting of points :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` such that the line px + qy + rz = 0 is tangent to Γ. See, for example, `Paul Yiu's Introduction to the Geometry of the Triangle, p. 125 <http://math.fau.edu/Yiu/YIUIntroductionToTriangleGeometry121226.pdf>`__.

  The dual of a permutation ellipse (defined in the preamble just before X_34341), is also a permutation ellipse. There exists a unique self-dual permutation ellipse, given by the equation

  x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + 4(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  If :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` is a point on the Steiner circumellipse, then the point

  D(U) = 3 u + (:math:`\sqrt{2}` - 1)(u + v + w) : :

  is on the self-dual permutation ellipse. The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that D(X_i) = X_j: (99,39103), (190,39104), (671,39105), (903,39106), (6189,39107), (6190,39108).

.. _guide-preamble-0525:

* **X_39141**–**X_39146** — **Perspectors related to the obverse triangle of X_69**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, June 25, 2020. The obverse triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` of :ref:`X_69 <X_69>` is the :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` given by

  :g:`A' <A'>` = -a^2 + b^2 + c^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2 : a^2 - b^2 + c^2.

  See the preamble just before X_24307 for the definition of obverse triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0526:

* **X_39158**–**X_39161** — **Foci of the real and imaginary Steiner ellipses**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 2-3, 2020. The foci of the Steiner circumellipse and the Steiner inellipse are all given by the following form for 1st barycentric:

  2\*a^6 - 2\*a^4\*b^2 + a^2\*b^4 - b^6 - 2\*a^4\*c^2 + b^4\*c^2 + a^2\*c^4 + b^2\*c^4 - c^6 - sgn1\*(2\*a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - b^4 - a^2\*c^2 + 2\*b^2\*c^2 - c^4)\*\ :math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}` + const\*S\*sgn2\*Sqrt[-2\*a^8 + 3\*a^6\*b^2 - 2\*a^4\*b^4 + 3\*a^2\*b^6 - 2\*b^8 + 3\*a^6\*c^2 - 2\*a^4\*b^2\*c^2 - 2\*a^2\*b^4\*c^2 + 3\*b^6\*c^2 - 2\*a^4\*c^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2\*c^4 - 2\*b^4\*c^4 + 3\*a^2\*c^6 + 3\*b^2\*c^6 - 2\*c^8 + sgn1\*2\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}`\ \*J^2]

  | The Steiner circumellipse has const = 1. Specifically, X_39158 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,1)
  | X_39159 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,-1)
  | X_39160 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,1)
  | X_39161 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,-1)

  | The Steiner inellipse has const = 2. Specifically, X_39162 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,1)
  | X_39163 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,-1)
  | X_39164 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,1)
  | X_39165 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,-1)

  See the preamble just before X_39202 for vertices of the two ellipses.

.. _guide-preamble-0527:

* **X_39177**–**X_39201** — **Vietnamese points**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, July 3, 2020. Suppose that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`U_{1}V_{1}W_{1} << U_1 V_1 W_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`U_{2}V_{2}W_{2} << U_2 V_2 W_2 >>` are triangles and that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is not perspective to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Let :g:`UVW << U V W >>` be the vertex triangle of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Let :g:`L_{U} <L_U>` = radical axis to the circles (:g:`UV_{1}W_{1} << U V_1 W_1 >>`) and (:g:`UV_{2}W_{2} << U V_2 W_2 >>`), and define :g:`L_{V} <L_V>` and :g:`L_{W} <L_W>` cyclically.

  The lines :g:`L_{U} <L_U>`, :g:`L_{V} <L_V>`, :g:`L_{W} <L_W>` concur in a point Vn(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`), here named the Vietnamese point of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, denoted by Vn(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`). This result is based on Problem 1 in the IMO (International Mathematics Olympiad) 1995 Vietnam TST (Team Selection Test).

  See **Vietnamese Point** (``VietnamesePoint.pdf``).

  Next, suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` are points, and let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = cevian triangle of U. Then

  Vn(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) = a^2 (p + q) (p + r) (u + v) (u + w) (r v - q w) : :

  Let :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` = :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`T_{4} <T_4>` = anticevian triangle of U. Then

  Vn(:g:`T_{3} <T_3>`, :g:`T_{4} <T_4>`) = (p - q - r) (-q u + p v) (u - v - w) (-r u + p w) (b^2 (-(q - r)^3 u^2 w + p^3 u w (-v + w) + p^2 (r u^2 (v - 2 w) - r (v - w)^3 + q u^2 w) + p u (q^2 (v - w) w + r^2 (u^2 - v^2 + 3 v w - 2 w^2) + q r (-u^2 + v^2 - 4 v w + 3 w^2))) + c^2 ((q - r)^3 u^2 v + p^3 u v (v - w) + p u (r^2 v (-v + w) + q^2 (u^2 - 2 v^2 + 3 v w - w^2) + q r (-u^2 + 3 v^2 - 4 v w + w^2)) + p^2 (r u^2 v + q ((v - w)^3 + u^2 (-2 v + w)))) + a^2 (p^3 u v w + (q - r) (r^2 v (-u^2 + v (v - w)) + 2 q r v w (-v + w) + q^2 w (u^2 + (v - w) w)) - p u (q^2 v w + r^2 v w + q r (-u^2 + v^2 - 4 v w + w^2)) - p^2 (q w (u^2 + (v - w) w) + r v (u^2 + v (-v + w))))) : :

  Let :g:`T_{5} <T_5>` = circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`T_{6} <T_6>` = circumcevian triangle of U. Then

  Vn(:g:`T_{5} <T_5>`, :g:`T_{6} <T_6>`) = a^2 (b^2 (r u - p w) + c^2 (p v - q u) - a^2 (q w - r v)) : : , this being the pole wrt the circumcircle of the line :g:`PU <[ P U ]>`

  Let :g:`O <X_3>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = circumcenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. If O, P, U are collinear, then Vn(:g:`T_{5} <T_5>`, :g:`T_{6} <T_6>`) is the infinite point on the line OPU.

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the Vietnamese point of the cevian triangle of X_i and the cevian triangle of X_j is X_k: (1,2,3733), (1,3,39177), (1,4,4560), (1,5,39178), (1,6,39179), (2,3,23286), (2,4,523), (2,5,39180), (2,6,18105), (3,4,15412), (3,5,39181), (3,6,39182), (4,5,39183), (4,6,4580), (5,6,39184)

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the Vietnamese point of the anticevian triangle of X_i and the anticevian triangle of X_j is X_k: (1,2,39185), (1,3,39186), (1,4,39187), (1,5,39188), (1,6,39189), (2,3,39190), (2,4,39192), (2,5,29192), (2,6,39193), (3,5,39194), (3,5,39195), (3,6,38861), (4,5,39196), (4,6,39197), (5,6,39198)

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the Vietnamese point of the circumcevian triangle of X_i and the circumcevian triangle of X_j is X_k: (1,2,4057), (1,3,513), (1,4,39199), (1,5,39200), (1,6,667), (2,3,523), (2,4,523), (2,5,523), (2,6,669), (3,4,523), (3,5,523), (3,6,512), (4,5,523), (4,6,39201), (5,6,34952)

.. _guide-preamble-0528:

* **X_39202**–**X_39207** — **Vertices of the real and imaginary Steiner ellipses**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 3, 2020. The vertices of the Steiner circumellipse and the Steiner inellipse are all given by the following form for 1st barycentric:

  2\*a^6 - 2\*a^4\*b^2 + a^2\*b^4 - b^6 - 2\*a^4\*c^2 + b^4\*c^2 + a^2\*c^4 + b^2\*c^4 - c^6 - sgn1\*(2\*a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - b^4 - a^2\*c^2 + 2\*b^2\*c^2 - c^4)\*\ :math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}` + 2\*const\*S\*sgn2\*Sqrt[:math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}`/(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + 2\*sgn1\*\ :math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}`)]\*Sqrt[sgn1\*(-2\*a^8 + 3\*a^6\*b^2 - 2\*a^4\*b^4 + 3\*a^2\*b^6 - 2\*b^8 + 3\*a^6\*c^2 - 2\*a^4\*b^2\*c^2 - 2\*a^2\*b^4\*c^2 + 3\*b^6\*c^2 - 2\*a^4\*c^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2\*c^4 - 2\*b^4\*c^4 + 3\*a^2\*c^6 + 3\*b^2\*c^6 - 2\*c^8 + 2\*sgn1\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{a^{4} - a^{2} b^{2} + b^{4} - a^{2} c^{2} - b^{2} c^{2} + c^{4}}`\ \*J^2)]

  | The Steiner circumellipse has const = 1. Specifically, X_39202 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,1)
  | X_39203 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (1,-1)
  | X_39204 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,1)
  | X_39205 is given by (sgn1,sgn2) = (-1,-1)

.. _guide-preamble-0529:

* **X_39210**–**X_39228** — **Centers of Vietnamese circles**

  :contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, July 4, 2020. Suppose that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`U_{1}V_{1}W_{1} << U_1 V_1 W_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`U_{2}V_{2}W_{2} << U_2 V_2 W_2 >>` are triangles and that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is not perspective to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Let :g:`UVW << U V W >>` be the vertex triangle of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Let :g:`L_{U} <L_U>` = radical axis to the circles (:g:`UV_{1}W_{1} << U V_1 W_1 >>`) and (:g:`UV_{2}W_{2} << U V_2 W_2 >>`), and define :g:`L_{V} <L_V>` and :g:`L_{W} <L_W>` cyclically.

  The lines :g:`L_{U} <L_U>`, :g:`L_{V} <L_V>`, :g:`L_{W} <L_W>` concur in a point Vn(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`), the Vietnamese point of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, denoted by Vn(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`), introduced in the preamble just before X_39177. Continuing, let :g:`U_{0} <U_0>` be the point, other than U, in which the circles (:g:`UV_{1}W_{1} << U V_1 W_1 >>`) and (:g:`UV_{2}W_{2} << U V_2 W_2 >>`) intersect and define :g:`V_{0} <V_0>` and :g:`W_{0} <W_0>` cyclically. Let :g:`M_{i} <M_i>` be the Miquel point of :g:`T_{i} <T_i>` for i = 1, 2; e.g.,

  :g:`M_{1} <M_1>` = (:g:`UV_{1}W_{1} << U V_1 W_1 >>`)∩(:g:`UV_{1}W_{1} << U V_1 W_1 >>`)∩(:g:`U_{1}V_{1}W << U_1 V_1 W >>`).

  The six points :g:`U_{0} <U_0>`,\ :g:`V_{0} <V_0>`,\ :g:`W_{0} <W_0>`,\ :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`,\ :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`,Vn lie on a circle, here named the Vietnamese circle of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, denoted by v(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`). The center of this circle is denoted by Vo(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`).

  See **Vietnamese Circle** (``VietnameseCircle.pdf``).

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` are distinct with distinct circumcevian triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` then v(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) passes through the circumcenter, O, and is the circumcircle-inverse of the line :g:`PU <[ P U ]>`. If P, U, O are collinear then v(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) is the circle of infinite radius - that is, the line at infinity, and Vo(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`,\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) = O.

  If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = cevian triangle of :g:`U <U>`, then the appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the center of the Vietnamese circle of the cevian triangle of X_i and the cevian triangle of X_j is X_k: (2,3,37084), (3,4,15451), (2,4,523)

.. _guide-preamble-0532:

* **X_39311**–**X_39334** — **Points associated with Paasche triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Dasari Naga Vijay Krishna <dasari-naga-vijay-krishna>`, July 24, 2020. In the preambles just before X_37994 and X_38487 we define points labeled as :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` , :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>`, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>`, :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>`, :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>`, :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>`, :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>` . Here, we define six more points, A''b, A''c, B''c, B''a, C''a, C''b as the respective reflections of :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` in the vertices :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`.; e.g., A''b = :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` in :g:`B <B>`, and A''c = reflection of :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` in :g:`C <C>`, etc.

  Barycentrics for the 6 points are as follows:

  | A"b = 0 : 2R+2c : -c
  | A"c =\ :math:`0 : -b : 2R`\ +2b
  | B"c= :math:`-a : 0 : 2R`\ +2a
  | B"a = 2R+\ :math:`2c : 0 : -c`
  | C''a = 2R+\ :math:`2b : -b : 0`
  | C''b = -a : 2R+2a : 0

  It is easy to verify that the 6 points, A"b , A"c, B"c, B"a, C''a, C''b, lie on an ellipse, here named the **Paasche Reflection Ellipse (PRE)**, given by the barycentric equation

  2 b c (R + a) x^2 + 2 c a (R + b) y^2 + 2 a b (R + c) z^2 + a (4 R^2 + 4 R b + 4 R c + 5 b c) y z + b (4 R^2 + 4 R c + 4 R c + 5 c a) x z + c (4 R^2 + 4 R a + 4 R b + 5 a b ) x y = 0.

  The center of the PRE is

  X_39311 = a(16R^4(b+c-a)+16R^3(b+c)(-a+b+c)+4R^2bc(-4a+5b+5c)+8Rb^2c^2+ab^2c^2) : :

  The PRE is a ":person:`Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` generalized Paasche conic" given by (p,q,r) = (2(R+a),2(R+b),2(R+c)) and (u,v,w) = (-a,-b,-c); see the preamble just before X_38310.

.. _guide-preamble-0533:

* **X_39335**–**X_39344** — **Points on the conic TC(X_1054)**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 24-25, 2020. This preamble extends the preamble just before X_36256, in which, for a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinears), the **trilinear permutation conic** denoted by TC(P), is defined as the conic that passes through the six points

  :math:`p : q : r`,\ :math:`q : r : p`,\ :math:`r : p : q`,\ :math:`p : r : q`,\ :math:`q : p : r`,\ :math:`r : q : p`.

  An equation for TC(P) is (q r + r p + p q)(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - (p^2 + q^2 + r^2)(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  Thus, TC(P) is analogous, and symbolically identical, to the permutation ellipse E(P), defined in the preamble just before X_34341.

  Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinears). For the rest of this paragraph,\ :math:`p:q:r` are trilinears, but all other coordinates, and the equation for TC(P), are in barycentric coordinates. The conic TC(P) passes through the six points

  :math:`ap : bq : cr`,\ :math:`aq : br : cp`,\ :math:`ar : bp : cq`,\ :math:`ap : br : cq`,\ :math:`aq : bp : cr`,\ :math:`ar : bq : cp`.

  (Note that these six points are not six permutations of :math:`ap : bq : cr`.)

  An equation for TC(P) is (q r + r p + p q)(b^2 c^2 x^2 + c^2 a^2 y^2 + a^2 b^2 z^2) - abc(p^2 + q^2 + r^2)(ayz + bzx + cxy) = 0.

  The conic TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`), given by the trilinear equation x^2 + 3 y z + (cyclic) = 0. Define :math:`f(x,y,z) = (x-y)(x-z) - (y-z)^{2}`. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (trilinears) is a point other than :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` =\ :math:`1:1:1` then the point F(X) =\ :math:`f(x,y,z) : f(y,z,x) : f(z,x,y)` is on TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`).

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that the point F(X_i) = X_j is on TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`):

  (2,9359), (4,2636), (6,1054), (19,2639), (31,2640), (100,9324), (171,9355), .

  Let f(:math:`x : y : z`) = (x - y)(x - z) - (y - z)^2. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` and :g:`X' <X'>` = x' : y ' : z' are collinear with :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, then f(:g:`X' <X'>`) = f(X), on TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`).

  If P is on the anti-orthic axis, (the line :ref:`X_44 <X_44>` :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`), then the P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` is on TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`.

  The excenters, with trilinears :math:`-1:1:1`,\ :math:`1:-1:1`,\ :math:`1:1:-1`, also lie on TC(:ref:`X_1054 <X_1054>`). Let :g:`EC <[ E C ]>` denote the circumconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` that passes through the excenters, so that :g:`EC <[ E C ]>` is given by the barycentric equation

  g(a,b,c) y z + g(b,c,a) z x + g(c,a,b) yz = 0, where :math:`g(a,b,c) = (a^{2} + b^{2} - c^{2})(a^{2} - b^{2} + c^{2})`.

  :g:`EC <[ E C ]>` passes through X_i for i = 107, 648, 653, 685, 687, 1897, 6330, 6331, 6335, 6336, 8764, 13149, 15352, 15459, 16080, 16081, 16082, 16813, 17983, 30450, 36306, 36309, 38342. Six examples follow:

  | :ref:`X_2640 <X_2640>` = X_16813-of-excentral-triangle

.. _guide-preamble-0534:

* **X_39345**–**X_39368** — **Points on the permutation ellipse E(X_4440)**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 25-28, 2020. This preamble extends the preamble just before X_34341, in which, for a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), the **barycentric permutation ellipse** denoted by E(P), is defined as the ellipse that passes through these six points:

  :math:`p : q : r`,\ :math:`q : r : p`,\ :math:`r : p : q`,\ :math:`p : r : q`,\ :math:`q : p : r`,\ :math:`r : q : p`.

  The ellipse E(X_4440), is given by the barycentric equation x^2 + 3 y z + (cyclic) = 0. Define :math:`f(x,y,z) = (x-y)(x-z) - (y-z)^{2}`. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (trilinears) is a point other than :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` =\ :math:`1:1:1` then the point F(X) =\ :math:`f(x,y,z) : f(y,z,x) : f(z,x,y)` is on E(X_4440).

  Let f(:math:`x : y : z`) = (x - y)(x - z) - (y - z)^2. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` and :g:`X' <X'>` = x' : y ' : z' are collinear with :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, then f(:g:`X' <X'>`) = f(X), on E(X_4440). Example: if X is on the Euler line (but is not :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`), then f(X) = X_39352.

.. _guide-preamble-0535:

* **X_39371**–**X_39372** — **Points associated with the Cip transform**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 3, 2020. The *Cip* transform is introduced in **Suren, Moses, and Kimberling, "The Circumcevian-Inversion Perspector of Two Triangles",** to appear in *Journal for Geometry and Graphics,* as follows: In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` be a point that is not on one of the sidelines, :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let Γ be the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`DEF << D E F >>` be the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`; that is, D is the point, other than A, in which the line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` meets Γ, and likewise for the vertices :g:`E <E>` and F. Let :g:`X <X>`, :g:`Y <Y>`, :g:`Z <Z>` be the reflections of :g:`P <P>` in :g:`D <D>`, :g:`E <E>`, :g:`F <F>`, respectively, and let :g:`X' <X'>`,\ :g:`Y' <Y'>`,\ :g:`Z' <Z'>` be the Γ-inverse of :g:`X <X>`, :g:`Y <Y>`, :g:`Z <Z>`, respectively. Let :g:`P' <P'>` = :g:`BY' <[ B Y' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CZ' <[ C Z' ]>`. Then :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`X'Y'Z' << X' Y' Z' >>` are perspective triangles, and :g:`P' <P'>` is the **circumcevian-inversion perspector** of :g:`X'Y'Z' << X' Y' Z' >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The mapping P → :g:`P' <P'>` is the **Cip transform.**

  If Λ is a conic that passes through the circumcenter, O, then it is the *Cip* transform of a circular cubic. If you have Geogebra, you can view seven examples, named according to the choice of Λ:

  | **CIP_ABCIO** (``CIP_ABCIO.ggb``).
  | **CIP_BrocardCircle** (``CIP_BrocardCircle.ggb``).
  | **CIP_FeuerbachOfTangential** (``CIP_FeuerbachOfTangential.ggb``).
  | **CIP_Jerabek** (``CIP_Jerabek.ggb``).
  | **CIP_KiepertOfMedial** (``CIP_KiepertOfMedial.ggb``).
  | **CIP_Lester** (``CIP_Lester.ggb``).
  | **CIP_Thomson-Gibert-Moses hyperbola** (``CIP_Thomson-Gibert-Moses%20hyperbola``).

  Names for the seven circular cubics are introduced here as **ABCIO circular cubic**, **Brocard circular cubic**, **Feuerbach-of-tangential circular cubic**, **Jerabek circular cubic**, **Kiepert-of-medial circular cubic**, **Lester circular cubic**, and **Thomson-Gibert-Moses-hyperbola circular cubic**. For each of these, O is the *Cip*-image of :g:`O <O>` and every point on the infinity line. Aside from :g:`O <O>`, two of the seven circular cubics have *Cip*-fixed points: :ref:`X_102 <X_102>` on the ABCIO circular cubic, and :ref:`X_110 <X_110>` on the Thomson-Gibert-Moses-hyperbola circular cubic.

  Another point on the ABCIO circular cubic is X_38599, and two on the Jerabek circular cubic are X_35372 and X_35465;

  If Λ is a conic that does not pass through :g:`O <O>`, then the curve having Λ as *Cip* image has formal degree 4. An example is the Steiner circumquartic , see **CIP_SteinerCircum** (``CIP_SteinerCircum.ggb``), which passes through X_12188.

.. _guide-preamble-0536:

* **X_39382**–**X_39640** — **and X_39628-X_39640, Circumcenters of circumcevian polar triangles**

  based on notes from Suren and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (August-September, 2020). Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the circumcevian triangle of a point :g:`P <P>` in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`L_{a} <L_a>` be the polar of :g:`A' <A'>` wrt the circumcircle of :g:`BPC << B P C >>`, and define :g:`L_{b} <L_b>` and :g:`L_{c} <L_c>` cyclically. Let :g:`A″ <A″>` = :g:`L_{b} <L_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{c} <L_c>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named the **circumcevian polar triangle** of P. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), then the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is given by :math:`u : v : w`, where [formulas omitted here].

  The circumcenter of :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`, denoted by MSV(P), is given by

  a^2/(c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*p^2\*q + 2\*a^2\*c^2\*p\*q^2 - b^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*p^2\*r + a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*q^2\*r - 2\*a^2\*b^2\*p\*r^2 - a^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r^2) : :

  | Theorems:
  | MSV(P) = circumcircle-antipode of the Vu circumcircle point of P (defined in the preamble just before X_38451.
  | If P lies on the cubic K269, then MSV(P) = :ref:`X_109 <X_109>`.
  | If P lies on the Neuberg, then MSV(P) = :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`.
  | If P lies on the cubic K270, then MSV(P) = :ref:`X_112 <X_112>`.
  | If P lies on the cubic K1156, then MSV(P) = :ref:`X_1296 <X_1296>`.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that MSV(X_i) = X_j:

  (2,1296), (3,110), (4,110), (5,1291), (6,1296), (7,20219), (8,39628), (9,28291), (13,110), (14,110), (15,110), (16,110), [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0537:

* **X_39389**–**X_39401** — **Circlecevian Perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, Auguist 21, 2020. The circlecevian triangle of a point is defined in the preamble just before X_37841, as follows: Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than P, in which the line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` meets the circle (:g:`PBC << P B C >>`), and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically; the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is called the circlecevian triangle of :g:`P <P>` with respect to triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` by :person:`Floor van Lamoen <floor-van-lamoen>` (:cite:`Hyacinthos #10039 <hyacinthos>`); see the preambles just before X_34520 and X_34892. Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the circlecevian triangle of P. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the point, other than A, of intersection of the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and :g:`AB_{1}C_{1} << A B_1 C_1 >>`), and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically. Theb :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is perspective to :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`, and the perspector, here named the **circlecevian perspector of P**, is given by

  V(P) = a^2 (c^2 p q^2 + b^2 p^2 r + 2 b^2 p q r + a^2 q^2 r + b^2 p r^2) (c^2 p^2 q + c^2 p q^2 + 2 c^2 p q r + b^2 p r^2 + a^2 q r^2) : :

  Let :g:`P* <P*>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`; then V(P) = V(:g:`P* <P*>`).

  See **Circlecevian Perspector** (``CirclecevianPerspector.pdf``). (Vu Thanh Tung)
