.. _guide-preamble-0538:

* **X_39402**–**X_39411** — **Vu Isodynamic Perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, August 21, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` be the 1st isodnamic point, :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, of triangle :g:`PBC << P B C >>`, and define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the point of intersection, other than A, of the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (:g:`AB_{1}C_{1} << A B_1 C_1 >>`), and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is perpsective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector, V(P), is here named the **1st Vu isodynamic perspector**. Note that :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of V(P).

  If the above construction is carried out with the 2nd isodynamic point, :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`, instead of :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, the resulting perspector, T(P), is the **2nd Vu isodynamic perspector**.

  Barycentrics were found by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (August 22, 2020):

  | V(P) = a^2/(:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*a^2\*((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r - b^2\*r^2 - c^2\*q^2) - 2\*(a^2\*q\*r + b^2\*r\*p + c^2\*p\*q)\*S) : :
  | T(P) = a^2/(:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*a^2\*((a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r - b^2\*r^2 - c^2\*q^2) + 2\*(a^2\*q\*r + b^2\*r\*p + c^2\*p\*q)\*S) : :

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j: (1,39402), (2,39404), (3,2981), (4,39406), (5,39408), (6,39410)

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that T(X_i) = X_j: (1,39403), (2,39405), (3,6151), (4,39407), (5,39409), (6,39411)

  See **Isodynamic Perspector** (``IsodynamicPerspector.pdf``). (Vu Thanh Tung)

.. _guide-preamble-0539:

* **X_39453** — **Vu Isogonal Perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, August 26, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` be a point such that P and its :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`, :g:`P' <P'>`, are distinct finite points. Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and let :g:`A'_{1}B'_{1}C'_{1} << A'_1 B'_1 C'_1 >>` be the pedal triangle of :g:`P' <P'>`. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the point of intersection, other than A, of the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (:g:`AA_{1}A'_{1} << A A_1 A'_1 >>`), and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is perpsective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector, V(P), is here named the **Vu isogonal perspector** of P. Note that V(:g:`P' <P'>`) = V(P), and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of V(P).

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), then

  V(P) = 1/(p\*(b^2\*r + SA\*q)\*(c^2q + SA\*r)) : :

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j: (2,39353), (3,4), (4,4), (5,39454), (6,39353), (7,39455), (8,39456), (9,39457), (10,39458), (31,39459), (32,39460), (75,39459), (76, 39460)

  Generalization (Vu Thanh Tung, August 28, 2020):

  **Theorem:** In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` and :g:`A'_{1} <A'_1>` be points on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` such that B, C, :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, and :g:`A'_{1} <A'_1>` are distinct. Define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically, and define :g:`B'_{1} <B'_1>` and :g:`C'_{1} <C'_1>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the point of intersection, other than A, of the circles (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) and (:g:`AA_{1}A'_{1} << A A_1 A'_1 >>`), and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>`, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically. Then :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` if and only if the points :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A'_{1} <A'_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B'_{1} <B'_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C'_{1} <C'_1>` lie on a conic.

  **Corollary:** Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and let :g:`A'_{1}B'_{1}C'_{1} << A'_1 B'_1 C'_1 >>` be the cevian triangle of :g:`P' <P'>`. Then the six vertices lie on the bicevian conic of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>`, and the perspector of the triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is the barycentric product :g:`P*P' <[ P* P' ]>`.

  See **Isogonal Perspector** (``IsogonalPerspector.pdf``) and **Six Points Conic** (``SixPointsConic.pdf``). (Vu Thanh Tung)

  Let :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` be the center of the involution {B, C}, {:g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A'_{1} <A'_1>`} (as in the preamble just before X_14782) and define :g:`O_{b} <O_b>` and :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` cyclically. The points :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, :g:`O_{b} <O_b>`, :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` are collinear on a line whose :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` is the Vu-isogonal perspector of :g:`P <P>` or :g:`P' <P'>`. (:person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 3, 2021.)

.. _guide-preamble-0540:

* **X_39469**–**X_39474** — **Yiu infinity points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 30, 2020. Suppose that :g:`F <F>` =\ :math:`f : g : h` (barycentrics) is a point on the infinity line, L. The :term:`orthopoint <orthopoint>` (a.k.a. orthogonal conjugate) of :g:`F <F>`, denoted here by :g:`F' <F'>` =\ :math:`f' : g' : h'` also lies on L. In *Introduction to the Geometry of the Triangle,*, :person:`Paul Yiu <paul-yiu>` notes that

  :math:`S_{A}`\ \*f\*f' + :math:`S_{B}`\ \*g\*g' + :math:`S_{C}`\ \*h\*h' = 0.

  Equialvently, the point :g:`F″ <F″>` = :math:`S_{A}`\ \*f\*f' : :math:`S_{B}`\ \*g\*g' : :math:`S_{C}`\ \*h\*h'

  also lies on L. The point :g:`F″ <F″>` is here named the **Yiu infinity point of F**. Note that :g:`F″ <F″>` = :g:`F*F' <[ F* F' ]>`/H, where H = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, the orthocenter.

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_i is on :g:`L <L>`, X_j = orthopoint of X_i, and X_k = Yiu infinity point of X_i:

  | (30, 523, 9033)
  | (511, 512, 39469)
  | (512, 511, 39469)
  | (513, 517, 8677)
  | (514, 516, 39470)
  | (515, 522, 39471)
  | (516, 514, 39470)
  | (517, 513, 8677)
  | (519, 3667, 39472)
  | (522, 515, 39471)
  | (523, 30, 9033)
  | (525, 1503, 39473)
  | (542, 690, 39574)
  | (690, 542, 39474)
  | (1503, 525, 39475)

  There is a connection between Yiu infinity point and the Psi mapping (:cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 80): If Q is the the Yiu infinite point of a point :g:`P <P>` and the orthopoint of :g:`P <P>`), and if U is a point on the line of :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, then Psi(U) is the isogonal conjugate of :g:`Q <Q>`. (Peter Moses, January 27, 2021)

* **X_39475**–**X_39481** — **Centers of circumcircle-inversion circles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 1, 2020. Suppose that Γ is the circle with powers (u,v,w) -- that is, u = power of :g:`A <A>` with respect to the circle. and v and w are defined cyclically. Suppose that L is a line, given by p x + q y + r z = 0 (barycentrics), that does not pass through :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. The Γ-inverse of :g:`L <L>` is a circle that passes through :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. This circle is here named the **Γ-inversion circle of L**, denoted by ((Γ, L)). The center of ((Γ, L)) is given by

  :math:`f(a,b,c,u,v,w,p,q,r) : f(b,c,a,v,w,u,q,r,p) : f(c,a,b,w,u,v,r,p,q)`, where [long equation omitted here].

  In particular, the center of ((circumcircle, L)) is the point

  a^2\*(a^2\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*p - b^2\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2)\*q - c^2\*(a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*r) : : , and the squared radius of ((circumcircle, L)) is

  (a^4\*b^4\*c^4\*(a^2\*p^2 + (-a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*p\*q + b^2\*q^2 + (-a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*p\*r + (a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r + c^2\*r^2))/((a + b - c)\*(a - b + c)\*(-a + b + c)\*(a + b + c)\*(a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*p - b^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*q - c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*r)^2).

  If P and :g:`P' <P'>` are distinct points on :g:`L <L>`, then ((circumcircle, L)) is the Vietnamese circle of the circumcevian triangles of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>`; see the preamble just before X_39210 and centers X_39219-X_39228.

  Perspectors:of triangles: [list omitted here]

.. _guide-preamble-0545:

* **X_39667**–**X_39678** — **Points associated with the 7th Brocard triangle**

  based on notes from :person:`Dan Reznik <dan-reznik>` and by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 14, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`O <X_3>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, the circumcenter. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than O, in which the line :g:`AO <[ A X_3 ]>` meets the Brocard circle, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, here named the **7th Brocard triangle**; the first six Brocard triangles are defined by :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>` at `Brocard triangles and related cubics <http://bernard-gibert.fr/gloss/brocardtriangles.html>`__.

  The 7th Brocard triangle is perspective to the following triangles, with perspector O: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, Lucas central, 2nd Hyacinth, and the Lucas antipodal and other Lucas triangles. Also, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to the :term:`2nd Brocard triangle <2nd-brocard-triangle>`, with perspector :ref:`X_184 <X_184>`, and to the :term:`symmedial triangle <symmedial-triangle>`, with perspector X_39643.

  The A vertex of the 7th Brocard triangle is given by

  :g:`A' <A'>` = a^4 + b^4 + c^4 - 2\*b^2\*c^2 : b^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2) : c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2).

  Let KK denote the cubic pK(X_39644,X_39645). If P is a point on KK, then the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` is perspective to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`. The cubic KK passes through the points X_i for i = 3, 6, 230, 5253, 6530, 8770.

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` under the Brocard porism (in which the circumcircle and Brocard inellipse are fixed; see :ref:`X_39 <X_39>`) can be viewed at `Loci of Centers of Ellipse-Mounted Triangles <https://dan-reznik.github.io/ellipse-mounted-loci-p5js/?sc=11.849&cx=181&cy=270&rot=90&bg=050519&lc1=vtx&mt1=brocard&tr1=brocard7&lc2=trilins&Xn2=3&mt2=brocard&tr2=brocard7&lc3=brocard_1&mt3=brocard&tr3=brocard7&lc4=brocard_2&mt4=brocard&tr4=brocard7>`__.) (Dan Reznik, September 14, 2020).

  See also `Brocard Porism: locus of 1st, 2nd, 5th, and 7th Brocard Triangles Vertices are Circles <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_bK-BCQv24A&feature=youtu.be>`__.) (Dan Reznik, September 21, 2020).

  Let :g:`A″ <A″>` = circumcircle-inverse of :g:`A' <A'>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`, here named the **8th Brocard triangle**, is given by

  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = 2\*a^4 : b^2\*(-a^2 + b^2 - c^2) : c^2\*(-a^2 - b^2 + c^2)
  | :g:`B″ <B″>` = a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) : 2\*b^4 : c^2\*(-a^2 - b^2 + c^2)
  | :g:`C″ <C″>` = a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) : b^2\*(-a^2 + b^2 - c^2) : 2\*c^4

  Note that :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are collinear (on the Lemoine axis), so that :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is a degenerate triangle.

  Let :g:`A* <A*>` = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`A″ <A″>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is here named the **9th Brocard triangle**. Barycentrics are given by

  | :g:`A* <A*>` = -((a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)) : 2\*a^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2) : 2\*a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)
  | :g:`B* <B*>` = 2\*b^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2) : -((a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2)) : 2\*b^2\*(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2)
  | :g:`C* <C*>` = 2\*c^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2) : 2\*c^2\*(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2) : -((a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2))

  The vertices :g:`A* <A*>`, :g:`B* <B*>`, :g:`C* <C*>` lies on the Steiner circumellipse.

  The 7th Brocard triangle is the dual-of-:term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` of the :term:`1st Brocard triangle <1st-brocard-triangle>`, and also the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of the orthic-of-1st-Brocard triangle. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, September 30, 2020)

  The 9th Brocard triangle is the Steiner-orthic triangle (the Steiner circumellipse counterpart to the circumorthic triangle). (Randy Hutson, September 30, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0546:

* **X_39693**–**X_39749** — **Cevian Centroid Isogonal Perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, September 18, 2020. Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`G_{a} <G_a>` be the centroid of :g:`PB_{1}C_{1} << P B_1 C_1 >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`G_{a} <G_a>` with respect to :g:`AB_{1}C_{1} << A B_1 C_1 >>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is given by

  V(P) = a^2 q r (p + q)(p + r)(p + 2q + 2r) : :

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j: (1,4658), (2,6), (3,49094), (4,631), (5,39667), (6,39668), (7,10389), (8,3361), (9,39669), (10,39670), (31,39671), (32,39672), (75,39673), (76,39674), (83,39675), (141,39676), (560,39677), (561,39678)

  See **Cevian Centroid Isogonal Perspector** (``CevianCentroidIsogonalPerspector.pdf``)

.. _guide-preamble-0547:

* **X_39765**–**X_39770** — **Points on cubics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, September 28, 2020.

  Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p(a,b,c) : p(b,c,a) : p(c,a,b)` is an polynomial :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` such that the point (b-c)p(a,b,c) : (c-a)p(b,c,a) : (a-b)p(c,a,b) is on the line at infinity; i.e.,

  (b-c)p(a,b,c) + (c-a)p(b,c,a) + (a-b)p(c,a,b) = 0.

  Let χ(P) denote the cubic given by

  (b+c)p(a,b,c)(y-z)(x+y)(x+z) + (c+a)p(b,c,a)(z-x)(y+z)(y+x) + (a+b)p(c,a,b)(x-y)(z+x)(z+y) = 0.

  This is the cubic pK(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`),\ :g:`P* <P*>`), where :g:`P* <P*>` = (b + c)\*p - (a + c)\*q - (a + b)\*r : :

  Let :g:`K_aK_bK_c << K_a K_b K_c >>` denote the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. It is easy to check that the following 9 points lie on χ(P): :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`K_a <K_a>`, :g:`K_b <K_b>`, :g:`K_c <K_c>`, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_75 <X_75>` .

  It is also easy to check that if U is a point on χ(P), then the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of U also lies on χ(P). This section consists of isotomic conjugates of points on cubics χ(P) for selected points :g:`P <P>`. In column 1 of the following table, the appearance of u(a,b,c) in a row means that the points indicated in column 2 lie on the cubic

  u(a,b,c)(y-z)(x+y)(x+z) + u(b,c,a)(z-x)(y+z)(y+x) + u(c,a,b)(x-y)(z+x)(z+y) = 0;

  so that the point :g:`P <P>` is given by u(a,b,c) = (b+c)p(a,b,c). The appearance of {i,j} in column 2 means that {X_i,X_j} are a pair of isotomic conjugate points that lie on χ(P) [table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0548:

* **X_39801**–**X_39913** — **Points on cubics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 1, 2020. Let :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` denote the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>`. The cubic given by

  a(b+c)^2 (b^2+c^2-a^2-bc)(y-z)(x+y)(x+z) + b(c+a)^2 (c^2+a^2-b^2-ca)(z-x)(y+z)(y+x) + c(a+b^2) (a^2+b^2-c^2-ab)(x-y)(z+x)(z+y) = 0

  is a self-isotomic cubic that passes through the following points: :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`, :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`, and also the six points X_39765 - X_39770.

.. _guide-preamble-0550:

* **X_39994**–**X_40106** — **Points on cubics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, October 7, 2020. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p(a,b,c) : p(b,c,a) : p(c,a,b)` is an polynomial :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` such that the point (b-c)p(a,b,c) : (c-a)p(b,c,a) : (a-b)p(c,a,b) is on the line at infinity; i.e.,

  (b-c)p(a,b,c) + (c-a)p(b,c,a) + (a-b)p(c,a,b) = 0.

  Let ζ(P) denote the cubic given by

  (b+c)p(a,b,c)(cy-bz)(bx+ay)(cx+az) + (c+a)p(b,c,a)(az-cx)(cy+bz)(ay+bx) + (a+b)p(c,a,b)(bx-ay)(az+cx)(bz+cy) = 0.

  Let :g:`J_aJ_bJ_c << J_a J_b J_c >>` denote the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. It is easy to check that the following 9 points lie on ζ(P): :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`J_a <J_a>`, :g:`J_b <J_b>`, :g:`J_c <J_c>`, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` .

  It is also easy to check that if U is a point on ζ(P), then the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of U also lies on ζ(P). This section consists of :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of points on cubics ζ(P) for selected points :g:`P <P>`. In column 1 of the following table, the appearance of u(a,b,c) in a row means that the points indicated in column 2 lie on the cubic

  u(a,b,c)(cy-bz)(bx+ay)(cx+az) + u(b,c,a)(az-cx)(cy+bz)(a+bx) + u(c,a,b)(bx-ay)(az+cx)(bz+cy) = 0;

  so that the point :g:`P <P>` is given by u(a,b,c) = (b+c)p(a,b,c). This is the cubic pK(:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,\ :g:`P* <P*>`), where :g:`P* <P*>` = a\*((b + c)\*p - (a + c)\*q - (a + b)\*r) : :

  The appearance of {i,j} in column 2 means that {X_i,X_j} are a pair of isogonal conjugate points that lie on ζ(P). [ Table omitted here]

.. _guide-preamble-0552:

* **X_40051**–**X_40070** — **Dao-perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 14, 2020. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be two perspective triangles, neither inscribed in the other. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` be the triangle bounded by the lines :g:`BC' <[ B C' ]>`, :g:`CA' <[ C A' ]>`, :g:`AB' <[ A B' ]>` and let :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` be the triangle bounded by the lines :g:`BA' <[ B A' ]>`, :g:`CB' <[ C B' ]>`, :g:`AC' <[ A C' ]>`. Then the vertices of :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` lie all on a conic (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, October 13, 2020). This conic will be named here the **Dao-perspeconic of ABC and A'B'C'**.

  The appearance of (T, n) in the following partial list means that the center of the Dao-perspeconic of triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and T is X_n:

  (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 3), (anti-Aquila, 40051), (anti-Ara, 40052), (anti-Conway, 15648), (2nd anti-Conway, 15649), (anti-excenters-reflections, 40053),[and others]

  Definitions of all triangles above mentioned can be found in the **index of triangles** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

  < p>

.. _guide-preamble-0553:

* **X_40139**–**X_40173** — **Hodpieces**

  :This preamble is based on notes received from Radosław Żak (October 29, 2020) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (October 29-30, 2020). In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` be a point, not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`DEF << D E F >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. The :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of line :g:`EF <[ E F ]>` is a conic. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the center of of the conic, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`BB' <[ B B' ]>`, :g:`CC' <[ C C' ]>` concur in a point here named the **hodpiece** of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by H(P). The name *hodpiece* is taken from James Joyce's book, *Finnegans Wake.* The unique point P such that :math:`H(P) = P`, indexed below as X_40139, is named the **Bloom point** after Leopold Bloom, the main character in Joyce's *Ulysses*. The point H(:ref:`X_5 <X_5>`) = X_40140 is the **Dedalus point**, and the H(:ref:`X_7 <X_7>`) = X_40141, the **Zana point**.

  An `article (in Polish) <http://www.deltami.edu.pl/delta/redakcja/konkurs_prac_uczniowskich/2020/09/26/zak-radoslaw.pdf>`__ about hodpieces by Żak won a gold medal in a competition for high school students organized by the Polish Mathematical Society. For an English translation, see **Isogonal conjugate and a few properties of the point X(25)** (``Isogonal%20conjugate%20and%20a%20few%20properties%20of%20the%20point%20X(25).pdf``).

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics), then :math:`H(P) = a^{2}/(p (-a^{2}/p + b^{2}/q + c^{2}/r)`: : .

  Let :g:`P* <P*>` = P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. Then :math:`H(P) = isogonal conjugate of P*-cross conjugate of P`.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that H(X_i) = X_j: (1,57), (2,25), (3,459), (4,394), (5,40140), (6,2), (7,40141), (9,1422), (10,40142), (13,40156), (14,40157), (15, 40158), (16,40159), [and others]

  Note that H(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) = H(X_8115) = H(X_8116) = :ref:`X_25 <X_25>`.

  For Vu Thanh Tung's generalization to U-hodpieces, see the preamble just before X_40212.

.. _guide-preamble-0554:

* **X_40197**–**X_40211** — **Points associated with Vu parallels conics**

  based on notes received from Vu Thanh Tung, October 31, 2020. > In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u:v:w` (barycentrics) be points. Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` be the point on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` such that :g:`PA_{1} <[ P A_1 ]>` is parallel to :g:`AU <[ A U ]>`, and define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` be the point on :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` such that :g:`PA_{2} <[ P A_2 ]>` is parallel to :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. The six points :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` lies on a conic, here named the **Vu parallels conic of P and U**. See **Vu Parallels Conic** (``VuParallelsConic.pdf``).

  :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (October 31, 2020) found that V(P,U) = [long omitted expression] and T(P,U) = [long omitted expression]

  Let V(P,U) denote the center, and T(P,U) the perspector, of the Vu parallels conic of :g:`P <P>` and U. The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that V(X_i,X_j) = X_k: (1,2,40197), (1,6,40199), (2,3,40201), (2,4,40203), (2,6,40305), (2,6,40205), (3,4,14767), (3,5,6709), (3,6,40209)

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that T(X_i,X_j) = X_k: (1,2,40198), (1,6,40200), (2,3,40202), (2,4,40204), (2,6,40206), (3,4,40207), (3,5,40208), (3,6,40210)

.. _guide-preamble-0555:

* **X_40212**–**X_40218** — **U-Hodpieces**

  based on notes received from Vu Thanh Tung, November 1, 2020. The definition of hodpiece in the preamble just before X_40137 generalizes as follows. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point, not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`DEF << D E F >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. Let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u:v:w` be a point. The P-:term:`reciprocal conjugate <reciprocal-conjugate>` of U (defined as :math:`u/p : v/q : w/r` in the Glossary of ETC), of the line :g:`EF <[ E F ]>` is a conic. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the center of the conic, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`BB' <[ B B' ]>`, :g:`CC' <[ C C' ]>` concur in the point

  u / (p\*(-u/p + v/q + w/r)) : v / (q\*(u/p - v/q + w/r)) : w / (r\*(u/p + v/q - w/r)),

  here named the **U-hodpiece of P**, so that the hodpiece of :g:`P <P>` is the :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`-hodpiece of :g:`P <P>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0556:

* **X_40236**–**X_40296** — **Tetrahedral projections**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 4, 2020. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle on a plane :g:`XY <[ X Y ]>`. Consider three segments :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`BB' <[ B B' ]>`, :g:`CC' <[ C C' ]>` with lengths :g:`U <U>`, :g:`V <V>`, :g:`W <W>`, respectively, and each having one fixed extreme in :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`, respectively, and the other extremes free to move outside the plane :g:`XY <[ X Y ]>`. Suppose that these segments are rotated around their fixed extremes in such a way that their free extremes coincide at a point :g:`D <D>`, forming, together with the sides of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the edges of a tetrahedron ABCD. Let :g:`D* <D*>` be the orthogonal projection of :g:`D <D>` on the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The point :g:`D* <D*>` is here named the **tetrahedral projection of ABC by (U, V, W)** or the **tetrahedral projection of ABC to A'B'C'**. Then

  | :g:`D* <D*>` = :math:`a^{2}` (SA - :math:`U^{2})` + SB :math:`W^{2}` + SC :math:`V^{2}` : :math:`b^{2}` (SB - :math:`V^{2})` + SC :math:`U^{2}` + SA :math:`W^{2}` : :math:`c^{2}` (SC - :math:`W^{2})` + SA :math:`V^{2}` + SB :math:`U^{2}` (1)
  | Z(D), the Z-coordinate of D , i.e., the height of the point D measured from :g:`D* <D*>` and orthogonally to the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, is given by:
  | Z(D) = ±\ :math:`\sqrt{∑ [2 (a^{2} U^{2} + V^{2} W^{2}) S_{A} - a^{2} U^{4}] - (a b c)^{2}}`/(2 S) (2)

  Equation (2) shows that D is real or imaginary according to the sign of the quantity under the square root. If this quantity is zero then D and :g:`D* <D*>` coincide on the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Moreover, the ± sign indicates that there are two possible points :g:`D <D>` and :g:`D' <D'>`, each in different sides with respect to the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Equation (1) shows that if :g:`U <U>`, :g:`V <V>`, :g:`W <W>` are real numbers then :g:`D* <D*>` is always real and also that, if :g:`U <U>`, :g:`V <V>`, :g:`W <W>` are cyclic values, i.e., if there exists a degree-1 function ƒ(a,b,c) such that :g:`U <U>`\ =ƒ(a,b,c), V=ƒ(b,c,a) and W=ƒ(c,a,b), then :g:`D* <D*>` is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`.

  | The appearance of (ƒ(a,b,c), n) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` by (:g:`U <U>`\ =ƒ(a,b,c), V=ƒ(b,c,a), W=ƒ(c,a,b)) is X_n:
  | (a, 20), (b+c, 962), (-a+b+c, 8148), (:math:`\sqrt{b^{2}+c^{2}}`, 4), (:math:`\sqrt{-a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}`, 382) The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of X_i is X_j: (2, 546), (4, 389), (7, 65), (39158, 3), (39159, 3) The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of X_i is X_j: (1, 1490), (2, 3146), (6, 40285) The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to the circumcevian triangle of X_i is X_j: (1, 40257), (3, 3), (4, 6241), (186, 74), (8697, 8697) The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to the circumanticevian triangle of X_i is X_j: (1, 40256), (2, 12111), (6, 3) The appearance of (T, n) in the following list means that the tetrahedral projection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to the triangle :g:`T <T>` is X_n:
  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 3), (anti-Aquila, 13624), (anti-Ara, 1885), (anti-Artzt, 5077), [and others]

  Definitions of all triangles above mentioned can be found in the **index of triangles** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

  Preamble edited on June 28, 2022.

.. _guide-preamble-0557:

* **X_40297**–**X_40305** — **Points associated with the power curve**

  contributed by Suren, November 4, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the locus of a point :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}` (barycentrics [or trilinears]) as t varies through the real numbers is the **power curve**, PC(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`), of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. (The term is introduced in :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, ":term:`Major Centers <major-center>` of Triangles," *American Math. Monthly* 104 (1997), 431-438.) Note that PC(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) passes through X_i for i = 1,2,6,31,75,76, and that eliminating t shows that PC(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) is given by the equations

  (log x)/(log a) = (log y)/(log b) = (log z)/(log c).

  (Here, "log" signifies the natural logarithm, but equivalent equations result under change of base for "log".) Centers X_40297-X_40305 involve the line tangent to :g:`PC <[ P C ]>` at :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`.

  In general, the line tangent to the power curve at a point :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}` has the direction (i.e., a point on the infinity line) given by

  (a\*c)\ :sup:`t` log(a/c) + (a\*b)\ :sup:`t` log(a/b) : : ,

  and the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of that point is the point :math:`a^{t}` log(c/b) : :math:`b^{t}` log(a/c) : :math:`c^{t}` log(b/a).

.. _guide-preamble-0558:

* **X_40306**–**X_40315** — **Points on Vu orthogonal conics**

  based on notes contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, November 5, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` and U be points. Let :g:`L <L>` be the line through :g:`P <P>` perpendicular to line :g:`AU <[ A U ]>`, and let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = L∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically. Let :g:`L' <L'>` be the line through :g:`U <U>` perpendicular to line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`. and :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`L' <L'>`\ ∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. The six points :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` lie on a conic, here named the **Vu orthogonal conic** of :g:`P <P>` and U, denoted by VOC(P,U).

  Let V(P,U) denote the center, and T(P,U) the perspector, of VOC(P,U). Note that VOC(U,P) = VOC(P,U), V(U,P) = V(P,U), and T(U,P) = T(P,U).

  See **Vu Orthogonal Conic** (``VuOrthogonalConic.pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0559:

* **X_40328**–**X_40336** — **Osiris points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 9, 2020. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P a point and Q the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of P. Denote by :g:`A' <A'>` the centroid of the quadrangle BCPQ and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>`. cyclically. Then :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, :g:`BB' <[ B B' ]>`, :g:`CC' <[ C C' ]>` concur at a point O(P)=O(Q), here named the **Osiris point of P**.

  For :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :math:`x:y:z` (barycentrics), O(P) = (y^2+5\*y\*z+z^2)\*x+2\*(y+z)\*(x^2+y\*z) : :

  | The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the Osiris point of X_i is X_j:
  | (1, 40328), (2, 2), (3, 40329), (4, 40330), (5, 40331), (6, 40332), (7, 40333), (8, 40333), (13, 40334), (14, 40335), (69, 40330), (75, 40328), (76, 40332), [and others]

  If :g:`P <P>` or :g:`Q <Q>` lie on the cubic K953, then its Osiris point lies on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  The mapping O takes certain cubics onto lines: O(K296) = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, O(K185) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, O(K953) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. (:person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 10, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0560:

* **X_40345**–**X_40346** — **Points on the tangential power curve**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, November 11, 2020. Let PC(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) by the power curve; i.e., the locus of the point :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}` (barycentrics) as t varies through the real numbers. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}` for fixed t, then the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` is the point :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`a^{-t} : b^{-t} : c^{-t}`. Equations for the lines tangent to PC(:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) at :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` are found using Suren's points on the line at infinity; see the preamble just before X_40296. If P is not the centroid of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then the tangent lines are distinct, and they meet in the point

  :g:`P″ <P″>` = :math:`a^{t}(b^{2t} - c^{2t})`/(log b - log c) : :math:`b^{t}(c^{2t} - a^{2t})`/(log c - log a) : :math:`c^{t}(a^{2t} - b^{2t})`/(log a - log b)

  The locus of :g:`P″ <P″>` as t varies through the positive real numbers is here named the (barycentric) **tangential power curve.**

  The corresponding normal lines at :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` meet in a point whose locus is the **normal power curve**.

  The trilinear tangential and normal power curves are defined in the same manner using trilinear coordindates throughout, using :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` instead of isotomic.

.. _guide-preamble-0561:

* **X_40359**–**X_40375** — **Ceva-conjugates associated with the power curve**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 17, 2020. Let P(t) =\ :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}`, on the power curve, as in the preambles just before X_40297 and X_40345. The P(t)-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of P(u), denoted by P(t)©P(u) is given by

  :math:`a^{u}(-a^{u-t} + b^{u-t} + c^{u-t})` : :math:`b^{u}(a^{u-t} - b^{u-t} + c^{u-t})` : :math:`c^{u}(a^{u-t} + b^{u-t} - c^{u-t})`,

  P(t)©P(u) is the perspector of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P(t) and the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of P(u).

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that P(t)©P(u) = X_k:

  (-9,-1,33807), (-8,-8,40359), (-8,-6,40360), (-8,-2,40361), (-8,0,33797), (-7,-1,33806), (-7,1,33791), (-6,-6,40362), (-6,-4,40050), [and others]

  For fixed t = :math:`t_{0}` and variable u, the locus of :math:`P(t_{0})`\ ©P(u) is here named the :math:`P(t_{0})`\ ©P(u)-Ceva power curve. For fixed variable t and fixed u = :math:`u_{0}`, the locus of P(t)©\ :math:`P(u_{0})` is here named the P(t)©\ :math:`P(u_{0})`-Ceva power curve.

.. _guide-preamble-0562:

* **X_40376**–**X_40383** — **Complements and anticomplements associated with the power curve**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 19, 2020. Suppose that P(t) =\ :math:`a^{t} : b^{t} : c^{t}` (barycentrics) is a point on the power curve. The :term:`complement <complement>` of P(t) is the point :math:`b^{t}` + :math:`c^{t}` : :math:`c^{t}` + :math:`a^{t}` : :math:`a^{t}` + :math:`b^{t}`. The :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of P(t) is the point -:math:`a^{t}` + :math:`b^{t}` + :math:`c^{t}` : :math:`a^{t}` - :math:`b^{t}` + :math:`c^{t}` : :math:`a^{t}` + :math:`b^{t}` - :math:`c^{t}`.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that the (complement of X_i) = X_j:

* **X_40469**–**X_40529** — **Centers and perspectors of cevapoint conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 30, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`L <L>` be the line u x + v y + w z = 0, and let :g:`U <U>` be the point :math:`u : v : w`, this being the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of L. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point. The **(U,P)-cevapoint conic**, introduced here as the locus of X such that the :term:`cevapoint <cevapoint>` of :g:`P <P>` and X is on the line LU is given by

  u (q x + p y)(r x + p z) + v (r y + q z)(p y + q x) + w (p z + r x)(q z + r y) = 0.

  The center of the conic is the point

  p\*(p^2\*(p - q - r) u^2 + q^2 (p - q + r) v^2 + r^2 (p + q - r) w^2 - 2 p q r v w + 2 p r (p - r) w u + 2 p q (p - q) u v) : : ,

  and the perspector, by

  p/(-p u + q r + r w) : q/(p u - q v + r w) : r/(p u + q v - r w).

  For every point :g:`U <U>`, the (U,P)-cevapoint conic passes through the vertices of the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0564:

* **X_40530**–**X_40564** — **Centers and perspectors of 1st Ceva conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 30, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`L <L>` be the line u x + v y + w z = 0, and let :g:`U <U>` be the point :math:`u : v : w`, this being the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of L. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point. The **1st (U,P)-Ceva conic**, introduced here as the locus of X such that the P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`X <X>` is on the line :g:`L <L>`, is given by

  u p (-p/x + q/y + r/z) + v q (p/x - q/y + r/z) + w r (p/x + q/y - r/z) = 0.

  The center of the conic is the point

  p (-p q^2 u v - 3 p q r u v + p q^2 v^2 - q^2 r v^2 - 3 p q r u w - p r^2 u w - 2 p q r v w - 3 q^2 r v w - 3 q r^2 v w + p r^2 w^2 - q r^2 w^2) : :

  If :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, then the center of the 1st (U,P)-Ceva conic is the :term:`complement <complement>` of the complement of :g:`P <P>`, which is also the centroid of {:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`}, and also the center of the bicevian conic of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and P. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, December 18, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0565:

* **X_40578**–**X_40629** — **Centers of 2nd Ceva conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 6, 2020. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`L <L>` be the line u x + v y + w z = 0, and let :g:`U <U>` be the point :math:`u : v : w`, this being the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of L. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point. The **2nd (U,P)-Ceva conic** is introduced here as the locus of X such that the X-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` is on the line :g:`L <L>`. This conic circumscribes :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and is given by

  p(-u p + v q + w r)/x + q(u p - v q + w r)/y + r(u p + v q - w r)/z = 0.

  The center of the conic is the point

  p\*((p+q+r) p^2 u^2 + (p+q-r) q^2 v^2 + (p-q+r) r^2 w^2 + 2 p q r v w - 2 p r (p+r) w u - 2 p q (p+q) u v) : :

  If :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, then the center of the 2nd (U,P)-Ceva conic is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-Ceva conjugate of :g:`P <P>`, and the perspector of the 2nd (U,P)-Ceva conic is P. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, December 18, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0566:

* **X_40632**–**X_40661** — **Points associated with bicevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 8, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be points in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the cevian triangle. Let :g:`A* <A*>` be the midpoint of :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is here named the **(P,U)-bicevian triangle:**

  | :g:`A* <A*>` = 0 : 2 q v + q w + r v : 2 r w + q w + r v
  | :g:`B* <B*>` = 2 p u + r u + p :math:`w : 0 : 2` r w + r u + p w
  | :g:`C* <C*>` = 2 p u + p v + q u : 2 q v + p v + q u : 0

  For example, let :g:`DEF << D E F >>` be the (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`)-bicevian triangle, so that :g:`D <D>` = 0 : 2 a^2 + b^2 - c^2 : a^2 - b^2 + c^2. The vertices :g:`D <D>`, :g:`E <E>`, :g:`F <F>` lie on the cubics K054 and K124 and on the Moses-Steiner ellipse (see X_6070.

  | These points lie on the Euler line of :g:`DEF << D E F >>`:
  | X_5943 = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-of-:g:`DEF << D E F >>`
  | X_8254 = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:g:`DEF << D E F >>`
  | X_6153 = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-of-:g:`DEF << D E F >>`
  | X_13365 = :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`-of-:g:`DEF << D E F >>`
  | X_40632 = :ref:`X_20 <X_20>`-of-:g:`DEF << D E F >>`

  The following triangles are perspective to :g:`DEF << D E F >>`, all with perspector :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`: 3rd and 4th :term:`Euler triangles <euler-triangle>`, submedial, infinite altitude, Ehrmann mid-triangle, Gemini 110, 1st and 2nd half-diamonds equilateral triangles, and 1st and 2nd half-diamonds triangles (X_33338.

  The circumcircle (M), of :g:`DEF << D E F >>`, passes through X_i for i = 125, 137, 11702, 14071, 30480 and has squared radius

  (2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)^2 - a^2\*b^2\*(-2 + J^2))\*(2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)^2 - a^2\*c^2\*(-2 + J^2))\*(2\*(-a^2 + b^2 + c^2)^2 - b^2\*c^2\*(-2 + J^2))/(64\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(-2 + J)^2\*(2 + J)^2\*S^2)

  Note that (M) meets the nine-point circle in the points :ref:`X_125 <X_125>` and :ref:`X_137 <X_137>`.

  :g:`DEF << D E F >>` is the :term:`reflection triangle <reflection-triangle>` of the medial-of-:term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` (which is also Gemini triangle 110, the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-midcevian triangle, and the :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>` of the submedial triangle, if :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is acute), and :g:`DEF << D E F >>` is homothetic to the reflection triangle at :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, December 18, 2020)

  Let :g:`D' <D'>` be the point, other than D, where (M) meets the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`E' <E'>` and :g:`F' <F'>` cyclically. Then

  Let :g:`D' <D'>` = 0 : (a^2 + 2\*b^2 - c^2)\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2) : (a^2 - b^2 + 2\*c^2)\*(a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2 + c^4).

  The triangle :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>`, here named the **Maia triangle,** is perspective to the following triangles, with perspectors as shown:

  | 1st orthosymmedial (see X_6792; perspector X_40633
  | infinite altitude; perspector :ref:`X_54 <X_54>`
  | orthic axes triangle (see X_25010); perspector :ref:`X_275 <X_275>`
  | Yiu tangents triangle (see X_7495; perspector X_40634

  The Maia triangle is homothetic to the polar triangle of the nine-point circle at X_8901. (Randy Hutson, December 18, 2020)

.. _guide-preamble-0568:

* **X_40674**–**X_40696** — **Points associated with midcevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 9, 2020. Let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>`, and let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the midpoint of the segment :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`. Define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically, so that

  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = v +\ :math:`w : v : w`
  | :g:`B″ <B″>` = u : w + u : w
  | :g:`C″ <C″>` =\ :math:`u : v : u` + v.

  The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named the **U-midcevian triangle.** Examples include

  | :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`-midcevian triangle = Gemini triangle 15
  | :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-midcevian triangle = Gemini triangle 110
  | :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-midcevian triangle = :term:`half-altitude triangle <half-altitude-triangle>`
  | :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`-midcevian triangle = 1st Zaniah triangle
  | :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`-midcevian triangle = 2nd Zaniah triangle
  | :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`-midcevian triangle = orthic-of-:term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` = anti-6th-mixtilinear = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of submedial triangle; see X_11363
  | :ref:`X_75 <X_75>`-midcevian triangle = Gemini triangle 16 = :term:`complement <complement>` of :term:`incentral triangle <incentral-triangle>` = n(Incentral)\*n(Medial) (ETC preamble before :ref:`X_3739 <X_3739>`)
  | :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`-midcevian triangle = :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :ref:`X_523 <X_523>` = Schroeter triangle (ETC X_8286 = diagonal triangle of Feuerbach quadrangle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (ETC X_10276

  In general, the U-midcevian triangle is perspective to the following triangles:

  | :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with perspector U
  | medial triangle, with perspector u v + u w : :
  | Wasat triangle (see X_21616), with perspector a u (b + c) - (b v - c w)(b - c) : :
  | Gemini 7 triangle, with perspector a u (a - b - c) - (b - c)((a - b + c) v + (a + b - c) w) : :

  Let T(U) denote the midcevian triangle of :g:`U <U>`, and let C(U) denote the cevian triangle of :g:`U <U>`.

  The locus of a point X such that T(U) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic pK(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :g:`U* <U*>`), where :g:`U* <U*>` = :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`.

  The locus of X such that T(U) is perspective to the anticevian triangle of :g:`X <X>` is the cubic pK(u\*(v + w) : : , -u + v + w : :). For example, if :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, then the cubic is K044.

  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K034.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K045.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K007.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K141.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_7 <X_7>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K200.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_8 <X_8>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K1078.
  | The locus of X such that T(X13)) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K264a.
  | The locus of X such that T(:ref:`X_14 <X_14>`) is perspective to C(X) is the cubic K264b.

.. _guide-preamble-0569:

* **X_40718**–**X_40725** — **Points associated with CCC cubics**

  | contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 16, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be points in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`D'E'F' << D' E' F' >>` = cevian triangle of U
  | :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` = :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`D″E″F″ << D″ E″ F″ >>` = anticevian triangle of U
  | :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`A'D″ <[ A' D″ ]>` ∩ :g:`A″E' <[ A″ E' ]>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically, so that

  | :g:`A* <A*>` = - p u : q u + p v : r u + p w
  | :g:`B* <B*>` = p v + q u : - q v : r v + q w
  | :g:`C* <C*>` = p w + r u : q w + r v : - r w

  The triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is here named the **(P,U)-cevian-cross triangle** (not to be confused with the cross-cevian triangle in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, p. 201)..

  The locus of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that the (P,U)-:term:`cevian <cevian>`-cross triangle is perspective to the cevian triangle of :g:`X <X>` is the **(P,U)-CCC cubic**, given by

  (r u + p w)(q^2 u^2 + p q u v + p^2 v^2) y z^2 - (q u + p v) (r^2 u^2 + p r u w + p^2 w^2) y^2 z + (cyclic) = 0

  The (P,U)-CCC cubic is the cubic pK(:g:`P* <P*>`,\ :g:`U* <U*>`), where

  | :g:`P* <P*>` = q^2 u^2 + p q u v + p^2 v^2)(r^2 u^2 + p r u w + p^2w^2) : :
  | :g:`U* <U*>` = (q^2 u^2 + p q u v + p^2\*v^2)(r^2 u^2 + p r u w + p^2 w^2)(r v + q w) : :

  | Examples:
  | (:ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`)-CCC cubic = pK(:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`) = K001
  | (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`)-CCC cubic = pK(:ref:`X_3407 <X_3407>`, X_14617) = K421

  The locus of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that the (P,U)-cevian-cross triangle is perspective to the anticevian triangle of :g:`X <X>` is the **(P,U)-CCA cubic**, given by

  2 p u (r^2 u v + 2 q r u w + 2 p r v w + p q w^2) y^2 z - 2 p u (2 q r u v + p r v^2 + q^2 u w + 2 p q v w) y z^2 + (cyclic) = 0.

  The (P,U)-CCA cubic is the cubic pK(:g:`P* <P*>`,\ :g:`U* <U*>`), where

  :g:`P* <P*>` = p u : : , and :g:`U* <U*>` = q r u^2 + p^2 v w + 2 p u (r v + q w)) : :

  | Examples:
  | ((:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, :ref:`X_458 <X_458>`) = K677
  | ((:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_3329 <X_3329>`) = K423
  | ((:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, X_8838) = K420b
  | ((:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, X_8836) = K420a
  | ((:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_30 <X_30>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) = K472
  | ((:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_98 <X_98>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_1976 <X_1976>`, :ref:`X_98 <X_98>`) = K380
  | ((:ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_1989 <X_1989>`, :ref:`X_265 <X_265>`) = K060
  | ((:ref:`X_15 <X_15>`, :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`)_CCA cubic = pK(:ref:`X_50 <X_50>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) = K073

.. _guide-preamble-0570:

* **X_40840**–**X_40842** — **Points associated with (X_1,U)-cevian-cross triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 31, 2020. Let :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,U)-:term:`cevian <cevian>`-cross triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is introduced in the preamble just before X_40718. The vertices are given by.

  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = u : u + v : u + w
  | :g:`B″ <B″>` = v +\ :math:`u : - v : v` + w
  | :g:`C″ <C″>` = w + u : w + v : - w.

  Triangles perspective to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and the perspectors include the following:

  | :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, (u+v)\*(u+w) : :
  | medial, u\*(u - v - w) : :
  | anticomplementary, u\*v + u\*w - v\*w : :
  | [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0571:

* **X_40843**–**X_40850** — **Points associated with paratriangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 31, 2020. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The point :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`p : r : q` is here named the **parapoint of P**. To contruct :g:`P' <P'>`, let :g:`L <L>` be the line through :g:`P <P>` parallel to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Let :g:`Q <Q>` = L∩AG , where G denotes the centroid of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Then :g:`P' <P'>` is the reflection of :g:`P <P>` in :g:`Q <Q>`.

  The **paratriangle of P** is the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` with vertices given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`p : r : q`
  | :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`r : q : p`
  | :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`q : p : r`

  If P is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` other than :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a noncentral triangle, but its perspector with other triangles can be a triangle center.

  (More generally, the paratriangle of a triangle :g:`UVW << U V W >>` is here defined as the triangle :g:`U'V'W' << U' V' W' >>`.)

  For fixed P with paratriangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, the locus of X such that the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>` is perspective to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the **cevian-associated cubic** given by

  q (p q - r^2) y z^2 - r (p r - q^2) y^2 z + (cyclic) = 0,

  which is the cubic pK(:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`,\ :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`), where :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` = (p r - q^2)(p q - r^2) and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` = P\*\ :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`.

  The appearance of (i,K___) in the following list means that if :g:`P <P>` = X_i, then the K___ is the :term:`cevian <cevian>`-associated cubic;

  | (4, K776)

  | (30, K860)
  | [and others]

* **X_40911**–**X_40920** — **Points associated the special dilation triangle**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 4, 2021. Let :g:`T <T>` denote the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. There is exactly one dilation of :g:`T <T>` from :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` that is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. It is the (-1)-dilation, here named the **special dilation triangle**, with vertices given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` = 4 a^2 : a^2 - b^2 + c^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 : 4 b^2 : b^2 - c^2 + a^2
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = c^2 - a^2 + b^2 : c^2 + a^2 - b^2 : 4 c^2.

  See Clark Kimberling and Peter J. C. Moses, "Dilation-Induced Perspectivities among Triangles", *Journal for Geometry and Graphics* 14 (2010) 1-14.

  :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-of-:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = X_5650, and :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :ref:`X_141 <X_141>`

  The appearance of (T,i) in the following list means that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`T <T>`, and the perspector is X_i:

  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 69)
  | (tangential. 31521)
  | (2nd Euler, 125)
  | (4th extouch, 69)
  | (Artzt, 2)
  | [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0576:

* **X_41016**–**X_41071** — **Altintas-isodynamic triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 11, 2021.

  Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle. The parallel line to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` from :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_15 <X_15>` (1st isodynamic point) intersects the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` in :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` and the Simson lines of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` cut at :g:`A' <A'>`. Define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is equilateral and its center lies on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. (Kadir Altintas, January 9, 2021)

  | :g:`A' <A'>` has barycentric coordinates:
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = -((S^2+SB\*SC)\*\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S+(SA+3\*SW)\*S^2-2\*(-SW\*SA+S^2+SW^2)\*SA)/(S^2-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S\*SA-2\*SW\*SA) : SC : SB
  | and squared-sidelength:
  | :g:`L' <L'>`:sup:`2` = S^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`/(3\*S+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*SW)

  | When :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_16 <X_16>` (2nd isodynamic point), the parallel line to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` from P intersect the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` in two imaginary points, but the Simson lines of these points still intersect in a real point :g:`A″ <A″>`. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` built in this way is also equilateral and:
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = -((-S^2+SB\*SC)\*\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S+(SA+3\*SW)\*S^2-2\*(-SW\*SA+S^2+SW^2)\*SA)/(S^2-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S\*SA-2\*SW\*SA) : SC : SB
  | and its squared-sidelength is:
  | :g:`L″ <L″>`:sup:`2` = S^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`/(-3\*S+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*SW)

  Triangles :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are referred here as **1st- and 2nd- Altintas-isodynamic triangles**, respectively. A list of relations among these triangles and others can be seen **here** (``X(41016).rtf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0578:

* **X_41133**–**X_41154** — **Inverses-in-permutation ellipses**

  :contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 25, 2021. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Suppose further that p,q,r are distinct homogeneous functions of a,b,c. The permutation ellipse of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by E(P), is introduced in the preamble just before X_34341 as the ellipse that passes through the six points :math:`p : q : r`,\ :math:`q : r : p`,\ :math:`r : p : q`,\ :math:`p : r : q`,\ :math:`q : p : r`,\ :math:`r : q : p`, given by

  (q r + r p + p q)(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - (p^2 + q^2 + r^2)(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  The centroid, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, is the center and the perspector of E(P).

  In C. Kimberling and P. Moses, 'Permutation Ellipses', *Journal for Geometry and Graphics* 24 (2020) 233-247, the following three special permutation ellipses are discussed: (1) trisector ellipse, (2) self-dual permutation ellipse; and (3) Steiner midway ellipse. Following are definitions and equations:

  (1) The trisector ellipse passes through the points :math:`0:1:2`,\ :math:`0:2:1`,\ :math:`1:0:2`,\ :math:`2:0:1`,\ :math:`1:2:0`,\ :math:`2:1:0`. These six points trisect the sides of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The ellipse is given by 2(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - 5(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  (2) The unique self-dual permutation ellipse is given by x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - 4 (y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  (3) The Steiner midway ellipse (SME), is, loosely speaking, the ellipse midway between the Steiner inellipse (SIE) and the Steiner circumellipse (SCE). That is, for each P on SCE, let :g:`P' <P'>` be the intersection of the ray GP with SIE, and let :g:`P″ <P″>` be the midpoint of :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>`. Then SME is the set of all such midpoints. SME is given by 7(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - 34(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  In general, the inverse of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` in an ellipse j (x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - k (y z + z x + x y) = 0 is the point k\*p^2 - j\*p\*q + j\*q^2 - j\*p\*r - k\*q\*r + j\*r^2 : : .

  The appearance of (m,n) in the following list means that the trisector-ellipse-inverse of X(m) is X_n:

  (6,8859), (69,41133), (99,41134), (115,41135), (141,41136), (183,41137), (190,41138), (193,41139), (148,14971), (230,5032), (239,25055), (297,3545), (325,21356), (401,5054), (441,10304), (448,15671), (671,9166), (1635,24508), (3524,40884), (5055,40885), (5215,40871), (7840,21358), (8591,9167), (11078,22489), (11092,22490), (15699,40853), (17310,19875), (19883,40891), (22510,25165), (22511,25155), (37907,40856), (39663,39908)

  The appearance of (m,n) in the following list means that the self-dual-permutation-ellipse-inverse of X(m) is X_n:

  (1,41140), (8,41141), (37,41142), (39,41143), (75,41144), (98,41145), (183,41146)

  The appearance of (m,n) in the following list means that the midway-ellipse-inverse of X(m) is X_n:

.. _guide-preamble-0580:

* **X_41163**–**X_41166** — **Points on the Terzic circle**

  based on notes from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 30, 2021. Points X_41163-X_41165 were found using the following theorem, which was introduced in the preamble just before :ref:`X_3027 <X_3027>`:

  | Suppose that :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and :g:`O_{2} <O_2>` are circles. Let :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` be a point on :g:`O_{1} <O_1>`, and let :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` be the :g:`O_{1} <O_1>`-antipode of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`. Let
  | :math:`S_{i}` = internal center of similitude of :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and :g:`O_{2} <O_2>`
  | :math:`S_{e}` = external center of similitude of :g:`O_{1} <O_1>` and :g:`O_{2} <O_2>`
  | :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` = :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`\ :math:`S_{i}`\ ∩\ :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`\ :math:`S_{e}`
  | :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>` = :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`\ :math:`S_{e}`\ ∩\ :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`\ :math:`S_{i}`

  Then :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` and :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>` are a pair of antipodes on :g:`O_{2} <O_2>`, and the lines :g:`P_{1}P_{2} <[ P_1 P_2 ]>` and :g:`P_{2}Q_{2} <[ P_2 Q_2 ]>` are parallel.

.. _guide-preamble-0581:

* **X_41202**–**X_41224** — **Christopher J. Bradley bicevian points and axes**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, Februry 05, 2021. This section is based on the work `On the Nine Intersections of Two Cevian Triangles (Article 20) <https://people.bath.ac.uk/masgcs/bradley.html>`__, by Christopher J. Bradley (with symmetrical notations by César Lozada).

  *Let :g:`U <U>`, :g:`X <X>` be two distinct points on the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, neither on its sidelines nor on a line parallel to a sideline through the opposite vertex. Let* :g:`A_{u}B_{u}C_{u} << A_u B_u C_u >>` and :g:`A_{x} <A_x>`\ :g:`B_{x} <B_x>`\ :g:`C_{x} <C_x>` *be the :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>` and X, respectively. We introduce the nine intersections of these two triangles:*

  :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = :g:`B_{u}C_{u} <[ B_u C_u ]>` ∩ :g:`B_{x}C_{x} <[ B_x C_x ]>`, and cyclically :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`

  :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`A_{u}B_{u} <[ A_u B_u ]>` ∩ :g:`A_{x}C_{x} <[ A_x C_x ]>`, and cyclically :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`

  :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`A_{x}B_{x} <[ A_x B_x ]>` ∩ :g:`A_{u}C_{u} <[ A_u C_u ]>`, and cyclically :g:`B_{3} <B_3>`, :g:`C_{3} <C_3>`

  *Then, assuming that* :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`X <X>` = x : y z (barycentrics):

  | A, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` are collinear on a line :math:`a_{1}`; B, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` are collinear on a line :math:`b_{1}`; C, :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` are collinear on a line :math:`c_{1}`. :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`B_{2}C_{2} <[ B_2 C_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{u}C_{x} <[ B_u C_x ]>` concrr in a point :g:`A' <A'>`; :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`C_{2}A_{2} <[ C_2 A_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{u}A_{x} <[ C_u A_x ]>` concur in a point :g:`B' <B'>`; :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2} <[ A_2 B_2 ]>`, :g:`A_{u}B_{x} <[ A_u B_x ]>` concur in a point :g:`C' <C'>`. :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`B_{3}C_{3} <[ B_3 C_3 ]>`, :g:`B_{x}C_{u} <[ B_x C_u ]>` concur in a point :g:`A″ <A″>`; :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`C_{3}A_{3} <[ C_3 A_3 ]>`, :g:`C_{x}A_{u} <[ C_x A_u ]>` concur in a point :g:`B″ <B″>`; :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`A_{3}B_{3} <[ A_3 B_3 ]>`, :g:`A_{x}B_{u} <[ A_x B_u ]>` concur in a point :g:`C″ <C″>`. :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` are collinear on a line :g:`L' <L'>` and also :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` are collinear on a line :g:`L″ <L″>`. Moreover, these two lines are concurrent with UX at a point O(U,X), here named the **Bradley bicevian point of (U, X)**.
  | Barycentric coordinates of this point are O(U, X) = u^2\*y\*z-x^2\*v\*w : : . In other words, O(U, X) is the U-:term:`Hirst inverse <hirst-inverse>`-of-:g:`X <X>` = :g:`X <X>`-Hirst inverse-of-U (see the **ETC glossary** (``glossary.html``)). A, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` are collinear, as are B, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and C, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`, :g:`C_{3} <C_3>`. The last result means that :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2} <[ A_2 B_2 ]>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3} <[ A_3 B_3 ]>` are perspective by pairs with common perspector Q(U,X) = (v\*z+w\*y)\*u\*x ::. :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is perspective to these triangles: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A_{u}B_{u}C_{u} << A_u B_u C_u >>`, :g:`A_{x}B_{x}C_{x} << A_x B_x C_x >>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`. Let :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (U,X) and :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`\ (U,X) be the perspectors of :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` with :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` and :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>`, respectively. Q(U,X), :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (U,X) and :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`\ (U,X) lie on a line, here named the **Bradley bicevian axis of (U, X)**, whose :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` has barycentric coordinates:

  T(U, X) = (x\*v^2\*z-y^2\*u\*w)\*(x^2\*w^2-z^2\*u^2)\*(y\*w^2\*x-z^2\*v\*u)\*(y^2\*u^2-x^2\*v^2) : :

  Note that :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the side-triangle of the U- and :g:`X <X>`-cevian triangles. For shortening, the term **side-of-cevians-of-(U,X)** will be used here for this triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0582:

* **X_41231**–**X_41278** — **Gibert quadratic transformations and inverses**

  based on notes from :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, and related points contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 11, 2021. Let X :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics) be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Define

  :math:`F(X) = b^{4} c^{2} x^{2}-b^{2} c^{4} x^{2}-a^{4} c^{2} x y+b^{2} c^{4} x y+a^{4} b^{2} x z-b^{4} c^{2} x z-a^{4} b^{2} y z+a^{4} c^{2} y z`: : ,

  with inverse given by

  invF(X) = a^2 (b^4 x^2-c^4 x^2-a^2 b^2 x y+c^4 x y-b^4 x z+a^2 c^2 x z+a^2 b^2 y z-a^2 c^2 y z) : :

  In the sequel, these transformations are denoted by BGF and invBGF.

  The singular points of BGF are :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, and :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`. If X is on :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, then F(X) = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. If X is on :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`, then F(X) = :ref:`X_83 <X_83>`. If X is on :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`, then F(X) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

  The fixed points of :g:`F <F>`; i.e., points X such that BG(X) = invBG(X) = X, are the points on the circumconic having perspector :ref:`X_669 <X_669>`.

  BGF maps every line through :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` onto itself; in particular, BGF(Euler line) = Euler line.

  BGF maps the circumconic having perspector :ref:`X_512 <X_512>` onto the Kiepert hyperbola.

  BGF maps the circumconic having perspector :ref:`X_688 <X_688>` onto the circumconic having perspector :ref:`X_512 <X_512>`.

  The transformations BGF and invBGF have many connections among pk cubics. In order to state a few of them, certain notations will be used: "/" denotes barycentric division, and "\*" denotes barycentric product, and if X is a point, then gX = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`X <X>`, and tX = :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`X <X>`.

  Let pk1 = pK(Ω,P) be a pK cubic and let pk2 = pK(Ω',\ :g:`P' <P'>`) be another pK cubic such that the isopivot of :g:`Q' <Q'>` is Ω'/:g:`P' <P'>`.

  (1) The cubics pk1 and pk2 meet the line at infinity at the same points if and only if :g:`Q' <Q'>` lies on a psK cubic that is a pK cubic if and only if the points :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, Ω, and P are collinear.

  (2) The cubics pk1 and pk2 meet the circumcircle at the same points if and only if the points :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, Ω/:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, and P are collinear; or, equivalently, the points :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`, Ω, and :g:`P* <P*>`\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` are collinear. Note that Ω/:ref:`X_6 <X_6>` = tgΩ and :g:`P* <P*>`\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` = gtΩ.

  | (3) Conditions (1) and (2) hold simultaneously if and only if
  | P lies on the lines :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ Ω and :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ tgΩ meeting at BGF(Ω) and
  | Ω lies on the lines :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` P and :ref:`X_32 <X_32>` gtP meeting at invBGF(P).

.. _guide-preamble-0583:

* **X_41279**–**X_41292** — **2nd Lozada perspectors**

  contributed by Vu Thanh Tung, February 14, 2021. As a sequel to the preamble just before X_6056, in which Lozada perspectors are introduced, this section is based on the following definition: Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (barycentrics) in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`L_{A} <L_A>` be the line, other than :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, that passes through :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` and is tangent to the :g:`A <A>`-excircle. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the touch point, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector, here named the **2nd Lozada perspector** of :g:`P <P>`, denoted by V(P), is given by

  V(P) = (a + b - c)(a - b + c) p^2 : (b + c - a)(b - c + a) q^2 : (c + a - b)(c - a + b) r^2.

  See **2nd Lozada Perspector** (``2ndLozadaPerspector.pdf``).

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that V(X_i) = X_j:

  (1,56), (2,7), (3,7335), (5,41279), (6,1397), (7,479), (8,8), (9,55), (10,12), (31,41280), (32,41281), (36,41282), (75,6063), (76,41283), (83,41284), (141,41285), (560,41286), (561,41287), (1501,41288), (1502, 41289), (1928,41290), (2321,6057), (2887,41291), (3676,451292)

.. _guide-preamble-0584:

* **X_41301**–**X_41308** — **Points associated with Steiner parabolas**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 21, 2021. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P a point on its plane. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` be the points at which the parallel line to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` through P cuts :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` and :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively and denote :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. It is well known that these six points lie on a conic and also that this conic is a parabola SP(P) if and only if P lies on the Steiner inellipse of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. This parabola is here named the **Steiner parabola of P**.

  The following algebraic method for calculating the focus F(P) of the Steiner parabola SP(P) follows from the preambles just before X_31644 and X_38017:

  Let :g:`X <X>` = 3\*PG/5, where G=\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and let :g:`X' <X'>` = barycentric product of :g:`P <P>` and X. Let Y = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>`-of-P. Since P lies on the Steiner inellipse, Y lies on the line at infinity. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of Y. Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective. Denote their perspector by :g:`Y' <Y'>`. The focus F(P) is the midpoint of :g:`X' <X'>` and :g:`Y' <Y'>`. The axis of SP(P) passes through Y.

.. _guide-preamble-0585:

* **X_41380**–**X_41388** — **Centers of antiparallels conics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 22, 2021. *Draw antiparallels through the symmedian point :g:`K <K>`. The points where these lines intersect the sides then lie on a circle, known as the cosine circle (or sometimes the second Lemoine circle)*. (Reference: `Weisstein, Eric W. "Cosine Circle." From MathWorld--A Wolfram Web Resource <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/CosineCircle.html>`__). More generally, if P is a point on the Jerabek circumhyperbola of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then the antiparallel lines through P cut the sidelines of the triangle in six points lying on a conic, here named the **antiparallels conic of P** and denoted as 𝕁(P).

  | The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the center of 𝕁(X_i) is X_j:
  | (3, 37864), (4, 6), (6, 6), (54, 41380), (64, 33584), (65, 41381), (66, 41382), (67, 41383), (68, 41384), (69, 41385), (70, 41386), (71, 41387), (72, 41388), (74, 40355).

  𝕁(P) is a circle for :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and a degenerated conic for :g:`P <P>` in {:ref:`X_1987 <X_1987>`, X_8678, X_8679}. 𝕁(P) is never a parabola.

.. _guide-preamble-0586:

* **X_41394**–**X_41430** — **Perspectors involving g-triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 25, 2021. Mappings g and h are defined in the preamble just before X_33628 as follows. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` is a point. The points

  q - r : r - p : p - q and 2p - q - r : 2q - r - p : 2r - p - q

  clearly lie on the line at infinity, so that their :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>`,

  :math:`g(P) = a^{2}/(q-r)`: b^2/(r-p) : c^2/(p-q) and :math:`h(P) = a^{2}/(2p-q-r)`: b^2/(2q-r-p) : c^2/(2r-p-q),

  lie on the circumcircle. Thus, if T is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`, then g(T) and h(T) are central triangles inscribed in the circumcircle.

  For many choices of triangle :g:`T <T>`, there are triangles :g:`T' <T'>` such that T is perspective to g(:g:`T' <T'>`). This section lists associated perspectors.

  The appearance of (T,\ :g:`T' <T'>`,i) in the following list means that T is perspective to g(:g:`T' <T'>`) and the perspector is X_i:

  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 3rd Brocard, 32)
  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, orthocentroidal, 6)
  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 2nd Parry, 187
  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, centers of the Apollonius circles, 32)
  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, Gemini 19, 649
  | (medial, MacBeath, 4)
  | (anticomplementary, Steiner, 99)
  | [and others]

  Following are two examples of pairs, (T,\ :g:`T' <T'>`) of named triangles :g:`T <T>` and :g:`T' <T'>` such that :g:`T <T>` = g(:g:`T' <T'>`):

  | orthocentroidal triangle = g(cirum-:term:`symmedial triangle <symmedial-triangle>`)
  | 1st cirumperp triangle = :math:`g(Gemini 7) = g(Gemini 15)`\ = :math:`g(Gemini 17) = g(Gemini 25)`

  The appearance of :g:`T <T>` in the following list means that T is perspective to :math:`g(T) = 1st cirumperp triangle`, and the perspector is :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`: medial, tangential, 2nd circumperp, inner Napoleon, outer Napoleon, inner Fermat, outer Fermat, inner Vecten, outer Vecten, 1st Neuberg, 2nd Neuberg, Fuhrmann, 1st Brocard, Kosnita, McCay, Trihn, reflection of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` in :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`, Ara, 2nd Euler

  The appearance of (T,i) in the following list means that T is perspectiive to :math:`g(T) = 1st cirumperp triangle`, and the perspector is X_i:

  (3rd Euler, 2), (4th Euler, 4), (intouch, 55), (hexyl, 40), (Yff central, 7589), (inner tangential mid-arc, 8075), (tangential of 1st circumperp, 11495), (tangential of 2nd circumperp, 12513), (1st Sharygin, 4220), (2nd Sharygin, 105), (Honsberger, 7676), (2nd Pamfilos-Zhou, 8224), (2nd extouch, 7580), (3rd mixtilinear, 1), (4th mixtilinear, 165), (6th mixtilinear, 165), (outer tangential mid-arc, 8076), (1st Conway, 7411), (incircle-inverse of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 57), (inner Hutson, 8107), (outer Hutson, 8108), (T(-2,1) in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, Art. 6.41, 9), (T(-1,3) in :cite:`TCCT <tcct>`, Art. 6.41, 7991), (Hutson intouch, 56), (1st EhrmannT, 165), (Atik, 10860),

  The appearance of (T,i) in the following list means that T is perspective to g(T), and the persepctor is X_i:

  (tangential,1627), (3rd Brocard, 32), (MacBeath, 25), (Thomson, 6), (anti-orthocentroidal, 110), (Wasat, 1691)

  The locus of a point X such that for :g:`T <T>` = :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>`, we have :math:`g(t) = T is the cubic K141`; see :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, `K141: pK(X(2),X(76)) <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k141.html>`__.

  The locus of a point X such that for :g:`T <T>` = :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>`, we have g(t) = T is the cubic pK(:ref:`X_308 <X_308>`, :ref:`X_380 <X_380>`), which passes through X_i for these i: 2, 76, 83, 264, 308, 1799, 17907.

  See :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, **Perspectivities involving the g and h mappings** (``g(T)_h(T).pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0588:

* **X_41537**–**X_41679** — **Pairs of orthologic pedal triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 07, 2021. *Let :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` be any two distinct, finite points not both on the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and such that they are collinear with its circumcenter :g:`O <O>`\ =\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. Then the :term:`pedal triangles <pedal-triangle>` :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>` are orthologic.*

  Let :g:`Q' <Q'>` and :g:`Q″ <Q″>` be the orthologic centers (:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` to :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`) and (:g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`), respectively. If :g:`P' <P'>` is fixed and :g:`P″ <P″>` moves along the line :g:`OP' <[ O P' ]>`, then :g:`Q' <Q'>` describes a rectangular hyperbola ℍ(:g:`P' <P'>`) circumscribed to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, whilst :g:`Q″ <Q″>` moves on a line 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`). ℍ(P) is named here the **bipedal circumcentral conic of P'** (shortened to the **BPC-conic of P'**) and 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`) is named here the **bipedal circumcentral line of P'**, abbreviated as the **BPC-line of P'**. If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x:y:z` (barycentrics), then

  | the center of ℍ(:g:`P' <P'>`) is:
  | ℍ\*(:g:`P' <P'>`) = (a^2\*b^4\*c^4\*x^3+((3\*SA-SW)\*S^2-2\*(SB+SC)^2\*SA)\*b^2\*c^2\*x\*y\*z+((S^2-SB^2)\*b^2\*z+(S^2-SC^2)\*c^2\*y)\*SA\*a^2\*y\*z-b^2\*c^2\*((2\*S^2-(2\*SB+SC)\*SB)\*b^2\*z+(2\*S^2-(SB+2\*SC)\*SC)\*c^2\*y)\*x^2+((S^2\*SA+SB^3)\*b^4\*z^2+(S^2\*SA+SC^3)\*c^4\*y^2)\*x)\*(SB+SC) : : the tripole of 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`) is:
  | 𝕃\*(:g:`P' <P'>`) = (SA\*a^2\*y-SB\*b^2\*x)\*(SA\*a^2\*z-SC\*c^2\*x)\*(b^2\*z+c^2\*y) : :
  | If :g:`P' <P'>` lies on K174, 𝕃, then \*(:g:`P' <P'>`) lies on the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the center of the :g:`BPC << B P C >>`-conic of X_i is X_j:

.. _guide-preamble-0589:

* **X_41684**–**X_41756** — **Pairs of orthologic reflection triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 08, 2021. If P is point on the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the reflections of :g:`P <P>` in the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are the vertices of a new triangle named the **reflection triangle of P**\ *Let :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` be any two distinct points on the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and such that they are collinear with its circumcenter :g:`O <O>`\ =\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. Then the :term:`reflection triangles <reflection-triangle>` :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>` are orthologic.*

  Let :g:`Q' <Q'>` and :g:`Q″ <Q″>` be the orthologic centers (:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` to :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`) and (:g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`), respectively. If :g:`P' <P'>` is fixed and :g:`P″ <P″>` moves along the line :g:`OP' <[ O P' ]>`, then :g:`Q' <Q'>` describes a rectangular hyperbola ℍ(:g:`P' <P'>`) circumscribed to :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, whilst :g:`Q″ <Q″>` moves on a line 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`). ℍ(:g:`P' <P'>`) is named here the **bireflection circumcentral conic of P'** (shortened to the **BRC-conic of P'**) and 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`) is named here the **bireflection circumcentral line of P'**, abbreviated as the **BRC-line of P'**.

  | If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics). The center of ℍ(:g:`P' <P'>`) is:
  | ℍ\*(:g:`P' <P'>`) = (a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*x - (S^2 - SB^2)\*b^2\*z - (S^2 - SC^2)\*c^2\*y)\*(b^2\*c^2\*x^2 - 2\*SA\*a^2\*y\*z - (SA - SB)\*b^2\*x\*z - (SA - SC)\*c^2\*x\*y)\*a^2 : :
  | ℍ\*(:g:`P' <P'>`) coincides with the Hatzipolakis-Moses nine-point image of :g:`P' <P'>`, denoted by HM(:g:`P' <P'>`), defined in X_12824. The tripole of 𝕃(:g:`P' <P'>`) is:
  | 𝕃\*(:g:`P' <P'>`) = b^2\*c^2\*(b^2\*SB\*x - a^2\*SA\*y)\*(c^2\*SC\*x - a^2\*SA\*z)\*
  | (2\*a^2\*c^2\*SB\*y^2 + c^2\*(S^2 - (SB - 2\*SC)\*SB)\*x\*y + b^2\*(S^2 - 3\*SB^2)\*x\*z + a^2\*(S^2 + (2\*SA - SB)\*SB)\*y\*z)\*
  | (2\*a^2\*b^2\*SC\*z^2 + b^2\*(S^2 - (SC - 2\*SB)\*SC)\*x\*z + c^2\*(S^2 - 3\*SC^2)\*x\*y + a^2\*(S^2 + (2\*SA - SC)\*SC)\*y\*z) : :

  Note: The orthologic center (reflection-of-:g:`P' <P'>` to reflection-of-:g:`P″ <P″>`) is the reflection in :g:`P' <P'>` of the orthologic center (pedal-of-:g:`P' <P'>` to pedal-of-:g:`P″ <P″>`). (See X_41537)

  The appearance of (i, j, m, n) in the following lists means that the orthological centers of the reflection triangles of X_i and X_j are X(m) and X_n: (1, 3, 1, 355), (1, 35, 79, 3585), (1, 36, 7972, 41684), (1, 40, 15071, 5693), [and others].

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the center of the BRC-conic of X_i is X_j: {1, 11570}, {2, 12824}, {4, 1986}, {5, 11557}, {6, 5477}, {15, 6783}, {16, 6782}, [and others].

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the tripole of the BRC-line of X_i is X_j: (2, 6331), (4, 30450), (5, 38342), [and others].
