.. _guide-preamble-0594:

* **X_41943**–**X_41980** — **Points on the Evans conic**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 14-16, 2021. For a discussion of the Evans conic, see `Evans Conic <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/EvansConic.html>`__. If k1 and k2 are functions symmetric in a,b,c and homogeneous of degree 0, then the points

  | :g:`E_{1} <E_1>`\ (k1,k2) = 3\*a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*k2 - 4\*k1\*S^2 - 2\*a^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{k1^{2} + 2 k1 k2 + 3 k2^{2}}`\ \*S : : and
  | :g:`E_{2} <E_2>`\ (k1,k2) = 3\*a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*k2 - 4\*k1\*S^2 + 2\*a^2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{k1^{2} + 2 k1 k2 + 3 k2^{2}}`\ \*S : :

  lie on the Evans conic. The lines tangent to the Evans conic at the two points meet on the Euler line in the point T(k1,k2) = (k1 + 3\*k2)\*\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` - (k1 + k2)\*\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`.

  | The appearance of (k1,k2) → (i,j); h in the following list means that :g:`E_{1} <E_1>`\ (k1,k2) = X_i, :g:`E_{2} <E_2>`\ (k1,k2) = X_j, and T(k1,k2) = X(h): ,br> (-2,1) → (14,13); 549
  | (0, 1) → (15,16); 5
  | (-6,1) → (18,17); 550
  | (-3,2) → (3071,3070); 140
  | , [and others].

  The points :g:`E_{1} <E_1>` and :g:`E_{2} <E_2>` defined above are also Gibert points, as defined in the preamble just before X_42085; specifically, in the notation of that preamble,

  | :g:`E_{1} <E_1>`\ (k1,k2) = (:math:`\sqrt{3 (k1^{2} + 2 k1 k2 + 3 k2^{2})}` , k1, 2\*k1 + 3\*k2) Gibert point;
  | :g:`E_{2} <E_2>`\ (k1,k2) = (-:math:`\sqrt{3 (k1^{2} + 2 k1 k2 + 3 k2^{2})}`, k1, 2\*k1 + 3\*k2) Gibert point.}

.. _guide-preamble-0595:

* **X_41993**–**X_42004** — **Points on Simmons inconics**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 17-18, 2021. See :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, `Simmons Conics <https://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2006volume6/FG200624.pdf>`__. In this section, the Simmons inconic with foci :ref:`X_13 <X_13>` and :ref:`X_15 <X_15>` is the **1st Simmons inconic** and the Simmons inconic with foci :ref:`X_14 <X_14>` and (16) is the **2nd Simmons inconic**.

  Suppose that :g:`IC <[ I C ]>` is an inconic, and let :g:`P <P>` be its perspector. Then the barycentric product :g:`P* <P*>`\ (Steiner inellipse) is on :g:`IC <[ I C ]>`. In particular, if U is on the line at infinity, then the barycentric product :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`\ \*U^2 is on the 1st Simmons inconic, and :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`\ \*U^2 is on the 2nd Simmons inconic.

.. _guide-preamble-0596:

* **X_42005**–**X_42066** — **Perpsectors associated with inverse triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 18, 2021. Suppose that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a triangle with vertices :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` represented in normalized barycentric coordinates. Let M be the matrix representation of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, and let inv(M) denote the inverse of M. Then the rows of inv(M), interpreted as vertices of a triangle, define the **inverse triangle** of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`. The row sums of the inverse triangle are all 1, so that this triangle is "automatically" normalized.

  Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point, and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, given by A ' =\ :math:`0 : q : r`, with :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` determined cycllically from :g:`A' <A'>`. The inverse triangle of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` given by :g:`A″ <A″>` = - q - r : q + r : p + q, with :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` determined cyclically from :g:`A″ <A″>`; thus, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of the point q + r : r + p : p + q.

  Here, let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the cevian triangle of P. The inverse of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` given by :g:`A″ <A″>` = 0 : p - q + r : p + q - r, with :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` determined cyclically from :g:`A″ <A″>`; thus :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is the cevian triangle of the point - p + q + r ; p - q + r : p + q - r.

  A triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>` if and only if its inverse circumscribes :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  See the preambles just before X_43280, X_43344, and X_46961.

.. _guide-preamble-0597:

(:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, May 31, 2021)

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 22, 2021. :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>` has noted a set of points in connecton with the cubic K1191. These points are given by the :term:`combo <combo>`

  :g:`SW* <[ S W* ]>`\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \*i + :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*\ :g:`S* <S*>`\ (j\*\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` + k\*\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) where (i,j,k) are constants or other 0-degree functions of a,b,c. See `K1191 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k1191.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0599:

* **X_42285**–**X_42286** — **Perpsectors associated with product triangles**

  | contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 23, 2021. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be a triangle, and let :g:`M_{1} <M_1>` be the matrix whose rows are the normalized barycentrics of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, respectively.
  | Let :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be a triangle, and let :g:`M_{2} <M_2>` be the matrix whose rows are the normalized barycentrics of :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`, respectively.
  | Let M be the matrix sum :g:`M_{1} <M_1>` + :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`. The **triangle sum** :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is here defined as the triangle whose vertices are given by the rows of :g:`M_{1} <M_1>` + :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`. (Note that triangle sum is non-associative and that there is no additive identity, hence no additive inverses.)

  In this section ":term:`cevian <cevian>`\ (P)" means the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, and "anticevian :g:`U″ <U″>` means the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>`.

  cevian(P)+anticevian(U) is perspective to both cevian(P) and anticevian(U), and the perspector is the P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`, given by

  u (-u/p + v/q + w/r) : v (-v/q + w/r + u/p) w (-w/r + u/p + v/q).

  If :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, then cevian(P) + anticevian(U) is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for :g:`U <U>` on a certain cubic through :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`, and :ref:`X_1125 <X_1125>`. If :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, the perspector is X_42285; if :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_1125 <X_1125>`, the perspector is :ref:`X_551 <X_551>`.

  If :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, then cevian(P) + anticevian(U) is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for :g:`U <U>` on a certain cubic through :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_141 <X_141>`, and :ref:`X_3589 <X_3589>`. If :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_141 <X_141>`, the perspector is X_42286.

.. _guide-preamble-0600:

* **X_42287**–**X_42410** — **Polarologic and Polelogic centers & T-isogonal-axes**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 24, 2021. *Let* T ' = :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` *and* :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` *be two distinct scalene triangles. Let* (a'), (b'), (c') *be the :term:`trilinear polars <trilinear-polar>` of the vertices of T ' with respect to :g:`T″ <T″>` and let* :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` *be the :term:`trilinear poles <trilinear-pole>` of the sidelines of T ' with respect to :g:`T″ <T″>`. Inversely, let* (a"), (b"), (c") *be the trilinear polars of the vertices of :g:`T″ <T″>` with respect to T ' and* :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` *the trilinear poles of the sidelines of :g:`T″ <T″>` with respect to T '. Then:*

  *If* (a'), (b'), (c') *concur in a point :g:`P' <P'>` then* (a"), (b"), (c") *also concur in a point :g:`P″ <P″>`.* *If* :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` *are collinear on a line ℓ' then* :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` *are also collinear on a line ℓ".* *If T ' and :g:`T″ <T″>` satisfy one of the properties (1) or (2), then they satisfy the other property.*

  T ' and :g:`T″ <T″>` have the concurrences in (1) and the collinearities in (2) if the :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of the vertices of T ' with respect to :g:`T″ <T″>` are collinear on a line 𝓂'. In this case, the isogonal conjugates of the vertices of :g:`T″ <T″>` with respect to T ' are also collinear on a line 𝓂".

  Here, points :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>` are named the **polarologic centers** of (T ' to :g:`T″ <T″>`) and (:g:`T″ <T″>` to T ') and the tripoles of lines ℓ' and ℓ" are referred as the **polelogic centers** of (T ' to :g:`T″ <T″>`) and (:g:`T″ <T″>` to T ') . Also, the lines 𝓂' and 𝓂" are introduced as the **T-isogonal-axes** of (T ' wrt :g:`T″ <T″>`) and (:g:`T″ <T″>` wrt T ').

  The appearance of (T, [i, j], [m, n]) in the following list means that triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and T have polarologic centers X_i, X_j and polelogic centers X(m), X_n: (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, [1350, 6], [42287, 69]), (1st anti-circumperp, [20477, 6], [30441, 670]), (anti-Honsberger, [182, 32], [42288, 83]), [and others].

  The appearance of (T, [i, j], [m, n]) in the following list means that triangles anticomplementary and T have polarologic centers X_i, X_j and polelogic centers X(m), X_n: (anti-Euler, [42329, 264], [42330, 95]), (3rd anti-Euler, [1510, 42331], [42332, 42333]), (Aquila, [42334, 86], [42335, 1268]), [and others].

  The appearance of (T, [i, j], [m, n]) in the following list means that triangles MEDIAL and T have polarologic centers X_i, X_j and polelogic centers X(m), X_n: (anti-Aquila, [15569, 3739], [39721, 7]), (Euler, [5480, 141], [42352, 253]), (2nd Euler, [42353, 141], [42354, 42355]), (3rd Euler, [42356, 141], [42357, 190]), [and others]

  The appearance of (T, [i, j], [m, n]) in the following list means that triangles ORTHIC and T have polarologic centers X_i, X_j and polelogic centers X(m), X_n: (anti-excenters-reflections, [36990, 6], [42373, 393]), (Euler, [5480, 53], [42374, 6]), (2nd Euler, [42353, 53], [42375, 42376]), (3rd Euler, [42356, 53], [--, --]), (4th Euler, [3826, 53], [--, --]), [and others]

  The appearance of (T, i, j) in the following list means that the tripoles of the T-isogonal-axes of triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and T are X_i and X_j: (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 2, 2), (1st anti-circumperp, 2, 2), (anti-Honsberger, 3407, 76), [and others].

The perspector of the hyperbola lies on the orthic axis.*

.. _guide-preamble-0604:

* **X_42437**–**X_42463** — **Products X(i)*T for selected triangles T**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 31, 2021. If X is a normalized :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` and T a normalized :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`, then the left-product :g:`X*T <[ X* T ]>` is a triangle center. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point. Centers X_42437-X_42450 are products X_i\*(:term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`), given by

  p (q + r) (p y + q y + p z + r z) : q (p + r) (p x + q x + q z + r z) : (p + q) r (p x + r x + q y + r y).

  Centers X_42451-X_42463 are products X_i\*(:term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`), given by p\*((p + q - r)\*(p - q + r)\*x + (p - q - r)\*(p + q - r)\*y + (p - q - r)\*(p - q + r)\*z) : :

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_i\*(cevian triangle of X_j = X_k (1,1,2292), (1,2,10), (1,4,65), (1,6,20969), (1,7,1), (1,8,8), (1,20,5930), (2,1,1962), (2,2,2), (2,3,32078), (2,4,51), (2,6,11205), (2,7,354), (2,8,210), (2,20,154), (2,30,3081), (3,2,5), (3,4,4), [and others].

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_i\*(anticevian triangle of X_j = X_k: (1,1,40), (1,2,8), (1,3,3157), (1,6,3556), (1,8,6552), (1,9,1), (1,10,10), (1,11,21132), (2,1,165), (2,2,2), (2,3,3167), (2,6,154), (2,7,32079), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0605:

* **X_42464**–**X_42471** — **Perspectors associated with product triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 28, 2021. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be a triangle, and let :g:`M_{1} <M_1>` be the matrix whose rows are the normalized barycentrics of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, respectively. Let :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be a triangle, and let :g:`M_{2} <M_2>` be the matrix whose rows are the normalized barycentrics of :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`, respectively. Let M be the matrix product :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`\ \*\ :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`. The **triangle product** :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is here defined as the triangle whose vertices are given by the rows of :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`\ \*\ :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`. The noncommutative operation denoted by \*, here named **triangle multiplication**, is associative.

  Abbreviate the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a pont :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` as :term:`cevian <cevian>`\ (P) and the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` as anticevian(U). Let

  | :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = anticevian(P), so that :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`-p : q : r`
  | :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` = anticevian triangle(U), so that :g:`A″ <A″>` = :math:`-u : v : w`.

  Then :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector, f(P,U), is given by

  | u (p u^2 - q u^2 + r u^2 - 2 r u v - p v^2 + q v^2 + r v^2 + 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 - q w^2 - r w^2) (p u^2 + q u^2 - r u^2 + 2 r u v - p v^2 - q v^2 - r v^2 - 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 + q w^2 + r w^2)
  | :
  | -v (p u^2 - q u^2 + r u^2 - 2 r u v - p v^2 + q v^2 + r v^2 + 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 - q w^2 - r w^2) (p u^2 + q u^2 + r u^2 - 2 r u v - p v^2 - q v^2 + r v^2 - 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 + q w^2 - r w^2)
  | :
  | -w (p u^2 + q u^2 + r u^2 - 2 r u v - p v^2 - q v^2 + r v^2 - 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 + q w^2 - r w^2) (p u^2 + q u^2 - r u^2 + 2 r u v - p v^2 - q v^2 - r v^2 - 2 q u w + 2 p v w - p w^2 + q w^2 + r w^2)

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that f(X_i,X_j) = X_k: (1,1,84), (1,2,7), (1,3,1069) [and others].

  The locus of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that f(P,X) lies on this line: at infinity is the bicevian conic of the points :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1` and -p + q + r : p - q + r : p + q - r, given by

  (p - q + r)(p + q - r) x^2 + 2 p (p - q - r) y z + (cyclic) = 0.

  This conic, denoted by BC(P), has center q + r : r + p : p+ q and perspector

  (p - q - r)/(p^2 - q r - r p - p q) : (q - r - p)/(q^2 - r p - p q - q r) : (r - p - q)/(r^2 - p q - q r - r p)

  If P lies inside the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, then BC(P) is an ellipse. If P lies on the nine-point circle, then BC(P) is a right hyperbola.

  The appearance of (i, [name]) in the following list means that BC(X_i) is the named conic:

  (2, Steiner inellipse), (3, nine-point circle), (5, bicevian conic of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, (10, circumellipse of the medial and :term:`incentral triangles <incentral-triangle>` [see X_34585], (115, Kiepert circumhyperbola of the medial triangle) (125, Jerabek circumhyperbola of the medial triangle)

  The appearance of (i, {:math:`n_{1}`, :math:`n_{2}`, ..., :math:`n_{k}`}) in the next list means that BC(X_i) is the conic that passes through the points: :math:`X(n_{1})`, :math:`X(n_{2})`, ..., :math:`X(n_{k})`: (1, {11, 1145, 1146, 2968, 3756, 4904, 6739, 6741, 7358, 8286, 16613, 38992, 39004, 39050, 40608, 40609}); (4, {122, 3184, 13611, 39020, 40616}), [and others].

  Inverse triangles are introduced in the preamble just before X_42005. If :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are triangles and :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is non-degenerate (so that its matrix is invertible), then there exists a unique triangle T such that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T <T>` = :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, and the solution is :g:`T <T>` = inverse(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`)\*\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`. Likewise, there exists a unique triangle T such that :g:`T* <T*>`\ :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, and the solution is :g:`T <T>` = :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ \*inverse(:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`). Following are eight examples [omitted here].

  1. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = cevian(P) and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = cevian(U). The triangle :g:`T <T>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` such that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ \*\ :g:`T <T>` = :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` = u (v + w) (2 p u + q u + r u + p v + r v + p w + q w) : v (u + w) (-q u - r u + p v - r v + p w + q w), (u + v) w (-q u - r u + p v + r v + p w - q w)
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = u (v + w) (q u - r u - p v - r v + p w + q w) : v (u + w) (q u + r u + p v + 2 q v + r v + p w + q w) : (u + v) w (q u + r u - p v - r v - p w + q w)
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = u (v + w) (-q u + r u + p v + r v - p w - q w) : -v (u + w) (-q u - r u + p v - r v + p w + q w) : (u + v) w (q u + r u + p v + r v + p w + q w + 2 r w)

  The locus of a point :g:`U <U>` = :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that T is perspective to the medial triangle is the cubic given by

  (p + r) (q + r) y^2 z + (p + q) (q + r) y z^2 + (cyclic) + 2 (p^2 + q^2 + r^2 + 3(q r + r p + p q)) x y z = 0.

  For :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_148 <X_148>`, this cubic is K185. For :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_150 <X_150>`, the cubic passes through X_i for i = 7, 8, 80, 320, 42482.

  2. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = cevian(P) and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = cevian(U). The triangle :g:`T <T>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` such that :g:`T* <T*>`\ :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` = (q + r) (r v + q w) : (p + r) (-r v + q w) : -(p + q) (-r v + q w)
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = (q + r) (-r u + p w) : (p + r) (r u + p w) : -(p + q) (-r u + p w)
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = (q + r) (-q u + p v), -(p + r) (-q u + p v), (p + q) (q u + p v)

  The locus of a point :g:`U <U>` = :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that T is perspective to the medial triangle is the cubic given by

  p^2 (r (p+r) (q+r) y^2 z - q (p+q) (q+r) y z^2) + (cyclic) = 0.

  | This cubic passes through :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` for every point :g:`P <P>`. For :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, the cubic is K621. The appearance of (i, {:math:`n_{1}`, :math:`n_{2}`, ..., :math:`n_{k}`}) in the next list means that the cubic passes through the points: :math:`X(n_{1})`, :math:`X(n_{2})`, ..., :math:`X(n_{k})`: (1, {1,2,6,37,81,3293,17147,39949,39964})
  | (3, {2,3,97,216,577})
  | (4, [K621],{2,4,6,24,393,847,2052,6515})
  | (5,{2,5,233,31610,36412})
  | [Further examples are omitted here.]

  The triangle sum, :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` of two arbitrary triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is defined in the preamble just before X_42285. The two distributive laws hold:; i.e., if T is a triangle, then

  | :g:`T* <T*>`\ (:g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`) = :g:`T* <T*>`\ :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T* <T*>`\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`)
  | (:g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`)\*\ :g:`T <T>` = (:g:`T_{1} <T_1>` + :g:`T* <T*>`\ :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`)\*T

  For arbitrary points :g:`P <P>` and U, the product triangle cevian(P)\*anticevian(U) is perspective to anticevian(U)\*cevian(P), and the perspector is the P-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`.

  | The product :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = cevian(P)\*cevian(U) is given by
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = (q u + r u + q v + r w) : r v (u + w) : q w (u + v)
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = u (q u + r u + q v + r w) : r v (u + w) : q w (u + v)
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = q u (v + w) : p v (u + w) : w (p u + q v + p w + q w)

  | In particular, the square of cevian(P) is given by
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = p (p q + q^2 + p r + r^2) : q r (p + r) : q r (p + q) :
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = p r (q + r) : q (p^2 + p q + q r + r^2) : p r (p + q) :
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = p q (q + r) : p q (p + r) : r (p^2 + q^2 + p r + q r)

.. _guide-preamble-0612:

* **X_42614**–**X_42621** — **Central angle points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 15, 2021. Suppose the P is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` = angle :g:`BPC << B P C >>`, :g:`B' <B'>` = angle :g:`CPA << C P A >>`, :g:`C' <C'>` = angle :g:`APB << A P B >>`, and assume that :g:`A' <A'>` = t\*A + u\*(B + C) for some real numbers t and u. Since B + :g:`C <C>` = π - A, the angle :g:`A' <A'>` is given by

  :g:`A' <A'>` = :g:`A' <A'>`\ (t) = t\*(3A - π)/2 + π - A, and :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` are determined cyclically, and the corresponding point :g:`P <P>` = P(t) is given by

  P(t)= 1/(cot(A) + cot(A - t\*(3\*A - π)/2)) : : ,

  so that P(t) is a :term:`major center <major-center>`, here named the **t-central angle point**. Let :g:`L <L>` denote the locus of P(t) as t traverses the real number line, and note that P(2 - t) = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P(t), so that if a point :g:`X <X>` is on :g:`L <L>`, then the isogonal conjugate of :g:`X <X>` is also on L. The appearance of (t,i) in the following list means :g:`P <P>` = X_i is the point for which :g:`A' <A'>`\ (t) = angle :g:`BPC << B P C >>`, :g:`B' <B'>`\ (t) = angle :g:`CPA << C P A >>`, :g:`C' <C'>`\ (t) = angle :g:`APB << A P B >>`. The list is presented in isogonal conjugate pairs:

  | (-2,5964); (4,5963)
  | (-1,41622); (3,42621)
  | (-2/3,42619; (8/3,42620)
  | (0,4); (2,3)
  | (1/3,42615); (5/3,42616)
  | (1/2,42618); (3/2,42614)
  | (2/3,13); (4/3,15)
  | (1,1); (1,1)

Then the point :g:`P″ <P″>` = (p/u)\*p' : (q/v)\*q' + (r/w)\*r' (p/u)\*p' : (q/v)\*q' + (r/w)\*r' lies on L For example, if :g:`P' <P'>` is on the Euler line and L is the Lemoine axis, :ref:`X_187 <X_187>`\ \ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`, then :g:`P″ <P″>` is on L. .. _guide-preamble-0615:

* **X_42676**–**X_42681** — **Centers on cubic K588**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 19, 2021. The three internal bisectors :g:`AI <[ A I ]>`, :g:`BI <[ B I ]>`, :g:`CI <[ C I ]>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are rotated about each corresponding vertex of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` of a same angle θ, all outwardly or all inwardly. The six rotated bisectors define a triangle :g:`N_{a}N_{b}N_{c} << N_a N_b N_c >>` which is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at a point :g:`P <P>`. The locus of :g:`P <P>` is K588. (Reference: `Bernard Gibert, CTC K588) <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k588.html>`__

  For a given angle θ, the perspector P(θ), here denoted by K588(θ), has barycentrics coordinates:

  P(θ) = a\*sin(A/2 - θ)/sin(A/2 + θ) : : , or, equivalently,

  P(t) = a\*((a+b+c)\*(-a+b+c)\*t-:g:`S* <S*>`\ (1-t^2))/((a+b+c)\*(-a+b+c)\*t+\ :g:`S* <S*>`\ (1-t^2)) : :, where t = tan(θ/2)

  Some perspectors K588(θ) are shown in the following table: [table omittd here]. Note: P(θ) and P(-θ) are :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>`.

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 23, 2021. Suppose that :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`p' : q' : r'` is a point on a line p x + q y + r z = 0 and that u x + v y + w z = 0 is a line, L. Then the point :g:`P″ <P″>` = (p/u)\*p' : (q/v)\*q' + (r/w)\*r' (p/u)\*p' : (q/v)\*q' + (r/w)\*r' lies on L For example, if :g:`P' <P'>` is on the line at infinity and L is the Sherman line, :ref:`X_3259 <X_3259>`\ \ :ref:`X_3326 <X_3326>`, then the point :g:`P' <P'>`\ \*X_10015 is on L. Points X_42750-X_42772 are obtained in this manner from the line at infinity, where, in the same order, :g:`P' <P'>` = X_i for i = 30, 511, 512, 513, 514, 515, 516, 517, 518, 523, 524, 525, 527, 528, 536, 537, 726, 740, 758, 912, 918, 926, 971.

.. _guide-preamble-0623:

* **X_42819**–**X_42887** — **Parallels-perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 27, 2021. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be a triangle perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector P. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` be the points at which the parallel line to :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` through P cuts :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` and :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively, and build :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. Then these six points lie on a conic **q**. Swapping the triangles, the six points :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>`, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>`, :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>`, :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>`, :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>` :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>`, constructed similarly, also lie on another conic **q'**.

  Conics **q** and **q'** are introduced here as the **parallels-perspeconic of ABC to A'B'C'** and the **parallels-perspeconic of A'B'C to ABC**, respectively.

  Assume :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is reference triangle, the perspector :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics) and Q, :g:`Q' <Q'>` are the centers of **q** and **q'**, respectively.

  | If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P then :g:`Q' <Q'>` = :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` = (y + z)\*x : :, i.e., Q is the :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and P. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of P then :g:`Q <Q>` = P and :g:`Q' <Q'>` = x\*(y + z-x): :, i.e., :g:`Q' <Q'>` is the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-CevaConjugate-of-P. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the circumcevian triangle of P then:
  | :g:`Q <Q>` = 2\*(y + z)\*b^2\*c^2\*x^3 + ((3\*a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*c^2\*y^2 + 4\*S^2\*y\*z + (3\*a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*b^2\*z^2)\*x^2 + 2\*((2\*y + z)\*z^2\*b^2 + (y + 2\*z)\*y^2\*c^2)\*a^2\*x + 2\*a^4\*y^2\*z^2 : :
  | :g:`Q' <Q'>` = 4\*(y + z)\*b^2\*c^2\*x^3 + x^2\*(c^2\*y^2 + b^2\*z^2)\*(3\*a^2 + b^2 + c^2)-x\*y\*z\*((a^2\*(a^2-b^2-c^2)-4\*b^2\*c^2)\*x + a^2\*(a^2-b^2-3\*c^2)\*y + a^2\*(a^2-3\*b^2-c^2)\*z)-2\*a^4\*y^2\*z^2 : :

  More generally: If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` perspective at :g:`P <P>` to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then there exists an homogeneous degree-0 function ƒ(a,b,c) such that :g:`PA' <[ P A' ]>`\ =ƒ(a,b,c)\*\ :g:`PA <[ P A ]>`, :g:`PB' <[ P B' ]>`\ =ƒ(b,c,a)\*\ :g:`PB <[ P B ]>` and :g:`PC' <[ P C' ]>`\ =ƒ(c,a,b)\*\ :g:`PC <[ P C ]>`. Shortening the notation to ƒ(a,b,c)=ƒ\ :sub:`a`, ƒ(b,c,a)=ƒ\ :sub:`b`, ƒ(c,a,b)=ƒ\ :sub:`c`, the centers of the conics are:

  :g:`Q <Q>` = ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c`\ \*((2\*((ƒ\ :sub:`b` + ƒ\ :sub:`c`)\*x + (y + z)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`))\*y\*z\*ƒ\ :sub:`a` + (-x^2\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c` + y^2\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c` + z^2\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`b`)\*x)\*x : :

  | :g:`Q' <Q'>` = x\*(ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c`\ \*((x + (y + z)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`)\*x^3\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c` - y\*z\*((y + 2\*z)\*z\*ƒ\ :sub:`b` + (2\*y + z)\*y\*ƒ\ :sub:`c` + 2\*y\*z)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ ^2) + x\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c`\ \*(((y^2 + 4\*y\*z + z^2)\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ \*ƒ\ :sub:`c` - 2\*(2\*y + z)\*z\*ƒ\ :sub:`b` - 2\*(y + 2\*z)\*y\*ƒ\ :sub:`c`)\*x
  | - ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ \*(y^3\*ƒ\ :sub:`c` + z^3\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`) - ((ƒ\ :sub:`c` + 4)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a` - 2\*(ƒ\ :sub:`b` - 2)\*ƒ\ :sub:`c`)\*y^2\*z - ((ƒ\ :sub:`b` + 4)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a` - 2\*(ƒ\ :sub:`c` - 2)\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`)\*y\*z^2) - ((ƒ\ :sub:`b` - 1)\*y^4\*ƒ\ :sub:`c`\ ^2 + (ƒ\ :sub:`c` - 1)\*z^4\*ƒ\ :sub:`b`\ ^2)\*ƒ\ :sub:`a`\ ^2) : :

  The appearance of (T, i, j) in the following partial list means that the centers of the parallels-perspeconics of triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-to-T and T-to-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` are X_i and X_j: (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 182, 3098), (anti-Aquila, 1001, 42819), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0625:

* **X_43034**–**X_43068** — **Points on the Gergonne line**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 3, 2021. The Gergonne line of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the line :ref:`X_241 <X_241>`\ \ :ref:`X_514 <X_514>`. If X is a point on the line at infinity, then the barycentric product :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`\ \*X is on the Gergonne line. Let g(X) denote the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of X. Then the :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`-:term:`isoconjugate <isoconjugate>` of g(X) lies on the circumcircle. More generally, if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r`, then the P-isoconjugate of the isogonal of the line at infinity is the line b\*c\*p + c\*a\*q + a\*b\*r = 0, and the P-isoconjugate of the line at infinity is the circumconic a^3\*q\*r\*y\*z + b^3\*r\*p\*x\*z + c^3\*p\*q\*x\*y = 0.

.. _guide-preamble-0626:

* **X_43118**–**X_43192** — **Points associated witrh co-Brocard circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 6, 2021. *If two non-equilateral triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` share the same Brocard axis then their Brocard points, which are symmetrical with respect to this axis, lie on a circle*. This circle is named here the **co-Brocard circle of T' and T"** and its center lies on the common Brocard axis. (Note: the given condition is sufficient for the circularity of Brocard points, but not necessary).

  The reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` shares its Brocard axis with these triangles: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 5th anti-Brocard, anti-inner-Grebe, anti-outer-Grebe, anti-1st Kenmotu-free-vertices, anti-2nd Kenmotu-free-vertices, anti-X3-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` reflections, Apollonius, 2nd Brocard, 5th Brocard, circumsymmedial, inner-Grebe, outer-Grebe, 1st Kenmotu-free-vertices, 2nd Kenmotu-free-vertices, Lucas inner, Lucas(-1) inner, Lucas tangents, Lucas(-1) tangents, X3-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` reflections. Other groups of triangles having common Brocard axes are showed in the following table [table omitted here].:

  In this section, a set of new anti-triangles is introduced: {anti-1st Auriga, anti-2nd Auriga, anti-Ehrmann-mid, anti-inner-Garcia, anti-1st Kenmotu-free-vertices, anti-2nd Kenmotu-free-vertices, anti-1st Parry, anti-2nd Parry, anti-3rd tri-squares-central, anti-4th tri-squares-central, anti-X3-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` reflections, anti-inner-Yff, anti-outer-Yff}. The anti-triangle of a triangle T (denoted anti-T) is defined as the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` such that T-of-:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. For coordinates of all triangles cited here, see the **Index of triangles referenced in ETC** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

  | -(b + c) (a b - a c + b c) : -(a + c) (a b + a c - b c) : (a + b) (a b + a c + b c)}

  The locus of a point X such that the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>` is perspective to the inverse of triangle Gemini 15 is the cubic K033 = pK(:ref:`X_37 <X_37>`,\ :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`), which passes through X_i for i = 1,4,8,10,40,65,72,3176,5930,39130,39131l.

.. _guide-preamble-0630:

* **X_43281**–**X_43290** — **Perpsectors of Gemini triangles and their inverses**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 12, 2021. For an introduction to inverse triangles, see the preamble just before X_42005. If :g:`T <T>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` of type 1 with :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`u : q : r`, then the inverse of :g:`T <T>` is a central of type 1 with :g:`A <A>`-vertex given by

  (v w - q r)(u + q + r) : q (r - w) (v + r + p) : r (q - v)( w + p + q).

  (To see that this inverse is central of type 1, divide the coordinates by (r - w) (q - v).)

  The appearance of (T,j) in the following list means that the triangle :g:`T <T>` is perspective to its inverse and that the perspector is X_j: (medial,2), (anticomplementary,2), (orthic,155), (tangential,159), (incentral, 3159), (excentral, 40), (intouch,3174), (extouch,40), (Euler,4), [and others]

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that the triangle Gemini i is perspective to its inverse and that the perspector is X_j:

  (1,43281), (2,100), (4,31310), (9,43282), (13,43283), (14,43284), (15,43220), (16,43224), [and others]

  Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`. The inverse of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` is the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of q + r : r + p : p + q, and the perspector is the :g:`P' <P'>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P″ <P″>`, where :g:`P' <P'>` = :term:`complement <complement>` of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`P″ <P″>` = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of P. The perspector is given by

  | (q + r)(q^2 r + q r^2 - r^2 p - r p^2 - p^2 q - p q^2) :
  | (r + p)(r^2 p + r P^2 - p^2 q - p q^2 - q^2 r - q r^2) :
  | (p + q)(p^2 q + p q^2 - q^2 r - q r^2 - r^2 p - r p^2).

  The inverse of the anticevian triangle of :g:`P <P>` is the cevian triangle of - p + q + r : p - q + r : p + q - r, and the perspector is the :g:`P' <P'>`-Ceva conjugate of :g:`P″ <P″>`, where :g:`P' <P'>` = anticomplement of :g:`P <P>`, and :g:`P″ <P″>` = complement of P. The perspector is given by

  | p (p^3 - q^3 - r^3 + q^2 r + q r^2 - r^2 p - r p^2 - p^2 q - p q^2 - 2 p q r) :
  | q (q^3 - r^3 - p^3 + r^2 p + r p^2 - p^2 q - p q^2 - q^2 r - q r^2 - 2 p q r) :
  | r (r^3 - p^3 - q^3 + p^2 q + p q^2 - q^2 r - q r^2 - r^2 p - r p^2 - 2 p q r).

  For circumcevian triangles and their inverses, see the preamble just before X_43344.

For an introduction to inverse triangles, see the preambles just before X_42005 and X43280). The perspector of the circumcevian triangle :g:`T <T>` of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and the inverse of T lies on the circumcircle. The :g:`A <A>`-vertex of :g:`T <T>` is -a^2 q r : (b^2 r + c^2 q) q : (b^2 r + c^2 q) r. The inverse of :g:`T <T>` is given by the following :g:`A <A>`-vertex:

  | a^2 q r ((a^2-b^2-c^2) q r - b^2 r^2 - c^2 q^2) :
  | q (b^2 r + c^2 q)((a^2 - b^2 + c^2) p r + a^2 r^2 + c^2 p^2) :
  | r (c^2 p + a^2 r)((a^2 + b^2 - c^2) p q + a^2 r^2 + b^2 p^2).

  The two triangles are perspective, and their perspector, f(P), is given by

  a^2/(a^2 (q - r) + (b^2 - c^2) p) : b^2 (b^2 (r - p) + (c^2 - a^2) q) : c^2 (c^2 (p - q) + (a^2 - b^2) r).

  Let L(P) denote the line of :g:`P <P>` and :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. If U lies on L(P), then :math:`f(U) = a^{2}/(a^{2}(v - w) + (b^{2}-c^{2})u)`: :

.. _guide-preamble-0635:

* **X_43390**–**X_43396** — **Points associated with the Kiss-Moses mapping**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 15, 2021. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, with circumcenter O and orthocenter H, let

  | :g:`D <D>` = :g:`AH <[ A H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BO <[ B O ]>`, :g:`E <E>` = :g:`BH <[ B H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CO <[ C O ]>`, :g:`F <F>` = :g:`CH <[ C H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`AO <[ A O ]>`
  | :g:`D' <D'>` = :g:`AH <[ A H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CO <[ C O ]>`, :g:`E' <E'>` = :g:`BH <[ B H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`AO <[ A O ]>`, :g:`F' <F'>` = :g:`CH <[ C H ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BO <[ B O ]>`
  | :g:`D″ <D″>` = midpoint(D,\ :g:`D' <D'>`), :g:`E″ <E″>` = midpoint(E,\ :g:`E' <E'>`), :g:`F″ <F″>` = midpoint(F,\ :g:`F' <F'>`)

  The points :g:`D <D>` and :g:`D' <D'>` and associated triangles, circles, and quadrangles comprise the Kiss-BirÃ³ configuration, introduced in "Two Remarkable Triangles of a Triangle and Their Circumcircles", by SÃ¡ndor Nagydonbai Kiss and BÃ¡lint BirÃ³. `Elemente der Mathematik (April 2020) <https://ems.press/journals/em/articles/690852>`__.

  Peter Moses noted that for many choices of i, the point X_i-of-:g:`D″E″F″ << D″ E″ F″ >>` = X_j-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` for some j. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` is a point and P-of-:g:`D″E″F″ << D″ E″ F″ >>` = :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`, then the mapping P → U is here named the **Kiss-Moses mapping**, and the image of :g:`P <P>` is denoted by KM(P). Moses established that this mapping is one-to-one and gave formulas for the mapping and its inverse, denoted by MK(U):

  KM(P) = a^2\*(2\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*p + c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*q + b^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2)\*r) : :

  MK(U) = a^2\*((a^8 - 3\*a^6\*b^2 + 3\*a^4\*b^4 - a^2\*b^6 - 3\*a^6\*c^2 + 7\*a^4\*b^2\*c^2 - 3\*a^2\*b^4\*c^2 - b^6\*c^2 + 3\*a^4\*c^4 - 3\*a^2\*b^2\*c^4 + 2\*b^4\*c^4 - a^2\*c^6 - b^2\*c^6)\*u + (a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 + a^2\*c^2 + b^2\*c^2 - 2\*c^4)\*(a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*v + (a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2)\*(a^4 + a^2\*b^2 - 2\*b^4 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 + b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*w) : :

  The fixed point of the two mappings is :ref:`X_54 <X_54>`.

  The appearance of i → j in the following list means that KM(X_i) = X_j:

  | 15035 → 2→ 9730
  | 110 → 3 → 5 → 13630
  | 43390 → 43391 → 14157 → 74 → 4→ 185 → 13403→ 43392 → 43393
  | [and others]

  If P is on the line at infinity, then KM(P) is also on the line at infinity, and KM(KM(P)) = P. The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that X_i is on the line at infinity and KM(X_i) = X_j:

  (30,5663), (511,542), (512,690), (513,8674), (514,2774), (515,2779), (516,2772), (517,2771), (518,2836), (519,2842), (520,9033), (521,2850), (522,2773), (523,526), (524,2854), (525,9517)

  If P is on the line at infinity, then the self-inversive restriction of the mapping KM (to the line at infinity), here denoted by IKM, is given by

  IKM(P) = a^2\*(c^2\*(a^2 - c^2)\*q + b^2\*(a^2 - b^2)\*r)^2\*((a^2 - b^2)\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*q - b^2\*(b^2 - c^2)\*r)\*(c^2\*(b^2 - c^2)\*q + (a^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*r)\*(-(c^2\*q^2) + (a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r - b^2\*r^2) : :

.. _guide-preamble-0641:

* **X_43630**–**X_43649** — **Points on the Pythagorean conic**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, June 7, 2021. As introduced by :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>` in `K1231 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k1231.html>`__, the **Pythagorean conic** is the set of KHO points (x,y,z) that satisfy :math:`z^{2}` = :math:`x^{2}` + :math:`y^{2}` but not x\*y\*z = 0. If (x,y,z) is such a point, then so are these seven points:

  (-x,y,z), (x,-y,z), (x,y,-z), (y,x,z), (-y,x,z), (y,-x,z), (y,x,-z).

  Thus, if (u,v,w) is a Pythagorean triple of integers, then then the Gibert (u,v,w) point lies on the Pythagorean conic.

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, June 20, 2021. Let KM and MK be the Kiss-Moses mapping and its inverse, as introduced in the preabmle just before X_43390. For many pairs of triangles :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>`, the triangle KM(U) is perspective to MK(V) and KM(V) is perspective to MK(U). In some cases, the two perspectors are the same point. This section presents several such points. The appearance of (i,U,V) in the following list means that KM(U) is perspective to MK(V) and KM(V) is perspective to MK(U) and that in both cases, the perspector is X_i [list omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0647:

* **X_43921**–**X_43933** — **Points on the circumparabola with center X_513**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 2, 2021. Suppose that :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The locus of of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that the circumconic {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`U <U>`,\ :g:`X <X>`}} is a parabola is given by the quartic equation f(u,v,w,x,y,z) + f(v,w,u,y,z,x) + :math:`f(w,u,v,z,x,y) = 0`, where

  :math:`f(u,v,w,x,y,z) = u^{2} (v + w)^{2} y^{2} z^{2} - 2 v w (-v w + u(u + v + w)x^{2} y z)`.

  If U lies on the line at infinity, then :g:`U <U>` = (b - c)(1 + b t + c t) : (c - a)(1 + c t + a t) : (a - b)(1 + a t + b t)

  for some function t that is symmetric in a,b,c and has degree 0 of homogeneity. In this case,

  :math:`f(x,y,z,u,v,w) = ((b - c)^{2} (1 + b t + c t)^{2} y z)^{2}`.

  The appearance of i, {:math:`j_{1}`, :math:`j_{2}`,..., :math:`j_{k}`} in the following list means that the circumparabola with center X_i passes through the points :math:`X(j_{1})`,\ :math:`X(j_{2})`,..., :math:`X(j_{k})`:

  | 30, {30,476,3233,4240,9141,16077}
  | 511, {511,805,877,14966,15631}
  | 512, {512,669,805,875,881,886,15630,32729,38241}
  | 513, {513,649,660,889,901,3572,3733,4581,7192,15635,17929,17940,23345,23836,32735,35365,38242,42921---43933}
  | 514, {514,693,927,3676,4444,4555,4583,4608,4817,6548,6549,7192,15634,17925,17930,37143}
  | 516, {516,927,3234,23973,41321}
  | 517, {517,901,15632,23981,38243}
  | 518, {518,660,677,883,2284,6078}
  | 519, {519,4555,6079,17780,38244}
  | [and others]

  {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,523,476}} is the "X-parabola of :g:`ABC″ << A B C″ >>`, as in X_12065.

  See Michel Bataille, :cite:`Forum Geometricorum <forum-geometricorum>` 11 (2011) 57-63, `On the Foci of Circumparabolas <https://forumgeom.fau.edu/FG2011volume11/FG201107.pdf>`__ and :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`, `Q077 <http://bernard-gibert.fr/curves/q077.html>`__

  If PP is one of these circumparabolas, let :g:`P' <P'>` be its perspector. Then if :g:`P″ <P″>` is a point on the circumcircle, then the point :g:`P″ <P″>`\ \*\ :g:`P' <P'>`/:ref:`X_6 <X_6>` is on PP. Various choices of :g:`P″ <P″>` yeild the points X_42921-X_43933.

  | [and others]

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that the 1st Vijay parallel transform of X_i is X_j:

  | {1,596}, {2,2}, {3,6662}, {4,68}, {6,6664}, {7,6601}, {8,4}, {20,3346}, {69,66}, {75,13476}, {76,27375}, {99,36955}, {144,42483}, {145,6553}, {192,2998}, {193,6339}, {194,42486}, {264,42487}, {329,34546}, {3869,42485}, {4329,42484}, {4560,15412}, {5905,6504}, {6360,34287}, {7057,8}, {16017,189}, {16018,39694}, {20346,7357}, {20534,7}, {40383,330}
  | Also, if X is on the line at infinity, then the 1st Vijay parallel transform of :g:`X <X>` is X.

  [Lists for other Vijay parallet transforms (numbered 2 to 13) are omitted here.]

  The Vijay 1st parallel transform of :g:`U <U>` is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the Vu tangential transform of :g:`U <U>`, and the perspector of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the reflection of the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>` in the centroid of ABCU. It is also the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of the centroid of {{[:term:`complement <complement>` of U], [vertices of anticevain triangle of complement of U]}}, and also the isogonal conjugate of the TCC-perspector of [isogonal conjugate of complement of U]. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, August 24, 2021)

* **X_44021**–**X_44025** — **Points associated with Vijay-Hutson triangles**

  | contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (July 21, 2021), based on notes from :person:`Dasari Naga Vijay Krishna <dasari-naga-vijay-krishna>`, July 21, 2021 and later from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let
  | :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` = parabola with A as its focus and :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` as its directrix, define :g:`P_{b} <P_b>` and :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = apex of equilateral triangle erected externally on the side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = apex of equilateral triangle erected internally on the side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = (triangle :g:`BCA' << B C A' >>`)∩\ :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically; see **Vijay 3 parabolas and 6 points.png** (``Vijay%203%20parabolas%20and%206%20points.png``) :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = (triangle :g:`BCA' << B C A' >>`) ∩\ :g:`P_{c} <P_c>`, and define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = (triangle :g:`BCA″ << B C A″ >>`)∩\ :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, and define :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>` and :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` = (triangle :g:`BCA″ << B C A″ >>`)∩\ :g:`P_{c} <P_c>`, and define :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>` and :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` = :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` = :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`A_{b}C_{b} <[ A_b C_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{c}A_{c} <[ B_c A_c ]>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` = :g:`C_{a}B_{a} <[ C_a B_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{c}A_{c} <[ B_c A_c ]>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` = :g:`C_{a}B_{a} <[ C_a B_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{b}C_{b} <[ A_b C_b ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`C'_{a}C'_{b} <[ C'_a C'_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}B'_{a} <[ B'_c B'_a ]>`, :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` = :g:`C'_{a}C'_{b} <[ C'_a C'_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A'_{b}A'_{c} <[ A'_b A'_c ]>`, :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` = :g:`A'_{b}A'_{c} <[ A'_b A'_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}B'_{a} <[ B'_c B'_a ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` = :g:`A'_{b}C'_{b} <[ A'_b C'_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}A'_{c} <[ B'_c A'_c ]>`, :g:`B_{4} <B_4>` = :g:`C'_{a}B'_{a} <[ C'_a B'_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}A'_{c} <[ B'_c A'_c ]>`, :g:`C_{4} <C_4>` = :g:`C'_{a}B'_{a} <[ C'_a B'_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A'_{b}C'_{b} <[ A'_b C'_b ]>`;

.. _guide-preamble-0651:

* **X_44039**–**X_44041** — **Points associated with Vijay incentral circles and excentral circles**

  | contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (July 26, 2021), based on notes from :person:`Dasari Naga Vijay Krishna <dasari-naga-vijay-krishna>`, July 25, 2021. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>`
  | :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` = circle with diameter :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`O_{b} <O_b>` and :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = :g:`BB' <[ B B' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = :g:`CC' <[ C C' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, and define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = :g:`A'C' <[ A' C' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, and define :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>` and :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` = :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, and define :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>` and :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>` cyclically;
  | Oe = circle {{:g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>`, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>`, :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>`, :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>`, :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>`, :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>`}}, here named the **Vijay excentral circle**;
  | :g:`OI_{a} <[ O I_a ]>` = circle {{:g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>`, :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`}}, here named the **Vijay a-incentral circle**;
  | :g:`OI_{b} <[ O I_b ]>` = circle {{:g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>`, :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`}}, here named the **Vijay b-incentral circle**;
  | :g:`OI_{c} <[ O I_c ]>` = circle {{:g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>`, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`}}, here named the **Vijay c-incentral circle**;
  | :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` = polar of :g:`A <A>` wrt Oe, and define :g:`P_{b} <P_b>` and :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`L'_{a} <L'_a>` = polar of :g:`A <A>` wrt :g:`OI_{a} <[ O I_a ]>`, and define :g:`L'_{b} <L'_b>` and :g:`L'_{c} <L'_c>` cyclically.

  Barycentric equations for Vijay incentral and excentral circles and their centers:

  | Vijay excentral circle:
  | (s - b)(s - c)x^2 + (s -c)(s - a)y^2 + (s - a)(s - b)z^2 + s(ayz + bzx + cxy) = 0, with center :ref:`X_10 <X_10>` = b + c : c + a : a + b

  | Vijay a-incentral circle:
  | (s - b)(s - c)x^2 - (s)(s - b)y^2 - (s)(s - c)z^2 + (s - a)(- ayz + bzx + cxy) = 0, with center b + c : c - a : b - a

  | Vijay b-incentral circle:
  | -s(s - a)x^2 +(s - a)(s - c)y^2 - (s)(s - c)z^2 + (s - b)(ayz - bzx + cxy) = 0, with center c - b : c + a : a - b

  | Vijay c-incentral circle:
  | -s(s - a)x^2 - (s)(s - b)y^2 + (s - a)(s - b)z^2 + (s - c)(ayz + bzx - cxy) = 0, with center b - c : a - c : a + b

  Define 6 points by the following intersections :

  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = :g:`B'_{c}B'_{a} <[ B'_c B'_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C'_{a}C'_{b} <[ C'_a C'_b ]>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` = :g:`C'_{a}C'_{b} <[ C'_a C'_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`A'_{b}A'_{c} <[ A'_b A'_c ]>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` = :g:`A'_{b}A'_{c} <[ A'_b A'_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}B'_{a} <[ B'_c B'_a ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` = :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` = :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`C'_{a}A'_{c} <[ C'_a A'_c ]>`\ ∩ :g:`B'_{a}A'_{b} <[ B'_a A'_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C_{a}A_{c} <[ C_a A_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B_{a}A_{b} <[ B_a A_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` = midpoint of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`,
  | :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` = :g:`B'_{a}A'_{b} <[ B'_a A'_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'_{c}C'_{b} <[ B'_c C'_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`B_{a}A_{b} <[ B_a A_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`B_{c}C_{b} <[ B_c C_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`CA <[ C A ]>` = midpoint of :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`,
  | :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` = :g:`B'_{c}C'_{b} <[ B'_c C'_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`C'_{a}A'_{c} <[ C'_a A'_c ]>`\ ∩ :g:`B_{c}C_{b} <[ B_c C_b ]>`\ ∩ :g:`C_{a}A_{c} <[ C_a A_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` = midpoint of :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`;
  | :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` = center of Vijay a-incentral circle, and define :g:`B_{4} <B_4>` and :g:`C_{4} <C_4>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{5} <A_5>` = :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`P_{c} <P_c>`, and define :g:`B_{5} <B_5>` and :g:`C_{5} <C_5>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{6} <A_6>` = :g:`L'_{b} <L'_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`L'_{c} <L'_c>`, and define :g:`B_{6} <B_6>` and :g:`C_{6} <C_6>` cyclically

  Barycentrics for points defined above:

  | :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = a : c - a : c, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` =\ :math:`a : b : b` - a
  | :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = -a : a + c : c, :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` = :math:`-a : b : a` + b
  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = :math:`-a(b + c) : S_{C} : S_{B}`
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = 0 : s - c : s - b
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` =\ :math:`0 : 1 : 1`;
  | :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` = b + c : c - a : b - a
  | :g:`A_{5} <A_5>` = 4\*(s - a)^2\*(s - b)\*(s - c) - s^2\*a^2 : s^2\*a\*b - 2\*s\*c\*(s - a)\*(s - b) : s^2\*a\*c - 2\*s\*b\*(s - c)\*(s - a)
  | :g:`A_{6} <A_6>` = ((b + c)\*(b + c - 2\*a)\*(s - b)\*(s - c)) : ((s - b)\*(a\*b\*(s - c) + 2\*c\*(s - a)\*(s - b))) : ((s - c)\*(a\*c\*(s - b) + 2\*b\*(s - a)\*(s - c)))

  Related triangles are here named:

  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = Vijay excentral triangle;
  | :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` = :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`;
  | :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` ;
  | :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` = Vijay abc-:term:`incentral triangle <incentral-triangle>`; Also, :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` = Wasat triangle
  | :g:`A_{5}B_{5}C_{5} << A_5 B_5 C_5 >>` = Vijay polar excentral triangle;
  | :g:`A_{6}B_{6}C_{6} << A_6 B_6 C_6 >>` = Vijay polar incentral triangle.

  Collinearities and Perspectors [omitted here]:

  The Vijay excentral circle is the Spieker radical circle. The Vijay incentral circles are the extraversions of the Spieker radical circle. That is, the Vijay a-incentral circle is the radical circle of the incircle and the B- and :g:`C <C>`-excircles, and cyclically for the Vijay b- and c-incentral circles. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, September 30, 2021)

  The Vijay excentral circle and the three Vijay incentral circles are Taylor circles of the excentral triangle. (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, October 26, 2021)

  :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = Vijay excentral triangle is the 2nd :term:`extouch triangle <extouch-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (:person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 6, 2022)

.. _guide-preamble-0652:

* **X_44077**–**X_44155** — **Points of the form tgX or gtX, where X is on the Euler line**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 8-11, 2021. For any :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` P, let gP and tP denote the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` and the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, respectively. Centers X_44077-X_44127 are points of the form tg(X), and X_44128-X_44155 of the form gt(X), where X lies on the Euler line. The appearance of (h,i,j,k,m) in the following list means that X_j is on the Euler line, and (X(h), X_i, X_j, X_k, X(m)) = (gtX, tX, X, gX, tgX): (6,2,2,6,76), (184,264,3,4,69), [and others]

  Recall that if L is a line, then gL and tL are conics, and tgL and gtL are lines. Each X on the Euler lines is given by a :term:`combo <combo>` :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` + k\*(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, and the locus of gtX is the line

  4\*(a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*(2 + 3\*k)\*S^2 :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` - 3\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(3 + J^2)\*k\*\ :ref:`X_25 <X_25>`, which, for each k, is a point on the line :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_25 <X_25>`.

  The locus of tgX is the line

  16\*S^4\*\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` - a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*(J^2 - 9 - 12\*k)\*\ :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`, which, for each k, is a point on the line :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`.

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 10-12, 2021. For any :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` P, let gP and tP denote the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` and the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, respectively. Centers X_44159-X_44173 are members of chains of points

.. _guide-preamble-0654:

* **X_44192**–**X_44200** — **Points associated with Vijay orthic polar triangle of circumcircle**

  contributed by :person:`Dasari Naga Vijay Krishna <dasari-naga-vijay-krishna>`, July 26, 2021.

  | In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`O <O>` = circumcircle of triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. let
  | :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` = circle with diameter :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`O_{b} <O_b>` and :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`L_{a} <L_a>` = The perpendicular from :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` of triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to side :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, define :g:`L_{b} <L_b>` and :g:`L_{c} <L_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`L_{a} <L_a>` ∩\ :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` such that :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` is nearer to A than :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, and define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically;
  | :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`, :g:`T'_{a} <T'_a>` = polar of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` wrt :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>`, :g:`T'_{b} <T'_b>`, :g:`T_{c} <T_c>`, :g:`T'_{c} <T'_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P'_{a} <P'_a>` = polar of :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` wrt O, define :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P'_{b} <P'_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` and :g:`P'_{c} <P'_c>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` ∩ :g:`T_{c} <T_c>`, :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` = :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` ∩ :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`, :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` = :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` ∩ :g:`T_{b} <T_b>`;
  | :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` = :g:`T'_{b} <T'_b>` ∩ :g:`T'_{c} <T'_c>`, :g:`B_{4} <B_4>`\ = :g:`T'_{c} <T'_c>` ∩ :g:`T'_{a} <T'_a>`, :g:`C_{4} <C_4>` = :g:`T'_{a} <T'_a>` ∩ :g:`T'_{b} <T'_b>`;
  | :g:`A_{5} <A_5>` = :g:`P_{b} <P_b>` ∩ :g:`P_{c} <P_c>`, :g:`B_{5} <B_5>`\ = :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` ∩ :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`C_{5} <C_5>` = :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` ∩ :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`;
  | :g:`A_{6} <A_6>` = :g:`P'_{b} <P'_b>` ∩ :g:`P'_{c} <P'_c>`, :g:`B_{6} <B_6>`\ = :g:`P'_{c} <P'_c>` ∩ :g:`P'_{a} <P'_a>`, :g:`C_{6} <C_6>` = :g:`P'_{a} <P'_a>` ∩ :g:`P'_{b} <P'_b>`;

  Barycentrics: [omitted here]

  Related triangles are here named as follows:

  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` = 1st Vijay orthic polar triangle of circumcircle;
  | :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` = 2nd Vijay orthic polar trriangle of circumcircle;
  | :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` = 3rd Vijay orthic polar trriangle of circumcircle;
  | :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` = 4th Vijay orthic polar trriangle of circumcircle;
  | :g:`A_{5}B_{5}C_{5} << A_5 B_5 C_5 >>` = 5th Vijay orthic polar trriangle of circumcircle;
  | :g:`A_{6}B_{6}C_{6} << A_6 B_6 C_6 >>` = 6th Vijay orthic polar trriangle of circumcircle.

  | The first four of those triangles have been introduced previously:
  | :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is the outer Vecten triangle.
  | :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` is the inner Vecten triangle.
  | :g:`A_{3}B_{3}C_{3} << A_3 B_3 C_3 >>` is the 1st anti-Kenmotu-centers triangle.
  | :g:`A_{4}B_{4}C_{4} << A_4 B_4 C_4 >>` is the 2nd anti-Kenmotu-centers triangle.

  f(a,b,c,x,y,z) + f(b,c,a,y,z x) + :math:`f(c,a,b,z,x,y) = 0`.

  Let :math:`g(a,b,c,x,y,z) = (b - c) (a^{3} - a b^{2} - a c^{2} - 2 a b c + 2 b^{2} c + 2 b c^{2}) (x^{2} - y z)`. The inverse of the line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` in the Steiner inellipse is the ellipse given by

* **X_44550**–**X_44555** — **Centers and perspectors of ellipses [SCE, line] [SIE, line]**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 24-30, 2021. bbreviations: SCE = Steiner circumellipse; SIE = Steiner inellipse. Suppose that L is a line given by u x + v y + w z = 0 (barycentrics). The SCE-inverse of :g:`L <L>`, denoted by [SCE, L], is given by

  u (x^2 - y z) + v (y^2 - z x) + w (z^2 - x y) = 0,

  and the SIE-inverse of :g:`L <L>`, denoted by [SIE, L], is given by

  (2u + v + w) (x^2 - y z) + (u + 2v + w) (y^2 - z x) + (u + v + 2w) (z^2 - x y) = 0.

  The center of [SCE, L] is -u + 2v + 2w : : = reflection of :math:`u : v : w` in :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

  The center of [SIE, L] is 2u + 5v + 5w : : = :term:`complement <complement>` of midpoint of :math:`u : v : w` and :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`.

  The perspector of [SCE, L] is (2 v^2 + u w) (u v + 2 w^2) : : .

  The perspector of [SIE, L] is (4 u^2 + 9 v^2 + 4 w^2 + 11 v w + 9 w u + 11 u v)\*(4 u^2 + 4 v^2 + 9 w^2 + 11 v w + 11 w u + 9 u v) : :

  The appearance of (L, k) in the following list means that X_k is the center of the ellipse [SCE, L]:

  (Brocard axis, 36900), (orthic axis, 1992), (anti-orthic axis, 4664), (Lemoine axis, 7757), (de Longchamps axis, 599), (Gergonne line, 3241), (Fermat line, 9979), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 31150), (Koiller line, 31169), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, 44550), (Soddy line, 44551), (van Aubel line, 44552), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`, 44553), (Napoleon axis, 44554), (Hatzipolakis axis, 44555)

  The appearance of (L, k) in the following list means that X_k is the perspector of the ellipse [SCE, L]:

  (orthic axis, 44556), (Lemoine aixs, 44557), (de Longchamps axis, 44558), (Gergonne line, 44559)

  The appearance of (L, k) in the following list means that X_k is the center of the ellipse [SIE, L]:

  (orthic axis, 597), (anti-orthic axis, 4755), (de Logchamps axis, 20582), (Gergonne line, 551), (brocard axis, 44560), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, 44561), (Lemoinne axis, 44562), (Soddy line, 44563), (Fermat line, 44564), (van Aubel line, 44565), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`, 44566), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 44567), (Napoleon axis, 44568), (Hatzipolakis axis, 44569), (Koiller line, 44570)

.. _guide-preamble-0663:

* **X_44575**–**X_44653** — **and X_44649-X_44653, E-inverses of points on the Euler line, where E is a permutation ellipse**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 1, 2021. Three specific permutation ellipses are described in the preamble just before X_41133, as follows:

  (1) The trisector ellipse passes through the points :math:`0:1:2`,\ :math:`0:2:1`,\ :math:`1:0:2`,\ :math:`2:0:1`,\ :math:`1:2:0`,\ :math:`2:1:0`. These six points trisect the sides of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The ellipse is given by 2(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - 5(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  (2) The unique self-dual permutation ellipse is given by x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - 4 (y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  (3) The Steiner midway ellipse (SME), is, loosely speaking, the ellipse midway between the Steiner inellipse (SIE) and the Steiner circumellipse (SCE). That is, for each P on SCE, let :g:`P' <P'>` be the intersection of the ray GP with SIE, and let :g:`P″ <P″>` be the midpoint of :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>`. Then SME is the set of all such midpoints. SME is given by 7(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - 34(y z + z x + x y) = 0.

  In general, the inverse of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` in an ellipse j (x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - k (y z + z x + x y) = 0 is the point k\*p^2 - j\*p\*q + j\*q^2 - j\*p\*r - k\*q\*r + j\*r^2 : : .

  The center of every permutation ellipse E is :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, so that the E-inverse of each point :g:`P <P>` on the Euler line is also on the Euler line. If :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` + t\*\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and E is give by h\*(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) - k (y z + z x + x y) = 0, then

  (E-inverse of :g:`P <P>`) = (4 (h - k) S^4 + 3 t ((2 h - k) S^4 - (2 h + k) SA SB SC SW)) :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` - 4 (h - k) (1 + t) S^4 :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`.

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_j = trisector-ellipse-inverse of X_i:

  {3,44575}, {4,44576}, {5,44577}, {297,3545}, {376,44578}, {381,44579}, {401,5054}, {441,10304}, {448,15671}, {3524,40884}, {3839,44216}, {5055,40885}, {15699,40853}, {37907,40856}

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_j = Steiner-midway-ellipse-inverse of X_i:

  {297,3860}, {401,44580}, {441,15690}, {12101,44216}, {15685,44335}, {15759,40884}, {19710,44346}, {33699,44334}

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_j = self-dual-ellipse-inverse of X_i: [list omitted here].

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_j = Steiner-circumellipse-inverse of X_i: [list omitted here].

  The appearance of {i,j} in the following list means that X_j = Steiner-incircle-ellipse-inverse of X_i: [list omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0664:

* **X_44582** — **Kenmotu-centers triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 1, 2021. Let :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` be the centers of the inner-Kenmotu squares, as showed in `MathWorld's Kenmotu Point <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/KenmotuPoint.html>`__. Triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is named here the **1st Kenmotu-centers triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. As there exists an outer version of these squares with centers :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`, the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is refered here as the **2nd Kenmotu-centers triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Barycentric coordinates of :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>` are:

  :g:`A' <A'>` = a^2+2\*S : b^2 : c^2

  :g:`A″ <A″>` = a^2-2\*S : b^2 : c^2

  Both triangles are homothetic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with homothetic center :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :ref:`X_371 <X_371>`-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` with respect to the 1st Kenmotu-diagonals triangle and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is the pedal triangle of :ref:`X_372 <X_372>`-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` with respect to the 2nd Kenmotu-diagonals triangle.

  In the following list, (T, i, j) means that pairs of triangles (T, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`), (T, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`) are perspective with perspectors X_i and X_j, respectively: [list omitted here]

.. _guide-preamble-0665:

* **X_44687**–**X_44729** — **Dao-conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, based on notes from :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, September 8, 2021. *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P a point on its plane and and Ω an arbitrary circumconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Lines :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`CP <[ C P ]>` cut again Ω at :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, respectively, and parallel lines through these points to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` cut Ω again at :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`, respectively. Then lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur. (Dao Thanh Oai, May 12, 2021).*

  If barycentric coordinates of the center X of Ω are :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` and :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p: q : r`, then D, the point of intersection of :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>`, is:

  :g:`D <D>` = D(X, P) = x\*(x - y - z)\*q\*r : :

  For a given X, this transformation is an involution. D(X, P) is introduced here as the **X-Dao conjugate of P**. More precisely, D(X, P) may be expressed as an *:term:`isoconjugate <isoconjugate>`*:

  (X-Dao conjugate of W) = W-isoconjugate of :g:`P <P>`, where W = W(X)= a^3\*(x - y + z)\*(x + y - z)\*y\*z : :

  The appearance of (m, n) in the following list means that (X(m)-Dao conjugate of :g:`P <P>`) = X_n-isoconjugate of-P for all points :g:`P <P>`: (1, 56), (2, 31), (3, 1), (4, 19614), (5, 2190), (6, 19), (8, 16945), (9, 6), (10, 58), (11, 109), (31, 7357), (37, 1333), (57, 2192), (66, 19616), (113, 36053), (114, 36051), (115, 163), (119, 36052), (124, 36050), (125, 162), [and others].

  The X-Dao conjugate of :g:`P <P>` is the trilinear quotient P / W, and, among all known kinds of conjugaties, the X-Dao conjugate of :g:`P <P>` is: the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, when Ω is the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (with center :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`), the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, when Ω is the Steiner circumellipse of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (with center :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`), the polar conjugate of :g:`P <P>`, when Ω is the circumconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with center :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_1249 <X_1249>`. This conic is described in :ref:`X1249 <X_1249>`.

  This **figure** (``DaoThreeCubics.png``) shows the locus of a point P such that for :g:`X <X>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, we have D(P,X) = D(X,P). Comparable loci result for other choices of X. In general, each such locus consists of three cubics, each of which passes through the vertices of the :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`, through :g:`X <X>`, and through the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of X. Also, the :g:`A <A>`-cubic passes through :g:`A <A>`, the :g:`B <B>`-cubic passes through :g:`B <B>`, and the :g:`C <C>`-cubic passes through :g:`C <C>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0666:

* **X_44733**–**X_44743** — **Points associated with Vijay ellipses**

  based on notes contributed by :person:`Dasari Naga Vijay Krishna <dasari-naga-vijay-krishna>`, September 6, 2021. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`M_aM_bM_c << M_a M_b M_c >>` = :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` = :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`, and let :g:`E_{a} <E_a>` denote the ellipse that passes through :g:`A <A>` and has foci :g:`M_b <M_b>` and :g:`M_c <M_c>`; clearly :g:`E_{a} <E_a>` passes through :g:`M_a <M_a>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`. Define ellipses :g:`E_{b} <E_b>` and :g:`E_{c} <E_c>` cyclically. Names and barycentric equations for these ellipses follow:

  | :g:`E_{a} <E_a>` = Vijay A-ellipse: (a^2 - b^2 + c^2) y^2 + (a^2 + b^2 - c^2) z^2 - 2 c (b + c) x y - 2 b (b + c) y z = 0
  | :g:`E_{b} <E_b>` = Vijay B-ellipse: (b^2 - c^2 + a^2) z^2 + (b^2 + c^2 - a^2) x^2 - 2 a (c + a) y z - 2 c (c + a) z x = 0
  | :g:`E_{c} <E_c>` = Vijay C-ellipse: (c^2 - a^2 + b^2) x^2 + (c^2 + a^2 - b^2) y^2 - 2 b (a + b) z x - 2 a (c + b) x y = 0

  See **Vijay A-ellipse** (``Vijay%20A-ellipse.pdf``), **Vijay B-ellipse** (``Vijay%20B-ellipse.pdf``), **Vijay C-ellipse** (``Vijay%20C-ellipse.pdf``).

  | Let
  | :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = the point, other than A, in :g:`E_{a} <E_a>`\ ∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = the point, other than A, in :g:`E_{a} <E_a>`\ ∩\ :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`, and define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` = :g:`A_{b}C_{b} <[ A_b C_b ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{c}B_{c} <[ A_c B_c ]>`, and define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>` and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` = :g:`B_{a}B_{c} <[ B_a B_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>`, and define :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{3} <A_3>` = :g:`A_{b}B_{c} <[ A_b B_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{c}C_{b} <[ A_c C_b ]>`, and define :g:`B_{3} <B_3>` and :g:`C_{3} <C_3>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` = :g:`A_{b}C_{a} <[ A_b C_a ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{c}B_{a} <[ A_c B_a ]>`, and define :g:`B_{4} <B_4>` and :g:`C_{4} <C_4>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{5} <A_5>` = the point in :g:`E_{b} <E_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`E_{c} <E_c>` that is closer to A than the other point in :g:`E_{b} <E_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`E_{c} <E_c>`, and define :g:`B_{5} <B_5>` and :g:`C_{5} <C_5>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{6} <A_6>` = the point in :g:`E_{b} <E_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`E_{c} <E_c>`, other than :g:`A_{5} <A_5>`, and define :g:`B_{6} <B_6>` and :g:`C_{6} <C_6>` cyclically;
  | :g:`A_{7} <A_7>` = :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{5}A_{6} <[ A_5 A_6 ]>`, and define :g:`B_{7} <B_7>` and :g:`C_{7} <C_7>` cyclically.

  Barycentrics for the nine points just above are as follows: [omtted herejj]. Collinearities:

  | :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`A_{3} <A_3>`, :g:`A_{4} <A_4>` are collinear.
  | :g:`A_{5} <A_5>`, :g:`A_{6} <A_6>`, :g:`A_{7} <A_7>` are collinear.
  | X_44733, X_44734, X_44739, X_44741 are collinear.
  | X_44733, X_44735, X_44738 are collinear.
  | X_44733, :ref:`X_1659 <X_1659>`, X_44742 are collinear.
  | X_44733, X_13390, X_44743 are collinear.
  | :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, X_44734, :ref:`X_27 <X_27>` are collinear.
  | :ref:`X_1659 <X_1659>`, X_13390, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` are collinear.
  | :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, X_44742, X_44743 are collinear.

  Collinearities and Properties are omitted here.

  The triangle AnBnCn is here named the nth **Vijay triangle**, for n = 1,2,3,4,5,6,7.

.. _guide-preamble-0667:

* **X_44805**–**X_44827** — **Centers of circumcircle-inverses of lines**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 17, 2021. The circumcircle-inverse of a line is a circle. (If the line, L, passes through :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, the circle is has infinite radius; i.e. the inverse is the line L itself.) Suppose that a line :g:`L <L>` is the :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of a point :math:`p : q : r`. The circumcircle-inverse of :g:`L <L>` is the circle with center X and A-power given as follows:

  :g:`X <X>` = a^2\*(c^2\*(a^4 - a^2\*b^2 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*p\*q + b^2\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - a^2\*c^2 - b^2\*c^2)\*p\*r - a^2\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 + c^4)\*q\*r) : :

  A-power: a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*q\*r / (b^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*p\*r + c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*p\*q - a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*q\*r)).

  The appearance of {{i,j}, {:math:`n_{1}`, :math:`n_{2}`, ..., :math:`n_{k}`}, m} in the following list means that the circumcircle-inverse of the line X_iX_j passes through the points :math:`X(n_{1})`, :math:`X(n_{2})`, ..., :math:`X(n_{k})` and has center X(m).

  | {{1,6}, {3,36,187,667,5144,11650,32625,32758},39227}
  | {{1,21}, {3,36,501,1325,1326,3733,5161,5197,5867},39210}
  | {{2,6}, {3,23,187,353,669,5866,5867,5937,5938,5939,5940,5941,6031,32531,34014},5926}
  | {{2,11}, {3,23,100,105,659,1155,5144,9471,14664,14667,19915,19916},44805}
  | {{2,98}, {3,23,98,110,2080,13558,14652,14673,19165,33900,42667,42668},14270}
  | {{2,99}, {3,23,99,111,2079,2930,5104,11641,11643,14669,14678,14682,15564,18773,18774,33998},11616}
