.. _guide-preamble-0668:

* **X_44840**–**X_44859** — **Perspectors involving 8th and 9th mixtilinear triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 18, 2021. :person:`Dan Reznik <dan-reznik>` defines 8th and 9th mixtilinear triangles as follows:

  Let ω':sub:`a`, ω':sub:`b` and ω':sub:`c` be the A-, B- and C- mixtilinear incircles of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and Ω\ :sub:`i` the inner Apollonius circle of them. Denote as :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` the touchpoints of Ω\ :sub:`i` and ω':sub:`a`, ω':sub:`b` and ω':sub:`c`, respectively. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the **8th-mixtilinear triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let ω":sub:`a`, ω":sub:`b` and ω":sub:`c` be the A-, B- and C- mixtilinear excircles of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and Ω\ :sub:`o` the outer Apollonius circle of them. Denote as :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` the touchpoints of Ω\ :sub:`o` and ω":sub:`a`, ω":sub:`b` and ω":sub:`c`, respectively. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is the **9th-mixtilinear triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Barycentric coordinates of the A-vertices of these triangles are:

  8th mixtilinear triangle: :g:`A' <A'>` = a\*(a^2 + 2\*(b + c)\*a - 3\*(b - c)^2)/2 : b^2\*(a - b + c) : c^2\*(a + b - c) 9th mixtilinear triangle: :g:`A″ <A″>` = a\*(a^2 - 2\*(b + c)\*a - 3\*(b - c)^2)/2 : b^2\*(a + b - c) : c^2\*(a - b + c)

  The appearance of (T, i) in the following list means that triangles 8th mixtilinear and T are perspective with perspector X_i: [list omitted here].

  The appearance of (T, i) in the following list means that triangles 9th mixtilinear and T are perspective with perspector X_i: [list omitted here].

  The following pairs of triangles are orthologic: (8th mixtilinear, 4th mixtilinear) and (9th mixtilinear, 3rd mixtilinear). No known triangle was found to be parallelogic to either :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` or :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`. The 9th mixtilinear triangle is also directly similar to these triangles: excenters-midpoints, Garcia-reflection (named Gemini 8 too) and 2nd Schiffler.

.. _guide-preamble-0669:

* **X_44886**–**X_44896** — **Line conjugates on the Euler line**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, September 25, 2021. See the preamble just before :ref:`X_237 <X_237>` for an introduction to :term:`line conjugates <line-conjugate>`. If P and U are points on the Euler line then the :g:`P <P>`-line conjugate of :g:`U <U>` is identical to the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-line conjugate of :g:`U <U>`, and if :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` + k :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, then the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-line conjugate of :g:`U <U>` is given by the :term:`combo <combo>`

  3\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(3\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(3 + J^2)\*k + 4\*(a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*S^2)\*\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` - 4\*S^2\*(3\*a^2\*b^2\*c^2\*(a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*k + 4\*(b^2\*c^2 + a^2\*(b^2 + c^2))\*S^2)\*\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0670:

* **X_44916**–**X_44934** — **Hatzipolakis-Lozada circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 2, 2021. *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`P <P>` a point and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the circumcevian triangle of P. Then the circumcircles of :g:`AA'A″ << A A' A″ >>`, :g:`BB'B″ << B B' B″ >>`, :g:`CC'C″ << C C' C″ >>` are coaxial and their radical axis is the line :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`\ :g:`P* <P*>`. (:person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>`, `euclid 2510 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/2510>`__, Sept. 27, 2021). Assume that O and H are the circumcenter and orthocenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, respectively.

  | For :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, the :term:`radical trace <radical-trace>` T(P) of the three circles is:
  | T(P)= SA\*x\*(y\*SB^2+SC^2\*z)+SB\*SC\*(y^2\*SB+z^2\*SC-2\*SA\*x\*(y+z))+(SB+SC)\*(SA^2\*x^2-SB\*SC\*y\*z) : : If P lies on the nine-point circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then T(P) = P. If P lies in the infinite, then T(P) lies on the circle with diameter OH. The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that T(X_i)=X_j:
  | (30, 3), (511, 31848), (512, 31850), (513, 31849), (514, 31851), (515, 31866), (516, 31852), (517, 31847), (518, 31865), (519, 31853), (523, 4), (524, 15098), (525, 43389), (542, 31854), (900, 18341), (952, 18342), (1503, 18338), (2574, 43396), (2575, 43395), (3564, 18348), (3566, 18347), (5965, 31864) he appearance of (i, j) in the following partial list means that T(X_i)=X_j, for P other than specified in (2) and (3):
  | (1, 16869), (2, 5159), (3, 10257), (5, 2072), [and others]. When P moves on a line L through :g:`H <H>`, :g:`T <T>`\ (P) moves also on the line :g:`L <L>`. In particular, if P is a point on the Euler line of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and such that :g:`OP <[ O P ]>`/OH = t, then OT/OH = (4\*R^2-SW)/(2\*OH\*(1-t)). When P moves on a line :g:`L* <L*>` no passing through :g:`H <H>`, the locus of T(P) is a circle Ω(:g:`L* <L*>`), here named the **Hatzipolakis-Lozada circle of line L\***. Ω(:g:`L* <L*>`) passes through :g:`H <H>` and, if :g:`P* <P*>` is the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of :g:`L* <L*>`, then the center :g:`O* <O*>` of Ω(:g:`L* <L*>`) is the dilation of :ref:`X_3091 <X_3091>` with center the polar-conjugate-of-P and ratio 5/4. If :g:`L* <L*>` is the orthic axis :ref:`X_231 <X_231>`\ \ :ref:`X_232 <X_232>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then :g:`O* <O*>`\ =\ :ref:`X_381 <X_381>`; if :g:`L* <L*>` is the Hatzipolakis axis :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`\ \ :ref:`X_523 <X_523>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then :g:`O* <O*>`\ =X_23323. For other named or notable lines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`O* <O*>` are given in X_44916 to X_44932. The transformation :g:`L* <L*>` → Ω(:g:`L* <L*>`) is not an inversion in a circle.

  A generalization follows: Let t be a real number and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the circumcevian triangle of a point :g:`P <P>`. Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the point given by the vector equation :g:`PA″ <[ P A″ ]>` = t\*\ :g:`PA' <[ P A' ]>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. Denote the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` by T(P,t). Suppose that U is a point other than P and k is a real number, and let A'''B'''C''' = T(U,k). The circles (AA"A'''), (BB''B'''), (CC''C''') are coaxial, and their radical axis is the line :g:`PU <[ P U ]>`. In the construction above, P is arbitrary, :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, t = 1, and k = 1/2. (Vu Thanh Tung, October 4, 2021)

.. _guide-preamble-0671:

* **X_44937**–**X_44966** — **Hatzipolakis-Suppa circle**

  contributed by :person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>` and Ercole Suppa, October 4, 2021. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let

  | H = :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` = orthocenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`;
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`H <H>`;
  | :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be the pedal triangle :g:`P <P>`;
  | (:g:`O_{a} <O_a>`) = circumcircle of, :g:`AA'A″ << A A' A″ >>`, and define (:g:`O_{b} <O_b>`) and (:g:`O_{c} <O_c>`) cyclically;
  | :math:`R_{a}` = radical axis of (:g:`O_{b} <O_b>`) and (:g:`O_{c} <O_c>`), and define :math:`R_{b}` and :math:`R_{c}` cyclically;
  | (:g:`O'_{a} <O'_a>`) = reflection of (:g:`O_{a} <O_a>`) in :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, and define (:g:`O'_{b} <O'_b>`) and (:g:`O'_{c} <O'_c>`) cyclically;
  | R'a = radical axis of (:g:`O'_{b} <O'_b>`) and (:g:`O'_{c} <O'_c>`), and R'b and R'c cyclically;
  | R'1 = reflection of R'a in :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define R'2 and R'3 cyclically.

  The locus of P such that the parallels to R'1, R'2, R'3 through :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, resp. concur is the union of the Euler line and the circle(:ref:`X_382 <X_382>`, R), where R = circumradius of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  The circle (:ref:`X_382 <X_382>`, R) is here named the **Hatzipolakis-Suppa Circle**, or **HS-circle**.

  Let :g:`Q <Q>`\ =Q(P) be the point in which the three parallels concur. The following properties hold:

  1. (:ref:`X_382 <X_382>`, R) is the reflection of the circumcircle in the orthocenter H.

  2. The appearance of {i, j} in the following list means that :g:`P <P>`\ =X_i lies on Euler line and Q(P)=X_j: {4,235}, {30,403}, {382,4}, {3146,5}, {3543,1596}, {5073,16868}, {10296,37984}, {10736,1312}, {10737,1313}, {12173,3089}, {15682,427}, {15684,7577}, {35480,25}, {35490,37197}, {44438,6623}

  3. The appearance of {i, j} in the following list means that :g:`P <P>`\ =X_i lies on HS-circle and Q(P)=X_j: {10152,133}, {10721,125}, {10722,115}, {10723,114}, {10724,119}, {10725,118}, {10726,124}, {10727,116}, {10728,11}, {10729,5511}, {10730,5510}, {10731,25640}, {10732,117}, {10733,113}, {10734,5512}, {10735,132}, {10736,1312}, {10737,1313}, {14989,3258}

  4. If P lies on HS-circle then Q(P) is the image of P under the homothety with center H and factor k = -1/2.

  5. When P moves on the Euler line the locus of point Q(P) is the Euler line.

  The function that maps the Euler line to the Euler line is here named the **1st Hatziplakis-Suppa transform (or 1st HS transform).**

  6. When P moves on HS-circle the locus of Q(P) is the nine-point circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  The function that maps the HS-circle to the nine-point circle is here named the **"2nd Hatzipolakis-Suppa" transform (or 2nd HS transform).**

.. _guide-preamble-0672:

* **X_45010**–**X_45124** — **1st and 2nd Aubert points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 6, 2021, based on a proposal by Ivan Pavlov. A complete quadrilateral Q formed by four lines :g:`ℓ_{1} <ℓ_1>`, :g:`ℓ_{2} <ℓ_2>`, :g:`ℓ_{3} <ℓ_3>`, :g:`ℓ_{4} <ℓ_4>` is denoted here as :g:`Q <Q>` = [:g:`ℓ_{1} <ℓ_1>`, :g:`ℓ_{2} <ℓ_2>`, :g:`ℓ_{3} <ℓ_3>`, :g:`ℓ_{4} <ℓ_4>`], or also as :g:`Q <Q>` = [ABCD], if it is composed by lines :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CD <[ C D ]>`, :g:`DA <[ D A ]>`.

  In every complete quadrilateral Q there are four component triangles, each bounded by three different lines of Q. It is well known that the orthocenters of these triangles are collinear on a line called the **Aubert line** (or Steiner line) of :g:`Q <Q>`.

  Let T '=\ :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`\ =\ :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two non-homothetic distinct triangles and let :g:`ℓ_{a} <ℓ_a>`, :g:`ℓ_{b} <ℓ_b>`, :g:`ℓ_{c} <ℓ_c>` be the Aubert lines of quadrilaterals [B':g:`C'B″C″ << C' B″ C″ >>`], [C':g:`A'C″A″ << A' C″ A″ >>`] and [A':g:`B'A″B″ << B' A″ B″ >>`], respectively. Then :g:`ℓ_{a} <ℓ_a>`, :g:`ℓ_{b} <ℓ_b>`, :g:`ℓ_{c} <ℓ_c>` concur in a point here named the **1st Aubert point of T' and T"**. (Note: If :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are homothetic, the described Aubert lines bound a triangle homothetic to :g:`T <T>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`).

  In the following list, (T, i) means that the 1st Aubert point of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and triangle :g:`T <T>` is X_i. [list omitted here]. Let T '=\ :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`\ =\ :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two triangles and let :g:`ℓ_{a} <ℓ_a>`, :g:`ℓ_{b} <ℓ_b>`, :g:`ℓ_{c} <ℓ_c>` be the Aubert lines of quadrilaterals [C':g:`A'B'A″ << A' B' A″ >>`], [A':g:`B'C'B″ << B' C' B″ >>`], [B':g:`C'A'C″ << C' A' C″ >>`], respectively. Let :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`ℓ_{b} <ℓ_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`ℓ_{c} <ℓ_c>`, :g:`B* <B*>` = :g:`ℓ_{c} <ℓ_c>`\ ∩\ :g:`ℓ_{a} <ℓ_a>` and :g:`C* <C*>` = :g:`ℓ_{a} <ℓ_a>`\ ∩\ :g:`ℓ_{b} <ℓ_b>`. Then, for some pairs of triangles T ' and :g:`T″ <T″>`, the lines :g:`A*A' <[ A* A' ]>`, :g:`B*B' <[ B* B' ]>` and :g:`C*C' <[ C* C' ]>` concur in a point here introduced as the **2nd Aubert point of T' to T"**.

  In the following list, (T, i) means that the 2nd Aubert point of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` to triangle :g:`T <T>` is X_i: [list omitted here].

  Similarly, in the below list, (T, i) indicates that the 2nd Aubert point of triangle :g:`T <T>` to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is X_i: [list omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0673:

* **X_45188**–**X_45194** — **V-perspeconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 15, 2021. Let :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two perspective triangles, neither inscribed in the other. Denote :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` = :g:`A'B″ <[ A' B″ ]>` ∩ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` and :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>` = :g:`A'C″ <[ A' C″ ]>` ∩ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, and cyclically :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>`, :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>`, :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>`, :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>`. Then these six points lie on a conic, here introduced as the **V-perspeconic of T' to T"**. A reciprocal V-perspeconic :g:`T″ <T″>` to :g:`T' <T'>` is found by swapping :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` in the previous construction.

  The appearance of (T, i, j) in the following list means that the centers of the V-perspeconics of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-to-T and T-to-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` are X_i and X_j, respectively:

  (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 17807, 45188), (Ehrmann-mid, 45191, 45192), (outer-Garcia, 3588, 45189), (Gemini 107, 2, 2), (Gemini 109, 2, 2), (Gemini 110, 2, 2), (Gemini 111, 2, 2), (Johnson, 31353, 45190), (5th mixtilinear, 45193, 45194)

* **X_45196**–**X_45215** — **Perspectors of Electra(B) triangles and cevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 17, 2021. In this paragraph (but not the next), all coordinates are trilinears. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w`, where neither P nor U lies on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let L(p,q,r,u,v,w) = p^2 \* (v^2 + w^2) - u\*(q v + r w), so that (as in the Glossary), the point :math:`L(u,v,w) : L(v,w,u) : L(w,u,v)` is the P-:term:`line conjugate <line-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>`, which lies on this line: :g:`PU <[ P U ]>`. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`U <U>`, so that :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`-u : w : w`, and :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` are determined cyclically. Let

  :g:`A″ <A″>` = :g:`P <P>`-line conjugate of :g:`A' <A'>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is here named the **(P,U)-Electra triangle**. If :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` =\ :math:`1:1:1`, then the locus of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` such that the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`X <X>` is perspective to the (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,U)-Electra triangle is given by

  v (u + w) (v^2 + w^2 + u v - u w) y^2 z - w (u + v) (v^2 + w^2 + u w - v w) y z^2 + (cyclic) - (v - w)(w - u)(u - v)(u + v + w) x y z = 0

  Next, suppose that all coordinates in the preceding paragraph are barycentrics. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is then the **(X(1),U)-Electra(B) triangle**. The appearance of (i,j,k)) in the following list means that the (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,X_i)-Electra(B) triangle is perspective to the cevian triangle of X_j, and the perspector is X_k:

  | (1,2,4357), (1,69,3687), (1,85,45196), (1,86,2), (1,1909,10), (1,6384,45197), (1,28660,76)
  | (3,2,45198), (3,95,2), (3,9291,5))
  | (4,2,41005), (4,264,2), (4,1975,3), (4,6340,45199), (4,6527,46200)
  | (6,2,6656), (6,83,2), (6,315,46201), (6,9230,141)
  | [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0676:

* **X_45238**–**X_45255** — **Vu-Miquel points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 20, 2021. *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` three any points on the sidelines :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively. Miquel theorem states that three circles* {{:g:`AB'C' << A B' C' >>`}}, {{:g:`BC'A' << B C' A' >>`}}, {{:g:`CA'B' << C A' B' >>`}} *have a common point.*

  Consider now two points :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`. Then the three conics ({:g:`AB' <[ A B' ]>`:g:`C'P_{1}P_{2} << C' P_1 P_2 >>`}}, {{:g:`BC' <[ B C' ]>`:g:`A'P_{1}P_{2} << A' P_1 P_2 >>`}} and {{:g:`CA' <[ C A' ]>`:g:`B'P_{1}P_{2} << B' P_1 P_2 >>`}} have a common point other than :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`. (Vu Thanh Tung, `Euclid 2699 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/2699>`__, October 12, 2021).

  The common intersection of that three conics is named here the Vu-Miquel point of (:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) with respect to {:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`}.

  | This section deals with Vu-Miquel points of (:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) with respect to {:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`} when :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` are the :term:`cevian <cevian>` traces of a point :g:`P <P>`. Assume :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`U : V : W` (trilinear coordinates used here), :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` =\ :math:`u_{1} : v_{1} : w_{1}` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` =\ :math:`u_{2} : v_{2} : w_{2}`. Then the common point of the three conics is:
  | Q(P, :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) = ((:g:`U* <U*>`\ :math:`d_{u}` + :g:`V* <V*>`\ :math:`d_{v}` + :g:`W* <W*>`\ :math:`d_{w})`\ \*\ :g:`U*V*W* << U* V* W* >>`\ :math:`s_{u}` + (V^2\*W^2\*\ :math:`u_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{2}` - (V^2\*\ :math:`w_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`w_{2}` + W^2\*\ :math:`v_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`v_{2})`\ \*U^2)\*\ :math:`d_{u})`\ \*\ :math:`u_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{2}`/(:g:`V* <V*>`\ :math:`d_{v}` + :g:`W* <W*>`\ :math:`d_{w})` : :
  | where :math:`d_{u}`, :math:`d_{v}`, :math:`d_{w}` are the cyclic differences:
  | :math:`d_{u}` = :math:`v_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`w_{2}` - :math:`v_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`w_{1}`, :math:`d_{v}` = :math:`w_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{2}` - :math:`w_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{1}`, :math:`d_{w}` = :math:`u_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`v_{2}` - :math:`u_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`v_{1}`
  | and :math:`s_{u}`, :math:`s_{v}`, :math:`s_{w}` are the cyclic sums:
  | :math:`s_{u}` = :math:`v_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`w_{2}` + :math:`v_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`w_{1}`, :math:`s_{v}` = :math:`w_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{2}` + :math:`w_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`u_{1}`, :math:`s_{w}` = :math:`u_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`v_{2}` + :math:`u_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`v_{1}`

  In the following list, (i, j, k, n) means that the Vu-Miquel point of (X_i, X_j) with respect to the cevian traces of X_k is X_n: (1, 2, 1, 192), (1, 3, 1, 3157), (1, 4, 1, 1148), (1, 5, 1, 45238), (1, 6, 1, 55), (1, 7, 1, 31526), (1, 8, 1, 19582), (1, 9, 1, 3158), (1, 10, 1, 3159), (1, 11, 1, 523), (1, 15, 1, 202), (1, 16, 1, 203), (1, 19, 1, 204), (1, 20, 1, 45239), (2, 6, 1, 45240), [and others]

.. _guide-preamble-0677:

* **X_45256**–**X_45265** — **1st and 2nd MacBeath-Simmons circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 21, 2021. In a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let Ω\ :sub:`1` and Ω\ :sub:`2` be two circles, both passing through :ref:`X_125 <X_125>` and with centers X_45256 and X_45257, respectively. Their respective squared radius are:

  ρ\ :sub:`1`\ :sup:`2` = (:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*(S^2+(4\*R^2-SW)^2)\*S-(16\*R^2-5\*SW)\*S^2+(4\*R^2-SW)\*(16\*R^4-3\*SW\*(4\*R^2-SW)))/(2\*(SW+\ :math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S-R^2))^2

  ρ\ :sub:`2`\ :sup:`2` = (-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*(S^2+(4\*R^2-SW)^2)\*S-(16\*R^2-5\*SW)\*S^2+(4\*R^2-SW)\*(16\*R^4-3\*SW\*(4\*R^2-SW)))/(2\*(SW-:math:`\sqrt{3}`\ \*S-R^2))^2

  Some properties of these circles are:

  Ω\ :sub:`1` and Ω\ :sub:`2` pass through :ref:`X_125 <X_125>` and :ref:`X_137 <X_137>`, both points on the nine-point circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Therefore Ω\ :sub:`1`, Ω\ :sub:`2` and the nine-point circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are coaxial. Ω\ :sub:`1` is the bicevian conic (or cyclocevian circle) of X_19712 and X_41898. Ω\ :sub:`2` is the bicevian conic (or cyclocevian circle) of X_19713 and X_41897. If :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is acute then Ω\ :sub:`1` passes through the four intersections of MacBeath inconic (foci :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`) and 1st Simmons inconic (foci :ref:`X_13 <X_13>` and :ref:`X_15 <X_15>`). If :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is obtuse then Ω\ :sub:`2` passes through the four intersections of MacBeath inconic and 2nd Simmons conic (foci :ref:`X_14 <X_14>` and :ref:`X_16 <X_16>`).

  Ω\ :sub:`1` and Ω\ :sub:`2` are named here the **1st MacbBeath-Simmons circle** and the **2nd MacbBeath-Simmons circle**, respectively.

  Note: Simmons conics were introduced in the preamble just before X_41993.

.. _guide-preamble-0678:

* **X_45266**–**X_45285** — **(B)-line conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 21, 2021. If points :g:`P <P>` and U, given by trilinears :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` are distinct, and neither lies on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, then the P-:term:`line conjugate <line-conjugate>` of :g:`U <U>` is the point given by trilinears

  p(v^2 + w^2) - u(qv + rw) : q(w^2 + u^2) - v(rw + pu) : r(u^2 + v^2) - w(pu + qv).

  Now suppose that :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` have barycentrics :math:`p : q : r` and :math:`u : v : w`, and define the **P-(B)line conjugate of U** as the point F(P,U) given by **barycentrics**

  p(v^2 + w^2) - u(qv + rw) : q(w^2 + u^2) - v(rw + pu) : r(u^2 + v^2) - w(pu + qv).

  The points X_45266 - X_45385 are (B)line conjugates.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that X_i and X_j are on the Euler line and F(X_i) = X_j, so that also, F(X_j) = X_i:

  (2,30), {3,297), (4,441), (5,401), (20,44334), (30,2), (140,40853), (297,3), (376,44216), (381,40884), (384,21536), (401,5), (427,15013), [and others].

  See also the preambles just before X_44886 and X_45196.

.. _guide-preamble-0679:

* **X_45289**–**X_45297** — **12th Vijay transforms**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 24, 2021. The Vijay 12th parallel transform, V12, is defined in the preamble just before X_43970 as follows: if :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics), then

  V12(U) = v\*w^2 - 3\*u\*w^2 + v^2\*w + 2\*u\*v\*w + u^2\*w - 3\*u\*v^2 + u^2\*v : :

  Let KK denote the cubic that is the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of K015. If X lies on infinity line or the Steiner circumellipse, then V12(X) lies on KK. The appearance of (i,j) in the following examples means that V12(X_i) = X_j:

  (30,45289), (512,44007), (513,44008), (514,44009), (519,20042), (522,45290), (523,44010), (524,45291), (525,45292), (527,45293), (690,45294), (900,48295).

.. _guide-preamble-0680:

* **X_45310**–**X_45693** — **and X_45657-X_45693, Midpoints of X_2 and other points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 31, 2021. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` (barycentrics). Then the P-(B):term:`line conjugate <line-conjugate>` of the line :g:`L <L>` at infinity is the point

  a\*(v^2 + w^2) + (v + w)\*(b\*v + c\*w) : :

  The locus of this point as U ranges through :g:`L <L>` is the ellipse, E(P,L), given by

  (q + r) x^2 + (r + p) y^2 + (p + q) z^2 - (q + r) y z - (r + p) z x - (p + q) x y = 0.

  The center of E(P,L) is the midpoint of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and P, with barycentrics

  4 p + q + r : p + 4 q + r : p + q + 4r.

  The perspector E(P,L) is 1/(p^2 + 2 q^2 + 2 r^2 + 5 q r + p q + p r) : : .

  The major axis of E(P,L) is parallel to the major axis of the Steiner circumellipse, and the minor axis of E(P,L) is parallel to the minor axis of the Steiner circumellipse. Thus, the ellipse E(P,L) is simply and translation and dilation of the Steiner circumellipse.

.. _guide-preamble-0681:

* **X_45345**–**X_45656** — **Inverse triangles and anti-triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 30, 2021. Inverse triangles were introduced by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` in the preamble just before X_42005 with more or less these terms: Suppose that :g:`T <T>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a triangle with vertices :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` represented in normalized barycentric coordinates. Let M be the matrix representation of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, and let :math:`M^{-1}` denote the inverse of M. Then the rows of :math:`M^{-1}`, interpreted as vertices of a triangle :math:`T^{-1}`, define the inverse triangle of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`.

  Matrices M and :math:`M^{-1}` algebraically behave as expected; i.e., products of matrices M.\ :math:`M^{-1}` = :math:`M^{-1}`.M = (3x3)-identity matrix, which represents :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Then it should be reasonable to expect that triangles T-of-:math:`T^{-1}` and :math:`T^{-1}`-of-T should be both :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, in other words, that :math:`T^{-1}` is the anti-triangle-of-T and vice-versa, but actually, this only occurs when T and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are similar or homothetic and, in both cases, T ' and T are homothetic triangles.

  The following properties can be deduced: [list and table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0682:

* **X_45695**–**X_45729** — **Ortho-perspective and para-perspective triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 1, 2021.

  (1) Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be two non-orthologic triangles. Denote as :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the triangle bounded by the lines through :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` perpendicular to :g:`B_{2}C_{2} <[ B_2 C_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{2}A_{2} <[ C_2 A_2 ]>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2} <[ A_2 B_2 ]>`, respectively, and denote as :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the triangle bounded by the lines through :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` perpendicular to :g:`B_{1}C_{1} <[ B_1 C_1 ]>`, :g:`C_{1}A_{1} <[ C_1 A_1 ]>`, :g:`A_{1}B_{1} <[ A_1 B_1 ]>`, respectively. Then for, some pairs of triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T' <T'>` are perspective if, and only if, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are perspective.

  (2) Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`\ =\ :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =\ :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be two non-parallelogic triangles. Denote as :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the triangle bounded by the lines through :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` parallel to :g:`B_{2}C_{2} <[ B_2 C_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{2}A_{2} <[ C_2 A_2 ]>`, :g:`A_{2}B_{2} <[ A_2 B_2 ]>`, respectively, and denote as :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the triangle bounded by the lines through :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` parallel to :g:`B_{1}C_{1} <[ B_1 C_1 ]>`, :g:`C_{1}A_{1} <[ C_1 A_1 ]>`, :g:`A_{1}B_{1} <[ A_1 B_1 ]>`, respectively. Then for, some pairs of triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T' <T'>` are perspective if, and only if, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are perspective.

  In case (1), triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are said to be **ortho-perspective** and perspectors (:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T' <T'>`) and (:g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`) are named here the ortho-perspector :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and ortho-perspector :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, respectively.

  In case (2), triangles :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` are said to be **para-perspective** and perspectors (:g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T' <T'>`) and (:g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`) are introduced here as the para-perspector :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` to :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` and para-perspector :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` to :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, respectively.

  Reference: `Vu Thanh Tung, Euclid 2834 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/2834>`__ (Message slightly modified by César Lozada).

.. _guide-preamble-0683:

* **X_45738**–**X_45744** — **Perspectors involving the Dao triangle**

  This preamble, based on notes from :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, was contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, Novermber 2, 2021, with amendments by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, November 7, 2021. Let (a) denote the A-Soddy ellipse, through :g:`A <A>` that has foci B and C. Define (b) and (c) cyclically. (The A-Soddy ellipse is defined by Randy Hutson at X_6349. The A-Soddy hyperbola also passes through :g:`A <A>` and has foci :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`; see :person:`Paul Yiu <paul-yiu>`, *Introduction to the Geometry of the Triangle*, p. 143). . Let

  d(a) = (b)∩(c); d(b) = (c)∩(a); d(c) = (a)∩(b); the lines d(a), d(b), d(c) concur in :ref:`X_20 <X_20>`.

  :g:`A' <A'>` = d(a)∩\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`; :g:`B' <B'>` = d(b)∩\ :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`; :g:`C' <C'>` = d(c)∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`; the lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur in :ref:`X_1043 <X_1043>`.

  The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, here named the **Dao triangle**, is perspective to certain other triangles, with perspectors X_45738-X_45744. (Actually, the Dao triangle is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :ref:`X_1043 <X_1043>`; Randy Hutson, November 7, 2021)

  The conic (a),

  2\*(a^2 + b^2 + 2\*b\*c + c^2)\*y\*z + 4\*(b + c)\*x\*(c\*y + b\*z) - (a - b - c)\*(a + b + c)\*(y^2 + z^2) = 0,

  passes through the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of these triangles: anticomplementary, orthic-of-anticomplementary (also called the Gemini 113 triangle, the dual of the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`, the 1st anti-circumperp triangle, and the circumanticevian triangle of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`).

  The line d(a) is given by

  (b - c)\*(a + b + c)^2\*x + (a + b - c)^2\*(a + c)\*y + (-a - b)\*(a - b + c)^2\*z = 0. The :g:`A <A>`-vertex of the Dao triangles is

  :g:`A' <A'>` = 0 : (a + b)\*(a - b + c)^2 : (a + b - c)^2\*(a + c),

  The Dao triangle is perspective to every :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>`; specifically, if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r`, then the perspector is

  p ((a + b - c)^2\*(a - b + c)^2\*(b + c)\*p - (a - b - c)^2\*(a + b - c)^2\*(a + c)\*q - (a + b)\*(a - b - c)^2\*(a - b + c)^2\*r) : :

  If P lies on the cubic K004, then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to the :term:`antipedal triangle <antipedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`.

  The conics (b) and (c) meet in two real points, assumed in the discussion above, and also two nonreal points, considered here. In this case, the points d(a), d(b), d(c) are nonreal, and the vertices :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, given by

  :g:`A' <A'>` = 0 : -a - b : a + c, :g:`B' <B'>` = b + a, 0, -b - c, :g:`C' <C'>` = -c - a, c + b, 0,

  are collinear on this line:

  (b + c) x + (c + a) y + (a + b) z = 0,

  which passes through X_i for these i: 239, 514, 649, 1019, 1021, 3218, 3798, 4025, 4063, 4091, [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0687:

* **X_46001**–**X_46008** — **Centers of Panchapakesan circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 15, 2021. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P, Q two :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` points (Q also denoted as :math:`P^{-1})`. Let :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` the centers of circles {{P,B,C}}, {{P,C,A}} and {{P,A,B}}, respectively, and similarly, let :g:`Q_{a} <Q_a>`, :g:`Q_{b} <Q_b>`, :g:`Q_{c} <Q_c>` the centers of circles {{Q,B,C}}, {{Q,C,A}} and {{Q,A,B}}, respectively. Denote :g:`A_{p} <A_p>` = :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` ∩ :g:`QQ_{a} <[ Q Q_a ]>` and cyclically :g:`B_{p} <B_p>` and :g:`C_{p} <C_p>`. Finally, denote :g:`A_{q} <A_q>`\ =\ :g:`AQ <[ A Q ]>` ∩ :g:`PP_{a} <[ P P_a ]>` and cyclically :g:`B_{q} <B_q>` and :g:`C_{q} <C_q>`. Then eight points :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>`, :g:`A_{p} <A_p>`, :g:`B_{p} <B_p>`, :g:`C_{p} <C_p>`, :g:`A_{q} <A_q>`, :g:`B_{q} <B_q>`, :g:`C_{q} <C_q>` lie on a circle. (Sriram Panchapakesan, `Euclid 3162 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/3162>`__, November 14, 2021.)

  The above described circle is named here the **Panchapakesan circle of P and Q**. For :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x:y:z`, its center :g:`O* <O*>` is:

  :g:`O* <O*>` = a^2\*(a^2\*y^2 + b^2\*x^2 + (a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*x\*y)\*(a^2\*z^2 + c^2\*x^2 + (a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*x\*z)\*(z^2\*b^2 - y^2\*c^2) : :

  Some properties of this circle are:

  :g:`O* <O*>` lies in the infinity if P (or Q) lie in the infinity, or on the circumcircle or on McCay cubic K003. (César Lozada, `Euclid 3174 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/3174>`__) If K(P, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`) denotes the Panchapakesan circle of :g:`P <P>` and :math:`P^{-1}`, then the four circles K(P, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`), K(A, :g:`BCP << B C P >>`), K(B, :g:`CAP << C A P >>`), K(C, :g:`ABP << A B P >>`) are concurrent in a point :g:`R* <R*>`\ (P). (Vu Thanh Tung, `Euclid 3175 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/3175>`__) :g:`R* <R*>`\ (P) is the circumcircle-inverse of :math:`P^{-1}` . (César Lozada, Euclid 3181) The circumcircle-inverses of :g:`P <P>` and :math:`P^{-1}` also lie on the Panchapakesan circle of :g:`P <P>` and :math:`P^{-1}`. (Elias M. Hagos , Euclid 3178) For any P, the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the Panchapakesan circle of :g:`P <P>` and :math:`P^{-1}` are orthogonal. (Sriram Panchapakesan, Euclid 3179)

  In the following list, (i, j) means that the center of the Panchapakesan circle of X_i and its isogonal conjugate is X_j: (2, 46001), (3, 523), (4, 523), (5, 46002), (6, 46001), (7, 46003), (8, 46004), (9, 46006), (11, 46007), (13, 6137), (14, 6138), (15, 6137), (16, 6138), (20, 46005), (36, 1769), (54, 46002), (55, 46003), (56, 46004), (57, 46006), (59, 46007), (64, 46005), (80, 1769), (186, 46008), (265, 46008), (1157, 46002), (1263, 46002).

  | :g:`U_{3} <U_3>` = antipode of :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, and :g:`T_{3} <T_3>` = line tangent to (O) at :g:`U_{3} <U_3>`;
  | :g:`U_{4} <U_4>` = antipode of :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`, and :g:`T_{4} <T_4>` = line tangent to (O) at :g:`U_{4} <U_4>`;

* **X_46681**–**X_46696** — **Mutual-reflections conics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 14, 2022. Let :g:`T' <T'>`\ =\ :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`\ =\ :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two triangles, :g:`A_{1} <A_1>` the reflection of :g:`A' <A'>` in :g:`B″C″ <[ B″ C″ ]>` and :g:`A_{2} <A_2>` the reflection of :g:`A″ <A″>` in :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`. Define :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. For some selected pairs of triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`, these six points lie on a conic, here named the **mutual-reflections conic of T' and T"** or, shortly, the **MR-conic of T' and T"**.

  The appearance of (:g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`, n) in the following partial list means that the center of the MR-conic of triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` is X_n: (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`-X3 reflections, 3), (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, anticomplementary, 3), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0695:

* **X_46706**–**X_46726** — **Points on cubics**

  :contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 18, 2022. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point that is not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than A, in which the :term:`cevian <cevian>` line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` intersects the Steiner circumellipse, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Then

  :g:`A' <A'>` = -a q r : (b r + c q) q : (b r + c q) r

  Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the points, other than A, in which the anticevian line of P intersects the Steiner circumellipse, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. Then

  :g:`A″ <A″>` = a q r : (c q - b r) q : (b r - c q) r

  Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to the :term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>`, and the perspector is the point

  U(P) = p^2\*q^2 + p^2\*r^2 - q^2\*r^2 : :

  Moreover, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is also perspective to the anticomplementary triangle, with perspector U(P), which is the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of P^2. The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that if X_i =\ :math:`p:q:r`, then X_j = U(P).

  (1,194), (2,2), (4,6392), (6,8264), (7,4452), (8,30695), [and others].

  Note that i = j if and only if X_i lies on the Steiner circumellipse.

* **X_46738**–**X_46759** — **Points on cubics pK(m^2 n^2, m^2 n^2 q r)**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 24, 2022. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`L <L>`, given by l x + m y + n z = 0, be a line, and let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point not on :g:`L <L>` and not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let

  Ap = L∩\ :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, Bp = L∩\ :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, Cp = L∩\ :g:`CP <[ C P ]>`.

  Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, so that

  :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`0 : y : z` , :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`x : 0 : z`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`x : y : 0`.

  The locus of X such that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to the (degenerate) triangle ApBpCp is the cubic pK(m^2 n^2, m^2 n^2 q r), given by

  p (m^2 q y^2 z - n^2 r y z^2) + (cyclic) = 0.

  The appearance of {{i,j}, {{Knnn}, {:math:`h_{1}`, :math:`h_{2}`, ...}}} in the following list means that if :math:`l : m : n` = X_i and :g:`P <P>` = X_j, then the cubic is Knnn in :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`'s catalogue (`CTC <http://bernard-gibert.fr/ctc.html>`__), and that the cubic passes through the points :math:`X(h_{1})`, :math:`X(h_{2})`, . . .

  | {{1,1},{{},{1,75,92,304,561,1760,46244}}}
  | {{1,2},{{K184},{2,69,75,76,85,264,312,15466,34403,34404,40702}}}
  | {{1,4},{{},{2,4,75,76,253,305,341,1088,1370,14615,20914,40009,40015,46738,46739,46740,46741}}}
  | {{1,10},{{},{2,10,75,76,310,4043,17135,40004,40005}}}
  | [and other]

  Each of these cubics is unicursal with node and singularity m n : n l : l m. As noted above, each cubic is of type pK(m^2 n^2, m^2 n^2 q r), which is equivalent to cK(# m n , m^2, n^2 q r). See `Special Isocubics in the Triangle Plane <http://bernard-gibert.fr/files/Resources/SITP.pdf>`__). (Bernard Gibert, January 28, 2022)

.. _guide-preamble-0698:

* **X_46826**–**X_46844** — **Points on cubics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`L <L>`, given by l x + m y + n z = 0, be a line, and let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point not on :g:`L <L>` and not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let

  Ap = L∩\ :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, Bp = L∩\ :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, Cp = L∩\ :g:`CP <[ C P ]>`.

  Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the generalized Gemini triangle 34 a point :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`; that is,

  :g:`A' <A'>` = :math:`-x : z : y`, :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`z : -y : x`, :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`y : x : -z` .

  The locus of X such that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to the (degenerate) triangle ApBpCp is the cubic, given by

  l p (n r - m q) x^3 - (l m p r + m^2 q r + l^2 p q + m n p q) y^2 z + (l n p q + n^2 q r + l^2 p r + m n p r) y z^2 + (cyclic) = 0.

  This section exemplifies the cubic for three cases:

  Case 1: :g:`L <L>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1` (the line at infinity). Here, the cubic is given by

  p (r - q) x^2 - (p r + q r + 2 p q) y^2 z + ) p q + q r + 2 p r) y z^2 + (cyclic) = 0.

  Case 2: :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1` (centroid). Here, the cubic is given by

  l (n - m) x^3 - (m^2 + l^2 + l m + m n) y^2 z + (n^2 + l^2 + l n + m n) y z^2 + (cyclic) = 0. Case 3: :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1` (centroid). Here, the cubic is given by

  a^2 ( c^2 - b^2) x^3 - (a^2 b (a + c) + b^2 c (a + b)) y^2 z + (a^2 c (a + b) + b c^2 (a + c)) y z^2 = 0.

  Examples for Cases 1, 3, and 3 are omitted here.

.. _guide-preamble-0700:

* **X_46894**–**X_46919** — **Type 1 Pappus points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 9-10, 2022. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, suppose that :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`, given by l1 x + m1 y + n1 z = 0, is a line, and :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` =\ :math:`p1:q1:r1` is a point not on :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. The :term:`cevians <cevian>` of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` are the lines :g:`AP_{1} <[ A P_1 ]>`, :g:`BP_{1} <[ B P_1 ]>`, :g:`CP_{1} <[ C P_1 ]>`, for which coefficients are

  :math:`0 : q : r`,\ :math:`p : 0 : r`,\ :math:`p : q : 0`, respectively. Let

  Ap = :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`\ ∩\ :g:`AP_{1} <[ A P_1 ]>`, Bp = :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ ∩\ :g:`BP_{1} <[ B P_1 ]>`, Cp = :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ ∩\ :g:`CP_{1} <[ C P_1 ]>`

  Similarly, suppose that :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`, given by l2 x + m2 y + n2 z = 0, is another line, and that :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` =\ :math:`p2:q2:r2` is a point not on :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` and not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let

  Au = :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ ∩\ :g:`AP_{2} <[ A P_2 ]>`, Bu = :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ ∩\ :g:`BP_{2} <[ B P_2 ]>`, Cu = :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ ∩\ :g:`CP_{2} <[ C P_2 ]>`

  By Pappus's Theorem, the points

  BpCu∩CpBu, CpAu∩ApCu, ApBu∩BpAu

  are collinear (on the **Pappus line** of the configuration). The **Type 1 Pappus Point** of :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`, :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` is the point whose barycentrics are coefficients of the Pappus line. Barycentrics for this point follow:

  l2 p2 q1 r1 (m1 q2 + n1 r2) + l1 p1 q1 r2 (l2 p2 + n2 r2) + l1 p1 q2 r1 (l2 p2 + m2 q2) : :

.. _guide-preamble-0701:

* **X_46961**–**X_46970** — **Perspectrors of circumcevian triangles and their inverses**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 20, 2022.For an introduction to inverse triangles, see the preambles just before X_42005, X_43280, and X_43343. This present section extends the section consisting of X_43344-X_43363.

  Let :g:`O <X_3>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = circumcenter fo :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and suppose that P is a point not on a sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let :g:`T <T>` be the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P <P>`, and let :g:`T' <T'>` be the inverse of :g:`T <T>`, as defined in the preamble just before X_42005. Then T and :g:`T' <T'>` are perspective, and the perspector is the point on the circumcircle whose :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` is the infinite point of intersection of all the lines perpendicular to :g:`OP <[ X_3 P ]>`. (Francisco Javier García Capitán , February 19, 2022)

  Continuing, let :g:`U <U>` be the isogonal conjugate just mentioned. The line :g:`OP <[ O P ]>` meets the infinity line in the orthogonal conjugate of U. For a discussion of orthogonal conjugates, see Clark Kimberling, "Polynomial :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` on the line at infinity": `Journal of Geometry 111, Article 10 <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00022-020-0522-y>`__)

  The appearance of (h,j,k) in the following list means that X_j is the perspector of the circumcevian triangle of X(h) and its inverse triangle, as defined near in the preamble just before X_42005, and that X_j is the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ X_j.

  (1,100,1), (2,110,3), (4,110,3), (5,110,3), (6,99,2), (7,43344,13404), (8,901,101), (9,934,57), (10,109,41), (11,6099,906), (12,43345,8071), (13,10409,2981), (14,10410,6151), (15,99,2), (16,99,2), (17,10409,2981), (18,10410,6151), (19,13395,1214), (20,110,3), (21,110,3), (22,110,3), (23,110,3), (24,110,3), (25,110,3), (26,110,3), (27,110,3), (28,110,3), (29,110,3), (30,110,3), [and others]

* **X_47006**–**X_47025** — **Infinity-Incircle-transform**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 26, 2022. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`A_{i}B_{i}C_{i} << A_i B_i C_i >>` the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P a point in the line at infinity. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the reflection of :g:`A_{i}B_{i}C_{i} << A_i B_i C_i >>` in the line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ P. Then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and Q(P), the isogonal-conjugate of the perspector, lies on the incircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  The point :g:`Q <Q>` is named here the **infinity-incircle-transform of P**. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (barycentrics) then

  Q(P) = a^2\*(a - b + c)\*(a + b - c)\*(c\*y - b\*z)^2 : :

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that Q( X_i ) = X_j:: (30, 3024), (511, 3023), (512, 3027), (513, 1317), (514, 1362), (515, 1364), (516, 3022), (517, 11), (518, 1358), (519, 1357), (520, 3324), (521, 1359), (522, 1361), (523, 3028), (524, 3325), (525, 3320), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0703:

* **X_47090**–**X_47101** — **Shinagawa-Euler Points**

  based on notes by :person:`Kiminari Shinagawa <kiminari-shinagawa>`, contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 8, 2022. The Euler coordinate system consists of an x-axis (the Euler line) and y-axis (the orthic axis). The axes meet in the origin, :ref:`X_468 <X_468>` = (0,0). Points on the x-axis and on the same side of (0,0) as the centroid, G, have positive x-coordinates. Points on the y-axis and on the same side of (0,0) as the bicentric point P(201) have positive y-coordinates.

  A point with barycentrics :math:`p : q : r` has Euler coordinates (x,y) given by

  | x = (SA\*p + SB\*q + SC\*r)/(p+q+r)
  | y = (SA(SB-SC)\*p + SB(SC-SA)\*q +SC(SA - SB)\*r)/(p+q+r).

  To convert from Euler coordinates (x,y) to barycentrics :math:`p : q : r`, let

  | S^2 = SB\*SC + SC\*SA + SA\*SB = 4\*(area of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`)^2
  | :g:`E <E>` = (SB + SC)(SC + SA)(SA + SB)/S^2
  | :g:`F <F>` = SA\*SB\*SC/S^2.

  Then

  | p = (E+F)\*SB\*SC - 3F S^2 - (3SB\*SC-S^2)x + (SB-SC)y
  | q = (E+F)\*SC\*SA - 3F S^2 - (3SC\*SA-S^2)x + (SC-SA)y
  | r = (E+F)\*SA\*SB - 3F S^2 - (3SA\*SB-S^2)x + (SA-SB)y

  Note that x must have degree 2 in a,b,c, and y must have degree 4.

  The appearance of (x,0;n) in the following list means that the point with Euler coordinates (x,0) is X_n:

  {(E/2,0); 10257}, {(-E/2,0); 37971}, {(E+F,0); 858}, {(2(E+F),0); 46517}, {(3(E+F),0); 5189}, {((E+F)/4,0);37911}, {(E-F,0); 2071}, {(F,0); 403}, {(2F,0); 10151}, {(4F,0); 13473}, {(F/2,0); 37942}, {(F/3,0); 37779}, {(-F,0); 186}, {(-2F,0); 37931}, {(-F/2,0); 37935}

  The appearance of (:math:`\$f(a,b,c)\$`,0;n) in the next list means that the point with Euler coordinates (f(a,b,c)+f(b,c,a)+f(c,a,b),0) is X_n, and that the point lies on the positive x-axis for all non-equilateral triangles:

  {(:math:`\$a^{2}\$`,0); 46517}, {(:math:`\$a^{2}\$`/4,0); 5159}, {(:math:`\$a^{2}\$`/6,0); 2}, {(:math:`\$aSA\$`/:math:`\$a\$`,0);3109}}

  For more examples, see **Euler Coordinates** (``Euler%20Coordinates.pdf``).

  See also the preambles just before X_47332 and X_47488.

.. _guide-preamble-0704:

(Note that SB z - SC y : : lies on the orthic axis, whereas SB y - SC z : : lies on the line at infinity.

  (3) Points X_47193-X_47195. The appearance of {i, j; k} in the following list means that X_k = X_i-:term:`line conjugate <line-conjugate>` of X_j:

  | {230, 232; 47194}
  | {230, 2501; 47195}
  | {231, 230; 46953}
  | {232, 230; 46953}

  | [and others].

  (4) Points X_47196-X_47198. The appearance of {h, i; j, k} in the following list means that X_k = {X_i, X_j-harmonic conjugate of X(h), so that also, X(h) = {X_i, X_j-harmonic conjugate of X_k: {230,231,232 47196}, {230,231,468,47197}, {230,468, 647,47198}

  (5) Points X_47199-X_47236. Four circles with center on the orthic axis are these: Stevanovic circle, Dao-Moses-Telv circle, Moses radical circle, and Moses-Parry circle. If P is a point on the orthic axis and (O) is a circle with center on the orthic axis, then the (O)(-inverse of :g:`P <P>` is also on the orthic axis, as exemplified by X_47199-X_47236.

.. _guide-preamble-0705:

* **X_47332**–**X_47342** — **Shinagawa-Euler points**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, :person:`Kiminari Shinagawa <kiminari-shinagawa>`, and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, April 1, 2022. Suppose that P and U are points, neither on the line at infinity, and that normed (i.e., "normalized") barycentrcis are given by :g:`P <P>`\ = (p,q,r) and :g:`U <U>` = (u,v,w) Then the point P-U defined by the :term:`combo <combo>` p-u : q - v : r - w is on the line at infinity. Let T(P,U) denote the point with Euler coordinates (x,y) given by

  | x = SA\*(p-u) + SB\*(q - r) + SC\*(r - w)
  | y = SA\*(SB - SC)\*(p-u) + SB\*(SC - SA)\*(q - r) + SC\*(SA - SB)\*(r - w)

  If P and U are on the Euler line, then y = 0, and P - :g:`U <U>` = :ref:`X_30 <X_30>`, and T(P,U) lies on the Euler line. The appearance of (i,j;k) in the following list means that T(X_i,X_j) = X_k.

  (2,3; 47332), (2,4; 47031), (2,5; 18579), (2,23; 47311), (2,376; 47310), (2,381; 47333), (3,2; 47333), (3,4; 47308), (3,5; 47335), (3,20; 47309), (3,140; 18571), (3,186; 10257), (3,376; 47332), (3,381; 47031), (4,2; 47310), (4,3; 47309), (4,5; 47336), (4,23; 47339), [and others].

  See also the preambles just before X_47090, X_47488, and X_47629.

.. _guide-preamble-0706:

* **X_47371**–**X_47398** — **Two-parallels points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 27, 2022. Let :g:`AA_{1} <[ A A_1 ]>`, :g:`BB_{1} <[ B B_1 ]>`, :g:`CC_{1} <[ C C_1 ]>` be the altitudes in acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`X <X>` be an arbitrary point. Let M, N, P, Q, R, S be the feet of the perpendiculars from :g:`X <X>` to the lines :g:`AA_{1} <[ A A_1 ]>`,\ :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`,\ :g:`BB_{1} <[ B B_1 ]>`,\ :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`,\ :g:`CC_{1} <[ C C_1 ]>`,\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Prove that MN, :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>`, RS are concurrent. (Source: `AOPS 713159 <https://artofproblemsolving.com/community/c6h126138p715139>`__, Dec 29, 2006.)

  The above can be generalized as follows: Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, X a point and P another point not on the side lines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` or on the :term:`cevian <cevian>` lines of X. The parallel lines through :g:`P <P>` to :g:`AX <[ A X ]>` and :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` cut :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and :g:`AX <[ A X ]>` at :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`, respectively; :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C' <C'>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` are built cyclically. Then the lines :g:`A'A″ <[ A' A″ ]>`, :g:`B'B″ <[ B' B″ ]>`, :g:`C'C″ <[ C' C″ ]>` concur.

  The point of intersection Q(X, P) of :g:`A'A″ <[ A' A″ ]>`, :g:`B'B″ <[ B' B″ ]>`, :g:`C'C″ <[ C' C″ ]>` is named here the **X-two parallels point of-P**. If :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`X : Y : Z` and :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z` (both barycentrics) then:

  Q(X, P) = x\*(-:g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>`\ \*x^2 + (Y + Z)\*X\*y\*z + (Y\*z + Z\*y)\*X\*x) : :

  Some properties: Q(X, P) is the midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and the X-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`. (:person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>`, March 28, 2022) For P on the line at infinity, Q(X, P) = P. For :g:`X <X>`\ =\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, Q(X,P) is W(P), the center of the parallel-conic described above X_10001. If :g:`X <X>`\ =\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` and P lies on the nine-point-circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then Q(X,P) is the :term:`complementary conjugate <complementary-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`.

  The appearance of (i, j, k) in the following lists means that X_i- two parallels point of -X_j is X_k: [long lists omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0707:

* **X_47405**–**X_47434** — **Points on the bicevian conic of X_3 and X_6**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. Let BCC denote the bicevian conic of :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, which is given by the equation

  b^4\*c^4\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*x^2 - 2\*a^2\*b^2\*c^6\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*x\*y - a^4\*c^4\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*y^2 - 2\*a^2\*b^6\*c^2\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*x\*z + 2\*a^6\*b^2\*c^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*y\*z - a^4\*b^4\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*z^2 = 0.

  This conic passes through the points X_i for these i: 3269, 7117, 9475, 15166, 15167, 20728, 20830, 20975, 22084, 22428. :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>` has noted that if P is a point on the line at infinity, then the :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of the barycentric product :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \*P is on BCC. (Equivalently, the :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`-Ceva conjugate of :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \*P is on BCC.) The line of :g:`P <P>` and the :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-Ceva conjugate of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \*P is tangent to the Steiner inellipse, which is bitangent to BCC. Moreover, if X is on the nine-point circle, then the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of the polar conjugate of :g:`X <X>` is on BCC.

* **X_47488**–**X_47508** — **Points T(P,U) for P and U on selected lines**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, :person:`Kiminari Shinagawa <kiminari-shinagawa>`, and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, April 7, 2022. As in the preamble just before X_47468, suppose that P and U are points, neither on the line at infinity, and that normed (i.e., "normalized") barycentrics are given by :g:`P <P>`\ = (p,q,r) and :g:`U <U>` = (u,v,w) Then the point P-U defined by the :term:`combo <combo>` p-u : q - v : r - w is on the line at infinity. Let T(P,U) denote the point with Euler coordinates (x,y) given by

  | x = SA\*(p-u) + SB\*(q - r) + SC\*(r - w)
  | y = SA\*(SB - SC)\*(p-u) + SB\*(SC - SA)\*(q - r) + SC\*(SA - SB)\*(r - w)

  The appearance of (i,j;k) in the following lists means that T(X_i,X_j) = X_k:

  | P and U on the Nagel line, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`:
  | (1,2; 47472), (1,8; 47489), (1,10; 47491), (1,145; 47490), (1,551; 47495)
  | (2,1; 47488), (2,8; 47493); (2,10;47495), [and others].

  | P and U on the IK line, :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`:
  | (1,6; 47477), (1,9; 47507), (6,1; 47506), (9,1; 47508)

  P and U on the Euler line, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`: see the preamble just before X_47332.

  | P and U on the GK line, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`:
  | (2,6;47473), (2,69; 47541), (2,81; 47542), (2,86; 47543), (2,141;47544)
  | (6,2;47545), (6,69;47546), (6,81; 47547), [and others].

  | P and U on the Brocard axis, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`:
  | (3,6; 47468), (3,32; 47567), (3,39; 47568), (3,182; 47569), (3,187; 47570)
  | (6,3; 47571), (6,32; 47572), (6,39; 47573), (6,187; 47574), [and others].

  | P and U on the anti-orthic axis, :ref:`X_44 <X_44>`\ \ :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`:
  | (649,650; 47499), (650,649; 47500)

  | P and U on the Lemoine axis, :ref:`X_187 <X_187>`\ \ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`:
  | (182,237;47502), (237,187; 47501), (237,647; 47504), (647,187; 47503); (647,237; 47505)

  Note that the transformation T is many-to-one; i.e., for each T(P,U), there are (infinitely) many pairs (:g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) such that T(:g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) = T(P,U). For example, T(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_551 <X_551>`) = T(:ref:`X_10 <X_10>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) = TX(551,\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`) = X_47562, as listed above.

  See also the preambles just before X_47090 and X_47332.

* **X_47650**–**X_47729** — **Points in a [L(31),L(32)]-coordinate system**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then the [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is here defined as a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  | :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` = L(31) = :ref:`X_514 <X_514>`\ \ :ref:`X_661 <X_661>` = :term:`trilinear polar <trilinear-polar>` of (75);
  | :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` is given by the equation a α + b β + c γ = 0.

  | :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` = L(32) = :ref:`X_325 <X_325>`\ \ :ref:`X_523 <X_523>` = deLongchamps axis = trilinear polar of :ref:`X_76 <X_76>`;
  | :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` is given by the equation a^2 α + b^2 β + c^2 γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_693 <X_693>` = b c (b + c) : c a (c + a) : a b (a + b) = :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :ref:`X_100 <X_100>`

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a point :g:`U <U>` = (x,y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = (b-c)(bc + x - (b+c) y) : (c-a)(ca + x - (c+a)y) : (b-c)(ab + x - (a+b)y),

  where, as functions of a,b,c, the coordinate x is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 2, and y is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 1. Note that these results depend on the repesentations of :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as shown, and that the systems [:g:`L_{2} <L_2>`,\ :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`] and [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`] differ.

  The appearance of (x,y), k in the following table means that (x,y) = X_k: [table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0719:

* **X_47412**–**X_48438** — **Odd minor triangle centers**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` asA :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p(a,b,c) : q(a,b,c) : r(a,b,c)` is **even** if p(a,b,c) = p(a,c,b) and **odd** if p(a,b,c) = - p(a,c,b); or equivalently, p(a,b,c) = (b - c) u(a,b,c), where :math:`u(a,b,c) : u(b,c,a) : u(c,a,b)` is even. These definitions follow **C. Kimberling, "Functional equations associated with triangle geometry," Aequationes Mathematicae 45 (1993) 127-152.** The triangle center P is **minor** if p(a,b,c) is invariant of a. (This definition is not closely related to "major" triangle center, defined elsewhere as a center that can be expressed in barycentrics :math:`m(A,B,C) : m(B,C,A) : m(C,A,B)` such that m(:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`) is invariant of :g:`B <B>` and C.)

  The odd minor centers in this section are all :term:`polynomial centers <polynomial-center>` of degree 3, with first barycentric given by the form (b - c)(h\*(b^2 + c^2) + k\* b c), where h and k are real numbers, not both zero.

  The appearance of {h,k,i} in the following list means that X_i = (b - c)(h\*(b^2 + c^2) + k\* b c):

  | {0,1}, 693}
  | {1,-2}, 6545}
  | {1,-1}, 3776}
  | {1,0}, 16892}
  | {1,1}, 824}
  | [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0721:

* **X_47543**–**X_48580** — **Points in a [X_2X_513, X_2X_514] coordinate system**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`: (2bc-ab-ac) α + (2ca-bc-ba) β + (2ab-ca-cb) γ = 0.

  :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`: (2a-b-c) α + (2b-c-a) β + (2c-a-b) γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1` .

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a point :g:`U <U>` = (x,y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = (b - c) ((a-b)(a-c) + ax + y) : : ,

  where, as functions of a,b,c, the coordinate x is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 1, and y is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 2.

  For the "reversed" coordinate system, [:g:`L_{2} <L_2>`,\ :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`], see X_47754 - X_47845.

  The appearance of {x,y},k in the following list means that (x,y) = X_k:

  | {-2 (a+b+c), -2 (a b+a c+b c)}, 47774
  | {-((2 (a b+a c+b c))/(a+b+c)), -a b-a c-b c}, 47826
  | {-2 (a+b+c), 0}, 47759
  | {-((2 (a^2+b^2+c^2))/(a+b+c)), 0}, 48164
  | {-((2 (a b+a c+b c))/(a+b+c)), 0}, 47821
  | {-2 (a+b+c), 1/2 (a^2+b^2+c^2)}, 47764
  | [and others].

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`: bc α + ca β + ab γ = 0.

  :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`: a α + b β + c γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_661 <X_661>` =\ :math:`a(b^{2}-c^{2}) : b(c^{2}-a^{2}) :c(a^{2}-b^{2})`.

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a point :g:`U <U>` = (x,y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = (b - c) (ab + ac - a x - y) : : ,

  where, as functions of a,b,c, the coordinate x is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 1, and y is symmetric and homogeneous of degree 2.

  For the "reversed" coordinate system, [:g:`L_{2} <L_2>`,\ :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`], see X_47900 - X_48151.

  | {(-2\*(a^2 + b^2 + c^2))/(a + b + c), -2\*(a\*b + a\*c + b\*c)}, 48583
  | {-2\*(a + b + c), -((a\*b\*c)/(a + b + c))}, 48584

* **X_47798**–**X_48833** — **Points in the [ [b-c,c-a,a-b], [(b^2 - c^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2), (c^2 - a^2)(b^2 - c^2 - a^2), (a^2 - b^2)(c^2 - a^2 - b^2)]] coordinate system**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` = Nagel line: (b-c) α + (c-a) β + (a-b) γ = 0.

  :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` = Euler line: (b^2 - c^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) α + (c^2 - a^2)(b^2 - c^2 - a^2) β + (a^2 - b^2)(c^2 - a^2 - b^2) γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1`.

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` :g:`U <U>` = (x,y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = (b-c)(a-b)(a-c) (a+b+c)^2 + (2a-b-c) x + (2 a^4-a^2 b^2-b^4-a^2 c^2+2 b^2 c^2-c^4) y : : ,

  where, as functions of a,b,c, the coordinate x is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 1, and y is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 2n; viz., x and y are of the form (b-c)(a-b)(a-c)z(a,b,c), where z(a,b,c) is symmetric in a,b,c..

  The appearance of {x,y},k in the following list means that (x,y) = X_k.

  | {-2 (a-b) (a-c) (b-c) (a+b+c), 0}, 8
  | {-((a-b) (a-c) (b-c) (a+b+c)), 0}, 3679
  | {-(1/2) (a-b) (a-c) (b-c) (a+b+c), 0}, 10
  | {0, -(((a-b) (a-c) (b-c))/(a^2+b^2+c^2))}, 11359
  | {0, 0}, 2
  | [and others].

If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`,\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  | :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` = Euler line: (b^2 - c^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) α + (c^2 - a^2)(b^2 - c^2 - a^2) β + (a^2 - b^2)(c^2 - a^2 - b^2) γ = 0.
  | :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`\ = Nagel line: (b-c) α + (c-a) β + (a-b) γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` =\ :math:`1 : 1 : 1`.

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a point :g:`U <U>` = (x,y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = (a - b) (a - c) (b - c) (a + b + c)^2 + (2 a^4 - a^2 b^2 - b^4 - a^2 c^2 + 2 b^2 c^2 - c^4) x + (2 a - b - c) y,

  where, as functions of a,b,c, the coordinate x is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 1, and y is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 2. For a [Nagel line, Euler line] coordinate system, see trhe preamble just before X_48798.

  | {-((2 (a-b) (a-c) (b-c))/(a^2+b^2+c^2)), -((a-b) (a-c) (b-c) (a+b+c))}, 48807

If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` = Brocard axis: b^2 c^2 (b^2 - c^2) α + c^2 a^2 (c^2 - a^2) β + a^2 b^2 (a^2 - b^2) γ = 0.

  :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` = Euler line: (b^2 - c^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) α + (c^2 - a^2)(b^2 - c^2 - a^2) β + (a^2 - b^2)(c^2 - a^2 - b^2) γ = 0.

  The origin is given by (0, 0) = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = a^2(a^2-b^2-c^2) : : .

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a point :g:`U <U>` = (x, y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = a^2(a^2-b^2-c^2)(b^2-c^2)(c^2-a^2)(a^2-b^2) - a^2(a^2(b^2+c^2) - b^4 - c^4) x + (a^2(-2a^2+b^2+c^2) + (b^2-c^2)^2)y : : ,

  where, as functions of a, b, c, the coordinate x is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 4, and y is antisymmetric and homogeneous of degree 6.

  The appearance of {x, y}, k in the following list means that (x, y) = X_k.

.. _guide-preamble-0752:

* **X_50032**–**X_50040** — **Miyamoto-Lozada centers**

  . The centers X_50032 - X_50040, except for X_50039, were noted and conjectured by Keita Miyamoto, and confirmed by :person:`César Lozada <cesar-lozada>`. All the barycentric coordinates and other properties were found by Lozada, who also discovered X_50039.

  These centers are associated with circles tangent to the 3 excircles. In particular, X_50037, X_50038, X_50040 involve Hart circles of the excircles. (See `Mathworld: Hart's Theorem.) <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/HartsTheorem.html>`__

  Here, the notation (O) means a circle with center O. Let (:g:`E_{a} <E_a>`), (:g:`E_{b} <E_b>`), (:g:`E_{c} <E_c>`) denote the excircles, and let (S) be their radical circle. There are 8 lines or circles each of which is tangent to (:g:`E_{a} <E_a>`), (:g:`E_{b} <E_b>`), (:g:`E_{c} <E_c>`) simultaneously. These 8 are:

  | sidelines :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`;
  | nine-point circle (N);
  | Apollonius circle (Ap); note that (Ap) is the (S)-inverse of (N);
  | The three Jenkins circles (:g:`J_{a} <J_a>`), (:g:`J_{b} <J_b>`), (:g:`J_{c} <J_c>`); the A-Jenkins circle (:g:`J_{a} <J_a>`) is the (S)--inverse of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`; and (:g:`J_{b} <J_b>`) and (:g:`J_{c} <J_c>`) are defined cyclically.

  Hart's theorem states that generally, other than (:g:`E_{a} <E_a>`), (:g:`E_{b} <E_b>`), (:g:`E_{c} <E_c>`), there are 14 circles in total each of which is tangent to 4 of the 8 simultaneously. Following are the 14 Hart circles of the excircles:

  | The incircle (I) is tangent to :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, internally tangent to (N).
  | The Moses hull circle (M) is (internally or externally) tangent to (:g:`J_{a} <J_a>`), (:g:`J_{b} <J_b>`), (:g:`J_{c} <J_c>`), (Ap). (If S lies on (I), then (M) is a line.)
  | (:g:`O_{1} <O_1>`) is tangent to :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, internally tangent to (:g:`J_{b} <J_b>`) and (:g:`J_{c} <J_c>`); the circles (:g:`O_{2} <O_2>`) and (:g:`O_{3} <O_3>`) are defined cyclically.
  | (:g:`O_{4} <O_4>`) is tangent to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, internally tangent to (Ap) and (:g:`J_{a} <J_a>`), and externally tangent to (N); the circles (:g:`O_{5} <O_5>`) and (:g:`O_{6} <O_6>`) are defined cyclically.
  | (:g:`O_{7} <O_7>`) is tangent to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, internally tangent to (N), and externally tangent to (:g:`J_{b} <J_b>`) and (:g:`J_{c} <J_c>`); the circles (:g:`O_{8} <O_8>`) and (:g:`O_{9} <O_9>`) are defined cyclically.
  | (O10) is tangent to :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, and externally tangent to (Ap) and (:g:`J_{a} <J_a>`); the circles (O11) and (O12) are defined cyclically.

  Among the 14 Hart circles, the 6 Hart circles (:g:`O_{1} <O_1>`), (:g:`O_{2} <O_2>`), (:g:`O_{3} <O_3>`), (:g:`O_{4} <O_4>`), (:g:`O_{5} <O_5>`), (:g:`O_{6} <O_6>`) are orthogonal to (S), while the 4 Hart circles (M), (O10), (O11), (O12) are the (S)-inverses of the other 4: (I), (:g:`O_{7} <O_7>`), (:g:`O_{8} <O_8>`), (:g:`O_{9} <O_9>`), respectively. Clearly, IM, O7O10, O8O11, O9O12 concur in S = :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`. Also, :g:`O_{1}O_{4} <[ O_1 O_4 ]>`, :g:`O_{2}O_{5} <[ O_2 O_5 ]>`, :g:`O_{3}O_{6} <[ O_3 O_6 ]>` concur in X_50037.

.. _guide-preamble-0753:

* **X_50041**–**X_50073** — **Points in a [[a(b-c),b(c-a),c(a-b)], [(b^2-c^2)(a^2-b^2-c^2), (c^2-a^2)(b^2-c^2-a^2), (a^2-b^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)]] coordinate system**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, undated. If :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are lines that meet in a point P not at infinity, then a [:g:`L_{1} <L_1>`, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`]-coordinate system is a bivariate coordinate system having :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` as x-axis, :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` as y-axis, and P as origin. In this section, :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` are the following lines:

  :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` is the line: a(b+c) α + b(c+a) β (a+)b γ = 0.

  :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` is the line (b^2-c^2)(a^2-b^2-c^2) α + (c^2-a^2)(b^2-c^2-a^2) β + (a^2-b^2)(a^2 - b^2 - c^2) γ = 0 (Euler line).

  The origin is given by (0,0) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` = 1 1 : 1 .

  Barycentrics :math:`u : v : w` for a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` :g:`U <U>` = (x, y) in this system are given by

  :math:`u : v : w` = -(a-b)(a-c)(b-c)(a^3+b^3+c^3+a^2b+ab^2+b^2c+bc^2+c^2a+a^2c+2abc) - (ab + ac - 2bc)x - (2a^4-b^4-c^4+2b^2c^2-a^2b^2-a^2c^2) y : : ,

  where, as functions of a, b, c, the coordinate x is antisymmetric of degree 4, and y is antisymmetric of degree 2.

* **X_52302**–**X_52343** — **4th tangent line ot two inconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 5, 2022. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` =\ :math:`x_{1} : y_{1} : z_{1}`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` =\ :math:`x_{2} : y_{2} : z_{2}` (barycentrics) two distinct points on the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and not on the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :math:`q_{1}`, :math:`q_{2}` be the inconics of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspectors :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, respectively.

  | There exists a 4th-common tangent line τ to :math:`q_{1}` and :math:`q_{2}`, other than the sidelines of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. It can be deduced that: The :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of τ has barycentrics:
  | Q(τ) = :math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`x_{2}`\ \*(:math:`y_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2}`-:math:`y_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1})` : :math:`y_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{2}`\ \*(:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1}`-:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2})` : :math:`z_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2}`\ \*(:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{2}`-:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{1})` The touchpoints :g:`T_{1} <T_1>`, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` of τ with :math:`q_{1}`, :math:`q_{2}`, respectively, are:
  | :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` = :math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`x_{2}`\ ^2\*(:math:`y_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2}`-:math:`y_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1})`\ ^2 : :math:`y_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{2}`\ ^2\*(:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1}`-:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2})`\ ^2 : :math:`z_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2}`\ ^2\*(:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{2}`-:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{1})`\ ^2
  | :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` = :math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`x_{1}`\ ^2\*(:math:`y_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1}`-:math:`y_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2})`\ ^2 : :math:`y_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{1}`\ ^2\*(:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{2}`-:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1})`\ ^2 : :math:`z_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{1}`\ ^2\*(:math:`x_{2}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{1}`-:math:`x_{1}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{2})`\ ^2

  The preceding coordinates have the following equivalences leading to geometric constructions of τ, :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`: Q(τ) is the perspector of the circumconic of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` passing through :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`.

  Consequently, if :g:`U' <U'>` and :g:`U″ <U″>` are two given points and :math:`q_{0}` is the circumconic {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`U' <U'>`,\ :g:`U″ <U″>`}}, then, for any pair of points :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` on :math:`q_{0}`, the inconics with perspectors :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` have the same 4th common tangent line and it is tripolar of the perspector of :math:`q_{0}`.

  | :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is the perspector of the :term:`cevian <cevian>`-triangle-of-:g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and the side-triangle-of-(cevian-triangle-of-:g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and cevian-triangle-of-:g:`P_{2} <P_2>`), which are always`perspective. (Note: the side-triangle :g:`A_{s}B_{s}C_{s} << A_s B_s C_s >>` of two triangles :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` has :g:`A <A>`-vertex :g:`A_{s} <A_s>` = :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` ∩ :g:`B″C″ <[ B″ C″ ]>` and cyclically :g:`B_{s} <B_s>` and :g:`C_{s} <C_s>`).
  | Symmetrically, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is the perspector of the cevian-triangle-of-:g:`P_{2} <P_2>` and the side-triangle-of-(cevian-triangle-of-:g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and cevian-triangle-of-:g:`P_{2} <P_2>`).
  | See centers X_41211 to X_41224, which are related to analogous perspectors. :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is also the :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`-:term:`ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of-Q(τ) and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is also the :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`-ceva conjugate of-Q(τ), which means that :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` is the perspector(cevian-of-:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, anticevian-of-Q(τ)) and :g:`T_{2} <T_2>` is the perspector(cevian-of-:g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, anticevian-of-Q(τ)).

  **For shortening, the inconic with perspector U will be denoted in this section as IwP(U).**

  The appearance of (i, j, m, n, u) in the following (reduced) list indicates that the 4th common tangent line of IwP(X_i) and IwP(X_j) touches them at X(m) and X_n, respectively, and has trilinear pole X(u): (1, 2, 244, 1015, 513), (1, 3, 2638, 3270, 652), (1, 4, 2310, 3270, 650), (1, 5, 41211, 41218, 2600), (1, 6, 3248, 1015, 649), (1, 7, 2310, 3022, 650), (1, 8, 2310, 3271, 650), (1, 10, 2643, 3122, 661), (1, 11, 52302, 52303, 46384), (2, 3, 35071, 2972, 520), (2, 4, 115, 125, 523), (2, 5, 39019, 35442, 6368), (2, 6, 1084, 3124, 512), [and others].
