* **X_52448**–**X_52456** — **A locus related to K616**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 15, 2022. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P a point on its plane. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`A″ <A″>` the midpoint of :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`. Let :g:`A* <A*>` be the orthogonal projection of :g:`A″ <A″>` in :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and build :g:`B* <B*>`, :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. Then the locus of P such that :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A*B*C << A* B* C >>` are perspective is the cubic K616 and the locus of the perspectors Q(P) is the cubic q' = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>`-of-K1265, given by:

  q': Σ[(SB\*(S^2+(2\*SB+SC)\*SC)\*y - SC\*(S^2+(SB+2\*SC)\*SB)\*z)\*y\*z] + (SB-SC)\*(SC-SA)\*(SA-SB) \*x\*y\*z = 0

  q' circumscribes :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and passes through X_n for these n: {2, 4, 3434, 4846, 11185, 14593, 30513, 34029, 41370, 52448, 52449, 52450, 52451, 52452, 52453, 52454, 52455, 52456}.

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that Q(X_i ) = X_j: (4, 4), (69, 2), (376, 4846), (1249, 52448), (3421, 30513), (5485, 11185), (6601, 3434), (9214, 52449), (34208, 14593), (36874, 52450), (36875, 52451), (36876, 52452), (36877, 52453), (36878, 52454), (51830, 52455), (51831, 41370), (51832, 52456)

.. _guide-preamble-0780:

* **X_52522**–**X_52523** — **Lachance-Moses-Briancon points**

  based on notes from Michael Lachance and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November, 2022. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, suppose that

  | :g:`A' <A'>` =\ :math:`a_{1} : a_{2} : a_{3}`
  | :g:`B' <B'>` =\ :math:`b_{1} : b_{2} : b_{3}`
  | :g:`C' <C'>` =\ :math:`c_{1} : c_{2} : c_{3}`

  | are points on the circumcircle.
  | Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` = (:math:`c^{2}`\ :math:`b_{1}` + :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`b_{3})`\ :math:`c_{1}` : :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`b_{3}`\ :math:`c_{2}` : 0, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically.

  Let :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` = (:math:`b^{2}`\ :math:`c_{1}` + :math:`a^{2}`\ :math:`c_{2})`\ :math:`b_{1} : 0 : a`\ :sup:`2`\ :math:`b_{3}`\ :math:`c_{2}`, and define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically.

  Then the lines :g:`B_{a}C_{a} <[ B_a C_a ]>`, :g:`C_{b}A_{b} <[ C_b A_b ]>`, :g:`A_{c}B_{c} <[ A_c B_c ]>` concur in the Brianchon point of the hexagon {{H(:g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`)}}. This point, denoted by LMB(:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`), is given by the following barycentrics:

  :math:`a_{2}`\ :math:`a_{3}`\ :math:`b_{1}`\ :math:`c_{1}(b^{2}b_{3}c_{1} + c^{2}b_{1}c_{2} + a^{2}b_{3}c_{2})` : :

  The following conic is inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>`:

  :math:`a^{4}` :math:`b_{3}`\ ^2 :math:`c_{2}`\ ^2 (:math:`c^{2}` :math:`a_{2}` + :math:`b^{2}` :math:`a_{3})`\ :sup:`2` :math:`x^{2}` + (cyclic) - 2 :math:`b^{2}` :math:`c^{2}` :math:`a_{2}` :math:`a_{3}` :math:`b_{1}` :math:`c_{1}` (:math:`a^{2}` :math:`b_{3}` + :math:`c^{2}` :math:`b_{1})`\ (:math:`a^{2}` :math:`c_{2}` + :math:`b^{2}` :math:`c_{1})` y z - (cyclic) = 0

  In particular, if :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the circumtangential triangle, then LMB(:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`) = X_52522, and the inscribed conic is the Kiepert parabola. If :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the circumnormal triangle, then LMB(:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`A' <A'>`,\ :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`) = X_52523.

.. _guide-preamble-0781:

* **X_52526**–**X_52548** — **Centers of inscribed conics**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 9, 2022. In the preamble just before X_52522, if :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r`, then the center of the inconic is given by

  p (b^2c^2 p (q+r) + a (c^2q^2 + b^2r^2) : :

  The inconic is here given the name **LMB-cevian-inconic of P.** See also the preamble just before X_52549.

.. _guide-preamble-0782:

* **X_52549**–**X_52561** — **Perspectors of inscribed conics**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, December 9, 2022. Referring to the preamble just before X_52526, the perspector of the LMB-:term:`cevian <cevian>`-inconic is given by

  b^2\*c^2\*p\*(b^2\*p + a^2\*q)\*(c^2\*p + a^2\*r) : :

  See also the preamble just before X_52549.

.. _guide-preamble-0783:

* **X_52726**–**X_52740** — **Clawson circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 4, 2023. Let 𝓁\ :sub:`1`, 𝓁\ :sub:`2`, 𝓁\ :sub:`3`, 𝓁\ :sub:`4` be four lines, no three of them being concurrent. Let :g:`T_{1} <T_1>` be the triangle bounded by lines 𝓁\ :sub:`2`, 𝓁\ :sub:`3`, 𝓁\ :sub:`4`, and denote :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`, :g:`T_{3} <T_3>`, :g:`T_{4} <T_4>` similarly. Then the circumcenters of these four triangles lie on a circle Ω, here named the **Clawson circle** of the given lines. Moreover, the circumcircles of the four triangles have a common point 𝒬. (`J. W. Clawson, #2898, The American Mathematical Monthly, Vol. 29, No. 5 (May, 1922), pp. 230-231 <https://www.jstor.org/stable/2299751#metadata_info_tab_contents>`__.)

  The center of the circle Ω is the point **QL-P5** in the `Encyclopedia of Quadri-Figures <https://www.chrisvantienhoven.nl/ql-items/ql-points/ql-p5>`__.

  | In this section, three of the lines are the sidelines of a reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the fourth line is given. Assume this last line is the polar trilinear of :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, then the center of Ω is given by:
  | Ω\ :sub:`o`\ (P) = a^2\*(x\*(y^2-z^2)\*(-a^2+b^2+c^2)+y\*z\*(-2\*(b^2-c^2)\*x+(a^2-c^2)\*y-(a^2-b^2)\*z)-(-a^2+b^2+2\*c^2)\*x^2\*y+(-a^2+2\*b^2+c^2)\*z\*x^2) : :
  | and the point 𝒬, obviously on the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, is:
  | 𝒬(P) = a^2\*(x-y)\*(x-z) : :, which corresponds to the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of - the infinite point of - the tripolar of - the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`.

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that Ω\ :sub:`o`\ (X_i) = X_j: (1, 52726), (3, 52737), (4, 44810), (5, 52738), (6, 14270), (7, 52730), (8, 52739), (9, 52740), (10, 44827), (25, 25644), (69, 8552), (76, 44826), (94, 14809), (107, 52734), (110, 52727), (111, 44821), (190, 52732), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0784:

* **X_52746**–**X_52768** — **Tripolar Centroidal Conjugates**

  based on a definition and notes by :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`; see `Tripolar Centroidal Cubics <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Classes/cl045.html>`__. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` is a point in the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The **tripolar centroidal conjugate** of :g:`P <P>` is given by

  TCC(P) = (-2 p + q + r) (p q - 2 p r + q r) (-2 p q + p r + q r) : :

  and TCC(P) = P if and only if P lies on the cubic K015.

  Let :g:`U <U>` = the infinite point of the line GP, and let :g:`P' <P'>` = tripolar centroid of P. Then TCCP is the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line :g:`UP' <[ U P' ]>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0785:

* **X_53805** — **Miyamoto-Moses Points**

  Part 1 is based on notes and figures by Keita Miyamoto. Part 2 is based on notes from Keita Miyamoto and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`.

  **Part 1.**

  Proposition 1.1 (inner case).

  In a scalene acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`M_{a}M_{b}M_{c} << M_a M_b M_c >>` be its :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`. Let Ωa be the circle centered at :g:`M_{a} <M_a>` and passing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`, and define Ωb and Ωc cyclically. Inside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let γa be the circle externally tangent to lines :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`,Ωa, and define γb and γc cyclically. Inside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let γ be the circle internally tangent to Ωa, Ωb, Ωc. Then there exists a circle Γ that is tangent to the four circles γ, γa, γb, γc.

  Let :g:`Z_{1} <Z_1>` denote the touchpoint of Γ and γ, and let :g:`Z_{2} <Z_2>` denote the center of Γ. The points :g:`Z_{1} <Z_1>` and :g:`Z_{2} <Z_2>` are the :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` X_52807 and X_52805, respectively. Here, the circle Γ is named the **1st Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius circle**, and the circle internally tangent to γa, γb and γc is named the **2nd Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius circle**. Let :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` be the touchpoint of Γ and γa, and define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` cyclically. Here, the triangle :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is named the **1st-Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius triangle**. See `Figure 1 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__.

  Proposition 1.1 also holds when :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is an obtuse triangle. In this case, suppose that angle :g:`A <A>` is obtuse. Let :g:`H_{b} <H_b>` be the point of intersection, other than A, of Ωc and line :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`. Let :g:`H_{c} <H_c>` be the point of intersection, other than A, of Ωb and line :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Let γa be the circle internally tangent to Ωa and segments :g:`AH_{b} <[ A H_b ]>` and :g:`AH_{c} <[ A H_c ]>`. This circle lies outside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, as in `Figure 2 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__.

  Proposition 1.2 (outer case).

  In a scalene acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`M_{a}M_{b}M_{c} << M_a M_b M_c >>` be its medial triangle. Let Ωa be the circle centered at :g:`M_{a} <M_a>` and passing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`, and define Ωb and Ωc cyclically. Let γa be the larger of the two circles internally tangent to lines :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, Ωa, and define γb and γc cyclically. Outside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let γ be the circle internally tangent to Ωa, Ωb, Ωc. Then there exists a circle Γ that is tangent to the four circles γ, γa, γb, γc.

  Let :g:`Z_{3} <Z_3>` denote the touchpoint of Γ and γ, and let :g:`Z_{4} <Z_4>` denote the center of Γ, as in `Figure 3 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__. The points :g:`Z_{3} <Z_3>` and :g:`Z_{4} <Z_4>` are the triangle centers X_52810 and X_52808, respectively. Here, the circle Γ is named the **3rd Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius circle**, and the circle internally tangent to γa, γb, γc other than Γ, is named the **4th Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius circle**. Let :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` be the touchpoint of Γ and γa, and define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` cyclically. Here, the triangle :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is named the **2nd Miyamoto-Moses-Apollonius triangle**.

  Proposition 1.2 also holds when :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is an obtuse triangle. In this case, suppose that angle :g:`A <A>` is obtuse. Let γa; be the smaller of the two circles, etc., as in `Figure 4 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__.

  It appears that Propositions 1.1 and 1.2 hold for any three circles Ωa, Ωb, Ωc, each of which passes through two of the three points :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`. Next, Proposition 1\* treats an example of this sort.

  Proposition 1\*.

  In a scalene acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`Tan_aTan_bTan_c << Tan_a Tan_b Tan_c >>` be the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>`. Let Ωa be the circle centered at :g:`Tan_a <Tan_a>` and pssing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`, and define Ωb and Ωc cyclically. Let γa be a circle tangent (internally or externally) to lines :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, Ωa, and define γb and γc cyclically. Let γ be the circle tangent to Ωa, Ωb, Ωc. Then there exists a circle Γ that is tangent to the four circles γ, γa, γb, γc.

  For Proposition 1\*, there are 4 cases, as indicated by these figures: `Figure 5 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, `Figure 6 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, `Figure 7 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, `Figure 8 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__. The 4 cases depend on internal and external tangencies.

  Proposition 2.

  Let γ be the incircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let γa be the circle through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` and internally tangent to γ. Define γb and γc cyclically. Outside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let Γa be the circle externally tangent to :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, γa, and let :g:`A' <A'>` be the center of Γa. Define Γb and Γc cyclically, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`L_{a} <L_a>` be the external common tangent, other than :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, of Γb and Γc, so that :g:`L_{a} <L_a>` is the reflection of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` in :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`. Define :g:`L_{b} <L_b>` and :g:`L_{c} <L_c>` cyclically. Let :g:`A″ <A″>`\ =\ :g:`L_{b} <L_b>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{c} <L_c>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The perspector is denoted by :g:`Z_{5} <Z_5>` in `Figure 9 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__. The point :g:`Z_{5} <Z_5>` is the triangle center X_52817. Here, the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is named the **Miyamoto-Moses triangle**.

  **Part 2.**

  Barycentrics for points defined in Part 1 are shown below and in a sequel to Figure 1 in GeoGebra: `Figure 10 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__. This file has a slider that can be used to observe the effect of changing S to - S in the barycentrics. In particular, the transformation S -> - S takes X_14121 to X_7090.

  The point :g:`Z_{5} <Z_5>` shown in Figure 9, appears as P in `Figure 11 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, and :g:`P <P>` = X_52817.

  The circles γa, γb;, γc have a Chinese name that translates roughly as pseudo-circumcircles. For example, let :g:`U <U>` denote the circular hull of the pseudo-circumcircles that pass through 2 vertices and are tangent to the incircle. Their circular hull has center :g:`O <O>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and radius R + r/2. In `Figure 12 <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, the points labeled tA and tA' are given by barycentrics as follows:

  tA = 4\*a^2\*(a + b - c)\*(a - b + c) : -((a - b - c)\*(a + b - c)^3) : -((a - b - c)\*(a - b + c)^3)

  tA'= 2\*a^2 : a^2 - 2\*a\*b - b^2 - 2\*a\*c + c^2 : a^2 - 2\*a\*b + b^2 - 2\*a\*c - c^2

  If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` is a point on the circumcircle, then the point

  :g:`P' <P'>` = (a^2\*b^2 - b^4 + 4\*a^2\*b\*c + 4\*a\*b^2\*c + a^2\*c^2 + 4\*a\*b\*c^2 + 2\*b^2\*c^2 - c^4)\*p + a^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*(q + r) : :

  lies on the the circular hull. The point :g:`P' <P'>` is here named the **Moses-Apollonius transform** of P. Examples are X_52820 to X_52834.

.. _guide-preamble-0786:

* **X_53006**–**X_53007** — **Miyamoto-Moses Points**

  This preamble continues the preamble just before X_52805. It is based on proposition 3 by Keita Miyamoto, with barycentrics found by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`.

  Proposition 3.

  In a scalene acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`T <T>` = :g:`T_aT_bT_c << T_a T_b T_c >>` be the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let γ be the incircle of :g:`T <T>`, and let Γa be the :g:`A <A>`-excircle of :g:`AT_bT_c << A T_b T_c >>`. Define Γb and Γc cyclically. Let γa be the circle tangent to :g:`T_bT_c <[ T_b T_c ]>` and internally tangent to the incircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :g:`T_a <T_a>`. Define γb and γc cyclically. Then there exists a circle ω that is tangent to all seven of the circles γ, Γa, Γb, Γc, γa, γb, γc. Here the circle ω is named the **Miyamoto-Moses circle**.

  The center of Γa, which is the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of the 2nd midarc triangle (see X_10491, given by

  a\*b - b^2 + a\*c + 2\*b\*c - c^2 - 2\*x : b\*(-a + b + c) : -((a - b - c)\*c : : , where

  x = sqrt[b\*c\*(a + b - c)\*(a - b + c)] = 2\*b\*c sin(A/2), and y and z are defined cyclically.

  The radius of Γa, is

  ((2\*b\*c + x)\*S)/(2\*b\*c\*(a + b + c)) = r\*(1 + Sin[A/2])

  The touch-point of Γa and ω, denoted by a2 in `Proposition 3 (GeoGebra). <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/KM>`__, is given by [expression omitted here].

  The center of the circle γa is given by

  2\*a\*x : 2\*b\*(a + b - c)\*c + x\*(-a + b + c) : 2\*b\*c\*(a - b + c) + x\*(-a + b + c)

  Let :g:`Z_{6} <Z_6>` be the touch-point of the circles ω and γ. Then :g:`Z_{6} <Z_6>` = X_53006, and :g:`Z_{6} <Z_6>`-of-:g:`T <T>` = :ref:`X_1357 <X_1357>`.

  Let :g:`Z_{7} <Z_7>` by the center of circle ω. Then :g:`Z_{7} <Z_7>` = X_53007, and :g:`Z_{7} <Z_7>`-of-:g:`T <T>` = X_53002. The triangle a2b2c2 is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at X_10489 and to the 2nd mid-arc triangle at X_53007. The triangle a3b3c3 is perspective to the intouch triangle at X_10489.

.. _guide-preamble-0787:

* **X_53246**–**X_53580** — **Intersections of lines tangent to conics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (definitions and presentation) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (formulas, data, and properties), April 25-May 1, 2023. Suppose that U and X are distinct points on a conic sΓ. Let (U) be the line tangent to Γ at :g:`U <U>`, and Let (X) be the line tangent to Γ at X. Define :math:`F(U,X) = (U)`\ ∩(X). Listed here are conics for which F(U,X) appears for selected pairs of points :g:`U <U>` and X:

  | circumcircle: X_53246-X_53330, X_53384, X_52385
  | Steiner circumellipse: X_53331-X_53383
  | Bevan circle: X_53389-X_53412
  | Stevanovich circel: X_53389, X_43413
  | other circumconics: X_53386-X_533898
  | Kiepert circumhyperbola: X_54314-X_54520
  | incircle: X_54521-X_54563
  | nine-point circle: X_53564-X_53577
  | Yff parabala: X_53588-X_535602
  | dual of Yff parabola; i.e., {:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`}: X_53588-X_535602

  Suppose :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p: q : r` is a point and Γ is the circumconic with perspector P. If :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` and :g:`X <X>` =\ :math:`x : y : z`, then the point :math:`f : g : h` : F(U,X) is given by the following barycentrics:

  :math:`f : g : h` : p(wy+vz)( (2qu+pv+qv-rv)x + (2pv+pu+qu-ru)y )( (2ru+pw+rw-qw)x + (2pw+pu+ru-qu)z ) : :

  In this case, :math:`F(U,X) = crossdifference of every pair of points on the line bcf`\ α + gcaβ + habγ = 0, so that F(U,X) is the :term:`trilinear pole <trilinear-pole>` of the line ghα + hfβ + fgγ = 0 .

.. _guide-preamble-0788:

* **X_53603**–**X_53613** — **Reflection points on the circumcircle**

  :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` May, 2023. The appearance of {i,j,k} in the following list means that X_k = reflection of X_i in the line :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ X_j:

  {74,98,43654}, {74,99,43654}, {74,100,43655}, {74,104,43655}, {74,110,74}, {74,1113,477}, {74,1114,477}, {74,1379,842}, {74,1380,842}, {74,1381,2687}, {74,1382,2687},

.. _guide-preamble-0789:

* **X_53621**–**X_53708** — **and X_53682-X_53708, Touchpoints on the circumcircle**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (definitions and presentation) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (formulas, data, and properties), May 6, 2023. A point :g:`P <P>`, as a function of (a,b,c), is here defined to be an **inner point** if P lies inside the circumcircle, Γ, for every triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (that is, for every (a,b,c) satisfying b+c>a and c+a>b and a+b>c); and an **outer point** otherwise. If X is an outer :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` (so that its Γ-invers is an inner triangle center), then X lies on two lines that are tangent to Γ, so that there are two touchpoints, which in some cases are triangle centers and in some cases are a bicentric pair. The appearance of X_i → (X_j,X_k in the following list means that X_i is an outer triangle center and X_j and X_k are the touchpoints

  | :ref:`X_190 <X_190>` → X(100, 932)
  | :ref:`X_351 <X_351>` → X(110, 111)
  | :ref:`X_659 <X_659>` → X(100, 105)
  | [and othersj].

  In the analogous context for the Steiner circumellipse, instead of the circumcircle, see the preamble just before X_53639.

.. _guide-preamble-0790:

* **X_52639**–**X_52659** — **Touchpoints on the Steiner circumellipse**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (definitions and presentation) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (formulas, data, and properties), May 7, 2023. In the manner of the preamble just before X_53621, a point :g:`P <P>`, as a function of (a,b,c), is defined in this section to be an **inner point** if P lies inside the Steiner circumellipse, SCE, for every triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (that is, for every (a,b,c) satisfying b+c>a and c+a>b and a+b>c); and an **outer point** otherwise. If X is an outer :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` (so that its SCE-inverse is an inner triangle center), then X lies on two lines that are tangent to SCE, so that there are two touchpoints, which in some cases are triangle centers and in some cases are a bicentric pair. The appearance of X_i → (X_j,X_k in the following list means that X_i is an outer triangle center and X_j and X_k are the touchpoints

  | :ref:`X_100 <X_100>` → X(190, 664)
  | :ref:`X_107 <X_107>` → X(648, 53639)
  | :ref:`X_110 <X_110>` → X(99, 648)
  | [and others].

  In the analogous context for the circumcircle, instead of the Steiner circumellipse, see the preamble just before X_53621.

.. _guide-preamble-0791:

* **X_53660**–**X_53671** — **Strictly inner points**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` (definitions and presentation) and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` (formulas, data, and properties), May 8, 2023. In the preamble just before X_53621, a point :g:`P <P>` is defined to be an **inner point** if P lies inside the circumcircle for all triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Here, a point :g:`P <P>` is defined to be a **strictly inner point** point if P lies inside :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for every nondegenerate triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. That is, if b+c>a and c+a>b and a+b>c, then P has barycentrics (and trilinears) that are all positive for all such (a,b,c). Many well-known :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` have this property (e.g., :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`, :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`, :ref:`X_37 <X_37>`.) A point :g:`P <P>` is a **strictly outer point** point if P lies outside :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for every nondegenerate triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0792:

* **X_53709**–**X_53763** — **Midpoints of points on the circumcircle**

The points all lie inside the circumcircle, Γ, so that, they are "inner points" as defined in the preamble just before X_53621. Conjecture: none of these midpoints is "strictly inner"; i.e., inside triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` for all :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`.

  Suppose that P is a fixed point on Γ and that X is a variable point on Γ. The locus of the midpoint of :g:`P <P>` and X is a circle, Γ(P,X). Let O(P,X) be the center of Γ(P,X). For example, O(:ref:`X_74 <X_74>`,X) passes through X_i for these i: 12041, 12042, 33813, 33814, 38599, 38600, 38601, 38602, 38607, 1511, 14650, 38608, 38609. If P is not fixed but goes around the circle, then the locus of the centers of the circles has center O and radius (1/2)\*circumradius. This circle, with perspector :ref:`X_3431 <X_3431>`, passes through X_i for these i: 1511, 12041,12042, 14650, 33813, 33814, 35231, 35232, 38599, 38600, 38601, 38602, 38603, 38604, 38605, 38606, 38607, 38608, 38609, 38610, 38611, 38612, 38613, 38614, 38615, 38616, 38617, 38618, 38619, 38620, 38621, 38622, 38623, 38624, 38625, 49119

* **X_54097**–**X_54113** — **Perspectors associated with Steiner-circumcevian triangles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` June 29, 2023. Let SCE be Steiner circumellipse of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a point not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the point, other than A, where the line :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` meets line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here named the **Steiner-circumcevian triangle of P**, denoted by SCC(P). The vertices of SCC(P) are given by

  | :g:`A' <A'>` = -q r : q (q + r) : r (q + r)
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = p (r + p) : - r p : r (r + p)
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = p (p + q) : q (p + q) : - p q

  The triangle SCC(P) is perspective to the anticomplementary. Let SC(P) denote the perspector. Then

  | SC(P) = :math:`P^{2}`-:term:`Ceva conjugate <ceva-conjugate>` of :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`
  | SC(P) = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :math:`P^{2}`.

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that SC(X_i) = X_j.

  (2996, 54097), (330, 54098), (7035, 54099), (276, 54100), (291, 54101), (514, 54102). (8781, 54103), (523, 54104), (40410, 54105), (262, 54106), (333, 54107), (18020, 54108), (314, 54109), (4998, 54110), (253, 54111), (310, 54112), (312, 54113)

  The triangle SCC(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`) is the triangle Gemini 107, and the triangle SCC(4) is the 9th Brocard triangle.

  Let :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` be the line tangent to SCC at :g:`A' <A'>`, and define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` cyclically. Let :g:`A* <A*>` = :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` ^ :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. Then :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is given by the point T(P) = 1 / (-q\*r + r\*p + p\*q) : : . The transformation T maps curves to curves, as in these examples:

  | T(Kiepert hyperbola) = Kiepert hyperbola
  | T(K184) = K007
  | T(K1023) = K1000
  | T(K868) = K1002
  | T(K1014) = K1037)
  | T(K342a) = K1053a)
  | T(K342b) = K1053n)

* **X_54449**–**X_55037** — **and X_55019-X_55037, Cyclocevian conjugates**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 11, 2023. As noted in the Glossary, suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (trilinear coordinates, not barycentric) is a point not on a sideline of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. The circumcircle of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` meets line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` in two points: :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`; pairs :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, and :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`C″ <C″>` are obtained cyclically. The lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` concur in the :term:`cyclocevian conjugate <cyclocevian-conjugate>` of P. Let

  :math:`g(a,b,c) = a/[p(qb + r_{c})]` and :math:`f(a,b,c) = bc/[g(b`,c,a) + g(c,a,b) - g(a,b,c)].

  The cyclocevian conjugate of :g:`P <P>` is given by

  :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)` (trilinears).

  | The cyclocevian conjugate of a point is the
  | :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>`
  | of the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>`
  | of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`
  | of the :term:`complement <complement>`
  | of the isotomic conjugate
  | of the point
  | (:person:`Darij Grinberg <darij-grinberg>`, January 24, 2003)

  Now switching to bartycentric coordinates, suppose that p x + q y + r z = 0 is a line. It's image under cyclocevian conjugationj is the octic curve given by [expression omitted here]

  The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that the cyclocevian conjugate of X_i is X_j: (1,1029, (2,4), (5,54449), (6,1031), (7,7), (8,189), (13,13483), (14,13484), (20,1032), (63,54450), (66,2998), (67,46275), (68,34287), (69,253), (75,8044), (76,41513), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0795:

* **X_54460**–**X_54467** — **H-conics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, July 15, 2023. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a right triangle at A. There exists a lot of finite centers in ETC lying on the hypotenuse :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` (produced included), in particular, those having first coordinates with a multiplying factor cos(A) or (-a^2+b^2+c^2).

  Let denote by ℋ the set of k such that X_k-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` lies on the hypotenuse :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. As an example, the subset o ℋ for k≤1000 is {3, 48, 49, 63, 68, 69, 71, 72, 73, 77, 78, 97, 122, 123, 125, 127, 130, 131, 155, 184, 185, [and others].

  **Application.**

  Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be an acute triangle . Build the rectangle :math:`BCC_{a}`\ :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` such that A lies on :g:`C_{a}B_{a} <[ C_a B_a ]>`. Two right triangles :g:`B_{a}BA << B_a B A >>` and :g:`C_{a}CA << C_a C A >>` are obtained. Now, for a given k ∈ ℋ, let :g:`B'_{a} <B'_a>` = X_k-of-:g:`B_{a}BA << B_a B A >>` and :g:`C'_{a} <C'_a>` = X_k-of-:g:`C_{a}CA << C_a C A >>`, these centers lying on their hipotenuses :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`, respectively. Define :g:`C'_{b} <C'_b>`, :g:`A'_{b} <A'_b>` and :g:`A'_{c} <A'_c>`, :g:`B'_{c} <B'_c>` cyclically. It is not hard to prove that, for any k∈ℋ, these six points lie on an conic 𝒞( X_k ), here named the **H-conic of X(k)** (H stands for *hypotenuses*).

  Depending on the chosen k, 𝒞( X_k ) can degenerate to two lines or to the line at infinity (as with :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_68 <X_68>` and others). Also, every pair of constructed points on a side of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` can coincide and the H-conic approaches to a circle, as occurs with :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`, for which the Taylor circle is obtained.

.. _guide-preamble-0796:

* **X_54474**–**X_55009** — **Orthology centers related to bicevian conics**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov, July 19, 2023. Let (c) be the bicevian conic of :g:`P <P>`\ ={u,v,w} and :g:`Q <Q>`\ ={p,q,r}. Lines :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`CP <[ C P ]>` intersect (c) at six points, three of which form the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. Denote the other three with :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, and :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`. Similarly, using Q, define :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, and :g:`C_{2} <C_2>`. The lines :g:`A_{1}A_{2} <[ A_1 A_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{1}B_{2} <[ B_1 B_2 ]>`, and :g:`C_{1}C_{2} <[ C_1 C_2 ]>` form a triangle :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>`, which is always perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  In the cases when a certain fourth degree relation holds, :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` are also orthologic. In the particular case when :g:`Q <Q>`\ =\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and P lies on the Kiepert hyperbola, the orthology center of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` also lies on the Kiepert hyperbola.

  In the particular case when :g:`Q <Q>`\ =\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` and P lies on the circumconic with perspector :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, the configuration is degenerate becasue :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`\ =\ :g:`T_{b} <T_b>`\ =\ :g:`T_{c} <T_c>`\ =H. The orthology center (which exists only in the limit) is the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of (SB u v+SC u w-a^2 v w : :) and lies on the Steiner circumellipse. When the orthology center of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` exists it lies on the Euler line.

  For more information on how each center arises see the documents attached to Euclid 5932 .

  Contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 21, 2023: The appearance of i in the following list means that X_i is a :term:`major center <major-center>` and lies on the Kiepert hyperbola: 54479, 54480, 54534, [and others].

* **X_55042**–**X_55073** — **Centers of circumconics**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` July 25, 2023. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` be distinct points. The center of the circumconic {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`,\ :g:`U <U>`}} is given by

  p u (r v - q w)(p v w (r - q) - q w u (p + r) + r u v (p + q ) : :

  See X_34585.

.. _guide-preamble-0804:

* **X_55917**–**X_56365** — **Kimberling-Pavlov conjugates**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov, August 14, 2023. Let :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`\ ={a1,a2,a3} and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`\ ={b1, b2, b3) be arbitrary points and let (cc) be the circumconic with perspector :g:`X <X>`\ ={u,v,w}. Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` and :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` be the traces on (cc) of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, respectively.

  The lines :g:`A_{1}A_{2} <[ A_1 A_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{1}B_{2} <[ B_1 B_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{1}C_{2} <[ C_1 C_2 ]>` form a triangle perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The perspector has the following barycentrics:

  u/(u^2/(a1\*b1)-(v/a2+w/a3)\*(v/b2+w/b3)) : v/(v^2/(a2\*b2)-(u/a1+w/a3)\*(u/b1+w/b3)) : w/(w^2/(a3\*b3)-(u/a1+v/a2)\*(u/b1+v/b2))

  This point is here introduced as the **Kimberling-Pavlov X-conjugate of P1 and P2**. It is obviously symmetric and involutory (i.e., it is a conjugation). In his article "Mappings Associated with Vertex Triangles" (*:cite:`Forum Geometricorum <forum-geometricorum>`*, 9 (2009) 27-39), :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` discusses this mapping for the case :g:`X <X>`\ =\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, and he denotes the mapping by :g:`M_{1} <M_1>`. He also proposes variations denoted by :g:`M_{2} <M_2>`, :g:`M_{3} <M_3>`, and :g:`M_{4} <M_4>`.

  Here, these mappings are generalized for any point :g:`X <X>`, and the equivalent of formula (6) on p.34 of the cited article gives the following barycentrics:

  | **(KP2(X)** of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) = u/(u^2/(a1\*b1)-(v/a2-w/a3)\*(v/b2-w/b3)) : v/(v^2/(a2\*b2)-(u/a1-w/a3)\*(u/b1-w/b3)) : w/(w^2/(a3\*b3)-(u/a1-v/a2)\*(u/b1-v/b2))
  | **(KP3(X)** of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) = u/(u^2/(a1\*b1)+(v/a2+w/a3)\*(v/b2+w/b3)) : v/(v^2/(a2\*b2)+(u/a1+w/a3)\*(u/b1+w/b3)) : w/(w^2/(a3\*b3)+(u/a1+v/a2)\*(u/b1+v/b2))
  | **(KP4(X)** of :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` and :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`) = u/(u^2/(a1\*b1)+(v/a2-w/a3)\*(v/b2-w/b3)) : v/(v^2/(a2\*b2)+(u/a1-w/a3)\*(u/b1-w/b3)) : w/(w^2/(a3\*b3)+(u/a1-v/a2)\*(u/b1-v/b2))

  Stated below are a few properties of these points:

  | **Theorem 1.**
  | Let I=\ :ref:`X_1 <X_1>` and
  | :g:`P' <P'>`\ = :term:`cevapoint <cevapoint>` of :g:`I <I>` and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of P
  | :g:`Q' <Q'>`\ = cevapoint of :g:`I <I>` and the isogonal conjugate of :g:`Q <Q>`.

  Then the Kimberling-Pavlov I-conjugate of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` is the intersection, other than :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, of the conics {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P <P>`,\ :g:`Q' <Q'>`}} and {{:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`Q <Q>`}}.

  | **Theorem 2.**
  | In the limiting case, where :g:`P <P>`\ =Q, the Kimberling-Pavlov I-conjugate of :g:`P <P>` and P is the cross-conjugate of :g:`I <I>` and the the isogonal conjugate of P(P).
  | Generally, the Kimberling-Pavlov X-conjugate of :g:`P <P>` and P is the :term:`cross conjugate <cross-conjugate>` of the X^2-:term:`reciprocal conjugate <reciprocal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` and P, where " ^ " denotes barycentric square.

  | **Theorem 3.**
  | The Kimberling-Pavlov :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`-conjugate of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` is the P-:term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of :g:`Q <Q>`.

  | **Theorem 4.**
  | Let 𝓒 be a circumconic through I. If P lies on 𝓒, then the Kimberling-Pavlov I-conjugate of :g:`I <I>` and P also lies on 𝓒.

  | **Theorem 5.**
  | The Kimberling-Pavlov G-conjugate of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` is the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of the midpoint of the barycentric quotients P/G and Q/G.

* **X_57042**–**X_57252** — **Triaxial points**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov, August 26, 2023. Triaxial points are defined in the preamble just before X_14272.
  | "Let :g:`F_{1} <F_1>`, :g:`F_{2} <F_2>`, :g:`F_{3} <F_3>` be three figures in perspective two and two in the same plane, show that if they have a common centre of perspective, their three perspectrix are concurrent." (Quoted from Lachlan, R.: *An Elementary Treatise on Modern Pure Geometry*, McMillan & Co., 1893, pp. 123). Let T(P,Q) denote the triaxial point of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the P-circumconcevian triangle of :g:`X <X>`\ ={u,v,w}, and the Q-circumconcevian triangle of X. Ten T(P,Q) depends only on the line :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` and coincides with
  | (1) the :term:`cevian <cevian>` quotient of the tripole of line :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` and X, and
  | (2) the pole of line :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` wrt the circumconic with perspector X
  | In barycentrics, if :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p1 : q1 : r1` and p2 =\ :math:`p2 : q2 : r2`, then

  T(P,Q) = u ((q2 r1 - q1 r2) u + (p2 r1 - p1 r2) v + (p1 q2 - p2 q1) w) : v ((q1 r2 - q2 r1) u + (p1 r2 - p2 r1) v + (p1 q2 - p2 q1) w) : w ((q1 r2 - q2 r1) u + (p2 r1 - p1 r2) v + (p2 q1 - p1 q2) w).

.. _guide-preamble-0808:

* **X_57297**–**X_57381** — **Homothetic centers involving nine-point centers**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on August 30, 2023. Let :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :math:`u : v : w` be a point upon the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and let :g:`P' <P'>` be the antipoade of P. Let :g:`O_{a} <O_a>`, :g:`O_{b} <O_b>`, :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` be the nine-point centers of :g:`BPC << B P C >>`, :g:`ACP << A C P >>`, :g:`ABP << A B P >>` resp.
  | Triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` is homothetic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The center of homothety is P\ :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`\ ∩\ :g:`P' <P'>`:ref:`X_140 <X_140>`, given by the following first barycentric:

  a^4\*u+(b^2-c^2)^2\*(2\*u+v+w)-a^2\*(b^2+c^2)\*(3\*u+v+w).

.. _guide-preamble-0810:

* **X_58747**–**X_58909** — **Tripolar triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 24, 2023. Let :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two perspective triangles, neither inscribed in the other. Denote their perspector Q and their axis of perspectivity r.

  Let :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` be the tripoles of :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, :g:`C'A' <[ C' A' ]>`, :g:`A'B' <[ A' B' ]>` with respect to :g:`T″ <T″>`, in the same order. The triangle :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` is named here the **tripolar triangle of T' with respect to T"** and denoted as TPT(:g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`).

  Let :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>` be the tripolar triangle of :g:`T″ <T″>` with respect to :g:`T' <T'>`, i.e, :g:`T_{2} <T_2>`\ =TPT(:g:`T″ <T″>`, :g:`T' <T'>`)

  Then: .LI{padding-bottom:12px;} a) :g:`T' <T'>` and TPT(:g:`T″ <T″>`, :g:`T' <T'>`) are perspective. Call their perspector :g:`Q' <Q'>` and their perspectrix r'. The point :g:`Q' <Q'>` is referred here as the **tripolar-perspector of T' to T"**. b) :g:`T″ <T″>` and TPT(:g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`) are perspective. Call their perspector :g:`Q″ <Q″>` and their perspectrix r". c) Q, :g:`Q' <Q'>`, :g:`Q″ <Q″>` are collinear on a line :g:`L <L>`. d) r, r', r" concur in a point, here named the **tripolar-triaxial point of T' and T"**. e) Call :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` the tripoles of :g:`L <L>` wrt :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>`, respectively. Then Q, :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` are collinear.

  A list of related centers for triangles :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and orthic can be seen **here** (``X(58747).txt``).

  Note: For definitions of triangles used in this section, check the **Index of triangles referenced in ETC** (``IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html``).

.. _guide-preamble-0811:

* **X_59137**–**X_59273** — **Polelogic and polarologic centers involving circumcevian triangles**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on September 26, 2023. The polelogic and polarologic centers of two triangles :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` are defined in the preamble just before X_42287. It can be shown that :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the circumcevian triangle (denoted :g:`T″ <T″>` below) of any point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`u : v : w` are polelogic.

  :g:`T' <T'>`-to-:g:`T″ <T″>`-polarologic center = a^2 c^2 u v - a^4 v w + b^2 u (2 c^2 u + a^2 w) : :

  > :g:`T' <T'>`-to-:g:`T″ <T″>`-polelogic center = u (b^2 u + a^2 v)(c^2 u + a^2 w)(-c^4 u v + c^2 (b^2 u + a^2 v) w + 2 a^2 b^2 w^2)(-2 a^2 c^2 v^2 + b^4 u w - b^2 v (c^2 u + a^2 w)) : :

  | :g:`T″ <T″>`-to-:g:`T' <T'>` polarologic center = :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`,
  | :g:`T″ <T″>`-to-:g:`T' <T'>` polelogic center = b^2 c^2 u (b^2 u + a^2 v)(c^2 u + a^2 w) : : .
  | These centers can be generalized by reference to circumconcevian triangles instead of circumcevian triangles. See `Euclid 5406 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/5406>`__ for details.

.. _guide-preamble-0812:

* **X_59294**–**X_59359** — **Harmonic means**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 30, 2023. The harmonic mean x of two numbers p, q is that satisfying :math:`x^{-1}` = (:math:`p^{-1}` + :math:`q^{-1})`/2. Similarly, in geometry, given three collinear points :g:`O <O>`, :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>`, their harmonic mean is the point :g:`X <X>`, on its same line, and such that OX is the harmonic mean of :g:`OP <[ O P ]>` and OQ (signed distances all).

  If O, P, Q are given and X is their harmonic mean, then X is the point for which (O, X) and (P, Q) are in harmonic range. X is denoted here as the **O-harmonic mean of (P, Q)**.

  A very simple geometrical construction of :g:`X <X>` = O-harmonic mean of (P, Q) follows, when O, P, Q are given: .LI li{padding-bottom:12px;} Take any point E outside the line OPQ and join OE and QE. Through P, draw a parallel line to QE, cutting OE at F. Let :g:`F* <F*>` be the reflection of :g:`F <F>` in P. The line :g:`EF* <[ E F* ]>` cuts the line OPQ in :g:`X <X>`, the O-harmonic mean of (P, Q).

  Algebraically, if λ = OQ/:g:`OP <[ O P ]>`, then OX = (2\*λ/(1+λ))\*\ :g:`OP <[ O P ]>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0813:

* **X_59437**–**X_59458** — **Inconics through two given points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 5, 2023. In *Eagles, Thomas Henry, Constructive Geometry of Plane Curves, McMillan and Co., London, 1885*, available in `www.archive.org <https://archive.org/details/constructivegeom00eagluoft>`__, there are expained and proved methods for constructing conics touching three distinct, not concurrent given lines and passing through two given points (problem 83, pp.134 and problem 112, pp. 182).

  Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be the triangle bounded by the three given tangents and P, Q the given points. Both :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` must be in the same side with respect to every tangent. This means that :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` must be both interior to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` (problem 83) or both exterior to it (problem 112).

  The construction by Eagles follows (using century XXI cyclic notation): .LI li{padding-bottom:12px;} Let :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` be the intersections of line :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` and :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively. Let :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>` be the double points of the involution {:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`} and {P, Q} (see preamble just before X_14782). Eagles call these double points the **foci of the involution** and he proves that these points lie on the chord joining the touchpoints of the inconic with :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`. Analogously, let :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` be the double points of the involution {:g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`} and {P, Q}. These points lie on the chord joining the touchpoints of the inconic with :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Take any point obtained in 2), for example :g:`B_{i} <B_i>`\ =\ :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, and any point obtained in 3), for example :g:`C_{j} <C_j>`\ =\ :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, and let :g:`H_{a} <H_a>` be the :g:`A' <A'>`-harmonic mean of (:g:`B_{i} <B_i>`, :g:`C_{j} <C_j>`). (See preamble just before X_59294) The line :g:`AH_{a} <[ A H_a ]>` cuts :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` at :g:`A* <A*>`, which is the touchpoint of the desired inconic with the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Then, from 2) and 3), the other touchpoints of the inconic are :g:`B* <B*>` = :g:`A* <A*>`\ :g:`B_{i} <B_i>`\ ∩\ :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` and :g:`C* <C*>` = :g:`A* <A*>`\ :g:`C_{j} <C_j>`\ ∩\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`. Now we have either five points on the conic or can get the perspector of the inconic; then the conic is unambigously determined. Repeat 4) and 5) with the other possible combinations of :g:`B_{i} <B_i>` and :g:`C_{j} <C_j>` and, finally, four conics are found, all touching the given lines and passing through the given points.

  Some remarks are needed here: The above construction was made by starting from :g:`A' <A'>`. If we start from :g:`B' <B'>` or :g:`C' <C'>`, the same set of inconics is obtained in each case. If P, Q are both interior to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then the four inconics are ellipses, but if they are both exterior to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then the resulting inconics can be of mixed types, i.e., some of them can be ellipses and some of them can be hyperbolas. Eagles does not mention this plurality in problem 112. When P, Q are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` or when they are a bicentric pair, it can be conjectured that just one out of the four inconics is a central inconic, which means that its perspector and center are both triangle centers. Also, it can be conjectured that the two triads of perspectors and centers of the remaining non-central inconics are, respectively, vertices of two :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>`. It is necessary to examine which combination of :g:`B_{i} <B_i>` and :g:`C_{j} <C_j>` leads to the central inconic, because the required combination depends on the relative positions of :g:`P <P>` and Q.

  | The appearance of (i, j, m, n) in the following list means that the central inellipse through X_i and X_j has perspector X(m) and center X_n: (1, 2, 59437, 59438), (1, 6, 59439, 59440), (1, 7, 59441, 59442), (1, 8, 59443, 59444), (1, 31, 765, 24036), (1, 32, 59445, 59446), (2, 3, 59447, 59448)\ :sup:`\*`, (2, 6, 1016, 4422), (2, 7, 59449, 59450), (2, 8, 55339, 59451), (2, 31, 59452, 59453), (2, 32, 4590, 620), (3, 4, 55346, 15252)\ :sup:`\*`, (7, 8, 4998, 3035), (7, 55, 59457, 59458), (7, 56, 4998, 3035), (8, 55, 4076, 3039), (8, 56, 4998, 3035), (31, 32, 59455, 59456), (55, 56, 59, 13006)
  | :sup:`(\*)`: For acute :g:`ABC << A B C >>` only. This fact guarantees that :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` are interior to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Note that all the other centers X_i, X_j used in this list are always interior to any acute or obtuse triangle.

  The inellipse through the Brocard points (PU(1)) has perspector X_52205 and center X_59454. The inellipse through their :term:`isotomic conjugates <isotomic-conjugate>`, PU(11), has perspector X_40098 and center X_26582.

  A general expression for the perspectors of these inconics can be seen **here** (``X(59437).pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0814:

* **X_59459**–**X_59483** — **Lateral-inconics and related triangles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 8, 2023. Continuing from the preamble just before X_59437, consider the three non-central inconics of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` passing through two given centers U, X.

  Ordered properly, these inconics seem to be related each to one vertex of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`T_{p} <T_p>` be the triangle with vertices in the perspectors of the lateral inconics of (U, X) and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` the triangle with vertices on their centers.

  | The appearance of (i, j, m, n) in the following list means that, if X_i, X_j are the given centers on the inconics, then the perspector (:g:`T_{p} <T_p>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`) is X(m) and the perspector (:g:`T_{c} <T_c>`, medial-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) is X_n: (1, 2, 59459, 59460), (1, 6, 59461, 59462), (1, 7, 59463, 59464), (1, 8, 59465, 59466), (1, 55, 59467, 59468), (1, 56, 59469, 59470), (2, 6, 1509, 17045), (2, 7, 59471, 59472), (2, 8, 59473, 59474), (7, 8, 6063, 2886), (7, 55, 59475, 59476), (7, 56, 552, 59477), (8, 55, 261, 4999), (8, 56, 59478, 59479), (55, 56, 7, 1), (3, 4, 59482, 59483)\ :sup:`\*`

For Brocard points PU(1), perspectors (:g:`T_{p} <T_p>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`), (:g:`T_{c} <T_c>`, medial-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) are X_59480, X_59481, respectively. For :term:`isotomic conjugates <isotomic-conjugate>` of Brocard points, PU(11), perspectors (:g:`T_{p} <T_p>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>`), (:g:`T_{c} <T_c>`, medial-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>`) are X_40099, X_26558, respectively.

  A list of coordinates of A-vertices for each :g:`T_{p} <T_p>`, :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` treated in this section can be seen **here** (``X(59459).pdf``).

.. _guide-preamble-0815:

* **X_59829**–**X_59993** — **Centers of orthogonal circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 22, 2023. .LI li{padding-bottom:12px;} *Given a circle Ω and two points :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>` not lying on a diameter of Ω, there exists an unique circle* Ω\ :sup:`⟂` *through :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` and orthogonal to Ω*.

  This circle is denoted here Ω\ :sup:`⟂`\ (P, Q). Its center is the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of :g:`PP' <[ P P' ]>` and :g:`QQ' <[ Q Q' ]>`, where :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`Q' <Q'>` are the inverses of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>` in Ω. Take in account that, when a point P approaches to Ω, the perpendicular bisector of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`P' <P'>` approaches to the tangent to Ω at :g:`P <P>`.

  *Given a circle Ω, a line 𝓁 not passing through the center of Ω, and a point :g:`P <P>` on 𝓁, there exists an unique circle* Ω\ :sup:`⟂` *orthogonal to Ω and tangent to 𝓁 at :g:`P* <P*>`.

  This circle is denoted here Ω\ :sup:`⟂`\ (𝓁, P). Its center is the intersection of the perpendicular to 𝓁 through :g:`P <P>` and the perpendicular bisector of :g:`P <P>` and its inverse :g:`P' <P'>` in Ω.

.. _preambles-part-31:

Part 31

.. _guide-preamble-0816:

* **X_60343**–**X_60352** — **Points associated with hyperbolas**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 3, 2023. Let :g:`H <H>` be a hyperbola. Let W be the center of :g:`H <H>`, and let :g:`L <L>` and :g:`L' <L'>` be the asymptotes of H. There exists a unique hyperbola :g:`H' <H'>` other than H that has center W and asymptotes L and :g:`L' <L'>`. The hyperbola :g:`H' <H'>` is the called the **conjugate** of H. If H is a circumhyperbola and L is given by

  u x + v y + w z = 0,

  then :g:`L' <L'>` is given by

  v w x + w u y + u v z = 0.

  The hyperbola H is given by u(v - w)^2 y z + (cyclic) = 0, with center u(v^2 - w^2) : : and perspector u(v - w)^2 y z : : .

  The conjugate hyperbola :g:`H' <H'>` is given by u(v+w)^2 y z + (cyclic) + 2 u v w (x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = 0, with center u(v^2 - w^2) : : and perspector

  u\*(v - w)\*(3\*u\*v + v^2 + u\*w + 3\*v\*w)\*(u\*v + 3\*u\*w + 3\*v\*w + w^2) : : .

  **Example 1. H = Kiepert hyperbola**

  Center of :g:`H <H>` and :g:`H' <H'>`: :ref:`X_115 <X_115>`

  Asymptotes, L and :g:`L' <L'>`, are the lines u x + v y + w z = 0, where :math:`u:v:w` = X_30508 and :math:`u:v:w` = X_30509.

  Equation for :g:`H <H>`: (b^2 - c^2) b y + (cyclic) = 0

  Equation for :g:`H' <H'>`: 2\*((a^2 - b^2)^3\*x\*y + (-a^2 + c^2)^3\*x\*z + (b^2 - c^2)^3\*y\*z) - (a^2 - b^2)\*(a^2 - c^2)\*(b^2 - c^2)\*(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = 0

  The point X_i lies on :g:`H' <H'>` for these i: 3413, 3414, 39107, 39108. The perspector of :g:`H' <H'>` is X_9293.

  **Example 2. H = Jerabek hyperbola**

  Center of :g:`H <H>` and :g:`H' <H'>`: :ref:`X_125 <X_125>`

  Asymptotes, L and :g:`L' <L'>`, are the lines u x + v y + w z = 0, where :math:`u:v:w` = X_50944 and :math:`u:v:w` = X_50945.

  Equation for :g:`H <H>`: a^2(b^2 - c^2)SA y z + (cyclic) = 0

  Equation for :g:`H' <H'>`: 2\*(a^2\*b^2\*(a^2 - b^2)^3\*(-a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*x\*y + a^2\*c^2\*(-a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(-a^2 + c^2)^3\*x\*z + b^2\*c^2\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*(b^2 - c^2)^3\*y\*z) - (a^2 - b^2)\*(a^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*(b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = 0

  The point X_i lies on :g:`H' <H'>` for these i: 2574, 2575. The perspector of :g:`H' <H'>` is X_60478.

  **Example 3. H = Feuerbach hyperbola**

  Center of :g:`H <H>` and :g:`H' <H'>`: :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`

  Asymptotes, L and :g:`L' <L'>`, are the lines u x + v y + w z = 0, where :math:`u:v:w` = X_60476 and :math:`u:v:w` = X_60477.

  Equation for :g:`H <H>`: a(b - c)(b + c - a) y z + (cyclic) = 0

  Equation for :g:`H' <H'>`: 2\*(a\*(a - b)^3\*b\*(a + b - c)\*x\*y + a\*c\*(-a + c)^3\*(a - b + c)\*x\*z + b\*(b - c)^3\*c\*(-a + b + c)\*y\*z) + (a - b)\*(b - c)\*(a + b - c)\*(-a + c)\*(a - b + c)\*(-a + b + c)\*(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) = 0

  The point X_i passes through :g:`H' <H'>` for these i: 3307, 3308. The perspector of :g:`H' <H'>` is X_42552.

  Starting with a line :g:`L <L>`, the **L-asymptotic circumhyperbola** is the hyperbola that passes through the vertices :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>` and has L as an asymptote. (Further examples are omitted here.]

.. _guide-preamble-0817:

* **X_60353**–**X_60475** — **Common point of radical axes**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 5, 2023. *Let ω be a circle and P, Q two distinct fixed points, none on ω. Then the radical axes of ω and all the circles through :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` have a common point* X(ω, P, Q).

  The pencil or set of circles through :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>` is denoted here OO(P, Q).

  Some properties: .LI li{padding-bottom:12px;} The common point X(ω, P, Q) lies on the line :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>`. Therefore, it is the intersection of this line with the radical axis of ω and any chosen circle in O(P, Q). A very simple proof of this fact can be seen **here** (``X60353.pdf``). X(ω, P, Q) is the radical center of ω and any pair of circles in O(P,Q). When P, Q and the center of ω are not collinear, X(ω, P, Q) = :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`P'Q' <[ P' Q' ]>`, where :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`Q' <Q'>` are the respective inverses of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>` in ω. If :g:`P <P>` or :g:`Q <Q>` is the center of ω then X(ω, P, Q) is the inverse of the other in ω. If ω is the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` then X(ω, P, Q) concides with the Vu (P,Q)-circle point (see preamble just before X_38458). If ω is the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`P <P>` or :g:`Q <Q>` is the centroid :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, then X(ω, P, Q) coincides with the Vu pole of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` (see preamble just before X_37756).

.. _guide-preamble-0818:

* **X_60530**–**X_60551** — **Dao-Lozada circum-bicevian-perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 10, 2023. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle with circumcircle ω. Let :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` be two interior points to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` their respective :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>`. Denote :math:`a_{t}` the circle through :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>` tangent to ω at :g:`A_{t} <A_t>`, with :g:`A_{t} <A_t>` lying on the arc :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` of ω not containing A. Define :math:`b_{t}`, :g:`B_{t} <B_t>`, :math:`c_{t}`, :g:`C_{t} <C_t>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA_{t} <[ A A_t ]>`, :g:`BB_{t} <[ B B_t ]>`, :g:`CC_{t} <[ C C_t ]>` concur at a point Q(:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`). (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>`, November 6, 2023).

  The point Q(:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) is named here the **Dao-Lozada circum-bicevian-perspector of P' and P"**.

  If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x' : y' : z'` and :g:`P″ <P″>` = x" : y" : z" (barycentrics), then :g:`A_{t} <A_t>` = -a^2/(c\*Y + b\*Z) : b/Z : c/Y and Q(:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) = a\*X : b\*Y : c\*Z where :g:`X <X>` = :math:`\sqrt{x'*x"}`, Y = :math:`\sqrt{y'*y"}`, Z = :math:`\sqrt{z'*z"}`.

  In general, the above concurrence does not occur for the second circles through the traces of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, tangent to ω and touching it at points on its positive arcs.

  The appearance of (i, j, k) in the following list means that Q(X_i, X_j) = X_k: (1, 2, 365), (1, 6, 18753), (1, 7, 266), (1, 8, 259), (1, 9, 60530), (1, 10, 60531), (1, 11, 60532), (1, 12, 60533), (2, 6, 6), (2, 7, 509), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0819:

* **X_60552**–**X_60564** — **Circumtangential-bicevian-perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 10, 2023. Continuing with the construction and notations in the previous section (see preamble just before X_60530), let :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` be the triangle bounded by the tangent lines to ω at :g:`A_{t} <A_t>`, :g:`B_{t} <B_t>`, :g:`C_{t} <C_t>`. Then :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector :g:`Q* <Q*>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`).

  This new perspector is referred here as the **circumtangential-bicevian-perspector of P' and P"**. Corresponding barycentrics coordinates are: :g:`A* <A*>` = -a\*(2\*b\*c\*X^2 + a\*(a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` + b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` + c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`)) : b^2\*(a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` + b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` - c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`) : c^2\*(a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` - b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` + c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`) and :g:`Q* <Q*>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) = a^2/(-a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` + b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` + c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`) : b^2/(a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` - b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` + c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`) : c^2/(a\*\ :g:`Y*Z <[ Y* Z ]>` + b\*\ :g:`Z*X <[ Z* X ]>` - c\*\ :g:`X*Y <[ X* Y ]>`)

  The circumtangential-bicevian-perspector of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>` results to be the U-:term:`vertex conjugate <vertex-conjugate>` of-U, where U is the Dao-Lozada-circum-bicevian perspector of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>` explained in the previous section.

.. _guide-preamble-0820:

* **X_60603**–**X_60611** — **Points associated with the Neuberg-Gibert hyperbola**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, November 14, 2023, based on notes about "hyperbola (P)" in :person:`Bernard Gibert <bernard-gibert>`'s webpage, `K001, the Neuberg cubic <http://bernard-gibert.fr/Exemples/k001.html>`__. Gibert's notes include the following: (P) is a very remarkable hyperbola passing through :ref:`X_476 <X_476>` and the vertices of the circumtangential triangle :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>`. It has two asymptotes making an angle of 60 degrees, so that its eccentricity is 2. :ref:`X_110 <X_110>` is one of its foci and the related directrix is the Euler line. The tangent at :ref:`X_476 <X_476>` is the real asymptote of the Neuberg cubic. The hyperbola (P) is here named the Neuberg-Gibert hyperbola. Associated :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` include the following:

  | X_60603 = center
  | X_60604 = focus, other than :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`
  | Pass-through points: :ref:`X_476 <X_476>` and X_i for these i: 60605, 60606, 60607, 60608, 60609, 60610, 60611. The asmptotes meet the infinity line in PU(215).

.. _guide-preamble-0821:

* **X_60614**–**X_60737** — **Bicevian Chordal Triangles**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on November 18, 2023. Let (c) be the bicevian conic of :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :math:`u:v:w` and :g:`Q <Q>`\ =\ :math:`p:q:r` in barycentrics. Denote by Ap, Aq the intersection points of :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`AQ <[ A Q ]>` and (c), and similarly define Bp, Bq, Cp, and Cq. The lines ApAq, BpBq, and CpCq form a triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` which we call the **bicevian chordal triangle** of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` (wrt :g:`ABC << A B C >>`).
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` are perspective with center which lies on the circumconic through :g:`P <P>` and Q. We call this center the **bicevian chordal perspector** of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` (wrt :g:`ABC << A B C >>`).
  | A first barycentric coordinate is p\*u\*(r^2\*u\*v+2\*r\*(q\*u+p\*v)\*w+p\*q\*w^2)\*(p\*r\*v^2+q^2\*u\*w+2\*q\*v\*(r\*u+p\*w))
  | For details, see `Euclid 6040 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6040>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0822:

* **X_60742**–**X_60773** — **Centers of coaxial circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, November 25, 2023. *Given two non-concentric circles* 𝒞\ :sub:`1` *and* 𝒞\ :sub:`2` *and a point* P, *neither on any of the given circles nor on their radical axis, there exists an unique circle through* P *and coaxial with the given circles*. (A simple proof and a method for determining this circle can be seen **here** (``X(60742).pdf``).)

  Such circle is denoted here as Ω\ :sub:`x`\ (𝒞\ :sub:`1`, 𝒞\ :sub:`2`, P).

.. _guide-preamble-0823:

* **X_60788**–**X_60843** — **Chordal perspectors of bicevian conics and pedal circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 3, 2023. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` two distinc points, none on their sidelines, and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` their respective :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>` with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Call 𝒞 the bicevian conic of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>`.

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point on the line :g:`P'P″ <[ P' P″ ]>` and denote :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` the second intersections of 𝒞 and the lines :g:`PA' <[ P A' ]>`, :g:`PB' <[ P B' ]>`, :g:`PC' <[ P C' ]>`, respectively. Similarly, denote :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` the second intersections of 𝒞 and the lines :g:`PA″ <[ P A″ ]>`, :g:`PB″ <[ P B″ ]>`, :g:`PC″ <[ P C″ ]>`, respectively. Then the lines :g:`AA_{1} <[ A A_1 ]>`, :g:`BB_{1} <[ B B_1 ]>`, :g:`CC_{1} <[ C C_1 ]>` concur in a point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` and the lines :g:`AA_{2} <[ A A_2 ]>`, :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`, :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>` concur in a point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`.

  The point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` is denoted here the **(P', P")-bicevian conic chordal perspector of-P** whilst the point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>` is denoted as the **(P", P')-bicevian conic chordal perspector of-P**.

  **⬥ Pedal triangles version**

  Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`P' <P'>` a point not on their sidelines, :g:`P″ <P″>` the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` their respective :term:`pedal triangles <pedal-triangle>` with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Call 𝒞 the circle through :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`, :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`.

  Let :g:`P <P>` be a point on the line :g:`P'P″ <[ P' P″ ]>` and denote :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>` the second intersections of 𝒞 and the lines :g:`PA' <[ P A' ]>`, :g:`PB' <[ P B' ]>`, :g:`PC' <[ P C' ]>`, respectively. Similarly, denote :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` the second intersections of 𝒞 and the lines :g:`PA″ <[ P A″ ]>`, :g:`PB″ <[ P B″ ]>`, :g:`PC″ <[ P C″ ]>`, respectively. Then the lines :g:`AA_{1} <[ A A_1 ]>`, :g:`BB_{1} <[ B B_1 ]>`, :g:`CC_{1} <[ C C_1 ]>` concur in a point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` and the lines :g:`AA_{2} <[ A A_2 ]>`, :g:`BB_{2} <[ B B_2 ]>`, :g:`CC_{2} <[ C C_2 ]>` concur in a point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`.

  In this case, the point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>` is denoted here the **P'-pedal circle chordal perspector of-P** and, naturally, the point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>` is denoted as the **P"-pedal circle chordal perspector of-P**. In this notation, the term "pedal circle" may be replaced with the name of the circle, if it has a given name. Therefore, the (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`)-bicevian conic chordal perspector of-P coincides with the :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-nine-point circle chordal perspector of-P and the (:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`)-bicevian conic chordal perspector of-P coincides with the :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-nine-point circle chordal perspector of-P.

.. _guide-preamble-0824:

* **X_60877**–**X_61035** — **Points related to the Aguilera triangle**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Dec 11, 2023. In a scalene acute triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`M_{a}M_{b}M_{c} << M_a M_b M_c >>` be its :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`. Let ωa be the circle centered at :g:`M_{a} <M_a>` and passing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>`, and define ωb and ωc cyclically. Inside :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`O_{a} <O_a>` be center of the circle, closest to :g:`A <A>`, which is externally tangent to ωa and is inscribed in angle :g:`BAC << B A C >>`. Define :g:`O_{b} <O_b>` and :g:`O_{c} <O_c>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`O_{a}O_{b}O_{c} << O_a O_b O_c >>` is called the **(1st) Aguilera triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and has the following barycentrics of the :g:`A <A>`-vertex, derived by Manuel Aguilera: a\*(-a + b + c)\*(a + b + c) + 2\*(b + c)\*S : b\*((-a + b + c)\*(a + b + c) - 2\*S) : c\*((-a + b + c)\*(a + b + c) - 2\*S)
  | If a point P lies on line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` is orthologic to the Aguilera triangle and the orthology center lies on line :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`.
  | The triangle inverse-in-incircle of the Aguilera triangle is called here the **(1st) Aguilera-Pavlov** triangle.
  | Its :g:`A <A>`-vertex has the following barycentrics: S (b + c) + 2 a b c : b (-S + 2 b c ) : c (-S + 2 b c )
  | The centroid of the Aguilera-Pavlov triangle coincides with the incenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.
  | If a point P lies on line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, the pedal triangle of :g:`P <P>` is orthologic to the Aguilera-Pavlov triangle.

.. _guide-preamble-0825:

* **X_61103**–**X_61138** — **Orthoptic or director circles**

  :contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, January 11, 2024. Let 𝒞 be a conic and let ℒ be the locus of points from which the tangent lines to 𝒞 are perpendicular. ℒ is, in general, a circle centered at the center of 𝒞 and named the **orthoptic** or **director circle of 𝒞**.

  If 𝒞 is a parabola then ℒ degenerates to the directrix of 𝒞, and, if 𝒞 is a rectangular hyperbola, ℒ degenerates to the center of 𝒞.

  When 𝒞 is an ellipse with semiaxes 𝒶 and 𝒷 then its orthoptic circle has squared-radius ρ\ :sup:`2` = 𝒶\ :sup:`2` + 𝒷\ :sup:`2`. This means that, if 𝒞 is a circle with radius 𝓇, then its orthoptic circle has squared-radius ρ\ :sup:`2` = 2\*𝓇\ :sup:`2`.

  Finally, if 𝒞 is an hyperbola with semiaxes 𝒶 (focal) and 𝒷 then its orthoptic circle has squared-radius ρ\ :sup:`2` = 𝒶\ :sup:`2` - 𝒷\ :sup:`2`. Therefore, the orthoptic circle exists only when 𝒶 ≥ 𝒷.

  In *S.L. Loney, The Elements of Coordinate Geometry, 1962, pp 365, #390*, a general expression is deduced for calculating the equation of the director or orthoptic circle of a conic (in cartesian coordinates). Such expression, when applied to the conic given in barycentric as 𝒞 = Σ(:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`\ \*x^2 + 2\*\ :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`\ \*y\*z) = 0, leads to the following equation for the squared-radius of the orthoptic circle:

  ρ^2 = (∑(:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`\ \*\ :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`\ ^2)-:g:`F_{A} <F_A>`\ \*\ :g:`F_{B} <F_B>`\ \*\ :g:`F_{C} <F_C>`-2\*\ :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`\ \*\ :g:`G_{B} <G_B>`\ \*\ :g:`G_{C} <G_C>`)\*∑((:g:`F_{B} <F_B>`\ +\ :g:`F_{C} <F_C>`-2\*\ :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`)\*SA)/∑(:g:`F_{B} <F_B>`\ \*\ :g:`F_{C} <F_C>`-2\*\ :g:`F_{A} <F_A>`\ \*\ :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`-:g:`G_{A} <G_A>`\ ^2+2\*\ :g:`G_{B} <G_B>`\ \*\ :g:`G_{C} <G_C>`)^2 (all sums are cyclic)

.. _guide-preamble-0826:

* **X_61146**–**X_61151** — **Points associated with circles**

  contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` and :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, January 16, 2024. Suppose that n >= 2 and that S = {O(1), O(2), ... , O(n)} is a set of n circles with centers and radii o(1), r(1); o(2), r(2); ...; o(n),r(n), where the centers o(i) are normalized barycentric coordinates.

  Definition 1. The **centroid of S** is the point o(1) + o(2) + ... + o(n), this being a :term:`combo <combo>` as defined in the Introduction (in Part 1 of ETC).

  Definition 2. The **centroid of circumferences of S** is the point r(1)\*o(1) + r(2)\*o(2) + ... + r(n)\*o(n).

  Definition 3. The **centroid of curvatures of S** is the point o(1)/r(1) + o(2)/r(2) + ... + o(n)/r(n).

  Definition 4. The **centroid of areas of S** is the point o(1)\*r(1)^2 + o(2)\*r(2)^2 + ... + o(n)\*r(n)^2.

  . Definition 5. The **centroid of reciprocal areas of S** is the point o(1)/r(1)^2 + o(2)/r(2)^2 + ... + o(n)/r(n)^2.

  All five centroids are given by the form o(1)\*r(1)^n + o(2)\*r(2)^n) + ... + + o(n)\*r(n)^n, where n is one of the numbers -2, -1, 0, 1, 2. In the following examples, the centroids are indexed by n, from -2, to 2, with these designations: G(-2), G(-1), G(0), G(1), G(2).

  | **Examp1e 1: S = {incircle, circumcircle}**
  | G(-2) = X_8071
  | G(-1) = :ref:`X_55 <X_55>`
  | G(0) = :ref:`X_1385 <X_1385>` G(1) = X_61146
  | G(2) = X_61147

  [Further examples are omittted here.]

.. _guide-preamble-0827:

* **X_61152**–**X_61297** — **and X_61244-X_61297, Miyamoto Perspectors**

  submitted by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, January 20, 2024, based on notes from Keita Miyamoto . Barycentrics for Miyamoto perspectors were found by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be a triangle homothetic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` at :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` with ratio k. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`\ =\ :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` cyclically. Let :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`\ =\ :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`, and define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. Let (I), (:g:`I_{a} <I_a>`), (:g:`I_{b} <I_b>`), (:g:`I_{c} <I_c>`) be the incircles of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`A'B_{c}C_{b} << A' B_c C_b >>`, :g:`B'C_{a}A_{c} << B' C_a A_c >>`, :g:`C'A_{b}B_{a} << C' A_b B_a >>`, respectively. Then there exists a circle (O(k)) tangent to all four circles, (I), (:g:`I_{a} <I_a>`), (:g:`I_{b} <I_b>`), (:g:`I_{c} <I_c>`). The touchpoint of (I) and (O(k)) is the Feuerbach point, :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`. Further, let :g:`T_{a} <T_a>` be the touchpoint of (:g:`I_{a} <I_a>`) and (O(k)), and define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` cyclically. The lines :g:`AT_{a} <[ A T_a ]>`, :g:`BT_{b} <[ B T_b ]>`, :g:`CT_{c} <[ C T_c ]>` concur in a point here named the Miyamoto (k)-perspector.

  Likewise, if :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is homothetic to an arbitrary triangle :g:`T <T>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` with ratio k, then the above construction yields a point here named named the (T,k)-Miyamoto perspector. Fifty-four (:term:`Euler triangle <euler-triangle>`, k)-Miyamoto perspectors, found by Peter Moses, are indexed at X_61244-X_61297.

  The points X_61152-X(61159 lie on the line :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`, and X_21244-X_61297 lie on :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`.

  The appearance of (k,X_i) in the following list means that X_i = Miyamoto (k)-perspector.

  (-5/6,61260), (-4/5,61261), (-3/4,61262), (-2/3,61263), (-3/5,61264), (-3/7,61265), (-2/5,61266), (-3/8,61267), (-2/7,61268), (-1/4,61269),

.. _guide-preamble-0828:

* **X_61301**–**X_61418** — **Vertex Square Sum and Product**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Jan 31, 2024. Given a reference triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, for any :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>` :g:`XYZ << X Y Z >>` the barycentric sum X^2+Y^2+Z^2 is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`. We call this expression the **vertex square sum** of :g:`XYZ << X Y Z >>`. A curious example is that the vertex square sum of the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of a point :g:`P <P>` is P^2. Some other examples: The vertex square sum of the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` is X_23653. The vertex square sum of the :term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>` is :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`. The vertex square sum of the :term:`1st Brocard triangle <1st-brocard-triangle>` is :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. The vertex square sum of the Moses-Soddy triangle is :ref:`X_1086 <X_1086>`. The vertex square sum of the Soddy triangle is :ref:`X_279 <X_279>`. The vertex square sum of the Pelletier triangle is X_14936. The vertex square sum of the Schroeter triangle is :ref:`X_115 <X_115>`. We call the barycentric product :g:`X*Y*Z << X* Y* Z >>` the **vertex product** of :g:`XYZ << X Y Z >>`. Note that the vertex product of the anticevian triangle of a point :g:`P <P>` is P^3.

.. _guide-preamble-0829:

* **X_61747**–**X_61761** — **Reflected-parallels circles**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 27, 2024. The following problem by C. Pohoata is published in `AOPS <https://artofproblemsolving.com/community/c6t48f6h1680386_reflections_of_3_parallel_lines_on_sides_of_triangles_incenter_locus>`__: Three parallel lines :math:`p_{a}`, :math:`p_{b}`, :math:`p_{c}` pass through the vertices of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Their reflections in :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively, form a triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`. Find the locus of the incenters of such triangles.

  When :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is acute, the required locus is a circle centered at the circumcenter :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:g:`ABC << A B C >>` and having radius ρ = 2\*R. But, as a matter of fact, similar constructions with centers X_n, for 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000, result each in a circle as locus (conjectured and not formally proven yet, but numerically tested). The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that the locus of centers X_i-of-:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is a circle with center X_j wrt :g:`ABC << A B C >>`: (1, 3), (2, 61747), (3, 156), (4, 9927), (5, 13406), (6, 61748), (7, 34507), (8, 22802), (9, 34117), (10, 61749), (11, 5), (12, 61750), (20, 61751), (21, 10274), (35, 1614), (36, 110), (40, 32139), (46, 11441), (55, 61752), (56, 61753), (57, 15068), (65, 5876), (79, 2888), (80, 4), (84, 58726), (90, 2904), (100, 6759), (101, 61754), (104, 1147), (105, 61755), (108, 61756), (109, 61757), (110, 61758), (113, 61759), (117, 61760), (118, 61761), (119, 15761), (149, 18381), (177, 5694), (191, 17824), (214, 10282), (238, 1576), (354, 15067), (355, 44279), (496, 49673), (551, 10182), (942, 11591), (946, 5449), (954, 19127), (960, 41589)

  The locus of X_i-of-:g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is denoted here as the **reflected-parallels circle of X(i)**. It must be taken in account that the given results are valid as long as :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is acute.

* **X_62249**–**X_62265** — **Tran-Lozada perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 16, 2024. The following two assertions, slightly modified, are proposed by Tran Viet Hung in `Romantics of geometry <https://www.facebook.com/groups/parmenides52/permalink/7312370985543211/>`__, March 15, 2023:

  1) Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` two distinct points and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` their respective circumcevian triangles, such that :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`A″ <A″>` are in the same side with respect to the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and similarly :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C' <C'>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`. Let (a\*) be the circle through :g:`A' <A'>` and :g:`A″ <A″>` tangent to sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, with center closer to the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Let :g:`A_{t} <A_t>` be the touchpoint of (a\*) and :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B_{t} <B_t>`, :g:`C_{t} <C_t>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA_{t} <[ A A_t ]>`, :g:`BB_{t} <[ B B_t ]>`, :g:`CC_{t} <[ C C_t ]>` are concurrent in a point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`).

  | The point of concurrence :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) is named here the **Tran-Lozada bi-circumcevian perspector of P and P'**. If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x' : y' : z'` and :g:`P″ <P″>` = x" : y" : z" (barycentrics), then :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) = :math:`\sqrt{x' x"}`/a : :math:`\sqrt{y' y"}`/b : :math:`\sqrt{z' z"}`/c. From here, it is clear than :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` must be both interior to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` in order :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`) to be real. The barycentric coordinates of the center :g:`A* <A*>` of (a\*) are:
  | :g:`A* <A*>` = a^2\*(2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{y'*y"*z'*z"}`\ \*SA-(y'\*z"+y"\*z')\*b\*c) : (2\*S^2\*c^2\*y'\*y"+((y'\*z"+y"\*z')\*c\*SC+2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{y'*y"*z'*z"}`\ \*b\*SB)\*b^3)/b^2 : (2\*S^2\*b^2\*z'\*z"+((y'\*z"+y"\*z')\*b\*SB+2\*\ :math:`\sqrt{y'*y"*z'*z"}`\ \*c\*SC)\*c^3)/c^2

  The appearance of (i, j, k) in the folowing list means that :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (X_i, X_j) = X_k:

  (1, 2, 18297), (1, 6, 366), (1, 31, 1), (1, 32, 365), (1, 75, 75), (1, 76, 62249), [and others].

  2) Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle with circumcircle (O), :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P_{o} <P_o>` two points, :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`A_{o}B_{o}C_{o} << A_o B_o C_o >>` the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`. Let (a\*) be the circle through :g:`A_{o} <A_o>` and tangent to sideline :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` at :g:`A' <A'>`. Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the second intersection of (O) and (a\*) and build :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, :g:`BB″ <[ B B″ ]>`, :g:`CC″ <[ C C″ ]>` are concurrent in a point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`).

  :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`) is named here the Tran-Lozada perspector of :term:`cevian <cevian>`-of-:g:`P' <P'>` and circumcevian-of-:g:`P_{o} <P_o>`. If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x' : y' : z'` and :g:`P_{o} <P_o>` =\ :math:`x_{o} : y_{o} : z_{o}` (barycentrics), then :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`) = (a\*x')^2/:math:`x_{o}` : (b\*y')^2/:math:`y_{o}` : (c\*z')^2/:math:`z_{o}`.

  The appearance of (i, j, k) in the folowing list means that :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (X_i, X_j) = X_k, for (i, j) ≤ 8:

  (1, 1, 31), (1, 2, 32), (1, 3, 25), (1, 4, 184), (1, 5, 54034), (1, 6, 6), (1, 7, 2175), (1, 8, 1397), (2, 1, 1), (2, 2, 6), (2, 3, 4), (2, 4, 3), (2, 5, 54), (2, 6, 2), (2, 7, 55), (2, 8, 56), [and others].
