* **X_62266**–**X_62278** — **Tran-Lozada CCO- and OOC- perspectors**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 18, 2024. The following two assertions, slightly modified, are proposed by Tran Viet Hung in `Romantics of geometry <https://www.facebook.com/groups/parmenides52/permalink/7325080894272220/>`__, March 17, 2023:

  1) Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle with circumcircle (O), :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, :g:`P_{o} <P_o>` three points, with :g:`P' <P'>` ≠ :g:`P″ <P″>`, and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, and :g:`A_{o}B_{o}C_{o} << A_o B_o C_o >>` the circumcevian triangle of :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`. Let :g:`A_{s} <A_s>` be the second intersection of circles (O) and (:g:`A'A″ <[ A' A″ ]>`:g:`A_{o} <A_o>`), and build :g:`B_{s} <B_s>`, :g:`C_{s} <C_s>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA_{s} <[ A A_s ]>`, :g:`BB_{s} <[ B B_s ]>`, :g:`CC_{s} <[ C C_s ]>` are concurrent in a point :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`; :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`).

  The point of concurrence :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`; :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`) is named here the Tran-Lozada CCO-perspector of (:g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`P″ <P″>`; :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`). If :g:`P' <P'>` =\ :math:`x' : y' : z'`, :g:`P″ <P″>` = x" : y" : z" and :g:`P_{o} <P_o>` =\ :math:`x_{o}: y_{o} : z_{o}` (barycentrics), then :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (:g:`P' <P'>`,\ :g:`P″ <P″>`; :g:`P_{o} <P_o>`) = a^2 x' x"/:math:`x_{o}` : b^2 y' y"/:math:`y_{o}` : c^2 z' z"/:math:`z_{o}`.

  The appearance of (i, j, k, n) in the folowing list means that :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`\ (X_i, X_j; X_k ) = X_n, for (i, j, k) ≤ 6:

  (1, 2, 1, 6), (1, 3, 1, 184), (1, 4, 1, 25), (1, 5, 1, 51), (1, 6, 1, 32), [and others].

  2) Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, :g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`, :g:`P_{i} <P_i>` three points with :g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>` ≠ :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`, :g:`A'_{o}B'_{o}C'_{o} << A'_o B'_o C'_o >>`, :g:`A″ <A″>`:sub:`o`\ :g:`B″ <B″>`:sub:`o`\ :g:`C″ <C″>`:sub:`o` the circumcevian triangles of :g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>` and :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`, respectively, and :g:`A_{i}B_{i}C_{i} << A_i B_i C_i >>` the cevian triangle of :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`. Let :g:`A_{s} <A_s>` be the second intersection of the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and the circle (:g:`A'_{o}A <[ A'_o A ]>`":sub:`o`\ :g:`A_{i} <A_i>`) and build :g:`B_{s} <B_s>`, :g:`C_{s} <C_s>` cyclically. Then the lines :g:`AA_{s} <[ A A_s ]>`, :g:`BB_{s} <[ B B_s ]>`, :g:`CC_{s} <[ C C_s ]>` are concurrent in a point :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`; :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`).

  :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`; :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`) is named here the Tran-Lozada OOC-perspector of (:g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`; :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`). If :g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>` =\ :math:`x'_{o} : y'_{o} : z'_{o}`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o` = x":sub:`o` : y":sub:`o` : z":sub:`o`, :g:`P_{i} <P_i>` =\ :math:`x_{i} : y_{i} : z_{i}` (barycentrics), then :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (:g:`P'_{o} <P'_o>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`:sub:`o`; :g:`P* <P*>`) = x':sub:`o` x":sub:`o`/(a^2\* :math:`x_{i})` : y':sub:`o` y":sub:`o`/(b^2 :math:`y_{i})` : z':sub:`o` z":sub:`o`/(c^2 :math:`z_{i})`.

  The appearance of (i, j, k, n) in the folowing list means that :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`\ (X_i, X_j; X_k ) = X_n, for (i, j, k) ≤ 6:

  Note added by César E. Lozada on March 10, 2025:

  The steps for finding CCO(U, V; W) and OOC(U, V; W) allow the geometric construction of points algebraically defined, as the barycentric and trilinear product or quotient of two points.

  Suppose that two points :g:`U_{1} <U_1>` and :g:`U_{2} <U_2>` are given. It can be easily proved that: .LI li{padding-bottom:8px; before.content: counter(list, decimal) ") "; } barycentric product :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`\ \*\ :g:`U_{2} <U_2>` = CCO(:g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`; :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` ) = OOC(:g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`; :ref:`X_76 <X_76>` ) barycentric quotient :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`/:g:`U_{2} <U_2>` = CCO(:ref:`X_76 <X_76>`, :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`; :g:`U_{2} <U_2>` ) = OOC(:ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`; :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`) trilinear product :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`\ \*\ :g:`U_{2} <U_2>` = CCO(:g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`; :ref:`X_31 <X_31>` ) = OOC(:g:`U_{1} <U_1>`, :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`; :ref:`X_75 <X_75>`) trilinear quotient :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`/:g:`U_{2} <U_2>` = CCO(:ref:`X_75 <X_75>`, :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`; :g:`U_{2} <U_2>` ) = OOC(:ref:`X_31 <X_31>`, :g:`U_{1} <U_1>`; :g:`U_{2} <U_2>`)

* **X_62280**–**X_62286** — **Seven-circles points**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 21, 2024.The following theorem appears in C. J. A. Evelyn, G. B. Money-Coutts, J. A. Tyrrell, *The seven circles theorem and other new theorems*, Great Britain, 1974:

  Let (:g:`A' <A'>`), (:g:`B' <B'>`), (:g:`C' <C'>`) be three circles externally tangent (or internally tangent) to a circle (O), and touching this at :g:`A_{1} <A_1>`, :g:`B_{1} <B_1>`, :g:`C_{1} <C_1>`, respectively. Let (:g:`A″ <A″>`) be the circle externally tangent to (:g:`B' <B'>`), (:g:`C' <C'>`), and externally tangent to (O) (or internally tangent to (O), but with center :g:`A″ <A″>` in the side of :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>` not containing :g:`A' <A'>`), touching (O) at :g:`A_{2} <A_2>`, and define (:g:`B″ <B″>`), (:g:`C″ <C″>`), :g:`B_{2} <B_2>`, :g:`C_{2} <C_2>` cyclically. Then, whenever the seven circles can be built, the lines :g:`A_{1}A_{2} <[ A_1 A_2 ]>`, :g:`B_{1}B_{2} <[ B_1 B_2 ]>`, :g:`C_{1}C_{2} <[ C_1 C_2 ]>` concur. (See figure **here** (``.\X(62280).jpg``))

  The points of concurrence :g:`Q_{e} <Q_e>` (or :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>`) for both cases are denoted here as the **external** (or **internal**) **seven circles point of circles (A'), (B'), (C')**.

  The appearance of (Γ, i, j) in the following list means that the external- and internal- seven circles points of circles Γ are X_i and X_j, respectively:

  (excircles, 62280, 62281), (excosine, 6221, 6398), [and others].

* **X_62489**–**X_62510** — **Infinity bisectors**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 5, 2024. Let :g:`O <X_3>` denote the circumcenter, (O) the circumcircle, and L the line at infinity. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u:v:w` are points on (O) and that P, O, U are noncollinear. Let :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` be the tangent to (O) at :g:`P <P>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` the tangent to (O) at U. Let :g:`D <D>` = :g:`L_{1} <L_1>`\ ∩\ :g:`L_{2} <L_2>` and M = OD∩L. As the line OM bisects the angle between :g:`L_{1} <L_1>` and :g:`L_{2} <L_2>`, the point M is here named the **(P,U)-infinity bisector**. Barycentrics for the (P,U)-infinity bisector are given by

  (:math:`a^{2}` - :math:`b^{2}` + :math:`c^{2})`\ (q u - p v) - (:math:`a^{2}` + :math:`b^{2}` - :math:`c^{2})`\ (r u - p w) - :math:`2a^{2}(r v - q w)` : :

  The appearance of {{i,j},k} in the following lists means that X_k = {X_i,X_j}-infinity bisector.

  {{74,98},542}, {{74,99},690}, {{74,100},8674}, {{74,101},2774}, {{74,102},2779}, {{74,103},2772}, {{74,104},2771}, {{74,105},2836}, {{74,106},2842}, {{74,107},9033}, {{74,108},2850}, {{74,109},2773}, {{74,110},526}, {{74,111},2854}, {{74,112},9517}, {{74,476},523}, {{74,477},30},

.. _guide-preamble-0836:

* **X_62500**–**X_63224** — **and X_62721-X_62733 and X_63216-X_63224, Centers associated with unary operations**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 2024.

  A unary operation on homogeneous coordinates :math:`x : y : z` (barycentric or trilinear) is a mapping that takes the point :math:`x:y:z` to the point f(:math:`x:y:z`} : f(y,z,x) : f(z,x,y) for some homoeneous function f. Introduced here are several examples:

  | u\ :sub:`1`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y-z)/x : (z-x)/y : (x-y)/z
  | u\ :sub:`2`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = x/(y-z) : y/(z-x) : z/(x-y)
  | u\ :sub:`3`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (-2x+y+z)/x : (-2y+z+x)/y : (-2z+x+y)/z
  | u\ :sub:`4`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = x/(-2x+y+z) : y/(-2y+z+x) : z/(-2z+x+y)
  | u\ :sub:`5`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y-z)/(y+z) : (z-x)/(z+x) : (x-y)/(x+y)
  | u\ :sub:`6`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y+z)/(y-z) : (z+x)/(z-x) : (x+y)/(x-y)
  | u\ :sub:`7`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (-2x+y+z)/(y+z) : (-2y+z+x)/(z+x) : (-2z+x+y)/(x+y)
  | u\ :sub:`8`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y+z)/(-2x+y+z) : (z+x)/(-2y+z+x) : (x+y)/(-2z+x+y)
  | u\ :sub:`9`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (yz-zx-xy)/(y^2-z^2) : (zx-xy-yz)/(z^2-x^2) : (xy-yz-zx)/(x^2-y^2)
  | u\ :sub:`10`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y^2-z^2)/(yz-zx-xy) : (z^2-x^2)/(zx-xy-yz) : (x^2-y^2)/(xy-yz-zx)
  | u\ :sub:`11`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (yz-zx-xy)/(y^2+z^2) : (zx-xy-yz)/(z^2+x^2) : (xy-yz-zx)/(x^2+y^2)
  | u\ :sub:`12`\ (:math:`x:y:z`) = (y^2+z^2)/(yz-zx-xy) : (z^2+x^2)/(zx-xy-yz) : (x^2y^2)/(xy-yz-zx)

  In that list above, the 12 unary operations are indexed so that for n = 1,2,3,4,5,6, :math:`u_{2n}(X)` is the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :math:`u_{2n-1}(X)` when the coordinates are barycentric, and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` when the coordinates are trilinear. In addition to the notations "u\ :sub:`n`\ (:math:`x:y:z`)" and ":math:`u_{n}(X)`" the notation "unary(n) of :g:`X″ <X″>` will be useful. In the naming of :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` "unary(n) of :g:`X″ <X″>` is used when the underlying coordinates are barycentric, and "trilinear unary(n) of :g:`X″ <X″>` when the coordinates of trilinear. For examples of such points, see X(63202-X_63205 and X_62734-X_62750.

  In the next table, column 1 represents the triangle centers :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, ..., :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`. The appearance of k in (row r, column n) means that :math:`u_{r}`\ (X_n) = X_k. In this table, it is assumed that the coordinates used to define the unary operations are barycentric coordinates. [Table omitted here.)

  In the next table, column 1 represents the triangle centers :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, ..., :ref:`X_11 <X_11>`. The appearance of k in (row r, column n) means that :math:`u_{r}`\ (X_n) = X_k. Here it is assumed that the coordinates used to define the unary operations are trilinear coordinates. [Table omitted here.]

.. _guide-preamble-0837:

* **X_62770**–**X_63195** — **Perspectors related to PTC triangles**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on April 26, 2024. For a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and arbitrary points :g:`P <P>`, :g:`Q <Q>`, and R not on its sides, let :g:`A' <A'>` be the intersection of :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` and the perpendicular through :g:`Q <Q>` to :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and similarly define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>`. Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the intersection of :g:`RA' <[ R A' ]>` and :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` and similarly define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>`. Below, we denote with **PTC(P,Q,R)** the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`. If P, Q, and R are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` then PTC(P,Q,R) is a :term:`central triangle <central-triangle>`.

  If in barycentrics :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :math:`u:v:w`, :g:`Q <Q>`\ =\ :math:`p:q:r`, and R=\ :math:`l:m:n` then the :g:`A <A>`-vertex of PTC(P,Q,R) is

  0 : (b^2 - c^2) (-l (q + r) v + m p (v + w)) - a^2 ((l (-q + r) + m (p + 2 r)) v - m (p + 2 q) w) : (b^2 - c^2) (-l (q + r) w + n p (v + w)) - a^2 (n (p + 2 r) v + (-n (p + 2 q) + l (-q + r)) w)

.. _guide-preamble-0838:

* **X_63254**–**X_63456** — **Points related to the 1st and 2nd Pavlov triangles**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on May 16, 2024. Let :g:`I_aI_bI_c << I_a I_b I_c >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of the incenter I for any triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Denote with :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` the projection of :g:`I_a <I_a>` upon :g:`BI <[ B I ]>`, and with :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` the projection of :g:`I_b <I_b>` upon :g:`AI <[ A I ]>`.Similarly define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`. Lines :g:`A_{b}B_{a} <[ A_b B_a ]>`, :g:`B_{c}C_{b} <[ B_c C_b ]>`, and :g:`A_{c}C_{a} <[ A_c C_a ]>` form a triangle :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>`, here named the **1st Pavlov triangle**. Lines :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` :g:`B_{C} <B_C>`, and :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>` form a triangle :g:`A_{2}B_{2}C_{2} << A_2 B_2 C_2 >>`, here named the **2nd Pavlov triangle**.
  | For more infomation see `Euclud 6171 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6171>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0839:

* **X_63478**–**X_63528** — **Bicevian centroidal collineation images**

  , contributed by Ivan Pavlov on May 21, 2024. We will call **{P,Q}-bicevian centroidal collineation** the collineation which takes the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>` = (:math:`u:v:w`) into the cevian triangle of :g:`Q <Q>`\ =(:math:`p:q:r`) and has a fixed point in the centroid G of the reference triangle.

  The general formula for the image of :g:`X <X>`\ =(:math:`x:y:z`) in barycentrics is

  𝓒𝓛(X,P,Q; G) = ( p (u (v + w) - v w) (v w (p u (q - r) (v - w) - q r v w) x + u (w y - v z) (p v w (q - r) - q r u (v - w))) : : )

  | This transformation has the obvious inverse: 𝓒𝓛(X,P,Q; G)\ :sup:`-1` = 𝓒𝓛(X,Q,P; G).
  | Some existing :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` are presented in the table below: [Table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0840:

* **X_63640**–**X_63655** — **Hatzipolakis-Euler images**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, May 28, 2024. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, P a point and Q a point on its Euler line. Let :g:`Q_{a} <Q_a>`, :g:`Q_{b} <Q_b>`, :g:`Q_{c} <Q_c>` the same to Q points on the Euler lines of the triangles :g:`PBC << P B C >>`, :g:`PCA << P C A >>`, :g:`PAB << P A B >>`, respectively. Let :math:`p_{a}`, :math:`p_{b}`, :math:`p_{c}` be parallel lines to :g:`PA <[ P A ]>`, :g:`PB <[ P B ]>`, :g:`PC <[ P C ]>` through :g:`Q_{a} <Q_a>`, :g:`Q_{b} <Q_b>`, :g:`Q_{c} <Q_c>`, respectively. What is the locus of P such that :math:`p_{a}`, :math:`p_{b}`, :math:`p_{c}` concur?. (:person:`Antreas Hatzipolakis <antreas-hatzipolakis>`, `euclid 6199 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6199>`__.)

  If Q is such that :g:`O_{Δ}Q_{Δ} <[ O_Δ Q_Δ ]>`/:g:`O_{Δ}H_{Δ} <[ O_Δ H_Δ ]>` = t = constant number, for a triangle Δ, then the lines :math:`p_{a}`, :math:`p_{b}`, :math:`p_{c}` concur for every P. (César Lozada, `euclid 6200 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6200>`__.)

  The point of intersection of the given three lines is named here the **Q-Hatzipolakis-Euler image of P**.

  Note that the Dao image of :g:`P <P>`, defined in the preamble just before X_15345, is the :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-Hatzipolakis-Euler image of P. In general, if :g:`P_{D} <P_D>` is the Dao image of :g:`P <P>`, :g:`G <G>` is the centroid :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and Z is the Q-Hatzipolakis-Euler of :g:`P <P>`, then GZ=(1-3\*t)\*\ :g:`GP_{D} <[ G P_D ]>`. From this, it is clear that, for t=1/3, i.e., for :g:`Q <Q>`\ =\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, the :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-Hatzipolakis-Euler image of :g:`P <P>` is :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, for every P.

  Another interesting property of this image is that (Q-Hatzipolakis-Euler image of :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`) = (Q-Hatzipolakis-Euler image of :ref:`X_14 <X_14>`) = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, for every Q.

  Some Q-Hatzipolakis-Euler images of :g:`P <P>` are showed in the following table: [table omitted here].

.. _guide-preamble-0841:

* **X_63656**–**X_63740** — **Points related to the 2nd Hatzipolakis-Moses triangle**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on May 29, 2024. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`. Denote Nab, Nac = the NPC centers of :g:`AHB' << A H B' >>`, :g:`AHC' << A H C' >>`. Similarly define Nbc, Nba and Nca, Ncb.
  | Let :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>`\ = triangle bounded by NabNac NbcNba, NcaNcb. It can be shown that :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are homothetic and this consutrction can be generalized for any :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>`.
  | For more information see `this Euclid thread <https://groups.io/g/euclid/topic/homothetic/106241203>`__.

  | Below we call :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` the **2nd Hatzipolakis-Moses triangle**. The barycentric coordinates of its :g:`A <A>`-vertex are: (
  | a^2 (-2 a^2 (b^2 - c^2)^2 + a^4 (b^2 + c^2) + (b^2 - c^2)^2 (b^2 + c^2)) :
  | -2 a^8 + (b^2 - c^2)^3 (b^2 + c^2) - a^4 (b^2 + 3 c^2)^2 + a^6 (4 b^2 + 7 c^2) - a^2 (2 b^6 + 3 b^4 c^2 - 5 c^6) :
  | -2 a^8 - (b^2 - c^2)^3 (b^2 + c^2) - a^4 (3 b^2 + c^2)^2 + a^6 (7 b^2 + 4 c^2) - a^2 (-5 b^6 + 3 b^2 c^4 + 2 c^6))

  Note that the **unary cofactor triangle** of a given triangle, which is used in the definition of some centers is defined here: `https://mathworld.wolfram.com/UnaryCofactorTriangle.html <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/UnaryCofactorTriangle.html>`__

.. _guide-preamble-0842:

* **X_63741**–**X_63745** — **Perspectors associated with triangles T(u_1,P*)**

  | contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, May 29, 2024. Let :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` be a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` and
  | :g:`A' <A'>` = (q - r)/(q + r) : - (q + 2r)/q : (2q + r)/r
  | :g:`B' <B'>` = (2r + p)/p : (r - p)/(r + p) : - (r + 2p)/r
  | :g:`C' <C'>` = - (p + 2q)/p : (2p + q)/q : (p - q)/(p + q)

  | The triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is here denoted by **T(u_1, P\*)**
  | If P lies on the Steiner circumellipse, then :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and the perspector is the barycentric quotient U/P, where :g:`U <U>` = reflection of :g:`P <P>` in :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. This perspector lies on the Tucker nodal cubic, K015. The appearance of (i,j) in the following list means that X_i is on the Steiner circumellipse, and the X_j is the perspector of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and T(u_1, X_i\*).

.. _guide-preamble-0844:

* **X_63787**–**X_63794** — **Dao-Zeeman perspectors**

  | :contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, June 9, 2024. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle, U a point on its plane, 𝓁 the tripolar of :g:`U <U>` with respect to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and P, Q any two distinct points on 𝓁.
  | Let :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` be the intersections of 𝓁 with :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively.
  | Denote by :g:`A_{P} <A_P>` the intersection of the parallel line to :g:`CP <[ C P ]>` through :g:`B' <B'>` and the parallel line to :g:`BP <[ B P ]>` through :g:`C' <C'>`, and define :g:`B_{P} <B_P>`, :g:`C_{P} <C_P>` cyclically.
  | Denote by :g:`A_{Q} <A_Q>` the intersection of the parallel line to :g:`CQ <[ C Q ]>` through :g:`B' <B'>` and the parallel line to :g:`BQ <[ B Q ]>` through :g:`C' <C'>`, and define :g:`B_{Q} <B_Q>`, :g:`C_{Q} <C_Q>` cyclically.
  | Then the triangle :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` bounded by the lines :g:`A_{P}A_{Q} <[ A_P A_Q ]>`, :g:`B_{P}B_{Q} <[ B_P B_Q ]>`, :g:`C_{P}C_{Q} <[ C_P C_Q ]>` is congruent and homothetic with :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the homothetic center H(P, Q) lies on the line 𝓁.
  | When :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` is the Euler line this result is Gossard perspector theorem.(See here) When :g:`PQ <[ P Q ]>` parallel to the Euler line, this result due to Zeeman generalization. (See here) When P is the centroid this result is the Yiu’s generalization. :person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>` - June 8, 2024.

  Notes added by César Eliud Lozada:

  The points :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`, :g:`H <H>`\ (P, Q) are independent of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` and depend only on :g:`U <U>` or, still better, on 𝓁. Therefore, H(P, Q) can be more simply expressed as H(U) or H(𝓁), this last form preferred here. H(𝓁) is referred here as the **Dao-Zeeman perspector of the line 𝓁**.

  If :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`x:y:z` (barycentrics) then :math:`H(U) = x (y-z) \cdot (x-y-z)`: :. It can be deduced that, algebraically, Q(U) = :term:`Complement <complement>`\ (IsotomicConjugate(:term:`Cevapoint <cevapoint>`\ (U, IdealPointOfTripolar(U)))).

  The appearance of (𝓁, n) in the following list means that H(𝓁) = X_n: (antiorthic axis :ref:`X_44 <X_44>`\ \ :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`, 650), (Brocard axis :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 34349), (Brocard line :ref:`X_39 <X_39>`\ \ :ref:`X_512 <X_512>`, 63787), (:person:`De Longchamps <gohier-de-longchamps>` line :ref:`X_325 <X_325>`\ \ :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`, 23301), (Euler line :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, 402), (Fermat axis :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_13 <X_13>`, 63788), (Gergonne line :ref:`X_241 <X_241>`\ \ :ref:`X_514 <X_514>`, 7658), (:g:`IO <[ I O ]>` line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, 34345), (Lemoine axis :ref:`X_187 <X_187>`\ \ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`, 647), (Nagel line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, 62630), (Napoleon axis :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`\ \ :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`, 63789), (orthic axis :ref:`X_230 <X_230>`\ \ :ref:`X_231 <X_231>`, 6587), (Sherman line :ref:`X_3259 <X_3259>`\ \ :ref:`X_3326 <X_3326>`, 45950), (Soddy line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`, 63790), (van Aubel line :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 63791), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, 63792), (:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 63793), (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 11053), (:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`\ \ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`, 63794)

  The appearance of (i, j) in the following list means that H(X_i) = X_j:

  (1, 650), (3, 647), (4, 6587), (5, 17434), (6, 647), (7, 7658), (8, 4521), (9, 650), (10, 661), (11, 17435), (25, 52588), (30, 14401), (37, 661), (39, 3005), (42, 52592), (57, 6129), (75, 3835), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0845:

* **X_63801**–**X_63809** — **Trigonometric Sums**

  contributed by Clark Kimbering and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, June 11, 2024. This section treats :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>` of the forms sin(nB+mC)+sin(mB+nC) and cos(nB+mC)+cos(mB+nC). The appearance of (n,m,k) in the following list means that X_k = sin(nB+mC)+sin(mB+nC):

.. _guide-preamble-0848:

* **X_63961**–**X_64000** — **Points related to crosspedal triangles, Part 1**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on June 29, 2024. [Editor's note: soon after acceptance, the centers somehow got lost. After recovery, they were published here on January 25, 2025.] Given a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and two points :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` not on its sides, let the line through :g:`Q <Q>` parallel to :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` intersect lines :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>` at points :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`. Similarly define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`. The lines :g:`B_{a}C_{a} <[ B_a C_a ]>`, :g:`A_{b}C_{b} <[ A_b C_b ]>`, :g:`A_{c}B_{c} <[ A_c B_c ]>` form a triangle called here the **P-crosspedal triangle of Q**. We remind the reader of two other definitions used for these centers:

  (1) Through Q construct a line parallel to :g:`AP <[ A P ]>` and let :g:`A' <A'>` be the intersection point with :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Similarly define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>`; :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` is called **P-pedal triangle of Q**.

  (2) The **P-antipedal triangle of Q** is the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` such that :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is :g:`P <P>`-pedal of :g:`Q <Q>` wrt :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`.

  For more information and properties see `Euclid 6286 <https://web.archive.org/web/20240716170620/https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6286>`__

* **X_64426**–**X_64437** — **Composites**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, July 3, 2024. Suppose that :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p(a,b,c) : p(b,c,a) : p(c,a,b)` and :g:`U <U>` =\ :math:`u(a,b,c) : u(b,c,a) : u(c,a,b)` are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, where p(a,b,c) and u(a,b,c) are polynomials in standard form (i.e., p(a,b,c) and p(b,c,a) are relatively prime, and the coefficient of the highest power of a is positive, or if p(a,b,c) is invariant of a then the coefficient of highest power of b is positive.)

  Define the composite P-of-U to be the triangle center given by

  P-of-:g:`U <U>` = p(u(a,b,c), u(b,c,a), u(c,a,b)) : p(u(b,c,a), u(c,a,b), u(a,b,c)) : p(u(c,a,b), u(a,b,c), u(b,c,a)).

  For example, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = :ref:`X_1147 <X_1147>` = a^4(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)(a^4 + b^4 + c^4 - 2 a^2 b^2 - 2 a^2 c^2) : :

  Suppose next that the Euler line is represented as a linear combination of :ref:`X_3 <X_3>` and :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` as follows:

  V(r,s) = a^2 (a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*r + (b^2 - c^2 - a^2)(c^2 - a^2 - b^2)\*s : : ,

  where r and s are not both 0. Let :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_10 <X_10>` = b + c : c + a : a + b.

  Then ":ref:`X_10 <X_10>`-of-Euler-line" is the line given by

  :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`-of-V(r,s), which as the linear combination

  (a^2 (b^2 + c^2) + (b^2 - c^2)^2)\*r - 2 a^2(a^2 - b^2 - c^2)\*s : :

  is essentially :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`\ \*r + :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \*s, the Euler line.

  Reversing the order of the composition gives "the Euler line of :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`", consisting of points

  W(r,s) = (b + c)^2 (a^2 - b c + a b + a c)\*r + 2(b^2 - c a + b c + b a)(c^2 - a b + c a + c b)\*s : :,

  which is essentially X_4075\*r + :ref:`X_596 <X_596>`\ \*s.

  The appearance of (r,s,k) in the following list means that r and s are not both 0 and W(r,s) = X_k:

  (r,0,4075), (0,s,596), (r,r,6532), (r,-r,6534), (2r,r,2), (2r,-r,24068), and in general, we have the :term:`combo <combo>`

  W(r,s) = 3\*r\*\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>` + (3\*s - r)\*\ :ref:`X_596 <X_596>`. The list continues:

  (-4,1,46426), (-10,3,46427), (-3,1, 46428), (-2,3,46429), (1,2,46430), (2,3,46431), (4,3,46432), (3,2,46433), (3,1,46434), (10,3,46435), (-1,1,46436), (-1,3,46437).

  | A selection of points of the form X_i-of-X_i appear next: :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`-of-:ref:`X_1 <X_1>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`
  | :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`-of-:ref:`X_2 <X_2>` = :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`
  | :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:ref:`X_3 <X_3>` = :ref:`X_1147 <X_1147>`
  | :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-of-:ref:`X_4 <X_4>` = :ref:`X_3346 <X_3346>`
  | :ref:`X_5 <X_5>`-of-:ref:`X_5 <X_5>` = X_64452
  | :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`-of-:ref:`X_6 <X_6>` = :ref:`X_32 <X_32>`
  | :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`-of-:ref:`X_7 <X_7>` = X_10405
  | :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`-of-:ref:`X_8 <X_8>` = :ref:`X_145 <X_145>`
  | :ref:`X_9 <X_9>`-of-:ref:`X_9 <X_9>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`
  | :ref:`X_10 <X_10>`-of-:ref:`X_10 <X_10>` = :ref:`X_1125 <X_1125>`
  | [and others].

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_i-of-X_j = X_k:

  (3,3,1147), (3,4,6523), (3,5,6663), (3,6,206), (3,7,17113), (3,8,6552), (3,9,6600), (3,10,4075), (3,11,64440), (4,1,4), (4,2,2), (4,3,68), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0850:

* **X_64446**–**X_64451** — **Miyamoto-mixtilinear related centers**

  | contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, July 8, 2024. The following conjectures are due to Keita Miyamoto, July 02, 2024: In a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with circumcircle ω, denote:
  | .LI li{padding-bottom:6px; before.content: counter(list, lower-alpha) ") ";} :math:`a_{1}`, :math:`b_{1}`, :math:`c_{1}`: the A-, B-, C- mixtilinear excircles of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, respectively. :math:`o_{1}`: the outer-Apollonius circle of :math:`a_{1}`, :math:`b_{1}`, :math:`c_{1}`. :math:`a_{2}`: the circle, other than ω, passing through :g:`B <B>` and :g:`C <C>` and internally tangent to :math:`a_{1}`. Cyclically :math:`b_{2}` and :math:`c_{2}`. :math:`o_{2}`: the outer-Apollonius circle of :math:`a_{2}`, :math:`b_{2}`, :math:`c_{2}`. :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`: the second intersections of :math:`a_{2}` and :g:`AC <[ A C ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>`, respectively. Similarly :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>` and :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`. :g:`A' <A'>`: the second intersection of :math:`b_{2}` and :math:`c_{2}`, and, cyclically :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`. :math:`t_{a}`: the common tangent of :math:`a_{1}` and :math:`a_{2}`, and, cyclically :math:`t_{b}`, :math:`t_{c}`.

  Then: (a) :math:`o_{1}` and :math:`o_{2}` are tangent. (b) :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and the triangle bounded by the lines :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>`, :g:`B_{c}B_{a} <[ B_c B_a ]>`, :g:`C_{a}C_{b} <[ C_a C_b ]>` are perspective. (c) :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and the triangle bounded by the lines :math:`t_{a}`, :math:`t_{b}`, :math:`t_{c}` are perspective.

  Results:

  The center of the circle :math:`o_{1}`, found by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, is X_8158. The touchpoints of the mixtilinear excircles and :math:`o_{1}` are the vertices of the 9th mixtilinear triangle. See X_8158. The center of the circle :math:`o_{2}`, found by :person:`Angel Montesdeoca <angel-montesdeoca>`, is X_35599. See X_35599. The touchpoint of :math:`o_{1}`, :math:`o_{2}`, in (a), is X_64446. The perspectors in (b) and (c) are X_64447 and X_64448, respectively.

  Similar points can be found by using mixtilinear incircles instead of mixtilinear excircles and inner-Apollonius circles instead of outer Apollonius circles. With this new construction: The center of the circle :math:`o_{1}`, found by Peter Moses, is X_6767. The touchpoints of the mixtilinear incircles and :math:`o_{1}` are the vertices of the 8th mixtilinear triangle. See X_6767. The center of the circle :math:`o_{2}` is X_64449. The touchpoint of :math:`o_{1}`, :math:`o_{2}`, in (a), is X_44858. The perspectors in (b) and (c) are X_64450 and X_64451, respectively.

.. _guide-preamble-0851:

* **X_64522**–**X_64584** — **Points related to the 1st Pavlov-Altintaş triangle**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on July 25, 2024. Let :g:`I_{a}I_{b}I_{c} << I_a I_b I_c >>` be the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`. Let :g:`AI <[ A I ]>` intersect :g:`I_{a}I_{b} <[ I_a I_b ]>` and :g:`I_{a}I_{c} <[ I_a I_c ]>` at points :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` resp. Let :g:`N_{a} <N_a>` be the nine-point center of :g:`I_{a}A_{b}A_{c} << I_a A_b A_c >>` and similarly define :g:`N_{b} <N_b>` and :g:`N_{c} <N_c>`. In the following, :g:`N_{a}N_{b}N_{c} << N_a N_b N_c >>` is called the **1st Pavlov-Altintaş triangle**. Its inverse triangle is called the **1st anti-Pavlov-Altintaş triangle**. The barycentric coordinates of their A-vertices are

  | 1st Pavlov-Altinta ş : -a\*(b-c)^2 : b\*((b-c)\*c+a\*(b+c)) : c\*(b\*(-b+c)+a\*(b+c))
  | 1st anti-Pavlov-Altinta ş : a-b-:math:`c : c : b`

  | The 1st Pavlov-Altinta ş triangle is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector X_13476. It is also bilogic to the intouch triangle and has the same centroid - :ref:`X_354 <X_354>`. The perspector of the intouch and 1st Pavlov-Altinta ş triangles is an infinite point, :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`. Some other triangles perspective to the 1st Pavlov-Altintas include: AAOA, Aquila, Artzt, 8th Brocard, circumsymmedial, Lucas central, Lucas inner, Lucas reflection, Lucas tangents, 1st Pamfilos-Zhou, 1st and 2nd Sharygin, symmedial, tangential, inner-Yff, outer-Yff.
  | The 1st anti-Pavlov-Altinta ş triangle is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with perspector :ref:`X_75 <X_75>`. Some other triangles perspective to it include: Gemini 16, Gemini 17, Gemini 111, Aquila, inner-Conway, inner-Garcia, Yff contact, inner-Yff, outer-Yff.
  | The 1st anti-Pavlov-Altinta ş triangle is orthologic to the intouch with orhtology center :ref:`X_3869 <X_3869>`. It is also orthologic to the 5th Conway and 1st Savin triangles with orthology centers resp. X_64002 and :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`.

  For more information on some related triangles see `this Euclid thread <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6477>`__.

Similarly define :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`. The lines :g:`B_{a}C_{a} <[ B_a C_a ]>`, :g:`A_{b}C_{b} <[ A_b C_b ]>`, :g:`A_{c}B_{c} <[ A_c B_c ]>` form a triangle called here the **P-crosspedal triangle of Q**.

  We remind the reader of two other definitions used for these centers:

.. _guide-preamble-0854:

* **X_64970**–**X_65084** — **Basepoints of perspective triangles**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Aug 26, 2024. Given two perspective, but non-homothetic :term:`central triangles <central-triangle>` :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` and :g:`Q_{1}Q_{2}Q_{3} << Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 >>` with perpsector S, determine the numbers :math:`x_{1}`, :math:`x_{2}`, and :math:`x_{3}` such that:
  | :math:`x_{i}`\ \*S + (1-:math:`x_{i})`\ \*\ :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>` = :g:`P_{i} <P_i>` for each i=1,2,3 where the sum and equality are barycentric operations.
  | If such numbers exist they are unique and (:math:`x_{1}:x_{2}:x_{3}`) is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>` which we call **1st basepoint** of :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` wrt :g:`Q_{1}Q_{2}Q_{3} << Q_1 Q_2 Q_3 >>`.
  | Similarly, using the conditions (1-:math:`x_{i})`\ \*S + :math:`x_{i}`\ \*\ :g:`Q_{i} <Q_i>` = :g:`P_{i} <P_i>`, we can define the **2nd basepoint**.
  | It can be proven that if the 1st basepoint exists, then the 2nd basepoint also exists.

  For more information and results see `this Euclid thread <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/6818>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0855:

* **X_65096**–**X_65106** — **Sign-images**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 28, 2024. Suppose that :g:`X <X>` = x(a,b,c) : : is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, and define

  | :math:`f(a,b,c) = x(a`,-b,c) and :math:`g(a,b,c) = x(a`,b,-c)
  | :g:`X' <X'>`\ (a,b,c) =\ :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)`
  | :g:`X″ <X″>`\ (a,b,c) =\ :math:`g(a,b,c) : g(b,c,a) : g(c,a,b)`.

  The point :g:`X' <X'>` = :g:`X' <X'>`\ (a,b,c) is here introduced as the **sign-image of X.** The set of triangle centers is partitioned by the sign-image operation into three subsets:

  | Type 1: self-sign-images X, for which :g:`X' <X'>`\ =X;
  | Type 2: triangle centers X such that :g:`X' <X'>` ≠ X and :g:`X' <X'>` = :g:`X″ <X″>`;
  | Type 3: triangle centers X such that :g:`X' <X'>` ≠ :g:`X″ <X″>`. In this case :g:`X' <X'>` and :g:`X″ <X″>` are a bicentric pair.

  | The appearance of k in the following list means that X_k is self-sign-image:
  | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31, 32, 38, 39, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 61, 62, 63, 64, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 74, 75, [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0856:

* **X_65112**–**X_65118** — **Double-sign-images**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, August 31, 2024. Suppose that :g:`X <X>` = x(a,b,c) : : is a :term:`triangle center <triangle-center>`, and define

  | :math:`f(a,b,c) = x(a`,-b,-c)
  | :g:`X* <X*>`\ (a,b,c) =\ :math:`f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b)`

  The point :g:`X* <X*>` = :g:`X* <X*>`\ (a,b,c) is here introduced as the **double-sign-image of X.** The set of triangle centers is partitioned by the double-sign-image operation into two subsets:

  | (1) double-self-sign-images X, for which :g:`X* <X*>`\ =X;
  | (2) triangle centers X such that :g:`X* <X*>` ≠ X.

.. _guide-preamble-0857:

* **X_65386**–**X_65524** — **Pairs of triangles with a common inconic**

  | contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, September 24, 2024. The following proposition is proved in Macaulay, F.S., *Geometrical conics*, Cambridge, 1895, pp 241:
  | *Prop. 77: If two triangles are circumscribed to a conic, they are also inscribed to a conic; and conversely.*

  In the preamble just before X_14713, there were described a set of conics circumscribing some selected pairs of triangles. Then, according to the reciprocal of the previous proposition, all pairs of triangles having a common circumconic also have a common inconic.

  Let :g:`T <T>`\ =\ :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, :g:`T' <T'>`\ =\ :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be two triangles. The cross-triangle of :g:`T <T>` and :g:`T' <T'>` is defined as the triangle :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>`, with :g:`A* <A*>`\ =\ :g:`BC' <[ B C' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`B'C <[ B' C ]>`, :g:`B* <B*>`\ =\ :g:`CA' <[ C A' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`C'A <[ C' A ]>` and :g:`C* <C*>`\ =\ :g:`AB' <[ A B' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A'B <[ A' B ]>`. Then, by Brianchon theorem, the points :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`, :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` lie on a conic if :g:`A* <A*>`, :g:`B* <B*>`, :g:`C* <C*>` are collinear or coincident points, i.e., if :g:`A*B*C* << A* B* C* >>` is a degenerate triangle. This is the required condition for :g:`T <T>` and :g:`T' <T'>` to be inscribed in a common conic and, consequently, to be circumscribed to another common conic.

  An extensive list of centers of inconics of pairs of triangles can be seen `here <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/X(65386).txt>`__. For definitions of all triangles listed here, check the `Index of triangles referenced in ETC <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0861:

* **X_65635**–**X_65650** — **P-antipodes of points on the circumcircle**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October, 2024. Suppose that P is a point on the circumcircle of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, and that U is the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>`, so that U is on the line at infinity. The **U-antipode of P** is the point, other than P, in which the line :g:`PU <[ P U ]>` meets the circumcircle. If :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p : q : r` (on the circumcircle), then a 1st barycentric for the U-antipode of :g:`P <P>` is given by

  a^2\*q\*r/(a^2\*q\*(q - r)\*r - p\*(q + r)\*(c^2\*q - b^2\*r)) : : .

  this being the Collings transform of the isogonal conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_k = X_j-antipode of X_i and k < 65000: (74,30,476), (98,511,805), (99,512,805), (100,513,901), (101,514,927), (102,515,1309), (103,516,927), (104,517,901), (105,518,6078), (106,519,6079), (107,520,6080), (108,521,6081), (109,522,1309), (110,523,476), (111,524,6082), (112,525,2867), (476,526,16170), (477,5663,16170), [and others].

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that X_k = X_j-antipode of X_i and k > 65000: (741,740,65635), (813,812,65636), (840,528,65637), (843,543,65638), (901,900,65639), [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0862:

* **X_65651**–**X_65709** — **Crosshexagon points and lines**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 13, 2024. Let :g:`T' <T'>` = :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`T″ <T″>` = :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` be two triangles circumscribed by a conic. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` = :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A″C″ <[ A″ C″ ]>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` = :g:`B'C' <[ B' C' ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A″B″ <[ A″ B″ ]>`, and denote :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` and :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. Let :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` = :g:`A_{b}B_{c} <[ A_b B_c ]>`\ ∩\ :g:`A_{c}C_{b} <[ A_c C_b ]>`, and define :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` cyclically. Then: Lines :g:`B_{c}C_{b} <[ B_c C_b ]>`, :g:`C_{a}A_{c} <[ C_a A_c ]>`, :g:`A_{b}B_{a} <[ A_b B_a ]>` concur in a point 𝒳. Points :g:`P_{a} <P_a>`, :g:`P_{b} <P_b>`, :g:`P_{c} <P_c>` lie on a line ℒ.

  The hexagon with vertices {:g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>`} is named here the **crosshexagon** of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`, and 𝒳 and ℒ will be referred here as the **crosshexagon point** and **crosshexagon line**, respectively, of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`.

  Lists of calculated and not calculated crosshexagon points are available **here** (``X(65651).txt``). For definitions of all triangles referred here, check the `Index of triangles referenced in ETC <https://faculty.evansville.edu/ck6/encyclopedia/IndexOfTrianglesReferencedInETC.html>`__.

* **X_65742**–**X_65752** — **D-maps**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 17, 2024. Suppose that :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` are given by normalized barycentrics :g:`U <U>` = (u,v,w) and :g:`U' <U'>` = (u',v',w'). The **D-map** of :g:`U <U>` and :g:`V <V>` is here introduced as the point :math:`u'' : v'' : w''` given by

  u'' = :math:`S_{A}(u - u')`\ :sup:`2`, v'' = :math:`S_{B}(v - v')`\ :sup:`2`, w'' = :math:`S_{C}(w - w')`\ :sup:`2`.

  The name D-map corresponds to the fact that \|\ :g:`UU' <[ U U' ]>`\ \|\ :sup:`2` = u''+v''+w''. If U and :g:`U' <U'>` lie on a line :g:`L <L>`, then every pair of points on L have the same D-map. If U and :g:`U' <U'>` are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then the D-map of :g:`U <U>` and :g:`U' <U'>` are triangle centers.

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the D-map of X_i and X_j is X_k, where k < 60000.

  | (8, 20, 38554)
  | (13, 15, 16163)
  | (14, 16, 16163)
  | (44, 513, 3937) (anti-orthic axis)
  | (230, 231, 125) (orthic axis)
  | (241, 514, 1565) (Gergonne line)
  | (325, 523, 125) (de Longchamps axis)
  | (522, 650, 2968) (Garcia-Reznik line)
  | (513, 663, 3937) (Helman line)

  The appearance of (i,j,k) in the following list means that the D-map of X_i and X_j is X_k, where k > 60000.

.. _guide-preamble-0864:

* **X_65784**–**X_65852** — **Bicevian-, bianticevian-, bipedal- and biantipedal- inconics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, October 19, 2024. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` two distinct points. The following facts are widely known: The circumcevian triangles :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are inscribed in the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The circumanticevian triangles :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are inscribed in the circumcircle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. The :term:`cevian triangles <cevian-triangle>` :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are circumscribed by a conic, named the **bicevian conic of P' and P"**. The :term:`anticevian triangles <anticevian-triangle>` :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are circumscribed by a conic, named the **bianticevian conic of P' and P"**. If :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` are :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>`, the :term:`pedal triangles <pedal-triangle>` :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are circumscribed by a circle, named the **pedal circle of P' or P"**. If :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>` are isogonal conjugates, the :term:`antipedal triangles <antipedal-triangle>` :g:`T' <T'>`, :g:`T″ <T″>` of :g:`P' <P'>`, :g:`P″ <P″>`, respectively, are circumscribed by a conic, named the **antipedal conic of P' or P"**, or the **apedal conic of P' or P"** (see preamble before X_8268).

  In all the previous cases, there are two triangles inscribed in a conic. Therefore, by the proposition *if two triangles are circumscribed to a conic, they are also inscribed to a conic; and conversely*, used in the preamble before X_65386, every pair of those of triangles are tangent to a common conic, here accordingly named, the **bicircumcevian-, bicircumanticevian-, bicevian-, bianticevian-, bipedal- and biantipedal- inconic** of :g:`T' <T'>` and :g:`T″ <T″>`.

  This section includes the centers and perspectors of these inconics for :g:`P' <P'>`\ =X_i and :g:`P″ <P″>`\ =X_j, with 1≤{i, j}≤11. A list of already known centers and perspectors can be seen **here** (``X(65784).pdf``).

  As a remarkable note, for any :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>`, :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is autopolar with respect to the bicevian inconic of :g:`P' <P'>` and :g:`P″ <P″>`.

.. _guide-preamble-0865:

* **X_65887**–**X_65947** — **W-maps**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, October 22, 2024. Suppose that distinct points :g:`U <U>` and :g:`U' <U'>` are given by normalized barycentrics :g:`U <U>` = (u,v,w) and :g:`U' <U'>` = (u',v',w'). The **W-map** of :g:`U <U>` and :g:`U' <U'>` is here introduced as the point W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) given by

  W = W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) = (u - u')\ :sup:`2` : (v - v')\ :sup:`2` : (w - w')\ :sup:`2`.

  As a barycentric square, the point W lies on the Steiner inellipse, and the point :g:`W* <W*>` = u-u' : v-v' : w-w' lies on the line at infinity. Let g(:g:`W* <W*>`) = :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`W* <W*>`, so that g(:g:`W* <W*>`) lies on the circumcircle. Then W = :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>`\ (:ref:`X_2 <X_2>` and :g:`W* <W*>`) = :term:`crosssum <crosssum>`\ (:ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and g(:g:`W* <W*>`)).

  The W-map is related to the D-map introduced in the preamble just before X_65742. If U and :g:`U' <U'>` lie on a line :g:`L <L>`, then every pair of points on L have the same W-map. Thus, W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) can be regarded as a mapping from the line :g:`L <L>` = :g:`UU' <[ U U' ]>` to W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`), for which we write W(L), as well as W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`). If U and :g:`U' <U'>` are :term:`triangle centers <triangle-center>`, then W(U,\ :g:`U' <U'>`) is a triangle center.

  | W(Euler line) = W(:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) = :ref:`X_3163 <X_3163>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_74 <X_74>`
  | W(Brocard axis) = W(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`,\ :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`) = X_11672 = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_98 <X_98>`
  | W(:g:`IO <[ I O ]>` line) = W(:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`) = X_23980 = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_104 <X_104>`
  | W(orthic axis) = W(:ref:`X_230 <X_230>`,\ :ref:`X_231 <X_231>`) = :ref:`X_115 <X_115>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`
  | W(anti-orthic axis) = W(:ref:`X_44 <X_44>`,\ :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`) = :ref:`X_1015 <X_1015>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_100 <X_100>`
  | W(Lemoine axis) = W(:ref:`X_187 <X_187>`,\ :ref:`X_237 <X_237>`) = :ref:`X_1084 <X_1084>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_99 <X_99>`
  | W(de Longchamps axis) = W(:ref:`X_325 <X_325>`,\ :ref:`X_523 <X_523>`) = :ref:`X_115 <X_115>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_110 <X_110>`
  | W(Gergonne line) = W(:ref:`X_241 <X_241>`,\ :ref:`X_514 <X_514>`) = :ref:`X_1086 <X_1086>` = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_101 <X_101>`
  | W(Soddy line) = W(:ref:`X_1 <X_1>`,\ :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`) = X_23972 = crosssum of :ref:`X_6 <X_6>` and :ref:`X_103 <X_103>`

.. _guide-preamble-0867:

* **X_66087**–**X_66089** — **Points releated to the orthic-of-Fuhrmann triangle,Points with coordinates generated using a Perspective Fieldc**

  contributed by Chris van Tienhoven, December 8, 2024. Points X_66087-X_66089 can be calculated in a simple form using the concepts of Perspective Fields. For more information, see the introduction of ETC (November 22, 2024) and the links provded there.

  | **Advantages of Perspective Fields**
  | One advantage of Perspective Fields is that, once the perspective coordinates (:math:`n1: n2: n3`) of a point are known in a Perspective Field [:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`; :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`], the actual coordinates can be calculated using this formula:

  Px = n1.det[:g:`P_{4} <P_4>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`].\ :g:`P_{1} <P_1>` + n2.det[:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`].\ :g:`P_{2} <P_2>` + n3.det[:g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{4} <P_4>`].\ :g:`P_{3} <P_3>`.

  This is particularly useful when working with points whose coordinates are given by elaborate trigonometric functions. By associating such points within a Perspective Field (PF) defined by four reference points---typically with simple coordinates---the calculations yield relatively straightforward results, as indicated by these three examples:

  X_66087 has perspective coordinates (:math:`1 : 2 : 0`) in PF[:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_356 <X_356>`, :ref:`X_1134 <X_1134>`; :ref:`X_1137 <X_1137>`].

  X_66089 has perspective coordinates (:math:`1 : -1: 1`) in PF[:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, :ref:`X_356 <X_356>`, :ref:`X_1134 <X_1134>`; :ref:`X_3279 <X_3279>`].

  X_5390 has perspective coordinates (:math:`2 : 1 : 2`) in PF[:ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_1136 <X_1136>`, :ref:`X_1137 <X_1137>`; :ref:`X_3273 <X_3273>`].

  | **Finding a Perspective Field for a point**
  | To determine the Perspective Field for a point, its perspective coordinates are calculated in different numeric configurations of two reference triangles. If the coordinates match for both configurations, the point is part of the Perspective Field, and its perspective coordinates are already known from previous calculations. Although it is impractical to perform theses calculations for many sets of four points in ETC, there are certainly many other sets of four points that are amenable to Mathematica, Maple, etc.

.. _guide-preamble-0870:

* **X_66193**–**X_66259** — **Points releated to the 1st Van-Khea-Pavlov triangle**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Nov 13, 2024. Let :g:`P_{a}P_{b}P_{c} << P_a P_b P_c >>` be the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>`. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>` and :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` be the reflections of :g:`P_{a} <P_a>` in the midpoints of :g:`BP_{b} <[ B P_b ]>` and :g:`CP_{c} <[ C P_c ]>`. Let :g:`A_{b}A_{c} <[ A_b A_c ]>` intersect :g:`P_{b}P_{c} <[ P_b P_c ]>` at point :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`, and similarly define :g:`T_{b} <T_b>` and :g:`T_{c} <T_c>`. :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is homothetic to the excenters-midpoints triangle with center :ref:`X_55 <X_55>` and ratio r/R. It is bilogic to the following triangles: :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, Garcia-reflection, 1st Pavlov, orthic-of-Fuhrmann. We call :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` the **1st Van-Khea-Pavlov triangle**. For more information see `this Euclid thread <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/7216>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0872:

* **X_66532**–**X_66547** — **Points related to the Kirikami-Steiner trifolium**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Dec 18, 2024. Let :g:`P <P>` be a point not on the sides of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and G its centroid. Denote :g:`A' <A'>` = `Kirikami center <https://chrisvantienhoven.nl/qg-items/qg-points/qg-p15>`__ of PBCQ, :g:`A″ <A″>` = Kirikami center of PCBQ and similarly define :g:`B' <B'>`,\ :g:`B″ <B″>`,\ :g:`C' <C'>`,\ :g:`C″ <C″>`. The locus of points :g:`P <P>` for which :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` are perspective is a circumquartic, which is called here the **Kirikami-Steiner trifolium**. It is tangent to the Steiner circumellipse at :g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, and :g:`C <C>` and has a triple point at G. The Kirikami-Steiner trifolium is the inverse image of K015 in the Steiner circumellipse. In the following list (i,j) means that for :g:`P <P>`\ =X_i the perspector of :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` and :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` is X_j: (1,66543), (3,66544), (6,66545), (37,66546), (39,66547). For more information see `this Euclid post <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/7408>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0873:

* **X_66554**–**X_66580** — **Perspectors related to Morley triangles**

  :contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, December 23, 2024. (Many thanks to Chris van Tienhoven for sharing his deep knowledge on this topic.) Two triangles related to the original Morley triangles are recovered and renamed here: The **Morley-homothetic-inscribed triangle** is the triangle inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and homothetic to the 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd- Morley triangles. This triangle was introduced by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>` as triangle :g:`J_{1} <J_1>`\ :g:`J_{2} <J_2>`\ :g:`J_{3} <J_3>` just before :ref:`X_3272 <X_3272>`. Its center is precisely :ref:`X_3272 <X_3272>` and it has :g:`A <A>`-vertex with trilinear coordinates: :g:`J_{1} <J_1>` = 0 : sin((A - C + π)/3) : sin((A - B + π)/3) (See Peter Moses, :ref:`X_3272 <X_3272>`) The **Morley-homothetic-circumscribed triangle** is the triangle circumscribed to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and homothetic to the 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd- Morley triangles. This triangle is cited by :person:`Randy Hutson <randy-hutson>` in a property of X_8011. Its center is X_8011 and it has :g:`A <A>`-vertex with trilinear coordinates: :g:`A″ <A″>` = -1 : (a\*(-1+4\*z^2)-(2\*(y-2\*x\*z))\*c)/((-1+4\*z^2)\*b-(2\*(x-2\*y\*z))\*c): (a\*(-1+4\*y^2)-(2\*(z-2\*x\*y))\*b)/((-1+4\*y^2)\*c-(2\*(x-2\*y\*z))\*b)

  where x = cos(A/3), y = cos(B/3), z = cos(C/3)

  | or, equivalently, :g:`A″ <A″>` = cos((2\*(B-C))/3)+2\*cos((B-C)/3)\*sin(A+π/6) :
  | -2\*csc((B-C+π)/3)\*sin((A-C+π)/3)\*(sin(C)\*sin((B-A+π)/3)+sin(A)\*sin((B-C+π)/3)) :
  | -2\*csc((C-B+π)/3)\*sin((A-B+π)/3)\*(sin(B)\*sin((C-A+π)/3)+sin(A)\*sin((C-B+π)/3))

* **X_66630**–**X_66869** — **Points related to some P-anticomplementary triangles**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Jan 14, 2025. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P a point and :g:`P_{a}P_{b}P_{c} << P_a P_b P_c >>` the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of P. Denote by :g:`M_{a} <M_a>`, :g:`M_{b} <M_b>`, :g:`M_{c} <M_c>` the midpoints of :g:`AP_{a} <[ A P_a ]>`, :g:`BP_{b} <[ B P_b ]>`, :g:`CP_{c} <[ C P_c ]>`, resp. and by :g:`P_{1} <P_1>`, :g:`P_{2} <P_2>`, :g:`P_{3} <P_3>` the the :term:`isogonal conjugates <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` wrt triangles :g:`M_{a}BC << M_a B C >>`, :g:`M_{b}CA << M_b C A >>`, :g:`M_{c}AB << M_c A B >>`, resp. If P lies on the circumcircle, :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` is similar to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and its circumcircle is the anticomplementary circle.
  | This fact suggests that for each point P we name the triangle :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` - **P-anticomplementary triangle**. Some other properties, if P lies on the circumcircle, include:
  | - The orthology center of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` is Λ(:ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, P), and lies on the circumcircle.
  | - The orthology center :g:`P_{1}P_{2}P_{3} << P_1 P_2 P_3 >>` and :g:`ABC << A B C >>` is the reflection of :ref:`X_20 <X_20>` in :g:`P <P>` and lies on the anticomplementary circle.
  | - The :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`-:term:`anticomplementary triangle <anticomplementary-triangle>` is homothetic to the Artzt triangle with center X_66632
  | - The :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`-anticomplementary triangle is homothetic to the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` with center :ref:`X_20 <X_20>`

  Some of the properties below refer to CTR-triangles. More info on these series of triangles is available `in this catalog <https://github.com/lejean2000/Kimberling/blob/main/ctr/README.md>`__.

* **X_66975**–**X_66989** — **Points on the Moses Inparabola**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, January 25, 2025. This preamble is based on notes received from :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, January 23-25, 2025. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, the **Moses inparabola** is here introduced as the curve given by the following barycentric equation:

  (a - b - c)^2\*(b - c)^2\*x^2 - 2\*(a - c)\*(a - b - c)\*(b - c)\*(a - b + c)\*x\*y + (a - c)^2\*(a - b + c)^2\*y^2 + 2\*(a - b)\*(a - b - c)\*(b - c)\*(a + b - c)\*x\*z + 2\*(a - b)\*(a - c)\*(a + b - c)\*(a - b + c)\*y\*z + (a - b)^2\*(a + b - c)^2\*z^2 = 0

  This curve, a parabola inscribed in :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, has these properties:

  | focus: :ref:`X_109 <X_109>`
  | directrix: :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`
  | vertex: X_66957
  | infinite point: :ref:`X_522 <X_522>`
  | perspector: :ref:`X_664 <X_664>`

  The Moses inparabola passes through X_i for these i: 522, 3676, 4105, 39771, 43924, 57241, 57252, 58858, 58877, 62579, 66287, 66957, 66967, 66968, 66969, and 66975 to 66989.

  Let :g:`A' <A'>` be the touchpoint of the parabola and line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. The appearance of (T, i) in the following list means that the triangle :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>`, being the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :ref:`X_664 <X_664>`, is perspective to :g:`T <T>`, and the perspector is X_i:

  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 664)
  | (anticomplementary, 522)
  | (tangential, 23865)
  | (excentral, 514)
  | [and othersj].

* **X_67010**–**X_67066** — **Points related to the 3rd Pavlov triangle**

  contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Jan 27, 2025. Let :g:`I <X_1>` be the incenter of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` and :g:`M_{a}M_{b}M_{c} << M_a M_b M_c >>` its :term:`medial triangle <medial-triangle>`. Let :g:`T_{a} <T_a>`, :g:`T_{b} <T_b>`, :g:`T_{c} <T_c>` be the reflections of :g:`M_{a} <M_a>`, :g:`M_{b} <M_b>`, :g:`M_{c} <M_c>` in :g:`AI <[ A X_1 ]>`, :g:`BI <[ B X_1 ]>`, :g:`CI <[ C X_1 ]>`, resp. Below, we call :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` the **3rd Pavlov triangle** of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` has the following :g:`A <A>`-vertex coordinates: {(b - c)^2, -b^2, -c^2}.

  | - :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with center :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`
  | - :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is perspective to the intouch and to the 1st Pavlov-Altintas triangles with center :ref:`X_513 <X_513>`.
  | - :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is perspective to the anti-Aquila and to the 2nd Pavlov triangles with center X_63292.
  | - :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is perspective to the 5th mixtilinear with center X_38496
  | - :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is orthologic to the 1st Ehrmann triangle with center :ref:`X_6 <X_6>`. - TaTbTcis orthologic to the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` with center :ref:`X_3244 <X_3244>`. The reciprocal orthology center is X_67018.
  | - The three triangles - intouch, 1st Pavlov-Altintas, and :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` - all have the same side-triangle, which is degenerate with veretices on the line :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`\ \ :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`.

  The inverse of :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is perspective to :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with center X_56179. :g:`T_{a}T_{b}T_{c} << T_a T_b T_c >>` is orthologic to the intouch triangle with center :ref:`X_78 <X_78>` and the reciprocal orthology center is X_12053.

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, February 4, 2025. *Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a scalene triangle and ℍ a rectangular circum-hyperbola of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, i.e., ℍ is an hyperbola through :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` with perspector P on the orthic axis :ref:`X_230 <X_230>`\ \ :ref:`X_231 <X_231>` of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`Q' <Q'>`, :g:`Q″ <Q″>` be two points on ℍ(P). Denote :g:`A' <A'>` the intersection of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` with the perpendicular to line :g:`AQ″ <[ A Q″ ]>` through :g:`Q' <Q'>`, and cyclically :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>`. Similarly, denote :g:`A″ <A″>` the intersection of :g:`BC <[ B C ]>` with the perpendicular to line :g:`AQ' <[ A Q' ]>` through :g:`Q″ <Q″>`, and cyclically :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`. Then: :g:`A' <A'>`, :g:`B' <B'>`, :g:`C' <C'>` are collinear on a line r' with tripole :g:`T' <T'>`. :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>` are collinear on a line r" with tripole :g:`T″ <T″>`. Lines r' and r" are parallel. If :g:`Q' <Q'>` = :g:`Q″ <Q″>` = Q then r' = r" = the orthotransversal of :g:`Q <Q>`. (:person:`Dao Thanh Oai <dao-thanh-oai>` - Dec. 20, 2024)*

* **X_67212**–**X_67222** — **Points on Warren circles**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, February 12, 2025. This preamble is based on notes from Benjamin Warren, February 7, 2025. The points X_67212-X_67222 and X_67225-X_67234 were contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 10-12, 2025.

  In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>` with centroid G and orthocenter H, let :g:`A' <A'>` be the reflection of G in the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B' <B'>` and :g:`C' <C'>` cyclically. Let :g:`G_{A} <G_A>` be the midpoint of segment :g:`AA' <[ A A' ]>`, and define :g:`G_{B} <G_B>` and :g:`G_{C} <G_C>` cyclically. The four points :g:`G <G>`, :g:`G_{A} <G_A>`, :g:`G_{B} <G_B>`, :g:`G_{C} <G_C>` lie on a circle, here named the **Warren G-circle**, which passes through the point X_i for these i: 2, 381, 5465, 9169, and 67212 through 67222.

  Let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the reflection of :g:`H <H>` in the line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically. Let :g:`H_{A} <H_A>` be the midpoint of segment :g:`AA″ <[ A A″ ]>`, and define :g:`H_{B} <H_B>` and :g:`H_{C} <H_C>` cyclically. The five points :g:`H_{A} <H_A>`, :g:`H_{B} <H_B>`, :g:`H_{C} <H_C>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` lie on a circle, here named the **Warren H-circle**, which passes through the point X_i for these i: 3, 4, 15098, 18338, 18341, 18342, 18347, 18348, 31847, 31848, 31849, 31850, 31851, 31852, 31853, 31854, 31864, 31865, 31866, 43389, 43395, 43396, 53716, 53727, and 67225 through 67235.

  The segment :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`\ \ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>` is a diameter of the Warren H-circle.

  The configurations for the Warren circles are partially generalized as follows: Let :g:`P <P>` be a point in the plane of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. Let :g:`A* <A*>` be the reflection of :g:`P <P>` in :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, and define :g:`B* <B*>` and :g:`C* <C*>` cyclically. Let :g:`P_{A} <P_A>` be the midpoint of segment :g:`AA* <[ A A* ]>`, and define :g:`P_{B} <P_B>` and :g:`P_{C} <P_C>` cyclically. Then :ref:`X_5 <X_5>` = :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`-of-:g:`P_{A}P_{B}H_{P} << P_A P_B H_P >>`. (Benjamin Warren, February 12, 2025)

  For further properties of the Warren H-circle and an introduction to the Warren H-triangle, see the preamble just before X_70270.

.. _guide-preamble-0880:

* **X_67279**–**X_67288** — **Points on the Hagos circle**

  :contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>`, based on notes by Elias M Hagos and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, February 27, 2025. Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle with orthocenter H, :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` :g:`H_{a}H_{b}H_{c} << H_a H_b H_c >>` and nine-point center N. Let :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` be the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of N. Let :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>` respectively be the projections of :g:`A' <A'>` on :g:`H_{a}H_{c} <[ H_a H_c ]>` and :g:`H_{a}H_{b} <[ H_a H_b ]>`, and define :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`B_{a} <B_a>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>` and :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` cyclically. The six points :g:`A_{b} <A_b>`, :g:`B_{c} <B_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`A_{c} <A_c>`, :g:`C_{a} <C_a>`, :g:`C_{b} <C_b>` lie on a circle having center X_51888 and radius

  (S^6 + SA^2\*SB^2\*SC^2)/(8\*\ :g:`R*S <[ R* S ]>`\ ^2\*SA\*SB\*SC),

  where R is the circumradius of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`. See `euclid 8026 <https://groups.io/g/euclid/message/8026>`__.

  This circle is here named the **Hagos circle**>, which is the Taylor-circle-inverse of the nine-point-circle-inverse of the orthic triangle. The point X_i lies on the Hagos circle for i = 67279, 67280, ..., 67288.

.. _guide-preamble-0881:

* **X_67324**–**X_67328** — **Orthogonal projections on the Euler line**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, March 8, 2025. The orthogonal projection of a point :g:`P <P>` =\ :math:`p:q:r` (barycentrics) on the Euler line is the point

.. _guide-preamble-0886:

* **X_67401**–**X_67413** — **Dao-Cevaconjugate-conics**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, March 10, 2025. The following theorem is due to **Dao Thanh Oai** (March 6, 2025):

  | Let :g:`ABC << A B C >>` be a triangle and P, Q two distinct points.
  | Let :g:`A_{p}B_{p}C_{p} << A_p B_p C_p >>` be the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`.
  | Parallel lines to :g:`AP <[ A P ]>`, :g:`BP <[ B P ]>`, :g:`CP <[ C P ]>` through Q cut :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`, :g:`CA <[ C A ]>`, :g:`AB <[ A B ]>` at :g:`A'_{q} <A'_q>`, :g:`B'_{q} <B'_q>`, :g:`C'_{q} <C'_q>`, respectively.
  | Let :g:`A″ <A″>`:sub:`q`, :g:`B″ <B″>`:sub:`q`, :g:`C″ <C″>`:sub:`q` be the reflections of :g:`Q <Q>` in :g:`A'_{q} <A'_q>`, :g:`B'_{q} <B'_q>`, :g:`C'_{q} <C'_q>`, respectively.
  | Then:
  | :g:`A_{p}B_{p}C_{p} << A_p B_p C_p >>` and :g:`A″ <A″>`:sub:`q`\ :g:`B″ <B″>`:sub:`q`\ :g:`C″ <C″>`:sub:`q` are perspective, with perspector Z(P, Q)=CevaConjugate(P, Q). Points {:g:`A″ <A″>`:sub:`q`, :g:`B″ <B″>`:sub:`q`, :g:`C″ <C″>`:sub:`q`, P, Q, Z(P,Q)} lie on a conic 𝒞(P, Q).

  The conic 𝒞(P, Q) is here named the **P-Dao-Cevaconjugate conic of-Q**.

  | If :g:`P <P>` = :math:`x_{p}`; :math:`y_{p}`; :math:`z_{p}` and :g:`Q <Q>` = :math:`x_{q}`; :math:`y_{q}`; :math:`z_{q}` (barycentrics), then
  | 𝒞(P, Q) = Σ( (:math:`y_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{q}`-:math:`y_{q}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{p})`\ \*(:math:`x_{p}`\ \*(:math:`y_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{q}`\ +\ :math:`y_{q}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{p})`\ +(:math:`y_{q}`\ +\ :math:`z_{q})`\ \*\ :math:`y_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{p})`\ \*x^2 - :math:`x_{q}`\ \*((:math:`y_{p}`-:math:`z_{p})`\ \*\ :math:`y_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`x_{q}`\ +(:math:`x_{p}`\ +\ :math:`z_{p})`\ \*\ :math:`x_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{q}`-(:math:`x_{p}`\ +\ :math:`y_{p})`\ \*\ :math:`x_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`y_{p}`\ \*\ :math:`z_{q})`\ \*y\*z ) = 0

  Note: 𝒞(P, Q) is a rectangular hyperbola if Q lies on the tripolar linear of the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>`-of-the cross difference of-(P and the :ref:`Orion transform of P <X_2055>`).

  The appearance of (i, j, n) in the following list means that the center of the X_i-Dao-Cevaconjugate conic of-X_j is X_n:

  (1, 2, 67401), (1, 3, 67402), (1, 4, 67403), (1, 6, 67404), (2, 1, 4432), (2, 3, 67405), (2, 4, 67406), (2, 6, 5026), (3, 2, 67407), (3, 4, 67408), (3, 6, 67409), (4, 1, 67410), (4, 2, 12824), (4, 3, 113), (4, 6, 67411), (6, 2, 67412), (6, 3, 67413)

.. _guide-preamble-0897:

* **X_67624**–**X_67642** — **Points associated with the Warren reflection triangle**

  contributed by :person:`Clark Kimberling <clark-kimberling>` and :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, based on notes from Benjamin Warren, March 13-16, 2025. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`A' <A'>` be the reflection of :g:`A <A>` in :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and let :g:`A″ <A″>` be the reflection of :g:`A' <A'>` in line :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`. Define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`B″ <B″>` cyclically. The triangle :g:`A″B″C << A″ B″ C >>` is here named the **Warren reflection triangle**, and its circumcircle, the **Warren reflection circle.** The vertices are given by

  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = a^2 : c^2 + a^2 - b^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2
  | :g:`B″ <B″>` = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 : b^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2
  | :g:`C″ <C″>` = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 : c^2 + a^2 - b^2: c^2

  Let A'''B'''C''' be the reflection of :g:`A″B″C″ << A″ B″ C″ >>` in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`. Then

  | A''' = a^2 : c^2 + a^2 - b^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2
  | B''' = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 : b^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2
  | C''' = b^2 + c^2 - a^2 : c^2 + a^2 - b^2: c^2

  | A''' = -(a^2\*(5\*a^4 - 4\*a^2\*b^2 - b^4 - 4\*a^2\*c^2 + 2\*b^2\*c^2 - c^4)) : (a^2 - b^2 + c^2)\*(a^4 + 4\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 - 2\*a^2\*c^2 - 2\*b^2\*c^2 + c^4) : (a^2 + b^2 - c^2)\*(a^4 - 2\*a^2\*b^2 + b^4 + 4\*a^2\*c^2 - 2\*b^2\*c^2 + c^4),
  | and B''' and C''' are given cyclically.

  Along with the six points :g:`A″ <A″>`, :g:`B″ <B″>`, :g:`C″ <C″>`, A''', B''',C''' on the Warren reflection circle are the points X_i for these i: 2, 376,1106, 14916, 67625 through 67642; at total of 24 points. The Warren reflection circle has persepctor X_67624 and is given by the following equation:

  | c^2\*x\*y + b^2\*x\*z + a^2\*y\*z
  | - (x + y + z)\*(((a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*x)/9
  | + ((a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*y)/9
  | + ((a^2 + b^2 + c^2)\*z)/9)
  | = 0.

  The appearance of (name, i) in the following list means that the Warren :term:`reflection triangle <reflection-triangle>` is perspective to the named triangle,a nd the perspector is X_i:

  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 69)
  | (:term:`tangential triangle <tangential-triangle>`, 2916)
  | (reflection triangle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>` in :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, 4549
  | (:term:`2nd Brocard triangle <2nd-brocard-triangle>` (CTC), 141)
  | (orthocentroidal triangle (see ETC X_5476), 2)
  | [and others].

  Returning to the Warren reflection triangle, the point, let A"" be the reflection of :g:`A″ <A″>` in :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, and define B"" and C"" cyclically. Then

  | A"" = a^2 : a^2 + b^2 - c^2 : a^2 + c^2 - b^2
  | B"" = b^2 + a^2 - c^2 : b^2 : b^2 + c^2 - a^2
  | C"" = c^2 + a^2 - b^2 : c^2 + b^2 - a^2 : c^2

  The vertices A"", B"", C"" lie on the orthocentroidal circle of :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  | For every point :g:`P <P>` on the cubic K060, A""B""C"" is perspective to the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`,
  | For every point :g:`P <P>` on the cubic K001, A""B""C"" is perspective to the :term:`anticevian triangle <anticevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`,
  | For every point :g:`P <P>` on the Keipert circumhyperbola, A""B""C"" is perspective to the :term:`pedal triangle <pedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`.
  | For every point :g:`P <P>` on the cubic K1279, A""B""C"" is perspective to the :term:`antipedal triangle <antipedal-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`.

  The appearance of (name, i) in the following list means that the triangle A""B""C"" is perspective to the named triangle, and the perspector is X_i:

  | (:g:`ABC << A B C >>`, 4)
  | (:term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>`, 4)
  | (:term:`excentral triangle <excentral-triangle>`, 3336)
  | (:term:`Euler triangle <euler-triangle>`, 4
  | [and others].

.. _guide-preamble-0902:

* **X_67844**–**X_68061** — **Points related to CTR28 triangles**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on March 25, 2025. If :g:`P_{a}P_{b}P_{c} << P_a P_b P_c >>` is the :term:`cevian triangle <cevian-triangle>` of :g:`P <P>`, `CTR28(P) <https://github.com/lejean2000/Kimberling/blob/main/ctr/README.md#ctr28>`__ is the triangle with vertices at the orthocenters of APbPc, BPaPc, and CPaPb. The points in this section are related to :g:`P <P>` = :ref:`X_1 <X_1>`, :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, :ref:`X_3 <X_3>`, :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`, :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`, :ref:`X_20 <X_20>`, :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`, :ref:`X_189 <X_189>`, :ref:`X_253 <X_253>`, :ref:`X_329 <X_329>`. Note that:
  | - CTR28-2, i.e when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`, is the Euler traingle.
  | - CTR28-4, i.e when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`, is the reflection of the :term:`orthic triangle <orthic-triangle>` in :ref:`X_389 <X_389>`.
  | - CTR28-7, i.e when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_7 <X_7>`, is the reflection of the :term:`intouch triangle <intouch-triangle>` in :ref:`X_942 <X_942>`.
  | - CTR28-8, i.e when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_8 <X_8>`, is the reflection of the :term:`extouch triangle <extouch-triangle>` in X_5777.
  | - CTR28-69, i.e when :g:`P <P>`\ =\ :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`, is homothetic to the midheight triangle with center :ref:`X_185 <X_185>`.

  In general, CTR28(P) is the reflection of the :term:`cevian <cevian>` trianlgle of :g:`P <P>`, whenever P lies on the Lucas cubic K007. In this case it is also bilogic to :g:`ABC << A B C >>`.

  Some of the properties in this section refer to CTR-triangles. More info on these series of triangles is available `in this catalog <https://github.com/lejean2000/Kimberling/blob/main/ctr/README.md>`__. Also, the abbreviation UCFT means `unary cofactor triangle <https://mathworld.wolfram.com/UnaryCofactorTriangle.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0905:

* **X_68179**–**X_68232** — **Harmonic pencil and harmonic lines**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 3, 2025. Let :math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`, :math:`r_{3}`, :math:`r_{4}` be four distinct lines concurrent in a point :g:`P <P>`. These four lines are said to be an **harmonic pencil** (or harmonic bundle) if there exists a line ρ, intersecting them at :g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`, :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`, :g:`Q_{4} <Q_4>`, respectively, and such that (:g:`Q_{1} <Q_1>`, :g:`Q_{2} <Q_2>`; :g:`Q_{3} <Q_3>`, :g:`Q_{4} <Q_4>`) are in harmonic range.

  The most important fact in the above definition is that if such harmonic range occurs for a line intersecting the pencil of lines, it occurs for any other line intersecting that pencil.

  In this section, three concurrent lines :math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`, :math:`r_{3}` are given and the tripole of the fourth line :math:`r_{4}` is calculated, such that :math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`, :math:`r_{3}`, :math:`r_{4}` form an harmonic pencil. This fourth line :math:`r_{4}` is denoted here as the {:math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`}-harmonic line of-:math:`r_{3}`.

  The appearance of (:math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`, :math:`r_{3})`\ →n in the following lists means that the tripole of the {:math:`r_{1}`, :math:`r_{2}`}-harmonic line of-:math:`r_{3}` is X_n: [lists omitted here].

  Note: These results come from a specific application of a more general theorem involving the conservation of cross-ratios. For more information, see `this link <http://users.math.uoc.gr/~pamfilos/eGallery/problems/Harmonic_Bundle.html>`__.

.. _guide-preamble-0906:

* **X_68268**–**X_68324** — **Co-normal points and co-normals hyperbolas**

  contributed by :person:`César Eliud Lozada <cesar-lozada>`, April 11, 2025. Let 𝒞 be a conic (not a circle) and 𝒩 a point on the plane of 𝒞 and not on it. The points on 𝒞 whose normals concur at 𝒩 are called the **𝒩-co-normal points of-𝒞**.

.. _guide-preamble-0907:

* **X_68326**–**X_68333** — **Points on Warren Q-circles**

  | based on notes from Benjamin Warren, April 10, 2025. The points X_68326-X_68333 and list of :g:`Q <Q>`-circles were contributed by :person:`Peter Moses <peter-moses>`, April 18, 2025. In the plane of a triangle :g:`ABC << A B C >>`, let :g:`P <P>` be a point. Let
  | :g:`A'B'C' << A' B' C' >>` = circumcevian triangle of P
  | :g:`M_{a} <M_a>` = midpoint of segment :g:`BC <[ B C ]>`
  | :g:`A″ <A″>` = reflection of :g:`A' <A'>` in :g:`M_{a} <M_a>`, and define :g:`B″ <B″>` and :g:`C″ <C″>` cyclically
  | :g:`P' <P'>` = :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of :g:`P <P>`.
  | The circle {{:g:`A″ <A″>`,\ :g:`B″ <B″>`,\ :g:`C″ <C″>`}}, here introduced as the **Warren Q-circle**, has diameter :g:`P' <P'>`:ref:`X_4 <X_4>`. See the note at :ref:`X_4 <X_4>`.

  The appearance of (n, (name), {i(1), i(2),..., i(k)}, m) in the following list means that if X_n = Q, then the points X(i(1)), X(i(2)),..., X(i(k)) lie on the circle, which has center X(m).

  (2, (orthocentroidal circle), {2, 4, 6235, 6324, 6785, 6787, 6788, 6792, 6794, 8426, 8427, 9144, 10773, 11005, 13522, 13524, 13531, 14700, 15924, 22540, 31862, 31863, 34235, 61729, 61730, 61731, 61732, 67224}, 381)

.. _guide-preamble-0908:

* **X_68334**–**X_68355** — **Antiproducts**

  | contributed by Ivan Pavlov on Apr 22, 2025. If :g:`P <P>`\ =(:math:`u:v:w`) and :g:`Q <Q>`\ =(:math:`p:q:r`) in barycentric coordinates, we define the antiproduct of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` as the point (-p u + q v + r w : p u - q v + r w : p u + q v - r w).
  | The antiproduct of two points can be conveniently constructed as the :term:`anticomplement <anticomplement>` of their barycentric product. Note that the antiproduct of :g:`P <P>` and the :term:`isogonal conjugate <isogonal-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` is always :ref:`X_69 <X_69>`. The antiproduct of :g:`P <P>` and the :term:`isotomic conjugate <isotomic-conjugate>` of :g:`P <P>` is always :ref:`X_2 <X_2>`. Of course, the antiproduct of any point :g:`P <P>` and the centroid is the anticomplement of :g:`P <P>`.
  | The following relations also holds:
  | (1) II-Caph point of :g:`P <P>` = antiproduct of :term:`complement <complement>` and anticomplement of P. See X_32001 for definition of II-Caph.
  | (2) Vijay 6th parallel transform of :g:`P <P>` = antiproduct of complement and isotomic conjugate of :g:`P <P>`.
  | (3) M(P) = antiproduct of G and (:g:`KP_{2} <[ K P_2 ]>`\ (G) of :g:`P <P>` and P), see the preambles of X_40896 and X_55917 for definitions of M and :g:`KP_{2} <[ K P_2 ]>`. G denotes the centroid.
  | (4) The antiproduct of the :term:`crosspoint <crosspoint>` and the :term:`cevian <cevian>` product of :g:`P <P>` and :g:`Q <Q>` coincides with the antiproduct of :g:`P <P>` and Q.
  | (5) The antiproduct of G and the infinity point of the tripolar of G coincides with the perspector of the conic {:g:`A <A>`, :g:`B <B>`, :g:`C <C>`,\ :g:`G <G>`,\ :g:`P <P>`}.
